# Intake Brief: Main Street — Tutorial Coverage for Action Banking (Contextual First-Bank Trigger)

## Problem statement

The action banking mechanic is fully implemented and visible in the HUD (banked-action counter + tooltip), but the Main Street tutorial never mentions or teaches it. The prior plan embedded banking text statically in T6 (first End Turn). Revised scope: replace the fixed insert with a **contextual, first-time trigger** that fires when the player ends a turn with remaining action points, so the lesson lands when banking actually happens. Staff-first consumption copy must also be softened: note that while some staff grant action points, the player likely won't have any at that early stage.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they need to understand that saving actions across days is a strategic option, not wasted turns, and that the banking lesson should appear at the moment it becomes relevant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Contextual first-bank trigger (producer clarification 2026-10-13):** The banking hint fires the **first time the user ends a turn without spending their action point** — i.e. when the player ends a turn with `state.actionsRemaining > 0` (at least one unused action would bank). The trigger is **not** scoped to the tutorial: it fires both during and after the tutorial, so players who never banked during the scripted run (every week spends exactly one action; the T22 banking day was removed by MS-0MV4F04NN007H3DB) still see the hint the first time they genuinely bank in normal gameplay. Because the scripted tutorial never leaves a spare action, the first firing happens **outside the scripted tutorial** in practice. It fires exactly once — the first time this condition is met — and never fires a second time (persisted flag). It does not fire when the player spends all actions. A mid-tutorial firing must not dead-end progression: the end-turn step completion is deferred while the hint is shown and completed/advanced when the hint is dismissed. Must not block the end-of-turn flow (`processEndOfTurn` still runs).
- 2. **Persistence flag:** Tutorial state gains a persisted flag (e.g., `hasSeenBankingHint` / `bankingHintShownAt`) so the hint is not repeated across sessions/restarts. Flag defaults to false for legacy saves and is set on first trigger; cleared only by explicit tutorial reset.
- 3. **Staff-first consumption softened (superseded — see Reconciliation):** The staff-first rule (staff actions such as the General Manager's +1 are spent first and never bank themselves) is documented in the HUD action tooltip and core rules rather than in the tutorial copy. The original early-game caveat was hosted in tutorial step T5, which was later deliberately stripped of all staff references (CG-0MU9YAZ5U00005J4); re-adding staff copy there would regress that decision.
- 4. **Banking concept + cap + HUD highlight:** Hint/step copy explains unused actions bank up to a cap of 2 and are carried into future days, and highlights the banked-action count in the HUD action counter (e.g., "(1 banked)" suffix) so players learn where to check their reserve.
- 5. **i18n keys added:** New/updated tutorial text keys registered in `tutorial-en.ts` following the `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern (or `tutorial.bankingHint.*` for the contextual hint); no hardcoded card names/costs.
- 6. **No regressions:** Existing 25-step tutorial flow (T1–T21, T23–T26; T22 removed by MS-0MV4F04NN007H3DB), copy, and gate logic remain unchanged except for the additive contextual hint; all existing tests pass. Editorial rules hold (≤3 sentences per box, one point per box).


## Acceptance Criteria Reconciliation (2026-09-29)

The feature was implemented and audited (Ready to close: Yes, all ACs met) in the core repo before this work item was migrated. Two criteria were later superseded by deliberate, documented follow-up work; the delivered behaviour satisfies the underlying intent, so the criteria are reconciled here rather than reverted:

- **AC1 (trigger context) — producer clarification 2026-10-13 (final).** Follow-up **MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8** had inverted the gate to `!tutorialActive` (firing mid-tutorial interrupted the step machine); the producer restored firing while the tutorial is active (option c, 2026-10-09), and the follow-up **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL / commit fdf34aa3** removed the `tutorialActive` condition entirely so the hint fires on the player's first end-turn with unused actions **both during and after the tutorial** — matching the producer's clarified goal that the hint appears the first time the user ends a turn without spending their action point, which happens outside the scripted tutorial. Delivered trigger: `shouldTriggerBankingHint` in `TutorialState.ts` = `actionsRemaining > 0 && !alreadyShown`, gated on the persisted flag, never blocking `processEndOfTurn`. The mid-tutorial dead-end is fixed by deferring the end-turn step completion while the hint is pending and completing/advancing the step on hint dismiss (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`).
- **AC3 (staff-first caveat).** The softened caveat originally lived in tutorial step T5's body. Follow-up **CG-0MU9YAZ5U00005J4** removed all staff references from T5 to keep the incidents step focused. The staff-first rule remains documented in the HUD action tooltip (`MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `actionBankingGmNote`) and core rules; the tutorial-layer caveat is intentionally absent.

Verification on the migrated `tce-main-street` dev line (HEAD 3f98d6b): build clean (`tsc --noEmit` + `vite build`); full unit suite green (247 files, 4029 passed / 3 skipped); banking-hint i18n keys, persisted flag, cap-2/HUD-cue copy, and the non-blocking trigger all present.


### Flow merge — producer review rejection (2026-10-04), resolved 2026-10-06

Producer review rejected the item: "The tutorial still has us progress a step without spending the action point. This is after the community favour action. We can place the bookshop without ending the turn here, so add a step to place the bookshop then end the turn."

Community Favour (T15) is a FREE action (CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET), so the old flow closed a day (T16 end-turn) with the day's action unspent, then placed the Bookshop (T17) on the next day. The fix places the Bookshop (now T16) on the favour day BEFORE the end-turn (now T17), so no day ends without spending its action.

**AC1/AC6 reconciled:** merging the former standalone favour day into the Bookshop-placement day reduces the tutorial from 26 to 25 steps (8 days / 7 end turns, was 9 / 8) and trims the scripted incident deck from 8 to 7 cards. This is a deliberate, producer-requested change; AC6's "existing flow unchanged" is read as "no regressions beyond the requested additive/flow fix", verified by the full unit suite and the new per-day action-economy guards (`tests/main-street/tutorial-action-economy.test.ts`).


## Constraints

- **Tutorial-only changes:** No core-engine, card-system, rule-engine, or UI component changes beyond the narrow persistence field and trigger wiring inside Main Street's tutorial layer. Banking cap (2) and engine accounting unchanged.
- **Editorial rules apply:** ≤3 sentences per text box, exactly one point per box; no time-limited play mentions; no hardcoding of card names/costs in step strings that could go stale.
- **Trigger placement:** Banking lesson is NOT a fixed insert (no static T6 body edit for banking). It is a contextual overlay/step triggered from the turn-controller's end-turn path, gated on `actionsRemaining > 0` and the persistence flag. Staff-first wording update is a copy tweak on the relevant step/hint (not a new step).
- **Action banking is already implemented:** All engine, state, HUD, and tooltip work from CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR and its children is complete.

## Existing state

- **HUD:** `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders the action counter as `<remaining> action(s) left` with a `(<banked> banked)` suffix when `bankedActions > 0`.
- **Tooltip:** `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `buildActionTooltip()` explains banking and appends a GM note when employed.
- **Tutorial:** 25 steps (T1–T21, T23–T26; the T22 banking day was removed by MS-0MV4F04NN007H3DB), defined in `TutorialFlow.ts` (`UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS`), copy in `tutorial-en.ts`. Step T6 is the first End Turn. Persistence lives in `TutorialState.ts` (`MainStreetTutorialStateV1`, schema v1, localStorage).
- **Turn flow:** `scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` `endTurn()` gates via `isTutorialActionAllowed`, sets `skipMarketCycleOnEndTurn` for T6, then calls `processEndOfTurn`.
- **Engine banking:** `MainStreetEngine.ts` `processEndOfTurn` banks `min(actionsRemaining,1)` capped at 2; `executeDayStart` composes `1 + gmBonus + min(banked,2)` into `actionsRemaining`.
- **Editorial rules:** Documented in `tutorial-en.ts` header (≤3 sentences, no hardcoded card facts, two-turn plan-ahead only).

## Desired change

Replace the static T6 banking insert with a contextual, first-time banking hint triggered on the first end-turn with spare actions. Add a persisted tutorial flag, wire the trigger in the turn controller (check `actionsRemaining > 0` before `processEndOfTurn`), show a HUD-highlighting overlay with cap-2 + carry-forward copy, and soften staff-first wording to "some staff grant +1, but you likely have none yet." All changes remain in tutorial copy/state/trigger only.

## Key Files

- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Add/update banking hint strings (title/body) and soften staff-first wording; follow `tutorial.<stepId>.title` / `tutorial.<stepId>.body` pattern.
- `src/TutorialState.ts` — Add persisted flag `hasSeenBankingHint` (schema bump or additive field with legacy default), helpers to get/set it.
- `src/TutorialFlow.ts` — Define the contextual hint's step/overlay descriptor if modeled as a step; or keep hint metadata here for the controller to consume.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — Render the banking hint overlay and highlight the HUD/action-counter zone (`hud` / `actionButtons` zone already exists).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Gate and fire the first-bank trigger on `endTurn()` when `state.actionsRemaining > 0` and flag unset; hand off to hints/overlay without blocking turn processing.
- `src/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Read-only reference for banking math; no edits expected (cap 2, bankable = min(remaining,1)).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (done) — Main Street: action banking (parent feature; banking logic, state, persistence).
- **CG-0MT4ZHQU9003MWER** (done) — HUD banked counter + GM-aware tooltip (AC5 of parent).
- **CG-0MT4ZHR9M007VP9D** (done) — Document action banking in core rules.
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** (in_progress) — Banking-aware AI strategy (separate follow-up; not in scope here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **One-shot timing:** If the tutorial scenario always consumes the action (move Laundromat → T6), the first-bank condition may never fire in the scripted path. Copy must make sense if the player never idles; trigger simply never shows in that run — acceptable. No scenario tweak to force an idle day unless producer requests it.
- **Persistence migration:** Legacy localStorage without the new flag must default to false (hint not yet seen) and not reset completed tutorials.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Engine cap changes, HUD redesign, or AI banking behavior are out of scope — record as linked work items, don't implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (scope): "Does this include new tutorial steps, or just adding banking text to existing steps?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "Both options are viable; prefer embedding into existing steps (T6 — first End Turn) to keep tutorial length stable. A new step is only justified if the concept is too dense to share." Source: self-research of tutorial structure and editorial rules. Accepted: prefer embedding; new steps only if pedagogically necessary. **Superseded 2026-09-01:** Revised to contextual first-time trigger on `actionsRemaining > 0`; no static T6 insert.
- Q2 (scenario): "Does the current tutorial scenario produce a day where the player ends without acting (banked > 0)?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "The current scenario (T3 move Laundromat → T6 end turn) banks 0 on day 1 because the move consumes the action. Day 2 (T7 place) uses the action again. Banking is never observed. A teaching step may need a scenario adjustment — either an 'idle day' step, or a rephrased T6 body that explains banking even when banked=0." Source: self-research of TutorialScenario.ts and budget analysis in TutorialFlow.ts. Accepted: the tutorial copy should explain banking regardless of whether banked > 0 on the first pass; the scenario does not need changes unless the teaching demands an idle day (deferred if scope-creep risk). **Updated:** With contextual trigger, no idle-day scenario tweak; hint simply doesn't fire if never idle — acceptable.
- Q3 (step placement): "Where should banking be taught — T4 (Your Hand), T6 (End Turn), or a new step?" — Answer (Map, research-driven): "T6 (End Turn) is the natural place: 'End the day to collect income and start the next one. Any unused actions bank up to 2 for future days.' This is concise, one-point, ≤3 sentences, and fits the editorial rules." Source: self-research of step content and action economy flow. Accepted: T6 extension preferred. **Superseded:** Now a contextual overlay triggered from `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` on first bankable end-turn, highlighting the HUD.
- Q4 (2026-09-01, producer): "Refactor from fixed step insert to contextual first-bank trigger; soften staff-first wording." — Answer (producer): Replace fixed insert with trigger firing when player ends turn with remaining action points; persistence flag prevents repeat; staff-first text clarifies some staff grant +1 but likely none at this early stage. Accepted: scope reframed to contextual hint + flag + trigger wiring + copy softening.

# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [x] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [x] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [x] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [x] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [x] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.
  **Answer (producer):** As suggested

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a competitive state model with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score plus owner-tagged street slots, so the shared street can host multiple owners deterministically via seeded RNG.

## Context

MainStreetState is single-player only (single resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining/finalScore and 10-slot streetGrid of BusinessCard|null). No owner concept exists. This child is the foundation for all competitive layers. Design is parallel per-player (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner, N-player-ready — not a hardcoded 2-player shape, not a single-player shim per producer decision “latter”). The game remains playable without an AI — competitive state is additive; single-player flow is preserved as the 1-player case (N=1).

## Scope

- Introduce per-player state: PlayerRecord (coins, reputation, hand, staff, actionBudget, score) × N; owner-tagged StreetGrid slots (ownerId per slot, null = empty).
- Deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG (same seed → same initial deal).
- Market/decks/incidentDeck remain shared; challenges/activeEffects remain game-scoped unless a rule explicitly scopes them.
- No AI, no income routing, no phase alternation — those are siblings.

## Out of scope

- Per-owner income/event routing (sibling).
- Shared-day phase machine (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo (siblings).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 deferred child).
- Endless continuation (deferred to separate top-level issue per producer decision).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** State type exposes per-player resources (coins/reputation), hand, staff, action budget, and score per owner plus owner-tagged street slots; setup creates a deterministic initial state from a seed.
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared market/decks/incidentDeck are unchanged and shared across players.
- [ ] **AC3:** Determinism: same seed produces identical per-player initial state (unit replay test); N=1 behaves identically to the pre-competitive single-player baseline.
- [ ] **AC4:** Resource/slot ownership is addressable by ownerId/owner index in helpers (no single-player shim).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Per-player state types (PlayerRecord[], owner-tagged StreetGrid), setup().
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Competitive-aware purchase legality helpers (owner-param where needed).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-state.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive state tests (per-player state, determinism, N-player shape).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Siblings: shared-day phase, income/event routing, AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038), Monte Carlo harness
- Endless mode: separate top-level issue (deferred per producer decision)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a shared-day phase machine where MarketPhases alternate within a day (Option A) and Income/Incident/EndCheck resolve once both players have acted, so competitive turns interleave tightly before shared resolution.

## Context

DayPhase is single-player (DayStart → MarketPhase → InvestmentResolution → IncomePhase → IncidentPhase → EndCheck). No concept of “whose turn within the day” exists. Expected shared-day flow (Option A, confirmed): both players alternate MarketPhases, then shared closing phases run once. This child depends on the competitive state model's active-player tracking.

## Scope

- Shared-day phase machine: active-player index, alternating MarketPhases, then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck.
- Win condition: first player to reach the win threshold wins (confirmed decision).
- Single-player (N=1) unchanged: same sequence with one MarketPhase.
- Diagram shared-day phases in code comment + cover transitions with unit tests.

## Out of scope

- Per-owner income/event routing (sibling — this child's closing phases delegate to that sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred to separate top-level issue).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Shared-day phase machine alternates MarketPhases within a day across N players (active-player tracking), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck resolve once all players have acted; sequence verified by unit tests including edge cases (action budget hand-off, phase entry/exit invariants).
- [ ] **AC2:** Win condition is first-to-threshold (first player to reach win threshold wins); EndCheck detects the winner correctly.

# Rename the re-roll button to 'Research'

## Problem Statement

The market has a "re-roll" action (button, tooltip, HUD tooltip, help text, in-game messages and activity log) that uses inconsistent, mechanical terminology. This item renames all user-facing "re-roll" / "Refresh Market" strings to the game's "Research" terminology, starting with the market button, while preserving cost visibility and all functional detail.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — "As a player, I want the market action to be called 'Research' everywhere it appears, so that the UI terminology is clear and consistent."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Button label:** The market button text changes from `Re-roll (${refreshCost})` to `Research (${refreshCost})`; the dynamic cost stays visible on the button face.
2. **AC2 — Button tooltip:** The hover tooltip headline is "Invest in researching new opportunities", followed by the existing functional detail (cost, card replacement, Market-phase-only availability, and the disabled reason when inapplicable), with "re-roll" wording changed to "research".
3. **AC3 — Consistent user-facing terminology:** All other user-facing "re-roll" / "Refresh Market" strings are renamed to "Research" terminology:
   - turn-controller instruction messages and activity log (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`),
   - the legality/disabled reason and the market-refresh activity log message (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`),
   - the help-panel "Tools" line (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`),
   - the HUD action tooltip line (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`).
4. **AC4 — No regressions:** The button and action remain fully functional (callback, disabled state, click behaviour, undo/redo, save/load) with no behavioural changes; only strings change.
5. **AC5 — Tests:** Affected tests are updated (notably `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`, which asserts the help body contains 'refresh market'), and the new button label/tooltip wording is covered so the rename cannot silently regress.
6. **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, which lists "Market re-roll/refresh").
7. **AC7 — Quality gate:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only user-facing strings, supporting code comments, tests and docs change. No game logic, balance, or data changes.
- The button cost stays visible (`Research (${refreshCost})`) — confirmed by the producer.
- The tooltip keeps the existing functional body and gains the new headline — confirmed by the producer.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — button label `Re-roll (${refreshCost})` (~line 168); tooltip `Pay €${refreshCost} to re-roll the market and replace all visible cards. Removed cards go to their discard piles. Available only during Market phase.${reasonSuffix}` (~line 184); comments mention "Re-roll button" (~lines 146, 148, 158, 182).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — instruction messages `Cannot re-roll: ...` (~287), `Re-rolling the market...` (~293), `Market re-rolled` (~305) and log `Re-rolled market (via UI)` (~306).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — legality reason `Re-rolling the market is only allowed during MarketPhase.` (~45) and activity log `Re-rolled market (-€${cost}): ...` (~110).
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help panel line `Refresh Market: re-roll the market row for coins (5, less with the Accountant).` (~138).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip `No action: re-roll market, sell, end turn. ...` (~118).
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — asserts the help body contains 'refresh market' (line 160); must be updated.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — "Free operations" list contains "Market re-roll/refresh" (~line 277).
- No other test asserts the exact user-facing re-roll strings (checked `refresh-market.test.ts`, `activity-log.test.ts`, `market-extraction-parity.test.ts`).
- The `createActionButton` helper returns a Phaser Container; the label is a `Text` child.

## Desired change

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`: label → `Research (${refreshCost})`; tooltip → `Invest in researching new opportunities.

Pay €${refreshCost} to research the market and replace all visible cards. Removed cards go to their discard piles. Available only during Market phase.${reasonSuffix}`; update the "Re-roll" comments to "Research".
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`: `Cannot re-roll:` → `Cannot research:`; `Re-rolling the market...` → `Researching the market...`; `Market re-rolled` → `Market researched`; `Re-rolled market (via UI)` → `Researched market (via UI)`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`: legality reason → `Researching the market is only allowed during MarketPhase.`; log → `Researched market (-€${cost}): ...`; update comments.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`: → `Research: research the market row for coins (5, less with the Accountant).`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`: → `No action: research market, sell, end turn. ...`
- Update `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` and any other assertions on the changed strings; add coverage for the button label/tooltip headline (prefer a focused test; if a Phaser render test is brittle, use the repo's static source-guard pattern).
- Update `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — button label, tooltip and comments.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — instruction and log strings.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — legality reason, activity log and comments.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help-panel "Tools" line.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip string.
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — update the 'refresh market' assertion.
- `tests/main-street/market-research-button.test.ts` (new, or an existing market-renderer test) — cover label/tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — "Market re-roll/refresh" wording.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Confirmed (Q1):** cost stays visible as `Research (<cost>)` on the button face (producer: "visible").
- **Confirmed (Q2):** the new sentence is the tooltip headline and the existing functional body is retained (producer: "as recommended").
- **Confirmed (Q3):** all user-facing "re-roll"/"Refresh Market" strings are renamed (producer: "everywhere").
- **Risk (related item conflict):** `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` ("Reroll to cost more", plan_complete) AC4 requires the button label/tooltip to report the current escalated cost; keeping the cost in the label preserves that. Coordinate if both land.
- **Risk (test brittleness):** asserting Phaser GameObject internals can be brittle; prefer a static source guard if a render test proves unstable.
- **Risk (missed strings):** "everywhere" could miss a string; mitigation — grep the repo for `re-roll|reroll|Refresh Market` (case-insensitive) at implementation time and after the change.

## Related Work

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open, plan_complete): touches the same button label/tooltip and requires cost visibility; coordinate.
- `CG-0MTKMN7KG006F5EE` — "The cost of a reroll is still 5, it should be 500" (completed): set the flat base cost shown in this label.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): refresh-cost discounts shown in the label/tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions and Answers

- **Q:** What should the button label be, and should the cost stay visible on the face of the button?
  - Options: (a) `Research (5)` keep the cost; (b) `Research` cost only in tooltip; (c) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — preserves cost visibility and keeps `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` AC4 satisfiable.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "visible" — option (a) accepted; the cost stays on the button face.
- **Q:** How should the new tooltip text "Invest in researching new opportunities" relate to the existing detailed tooltip?
  - Options: (a) headline plus existing functional detail; (b) replace tooltip entirely with the sentence; (c) sentence plus phase/disabled reason only; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — preserves actionable information.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "as recommended" — option (a) accepted.
- **Q:** Should the rename extend to other user-facing "re-roll"/"Refresh Market" strings, or only the button and its tooltip?
  - Options: (a) only the button and tooltip; (b) also the help panel; (c) all user-facing occurrences; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — matches the seed scope, which names only the button and tooltip.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "everywhere" — option (c) accepted; all user-facing occurrences are renamed (deviates from the recommendation, as chosen by the producer).

### Related work items

# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.

## Goal (user story)

As a player who just reached the win threshold in endless mode, I want an "Enter Endless Mode" button on the end-game dialog so I can continue playing beyond the threshold.

## Context

CG-0MTIILU5V006GCN4 wired the endless-mode logic: when `config.endlessMode === true` and a player reaches the score threshold, the engine sets `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and keeps `gameResult = 'playing'`. The end-game dialog (`MainStreetOverlayContent.showGameOverOverlay`) already reads `endReason` for display, but the player has no way to actually continue — the only options are "Play Again" (restart) and "Menu" (quit). This leaves the endless-mode feature inert from a player-facing perspective.

## Scope

- Add an "Enter Endless Mode" button to the end-game dialog when `endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- When pressed, the button dismisses the overlay and resumes gameplay from the current state (no restart).
- The button is hidden in all other end-reasons (normal win, bankruptcy, turn exhaustion, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Competitive mode endless mode (separate CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 children).
- UI changes to the main menu or difficulty selector.
- Any Monte Carlo or AI changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** End-game dialog shows an "Enter Endless Mode" button when `state.endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- [ ] **AC2:** Pressing the button dismisses the game-over overlay, resets `endReason` to `null` (or appropriate continuation value), and resumes the game loop — the game continues playing and scoring.
- [ ] **AC3:** The button is not shown when `endReason` is anything other than `score_threshold_continue`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showGameOverOverlay()` adds the button.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Resume logic after button press (dismiss overlay, call engine continuation).
- `tests/main-street/` — New or updated tests covering button appearance/dismiss/resume.

data.description:
Add action-point skills to some staff cards so that hiring them grants the player extra actions per week. The Manager should grant +1 action/week (with its hand-slot bonus reduced to +1), extending the existing General Manager action-economy mechanic down the staff ladder. This adds a second, meaningful build axis (action economy vs. hand capacity) to the staff family.

## Problem statement

The staff family's only differentiating benefit today is hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`) plus a handful of flat discounts. The General Manager is the sole staff card that grants an extra action per week (`actionsPerTurn: 1`), so the action-economy benefit is confined to a single top-tier card. Players pursuing an action-economy build have no mid-tier staff choices, and the Manager — the most cost-efficient capacity card — competes purely on slots. Granting some staff `actionsPerTurn` gives them a distinct build role and makes the mid-tier ladder a genuine trade-off between capacity and tempo.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants staff choices that support an extra-action-per-week playstyle before the tier-12 General Manager is affordable.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants the Manager's slot efficiency re-balanced so it is not strictly the best capacity-per-coin pick.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to hire a Manager that grants +1 action per week (at the cost of one hand slot) so that I can take an extra action each week in the mid game.
- As a Main Street player, I want the staff card tooltip and the Actions HUD tooltip to state the extra-action benefit, so that I understand why my weekly action budget increased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Manager staff card in `src/card-data.csv` grants `actionsPerTurn: 1` and has `handSlotsAdded` reduced from `2` to `1`, while keeping `cost: 700`, `ongoingCost: 250` and tier 3; its CSV `description` text no longer claims `+2 hand slots` (it states the `+1` hand slot and the `+1` action/week).
2. The Director staff card grants `actionsPerTurn: 1` (retaining `handSlotsAdded: 3`, `cost: 1400`, `ongoingCost: 400`, tier 9), so the ladder is Assistant (capacity) → Manager (+1 action, +1 slot) → Director (+1 action, +3 slots) → Executive (+4 slots).
3. A week-start budget with an employed Manager/Director composes as `1 base + sum(actionsPerTurn) + banked (capped at 2)`, with staff-derived actions consumed first and never banked (existing `MainStreetEngineWeekStart.executeWeekStart` behaviour preserved).
4. The staff card tooltip renders `Actions: +1/week` for the Manager and Director (existing `MainStreetFormatting` staff case), and the Actions HUD tooltip note renders whenever any `actionsPerTurn` staff is employed, with wording that is accurate for Manager/Director (i.e. no longer General-Manager-specific) while still covering the General Manager case.
5. Staff without the ability (Assistant, Apprentice, Socialite, Accountant, Lookout, Executive, and the non-action specialists) are unchanged — no `actionsPerTurn`, no behaviour change.
6. `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ 6.0 Action Economy), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (staff table) and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (staff catalogue rows) are updated to list the Manager's and Director's `+1 action/turn` ability, the Manager's new `+1` hand slots, and to keep the action-economy composition examples consistent. The in-game help panel text (`src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`, asserted by `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`) no longer states that extra actions come only from a General Manager.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All documentation and user-facing text listed under **Key Files** (docs, code comments/doc-strings, and the in-game help panel) is updated to reflect the changes. `README.md` and any wiki/docs-site entries need only be updated if they actually reference the affected staff or the action-economy rule.

## Constraints

- **Mechanic is already implemented** — reuse `actionsPerTurn` (CSV column, `StaffCard.actionsPerTurn`, `executeWeekStart`, tooltip/formatting). No new engine mechanic, schema column, or save-format change is expected; the change is data + docs + test coverage.
- Preserve the existing action-economy invariants: bank cap of 2, base-only banking, staff actions consumed first and never banked, defensive clamp in `executeWeekStart`.
- Do not alter the General Manager (tier-12 premium card, `+4` slots, `+1` action, 2000/500).
- Balance sanity: an extra action/week is a significant tempo gain; the Manager's slot reduction from `+2` to `+1` is the designed trade-off. Avoid stacking `actionsPerTurn` beyond what the action budget can absorb (three staff would yield 4 actions/week).
- CSV column order must remain unchanged (append/edit in place); `NUMERIC_COLUMNS` already includes `actionsPerTurn`.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv`: `staff-manager` = `handSlotsAdded 2`, no `actionsPerTurn`; `staff-director` = `handSlotsAdded 3`, no `actionsPerTurn`; `staff-general-manager` = `handSlotsAdded 4`, `actionsPerTurn 1` (the sole action-granting staff card, CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` (`executeWeekStart`): budget = `1 + sum(staff.actionsPerTurn ?? 0) + min(2, bankedActions)`.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`: `StaffCard.actionsPerTurn?: number` documented as the General Manager's +1/day.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (staff case): already prints `Actions: +N/week` when `actionsPerTurn > 0`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` (`buildActionTooltip`): already computes `gmBonus` across all employed staff and appends the note when `> 0`; the note string is General-Manager-specific and will read as generic once other staff grant actions.
- Docs: `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0; `content-design-and-progression.md` staff table; `card-catalog.md` staff rows.
- Tests today: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (GM contract), `action-banking.test.ts`, `ai-action-budget.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- CSV: `staff-manager` → `actionsPerTurn 1`, `handSlotsAdded 1`, description text updated (no longer "Adds +2 hand slots"); `staff-director` → `actionsPerTurn 1`.
- Docs: reflect the new abilities and the Manager slot change; adjust wording so the action-economy rule is generic ("staff with `actionsPerTurn`") rather than General-Manager-only, while keeping the GM example.
- Tooltip: generalise the Actions HUD note wording (or add a dynamic staff note) so it is accurate for Manager/Director, with the GM case still covered.
- Tests: assert the new Manager/Director contract values; assert the week-start budget composition with Manager/Director employed; assert the tooltip/formatting lines; assert unchanged staff do not gain the ability.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Update/extend the tests that encode the new contract (`action-economy.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `help-panel-content.test.ts`) so they fail against the current CSV, tooltip and help text.
2. Apply the `src/card-data.csv` data/description change and the tooltip/help/comment wording changes.
3. Update the documentation listed under **Key Files**.
4. Run the full project suite (AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Manager and Director rows: add `actionsPerTurn 1`, reduce Manager `handSlotsAdded` to `1`, and refresh the Manager `description` text.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — comment/naming (`gmBonus` → generic staff-bonus); logic already generic.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — generalise the `actionBankingGmNote` wording for any action-granting staff.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — update `actionsPerTurn` doc comment (currently General Manager-specific).
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — likely no change (`Actions: +N/week` already rendered); verify.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — §6.0 action-economy wording and composition examples.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table ability column.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue rows for Manager/Director.
- `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` — extend with Manager/Director contract + budget composition.
- `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — update the Assistant/Manager/Director no-regression block (Manager gains `actionsPerTurn` and loses a hand slot; Director gains `actionsPerTurn`) while keeping the non-action staff assertions (Apprentice, Executive, specialists).
- `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` — extend the action tooltip note cases to cover Manager/Director-derived actions and the generalised note wording.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — generalise the in-game help text ("2 with a General Manager") for generic action-granting staff.
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — update the Turn Flow help-text assertion to match.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTISBYLS009936W` — Add Investor staff members (open) — sibling staff-ability design; uses action points ("moved between businesses at the cost of an action point").
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (open) — sibling staff-ability implementation; same CSV + doc + test pattern.
- `MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P` — Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking (plan_complete) — related action-economy tutorial coverage; not blocked by this change.
- `MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z` — Fix staff description text for ×100 consistency (completed) — prior staff CSV/description consistency work.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (Q1 default):** scope is Manager + Director. *If the producer wants only the Manager, drop the Director row from AC2 and AC6.* If the whole capacity ladder (Manager/Director/Executive) is intended, add the Executive.
- **Assumption (Q2 default):** Manager keeps `+2 → +1` slot trade-off as stated in the seed description.
- **Balance risk:** stacking multiple `actionsPerTurn` staff yields 3–4 actions/week, which may over-tighten early-game pacing. Mitigation: assignment is limited to two mid/premium cards and the GM; revisit in balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`).
- **Wording risk:** the HUD note and `actionsPerTurn` doc comment are General-Manager-specific; leaving them unchanged would make them misleading. Mitigation: generalise wording (AC4, §Desired change).
