## Goal

A content designer can run `npm run storylines:editor` and see the committed
storyline graph rendered from `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json`, with
storyline grouping, choice-card distinction, cycle marking, pan/zoom and node
selection. Read-only in this slice — no writes.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
understand an arc before changing it."

## Scope

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — `vite-node` entry point with `--help`,
  `--port` and `--host`; boots the editor host and exits 0 on `--help`.
- Editor host serving the dev page via a dedicated `vite.editor.config.ts`
  (the root `vite.config.ts` is auto-generated and must not be hand-edited).
- `view-model.ts` — pure loader/mapper from the manifest (keys `version`,
  `source`, `storylineIds`, `nodes`, `edges`, `cycles`) to a render-ready view
  model (nodes, edges, storyline groups, choice flags, cycle flags).
- `graph-renderer.ts` — SVG graph rendering (no new runtime dependency) with
  pan/zoom, node selection, storyline grouping, choice-card styling, cycle-edge
  marking.
- Toolbar/sidebar shell showing a selected node's links and metadata.
- Reuse the exported read-only helpers in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`
  (`filterManifestByStoryline`, `nodeLabel`, `briefEventDescription`,
  `describeEventImpact`, `describeChoiceRouting`) for per-storyline grouping and
  node labels instead of re-deriving them in the editor.
- Scale: the committed manifest holds 5 storylines, 71 nodes, 15 edges and 1
  cycle; the viewer must render from one loaded manifest and stay responsive at
  that scale (no per-node network round-trip).
- The static docs renderer `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph.ts`
  (`npm run storylines:graph:svg`, completed in `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`) is
  server-side and docs-only — do not call it from the browser viewer; match its
  per-storyline grouping conventions instead.
- `./package.json` — add the `storylines:editor` script.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run storylines:editor -- --help` exits 0 from the repo root on the
  existing Vite/`vite-node` toolchain; no new runtime dependency is added.
- The rendered graph shows every node and edge in the committed manifest;
  choice cards are visually distinct, storyline grouping and cycle edges are
  shown, and pan/zoom plus node selection work.
- Selecting a node shows its links and metadata (name, effect, coin/reputation
  deltas, accept/reject targets, storyline id/title).
- A unit test diffs the view model (nodes, edges, storyline ids/titles, cycle
  flags) against the committed manifest and finds them identical.
- A browser test covers the viewer rendering and node selection.
- No editor file is reachable from the production game entry graph
  (`./index.html` / `./main.ts`); a build-exclusion assertion passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-cli.ts` — **new** entry point.
- `./vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor host config.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/index.html` — **new** editor page.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/app.ts` — **new** page shell.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — **reuse** (read-only) manifest types and
  filtering/label helpers.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/view-model.ts` — **new** manifest view model.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/graph-renderer.ts` — **new** SVG renderer.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/view-model.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/viewer.browser.test.ts` — **new**.
- `./package.json` — **edit** add the `storylines:editor` script.

## Deliverables

- Launchable read-only editor, view model, SVG renderer, unit + browser tests,
  build-exclusion guard.

data.description:
## Goal

Edits from the editor are routed through the existing transactional author API,
previewed and validated before writing, with committed artefacts regenerated and
a concurrency guard preventing lost updates.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want an edit to be previewed and validated before it
is written, so I cannot write a dangling chain or clobber someone else's edit."

## Scope

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — thin bridge over the existing modules,
  reusing their exported functions:
  - `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — `parseCsv`, `addCard`, `linkCard`,
    `applyToFile`, `parseAuthorArgs` (`add-card` / `link`). Storyline assignment
    and retitling go through `linkCard`'s `storylineId` / `storylineTitle`
    fields; expose them as a `setStoryline` bridge wrapper for F4. Note: the
    module header documents a `set-storyline` command, but the CLI implements
    only `add-card` and `link` today — do not depend on an unimplemented
    command or add a second CSV write path.
  - `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — `validateStorylines`,
    `formatStorylineReport`, `storylineReportToJson`.
  - `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — `buildStorylineManifest`,
    `serializeManifest`, `renderMermaid`.
  Expose `previewEdit`, `validateEdit`, `applyEdit`, `regenerateArtefacts`.
- Editor host API endpoints (same Vite/`vite-node` toolchain so the `?raw` CSV
  import resolves) for preview / validate / apply.
- Diff/preview response: before/after CSV rows for the affected card(s) plus the
  validation report.
- Concurrency guard: content hash of `src/card-data.csv` captured at load,
  compared before any write; on mismatch refuse and instruct a reload. Reuse
  `computeCsvChecksum` from `src/CsvChecksum.ts` (already the CSV change-
  detection hash) rather than inventing a second hash.
- All writes go through `applyToFile` in `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`,
  which already writes atomically (temp file + `renameSync`) after in-memory
  validation; the bridge must not write the CSV itself.
- Artefact regeneration after an accepted edit: write `storyline-graph.mmd` and
  `storyline-manifest.json` (deterministic/timestamp-free generators) **and**
  the generated docs derived from the manifest — `npm run storylines:graph:svg`
  writes `docs/game/storylines/*.md`, `docs/game/storyline-incident-index.md`
  and the per-storyline SVGs under `docs/game/assets/`, all byte-checked by
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph-svg.test.ts`.
- Hand-written doc sections are **not** machine-generated: the §7.2 shipped-graph
  table in `docs/game/storylines.md` (id/name/storyline/accept/reject, guarded by
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`) and the `src/README.md`
  references. When an edit touches a documented row, the bridge must return an
  explicit "manual documentation update required" result naming the check that
  now fails, instead of claiming the drift guard passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every edit returns a preview/diff and runs the validator before writing; an
  invalid edit exits non-zero, leaves `src/card-data.csv` byte-identical, and
  surfaces the offending card/link.
- After an accepted edit, `docs/dev/assets/storyline-graph.mmd`,
  `docs/dev/assets/storyline-manifest.json` and the generated docs
  (`npm run storylines:graph:svg` output) are regenerated;
  `npm run storylines:graph -- --format json --check`,
  `npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` and
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` pass.
- If `src/card-data.csv` changed on disk since load, the bridge refuses to write
  and returns a reload instruction (unit test).
- No editor module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through
  `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`; the T1 write-path guard passes.
- A round-trip test on a fixture proves a valid edited fixture validates and,
  when the edit changes a hand-documented row, the bridge reports the required
  manual doc update naming `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-api.ts` — **new** author/validator/graph bridge.
- `src/CsvChecksum.ts` — **reuse** `computeCsvChecksum` for the concurrency guard.
- `src/scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` — **new** host API endpoints.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/bridge.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/preview-validate.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/concurrency.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Write bridge, host API endpoints, preview/diff payload, concurrency guard,
  artefact regeneration, unit tests.

## Goal

Authors can edit existing card fields and add/relink a card through guided forms
that show a diff preview and inline validation before committing.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor links
in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write a dangling
chain."

## Scope

- Edit form for existing card fields: `name`, effect text, coin/reputation
  deltas, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, `storylineId`,
  `storylineTitle`.
- Guided "add card" form that creates a card and links it into a storyline
  (`addCard` + `linkCard` through the F2 bridge).
- Preview panel showing the pending diff; inline validation errors that block
  the write, rendered from `formatStorylineReport` / `storylineReportToJson`
  (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) so the editor and the CLI report
  identically.
- Discard pending (unwritten) changes before committing, leaving the CSV
  untouched.
- Wire the forms to the F2 bridge (`previewEdit` / `validateEdit` / `applyEdit`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The editor edits every field listed above; a round-trip test proves the edit
  validates and is written through the author API.
- The add-card form creates a card and links it into a storyline.
- Pending (unwritten) changes can be discarded before committing, leaving the
  CSV byte-identical.
- A preview/diff is shown before each accepted edit; validation errors surface
  inline and block the write.
- A browser test drives a representative edit round-trip on a fixture.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/tools/storyline-editor/edit-forms.ts` — **new** card field/edit forms.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/add-card-form.ts` — **new** guided add/link form.
- `src/tools/storyline-editor/preview-panel.ts` — **new** diff + validation panel.

- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/edit-roundtrip.browser.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

## Goal

Authors can create or rename a storyline group and reassign member cards through
the editor, driven through the same transactional author API (`linkCard`'s
`storylineId` / `storylineTitle` fields, exposed by F2 as a `setStoryline`
wrapper — the author CLI's `set-storyline` is documented but not implemented).

## Scope

- Storyline list view (the five shipped storylines plus any created in-session),
  derived from the manifest's `storylineIds` and node `storylineId` /
  `storylineTitle`.
- Create a new `storylineId` / `storylineTitle` group. A storyline exists
  implicitly through its member cards' `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`; there is
  no separate declaration file to edit.
- Rename an existing group and retitle it — a batch over every member card:
  apply the storyline fields to each member in memory (`setStoryline`), validate
  the combined result once before the first write, then write once through
  `applyToFile`.
- Reassign member cards to a group.
- All operations route through the F2 bridge and validate before write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating a storyline group, renaming one, and reassigning member cards all
  route through the F2 `setStoryline` bridge (backed by `linkCard`) and the
  validator before write.
- The storyline list reflects the manifest after an accepted edit.
- Tests cover create/rename/reassign against a fixture CSV without mutating the
  committed CSV.
- The T1 write-path guard still passes (no second CSV write path is introduced).

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

- `src/tools/storyline-editor/storyline-manager.ts` — **new** storyline CRUD UI.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/storyline-manager.test.ts` — **new**.

## Deliverables

- Storyline management UI, create/rename/reassign operations, unit tests.

## Goal

Document the visual storyline editor for content designers and developers, and
run the final full-suite regression sweep once all editor features have landed.

## Context

`tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` pins the canonical doc
structure: headings `## 1. Concepts` … `## 10. Roadmap` (the doc also carries
`## 11. Related documents`), the five CSV columns, the tooling commands
(`validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph`, `storylines:author`), and
cross-references from `src/README.md` and
`docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md`. New editor documentation must
extend those sections **without breaking the pinned headings or the drift
guard**.

The generated storyline pages (`docs/game/storylines/*.md`,
`docs/game/storyline-incident-index.md` and the SVG assets under
`docs/game/assets/`) are produced by `npm run storylines:graph:svg`; only the
hand-written prose sections may be edited — run
`npm run storylines:graph:svg -- --check` after touching anything generated.

## Scope

- `docs/game/storylines.md` — document `npm run storylines:editor`
  (launch), the read-only viewer, the edit workflow, preview/validation,
  artefact regeneration and storyline management, within the existing §5
  (Tooling) and §7 (Authoring walkthrough) structure.
- `src/README.md` — reference the `storylines:editor` script alongside the
  existing script/column references.
- `docs/game/content-design-and-progression.md` — reference the editor
  where the authoring workflow is described, if needed.
- Accurate code comments on the new editor modules.
- Final full-suite regression sweep, including the doc-drift and storylines
  tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/game/storylines.md` documents `npm run storylines:editor`, the
  viewer, the edit workflow, validation and artefact regeneration.
- `src/README.md` references the editor script and any new fields.

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play against one or more AI opponents from the game UI, so that I can enjoy a competitive mode without needing a second human player.

This epic covers the three enabling steps required to make **AI competitive mode playable**:

1. Plan the UI/scene work (design the competitive-mode rendering, input, turn orchestration and overlay changes).
2. Add a game-mode selector (Single-player vs Competitive, with opponent count and per-AI strategy/difficulty).
3. Wire up the AI player so `MainStreetAiPlayer` drives AI turns against the engine's competitive turn orchestrator, interleaved with human turns.

## Background

- The engine-level competitive mode (shared day, per-player wallets/ownership, N-player-ready, `competitiveWinnerId`) shipped as a deliberate scope extension (`CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`) in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` and `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`.
- Milestone 3 explicitly deferred the UI: "AI vs. player (competitive mode) | **Superseded** — engine-level competitive mode shipped …; rendering/scene deferred to a planning child" (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`).
- Three selectable AI strategies already exist in `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `Random`, `Greedy`, `BankingGreedy` — plus the `MainStreetAiPlayer` wrapper and `enumerateLegalActions`/`executeAction` seams. They are currently used headlessly only (Monte Carlo balance harness, hint generation, auto-play).
- Game setup currently presents a single-player flow only (`configs/game.json` selects one game; `MainStreetScene` has no mode selector).

## Scope

### 1. Plan the UI/scene work
Produce a design/plan (via `/skill:plan`) for competitive-mode scene changes: player roster/score display, per-player turn indication, action routing between human and AI seats, overlay/HUD changes, and persistence/save-load across multiple players.

### 2. Add a game-mode selector
Let the player choose **Single-player** vs **Competitive (human vs AI)** at game start, including:
- number of AI opponents (>= 1);
- per-opponent AI strategy (Random / Greedy / BankingGreedy) and difficulty (Easy / Medium / Hard);
- propagate the selection into the competitive state created by the engine.

### 3. Wire up the AI player
Drive `MainStreetAiPlayer` to consume engine actions on each AI player's turn under the shared-day competitive turn orchestrator, returning control to the human player between seats, with no manual intervention and no stalls.

## Out of scope

- Spectator/replay visuals for AI-vs-AI matches — tracked as a separate work item (discovered-from this epic).
- Networked or local multi-human play; competitive mode is human vs AI only for this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive game can be started from the UI.** The player can start a new game in Competitive mode, choosing at least one AI opponent and each AI's strategy/difficulty, and the selection is reflected in the created game state. *Metric: manual playthrough plus a test asserting the state's `players[]` and per-player strategy/difficulty match the selection.*
2. **AI turns are driven end-to-end.** Each AI seat's actions are chosen by `MainStreetAiPlayer` and applied through the competitive engine path with no manual intervention. *Metric: an automated integration test plays a full competitive game to a terminal condition.*
3. **Human and AI share the competitive path.** The human player's actions are routed through the same competitive engine path as the AI (shared day), and per-player coins/reputation/score are correct for every player. *Metric: integration test asserts per-player state divergence; UI displays each player's wallet and score.*
4. **Games resolve without deadlock.** A full competitive game completes and resolves a winner via the engine end conditions (`competitiveWinnerId` / score / bankruptcy / reputation collapse). *Metric: test plays multiple seeds to completion with no timeouts or stalls.*
5. **Single-player is unchanged.** Single-player mode has no behavioural or balance regression. *Metric: existing single-player unit/integration tests pass and Monte Carlo baselines are unchanged.*

## Dependencies and notes

- Child items will be created under this epic by the plan phase; the design/plan item (scope 1) blocks the selector and AI-wiring children.
- Reuse the engine AI seams (`enumerateLegalActions`, `scoreAction`, `executeAction`) rather than duplicating game logic.
- Keep save/load working for competitive states (`src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`).

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player or observer, I want to watch AI-vs-AI competitive matches with spectator/replay visuals, so that I can study the AI strategies and enjoy demos without taking a turn.

## Background

- Discovered from epic **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** (Playable AI competitive mode). That epic covers the human-vs-AI playable mode; this item adds the all-AI observer experience on top and is **not** a dependency of the epic.
- The engine competitive mode and the selectable AI strategies (`Random`, `Greedy`, `BankingGreedy`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) already exist (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`).
- Replay infrastructure exists: `src/scripts/adapters/MainStreetReplayAdapter.ts` (referenced by `configs/game.json`) and transcript recording via `recordMainStreetEvent` (`src/MainStreetTranscript.ts`).
- This item assumes the competitive UI from the epic exists (or an equivalent headless entry point) before it can be started.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AI-vs-AI match can be started.** A spectator can start a match where every seat is AI-controlled, choosing each AI's strategy/difficulty. *Metric: manual playthrough; all seats shown as AI with the chosen strategy.*
2. **Actions are visible as they happen.** Each AI action is presented in order (e.g. active-seat/turn indicator plus a transcript/log entry) so a spectator can follow the match. *Metric: visual verification of every AI action in a short match.*
3. **Deterministic replay.** A completed AI-vs-AI match can be replayed from its seed/transcript and yields the identical final state as the live run. *Metric: automated test replays a recorded match and asserts equality of the terminal state.*
4. **Playback controls.** The spectator can pause, resume, step and change playback speed. *Metric: manual verification of each control.*
5. **No regressions.** Single-player and the human-vs-AI competitive mode are unaffected. *Metric: existing unit/integration tests pass.*

## Notes

- Rendering/visual items may require manual verification; keep the deterministic-replay AC automated.
- Reuse the transcript/seed determinism already required by the engine rather than adding a parallel recording mechanism.

# Intake Brief: Avoid duplicate Main Street card SVG regeneration on game start (MS-0MUTU19SF007791K)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> Main Street regenerates all 174 card SVGs from CSV data twice on every game start, because `loadCampaignAndSetup()` regenerates synchronously and then regenerates again after the async static-SVG fetches resolve. The duplicate work wastes startup CPU and emits a misleading duplicate console log.

## Problem Statement

When a Main Street game starts, `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` runs twice, producing the duplicate console line:

```
MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts:112 [MainStreetSvgTextureManager] Regenerated 174 card SVGs from CSV data
MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts:112 [MainStreetSvgTextureManager] Regenerated 174 card SVGs from CSV data
```

The second regeneration exists as a defensive re-apply: `loadCardSvgSources()` (called from `preload()`) starts async `fetch()`es for the static SVG assets, and those fetch callbacks call `cardSvgSources.set(...)` unconditionally, so a late-resolving fetch can clobber the CSV-fresh SVG that the synchronous regeneration just produced. To defeat that race, `loadCampaignAndSetup()` chains a second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` onto `cardSvgLoadPromise`.

That is correct but wasteful: the whole 174-row `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow()` pass (including embedded base64 card art) runs twice on every boot, and the duplicate log makes it look like the startup pipeline is broken. The same redundancy is latent in `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()`, which regenerates a third time whenever a CSV mismatch is detected — even though the synchronous early regeneration has already made the sources fresh.

## Users

- **Developer:** Starting the dev server and reading the browser console. A duplicate "Regenerated 174 card SVGs" line is confusing and suggests the CSV/SVG startup pipeline is firing twice.
  - *"As a developer, I want the startup log to clearly show one regeneration, so I can trust that the CSV→SVG pipeline runs once and is not double-initialised."*
- **Player (startup latency):** Card SVG generation is on the boot critical path. Doing it twice adds avoidable work before the first frame renders.
  - *"As a player, I want the game to start as quickly as possible and not do redundant work while loading."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Single regeneration per CSV content per manager:** `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` is idempotent for an unchanged `CSV_CHECKSUM` — calling it twice in a row generates the CSV SVGs once, logs the "Regenerated … card SVGs" message once, and the second call is a cheap no-op. Verified by a unit test that spies on the generation pass / log and asserts one run.
- 2. **Fetched static SVGs never clobber CSV-fresh sources:** `loadCardSvgSources()` does not overwrite a `cardSvgSources` entry that is already populated, so a late-resolving static-SVG `fetch()` cannot replace a CSV-regenerated source. Verified by a unit test with a mocked `fetch` that pre-populates a template id and asserts it is unchanged after the fetch resolves.
- 3. **No regression in CSV freshness:** After the async `cardSvgLoadPromise` chain completes on a boot with unchanged CSV, every template id present in the CSV still maps to the CSV-generated SVG (not the static asset) and the non-CSV card-back template remains populated. Verified by an existing/added test.
- 4. **Redundant re-apply chain removed:** `loadCampaignAndSetup()` no longer performs a second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` after `cardSvgLoadPromise`; the synchronous early regeneration remains, and prewarming is still guaranteed to run after a fresh regeneration. Verified by code inspection + the no-console-errors E2E remains green.
- 5. **Mismatch path is non-redundant:** When `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` runs against sources already regenerated for the current `CSV_CHECKSUM`, it does not trigger another full generation pass.
- 6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments (the JSDoc in `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` and the comments in `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`), README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- 7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve the CSV-freshness guarantee:** the fix must not reintroduce the race fixed by `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` (stale static SVGs winning over CSV data).
- **Keep the synchronous early regeneration:** it populates `cardSvgSources` before the async fetches resolve, so the first synchronous `refreshAll()` renders CSV-fresh cards rather than fallback placeholders. Removing it would regress first paint.
- **No new dependencies / no build-pipeline change:** work within the existing Vite + Phaser setup.
- **Game repo only:** this is a Main Street change (`tce-main-street`); no core-engine API changes are expected.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` loops `getCsvRows()` and calls `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow(row)` for each row, storing results in `scene.cardSvgSources` and logging on success.
- `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.loadCardSvgSources()` fetches static SVGs (one per template id + the card back) and sets `cardSvgSources` unconditionally in each `.then()` callback.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.loadCampaignAndSetup()` calls `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` synchronously and then reassigns `s.cardSvgLoadPromise = s.cardSvgLoadPromise.then(() => regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv())` — the source of the duplicate.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` may call `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` a third time.
- Existing unit tests in `tests/main-street/svg-texture-cache-invalidation.test.ts` cover regeneration + prewarm-at-DPR invalidation, but not idempotency or the fetch-overwrite guard.
- Background/design: `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` ("Ensure card data is loaded from CSV when a new game starts") introduced the synchronous early regeneration and documented the race; this item tidies the defensive double-regeneration it left behind.

## Desired Change

Make regeneration idempotent and remove the redundant re-apply:

1. **Track provenance for fetched vs regenerated sources.** In `loadCardSvgSources()`, only set a `cardSvgSources` entry when one is not already present (or otherwise record that CSV regeneration owns those keys), so static-SVG fetches can never overwrite CSV-fresh entries. The card-back template (not in the CSV) is still set by its fetch.
2. **Memoise CSV regeneration.** Record the `CSV_CHECKSUM` that `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` last generated for; a subsequent call with the same checksum returns early (no generation pass, no log). This makes the `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` path a no-op when sources are already fresh, and makes "Reset All Progress" (`StatsOverlay` re-invokes `loadCampaignAndSetup()`) cheap.
3. **Remove the redundant re-apply chain** in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`; keep the synchronous early regeneration and the existing `cardSvgLoadPromise.then(prewarm…)` ordering so prewarming still only sees fresh sources.
4. Update the surrounding comments/JSDoc to describe the new single-regeneration contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — Add CSV-checksum memoisation to `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` and a no-overwrite guard to `loadCardSvgSources()`; update JSDoc.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` — Remove the second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` re-apply chain in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`; update comments.
- `tests/main-street/svg-texture-cache-invalidation.test.ts` — Add unit tests for regeneration idempotency and the fetch no-overwrite guard.
- `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` — Existing guard that the boot pipeline stays console-clean; keep green (no change expected).

## Related Work

- `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` — [Completed] "Ensure card data is loaded from CSV when a new game starts". Introduced the synchronous early regeneration and the race-avoidance design that this item simplifies.
- `CG-0MRF343AJ004N6ZW` — [Completed] "Ensure SVGs are regenerated when CSV changes on game start and load". Added the CSV checksum + regeneration pipeline.
- `CG-0MRBDPFPH009Y8M0` — Game balance tooling built on CSV-driven card data (consumes the same `cardSvgSources`/regeneration seam).
- `MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY` — Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard (doc-relevant).

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Stale-source regression:** if the no-overwrite guard is too broad, the card-back template or any template absent from the CSV could be left unpopulated. Mitigation: guard by presence of an existing entry only; do not filter by `ms_card_` prefix, and keep the guard template-agnostic so non-CSV assets still load.
- **Memoisation masking a legitimate re-generation.** If SVG generation ever becomes state-dependent (not purely CSV-derived), the checksum key would be insufficient. Mitigation: key the memo on `CSV_CHECKSUM` and document the invariant that generated SVGs are a pure function of the CSV.
- **Scene-restart map persistence:** `scene.cardSvgSources` is a scene-level `Map` that survives a scene restart; the memo lives on the (freshly constructed) manager. Mitigation: the synchronous regeneration still runs once per new manager and overwrites CSV keys, so restart remains correct.
- **Scope creep:** eliminating the static SVG fetch path entirely, or moving to runtime-only generation, is out of scope. Record such opportunities as linked work items.
- **Test brittleness:** asserting on `console.info` text is fragile. Prefer asserting on a spied generation call count / returned count, with the log check as a secondary assertion.

### Assumptions

- The two observed log lines come from the synchronous regeneration (`loadCampaignAndSetup`) plus the `cardSvgLoadPromise` re-apply, not from a second scene instance or the `StatsOverlay` "Reset All" path (that path is only reachable from the stats-confirm overlay).
- `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow()` output is a pure function of the CSV rows, so regeneration is safely memoised by `CSV_CHECKSUM`.
- The static SVGs are only a fallback for when CSV regeneration is unavailable/fails.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1: Is the duplicate regeneration a correctness bug or a performance/observability concern?**
  - Answer (operator, freeform seed): reported as a bug — the console output shows two identical regeneration lines. Analysis: the final rendered cards are correct (the defensive second pass wins); the impact is wasted startup work, a misleading log, and a fragile double-regeneration contract. Research: traced the two calls to `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.loadCampaignAndSetup()` (synchronous early call + `cardSvgLoadPromise` re-apply), with a latent third call in `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()`.
  - Final: treat as a medium-priority bug (redundant work + misleading observability), not a rendering-correctness failure.
- **Q2: Which repository/store should own this work?**
  - Answer (agent, per project multi-repo rules): the change is entirely within the sibling game repo `tce-main-street`, which has its own Worklog store (prefix `MS`), so the item is created there (`MS-0MUTU19SF007791K`). Historical related items live in the core `CG` store because Main Street was previously part of the core repo.
  - Final: Main Street store (`MS`).
- **Q3: Should the fix remove the static-SVG fetch path or just stop it clobbering regenerated sources?**
  - Answer (agent, scope control): out of scope. The minimal, robust change is to (a) prevent fetches from overwriting CSV-fresh entries and (b) memoise regeneration, leaving the static SVGs as the fallback path.
  - Final: keep the fetch/fallback path; only prevent overwrite and redundant regeneration.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** – Storyline model & extraction seam (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: again, async, avoid, boot, bug, calls, canvas, card, console, csv, data, defeat, dev, duplicate, fetch, game, line, main, observed, phaser, regeneration, renderer, report, scenes, see, seed, sequence, server, shown, src, start, street, svg, svgs, synchronously, via
- `core/docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` — matched: again, boot, bug, calls, canvas, card, console, csv, data, dev, duplicate, game, line, main, phaser, renderer, report, scenes, see, seed, sequence, server, src, start, street, svg, svgs, via
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: again, avoid, boot, bug, calls, canvas, card, csv, data, dev, fetch, game, line, main, phaser, renderer, report, scenes, see, seed, sequence, server, src, start, street, svg, via

## Goal (user story)

As a developer delivering playable competitive mode, I want a headless acceptance harness that drives a full human-vs-AI competitive game to a terminal condition, so that AI turn wiring and the per-player economy are verified automatically before UI work lands.

## Context

- Test-first child of **Playable AI competitive mode (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP)**. No production behaviour changes in this item.
- Reuses the existing engine seams: `createCompetitiveState`, `executeCompetitiveWeekStart`, `bindCompetitiveSeat`/`restoreCompetitiveSeat`, `executeAction`, `endCompetitiveMarketTurn`, `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`, `resolveCompetitivePendingChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`, `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`).
- Establishes the regression net that the sibling seat-config and scene-orchestration children must keep green.

## Scope

- **In:** a reusable headless turn-driver helper plus an integration spec under `tests/main-street/`.
- **Out:** scene/UI rendering, save/load, per-seat configuration model (sibling items).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The harness drives a competitive game end-to-end: `executeCompetitiveWeekStart` → per-seat MarketPhase (bind seat, choose/execute actions, restore seat, `endCompetitiveMarketTurn`) → `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (and `resolveCompetitivePendingChoice` when paused) until `gameResult` is terminal or a bounded day cap is reached.
- An integration test plays at least five seeds to a terminal condition within the cap with no timeout or stall, asserting a resolved terminal state (`competitiveWinnerId` or a loss end condition).
- **Per-player divergence:** at least one pair of players differs in coins, reputation or score at the end, proving the per-owner economy is routed.
- **Determinism:** the same seed and strategy sequence produce an identical terminal per-player state across two runs.
- AI actions are recorded to the transcript, mirroring the scene contract.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `tests/main-street/helpers/competitiveTurnDriver.ts` exporting the headless day-loop driver.
- Add `tests/main-street/competitive-play-acceptance.test.ts` covering the seeds, divergence, determinism and no-stall assertions.
- Reuse `CompetitiveGreedyStrategy` for the AI seats and a deterministic seeded RNG per seat.

## Out of scope

- Rendering, HUD, mode selector, save/load — sibling children.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/main-street/helpers/competitiveTurnDriver.ts` — headless competitive turn driver (test support).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-play-acceptance.test.ts` — acceptance integration spec.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — engine shared-day flow exercised by the driver.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — seat binding and competitive strategy seams.

## Dependencies

- None — the driver is green against the existing engine.

## Deliverables

- Headless competitive turn driver + integration spec, with a documented seed/determinism contract.

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want each competitive seat to carry its own controller (human or AI), AI strategy and AI difficulty, so that a game-mode selection can be represented faithfully in the competitive state.

## Context

- Child of **Playable AI competitive mode (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP)** (epic AC1 and AC3).
- `PlayerRecord` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) currently holds only game resources; there is no controller/strategy/difficulty. `createCompetitiveState` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) accepts only `playerCount`. Serialisation (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`) already round-trips the competitive fields.
- Difficulty is currently a single global `state.config.difficultyName` that already influences AI behaviour (banking aggressiveness in `scoreBankOption`, event-choice policy via `decideEventChoice`). Per Q3 the producer chose: per-opponent difficulty controls the **AI decision policy only**; the shared economy keeps the player's global difficulty.

## Scope

- **In:** per-seat controller/strategy/difficulty fields, a setup API that builds them from a mode selection, validation, and save/load round-trip.
- **Out:** the selector UI (sibling), driving AI turns in the scene (sibling), full owner-coloured rendering (`MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A competitive seat records `controller` (`'human' | 'ai'`), an AI strategy identifier (`Random | Greedy | BankingGreedy`, extending the existing `MainStreetAiStrategy` names) and an AI difficulty (`Easy | Medium | Hard`); the human seat is player 0 with `controller: 'human'`.
- A setup entry point (extending `CompetitiveStateOptions` or a new mode-state factory) accepts `playerCount` plus a per-opponent strategy/difficulty list and populates every seat correctly.
- Invalid selections throw a clear error: zero AI opponents when competitive is selected, unknown strategy/difficulty, or a seat list whose length does not match `playerCount - 1`.
- Single-player setup (`setupMainStreetGame`) produces no seat records and is byte-identical for the same seed/difficulty (no behavioural change).
- Save/load round-trips the new seat fields; older saves that lack them remain loadable (defaulted to human/all-seat compatibility).
- Unit tests cover the mapping, validation and serialisation round-trip.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `PlayerRecord` (or add an adjacent `SeatConfig`) with `controller`, `aiStrategy`, `aiDifficulty`.
- Extend `CompetitiveStateOptions` and `createCompetitiveState` to accept and validate per-opponent configuration.
- Extend `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` serialise/deserialise for the new fields with backward-compatible defaults.
- Provide a per-seat difficulty resolver used later by the AI policy (e.g. a helper that returns the acting seat's difficulty).

## Out of scope

- Rendering the seats or selecting them in the UI.

**Key Files:**

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PlayerRecord`, `CompetitiveStateOptions` seat fields.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — `createCompetitiveState` per-seat construction and validation.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — save/load round-trip of seat configuration.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — strategy identifiers and per-seat difficulty resolver.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-state.test.ts` — extend with seat-config coverage.

## Dependencies

- None (foundational). The mode-selector and scene-orchestration children depend on it.

## Deliverables

- Per-seat competitive configuration model, validation, setup API and save/load round-trip with unit tests.

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want a blocking "New Game" overlay at scene boot where I can start either single-player or competitive mode — choosing the number of AI opponents and each opponent's strategy and difficulty — so that I can start an AI competitive game directly from the UI.

## Context

- Child of **Playable AI competitive mode (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP)** (epic AC1, AC5).
- The game currently auto-starts single-player (`loadCampaignAndSetup` in `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`); difficulty is selectable only via the SettingsPanel and the game-over "Play Again" overlay (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`). There is no pre-game screen.
- Per producer Q2 the selector is a **blocking pre-game "New Game" overlay at scene boot**, before the first day begins (mirrors the tutorial-offer and resume overlays).
- Depends on the per-seat configuration model child (seat `controller`/`aiStrategy`/`aiDifficulty` and the setup API).

## Scope

- **In:** the pre-game overlay, its selection model and the mapping from selection to game setup, plus a browser smoke test.
- **Out:** driving AI turns (sibling), the competitive scoreboard (sibling), full owner-coloured rendering + SFX (`MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A blocking "New Game" overlay appears at scene boot before the first day starts, offering Single-player vs Competitive; choosing Competitive reveals an opponent count (1–3) and a strategy (`Random | Greedy | BankingGreedy`) plus difficulty (`Easy | Medium | Hard`) control per opponent.
- Confirming **Single-player** starts the game unchanged (same state as today for the same difficulty/seed) and the overlay does not reappear mid-run.
- Confirming **Competitive** creates a competitive game whose `players[]`/seat configuration exactly matches the selection (human seat 0 plus the chosen AI seats, counts, strategies and difficulties).
- The selection model is a pure builder (selection → setup options) unit-tested independently of Phaser, with an invalid selection (e.g. zero opponents) rejected before state creation.
- A browser smoke test opens the overlay, selects Competitive with one AI opponent, starts the game and asserts the resulting state is competitive.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameOverlay.ts` (overlay UI) and `src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameSelection.ts` (pure selection model → setup options).
- Hook the overlay into scene boot in `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`, gating `startTurnPhase` until the player confirms.
- Reuse the existing overlay button/backdrop patterns (`createOverlayButton`, overlay depth convention) and the seat-config setup API from the dependency child.

## Out of scope

- Runtime mode switching after a game has started.
- Full owner-coloured street rendering and action SFX.

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want AI seats to take their turns automatically under the shared-day competitive flow — interleaved with my own turn and with control returned to me between seats — so that I can play a full competitive game without a second human.

## Context

- Child of **Playable AI competitive mode (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP)** (epic AC2, AC3, AC4).
- The scene currently drives a single-player day via `startTurnPhase` → `executeWeekStart` → player actions → `processEndOfTurn` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`). `MainStreetAiPlayer` is used only headlessly (`src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`), and `src/scenes/` contains no competitive references.
- Per producer Q3 an opponent's difficulty controls its decision policy only (banking aggressiveness, event-choice policy, look-ahead); the shared economy keeps the player's global difficulty.
- Depends on the acceptance harness (turn-loop contract) and the per-seat configuration model.

## Scope

- **In:** the scene-level competitive shared-day orchestration and the AI-seat turn driver.
- **Out:** the mode selector (sibling), the scoreboard/HUD (sibling), full owner-coloured rendering + SFX (`MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- In competitive mode the scene starts days with `executeCompetitiveWeekStart`, accepts input only when the active seat is the human (`activePlayerId === 0`), and advances the seat via `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` when the human ends their MarketPhase.
- Each AI seat, when active, has its seat bound (`bindCompetitiveSeat`), chooses actions with a `MainStreetAiPlayer` configured from that seat's strategy/difficulty, executes them through `executeAction`, and restores the seat — with a bounded guard so an AI seat can never loop forever; control returns to the human with no manual intervention.
- After all seats act, the scene runs `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` and completes a paused `resolveCompetitivePendingChoice`; game-over is driven by `competitiveWinnerId`/`gameResult` and never stalls.
- AI actions are visible as they happen (active-seat indicator update and transcript/log entry) and a per-seat difficulty override reaches the AI decision policy.
- An integration/browser test plays a full human-vs-AI competitive game through the scene path to a terminal condition across multiple seeds.
- Single-player turn flow is unchanged (existing turn-flow tests pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a competitive turn-flow module (e.g. `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`) extending the existing turn controller with the shared-day sequence and the AI-seat driver.
- Reuse `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `PlayerAction`, `bindCompetitiveSeat`/`restoreCompetitiveSeat`, `endCompetitiveMarketTurn`, `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`, `resolveCompetitivePendingChoice`.
- Thread per-seat difficulty into the AI policy (via the resolver from the seat-config child) without mutating the shared economy config.
- Gate input through the existing input manager/command enforcement points while an AI seat is active.

## Out of scope

- Mode selection UI, scoreboard rendering, save/load (siblings).

## **Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — competitive shared-day orchestration + AI-seat driver.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — entry point delegating to the competitive flow.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — human turn/closing integration points.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — shared-day engine flow.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `MainStreetAiPlayer`, seat binding, per-seat difficulty.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene-turn-flow.test.ts` — scene-path integration test.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetCompetitive.browser.test.ts` — browser playthrough smoke test.

## Dependencies

- Competitive play acceptance harness (sibling, created first).
- AI seat configuration model (sibling, created first).

## Deliverables

- Scene competitive turn orchestration, AI-seat driver with bounded guards, per-seat difficulty policy threading, integration + browser tests.

# Reject illegal moves before animation and action-point deduction

> **Headline:** A move that cannot be completed must be rejected by a non-mutating legality check before any animation starts or any action/coin is spent; on rejection the player gets illegal-move feedback and keeps their selection to try a different move.

## Problem statement

When the player attempts a move that cannot be completed — most obviously placing a business from hand with too few coins — the UI starts the card-transfer animation and the action point is deducted before the failure is discovered. The player loses a weekly action and sees a transfer that never actually lands. Legality should be established **before** any animation, phase change, or state mutation; an illegal attempt should give feedback and leave the game exactly as it was so the player can choose another move.

## Users

- **Main Street player (MarketPhase)** — "As a player, when I click a slot I cannot legally place on, I want to be told immediately and lose nothing, so I can pick a different slot or a different move without wasting my week's action."
- **Main Street player (held card)** — "As a player holding a card from a previous week, if I no longer have enough coins, I want the illegal-move feedback rather than a phantom animation and a spent action."
- **Main Street player (upgrades)** — "As a player applying an upgrade I cannot afford, I want the same no-cost rejection and to keep the upgrade selected so I can retarget."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Placing a hand business on an empty slot with insufficient coins performs **no** card-transfer animation, leaves `actionsRemaining`, `bankedActions`, `resourceBank.coins`, the hand contents, `uiPhase` and the selected hand card **unchanged**, and plays the standard illegal-move feedback (`playIllegalFeedback` — ILLEGAL_MOVE SFX + shake) with a clear instruction message (e.g. "Not enough coins… need X, have Y").
2. Applying an upgrade from hand with insufficient coins (or an otherwise illegal target) likewise leaves the action budget, coins, hand, target business and pending selection unchanged, and shows illegal feedback **without** starting the transfer animation.
3. The invariant holds for **every action-consuming UI move path** (place-business-from-hand, apply-upgrade-from-hand, buy-and-place drag for business/upgrade, move-to-hand for business/upgrade/event, buy/play event, hire-staff, peek, community-favour, close-business, end-turn): legality is checked with a non-mutating predicate **before** any mutation, and action consumption is atomic with a successful operation (a failed command must not consume an action). The command layer reaches parity with the engine `executeAction` path, which already restores the action on failure.
4. After an illegal attempt the player can immediately try another legal target or move (selection retained), and no path leaves the scene stuck in `uiPhase === 'animating'`.
5. Automated regression tests cover the not-enough-coins placement and upgrade cases at the controller/command level, asserting that no action/coins/hand change and no transfer animation starts; the command layer's restore-on-throw behaviour is covered by extending the existing action-restore suite.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing same-week composite pricing (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN): the +50% premium replaces the missing action, and the premium explainer dialog ordering must not regress.
- Preserve undo/redo correctness: action/coin/state snapshots must still restore exactly (the undo manager snapshots on first `do()`).
- No new gameplay rules — this is a timing/atomicity fix only; move legality rules themselves are unchanged.
- Keep existing legal-move behaviour and feedback messages intact; reuse `playIllegalFeedback` and the current instruction-text conventions.
- Follow the repo's existing controller/command split; no engine rule changes beyond adding/using non-mutating legality predicates.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` → `onSlotClick()` (place-from-hand branch): clears `pendingHandIndex`, sets `uiPhase = 'animating'`, and calls `animateTransferFromMarket(...)` **before** any legality check. The placement command runs in `afterTransfer()`. Only the premium sub-branch pre-gates affordability (`coins < premiumCost`); the held-card / listed-cost branch has no pre-gate.
- `MainStreetCommands.ts` → `playBusinessFromHandCommand()` calls `consumeAction(s)` **then** `playBusinessFromHand(...)`; `playBusinessFromHand()` throws `Not enough coins…` before mutating. `snapshotAction`'s `do()` has no try/catch restore, and `UndoRedoManager.execute()` pushes the command only after `do()` succeeds — so the spent action persists after the throw.
- Same pattern for `playUpgradeFromHandCommand()` → `consumeAction()` then `playUpgradeFromHand()` (throws `Not enough coins…`).
- The engine path `executeAction()` **does** restore actions on failure (covered by `tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts`) — the gap is the UI/command path used by click and drag handlers.
- Non-mutating predicates already exist and should be reused: `canPlaceFromHand` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`), `canSellBusiness`, `canPurchaseBusiness`, `canPurchaseEvent`, `canPurchaseStaff`, `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `isEligibleUpgradeTarget`.
- Pre-flight gating already exists in sibling handlers (`onBusinessCardClick`, `onEventCardClick`, `onUpgradeCardClick`, `onStaffCardClick`, `onRefreshMarketClick`, `onPeekClick`, `onCommunityFavourClick`) — `onSlotClick`/`applyHandUpgradeToSlot` are the outliers.

## Desired change

1. In `onSlotClick` (place-from-hand) and `applyHandUpgradeToSlot`, run the non-mutating legality predicate (occupancy, affordability against the applicable listed/premium cost, upgrade target eligibility, tutorial gating) **before** clearing the selection, changing `uiPhase`, or starting `animateTransferFromMarket`. On failure: call `playIllegalFeedback`, set the instruction text, **keep the selection**, and return.
2. Make action consumption atomic in the command layer: either consume the action only after the underlying operation succeeds, or have the snapshot action restore its pre-snapshot when `do()` throws. This removes the class of bug for any future callers.
3. Audit every action-consuming handler enumerated in AC3 for the same "animate/consume before validate" ordering and fix any other offenders found.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` — pre-flight legality before animation in `onSlotClick` and `applyHandUpgradeToSlot`; retain selection and `uiPhase` on failure.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — atomic action consumption / restore-on-throw for the `*Command` factories (`playBusinessFromHandCommand`, `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`, `buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`, `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand`, `moveToHandCommand`, `moveEventToHandCommand`, `hireStaffCardCommand`, `closeBusinessCommand`).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — reuse `canPlaceFromHand`; add a non-mutating affordability predicate for `playUpgradeFromHand` if one is missing.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playUpgradeFromHand` verification/reuse; `canPurchaseBusiness`/`canAddToHand` predicates.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts` — drag drop handlers (`onDragDropBusiness`, `onDragDropUpgrade`) audited for pre-drop legality and preservation of existing selection on failure.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts` — `playIllegalFeedback` (reuse; no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts` — extend to cover the command layer's restore-on-throw.
- `tests/main-street/click-place.browser.test.ts` — browser regression: illegal placement does not animate, does not spend an action, and keeps the card selected/playable.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts` — controller-level legality/affordability assertions.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document that transfer animations only start for legal moves and that illegal feedback precedes any mutation.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — clarify the "legality before action spend" invariant in the action-economy notes.

## Related work

- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — card transfer feedback, illegal feedback, and commit-before-feedback conventions.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — action economy and same-week composite pricing (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN).
- `Text the dialog for selling/closing a business` (MS-0MURC68DH0066UPK) — recent sell/close dialog/feedback text work.
- `Some staff cards should add action points` (MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0) — action-budget semantics.
- `Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects` (MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M) — premium/discount pricing interplay.
- `Bank your spare action is a dead end in the tutorial` (MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8) — action-economy edge cases.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the engine `executeAction` path is already correct (restores on failure); the defect lives in the UI/command path. Verified by reading `snapshotAction`/`UndoRedoManager.execute` and `tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts`.
- **Assumption:** "illegal-move feedback" means `playIllegalFeedback()` plus an instruction-text message, matching sibling handlers.
- **Assumption:** a full audit of action-consuming UI paths is in scope (the report says "it might happen elsewhere too"; the apply-upgrade path is confirmed affected by inspection).
- **Risk (undo/redo):** changing consumption ordering could alter snapshots; mitigate with explicit undo/redo tests for the touched commands.
- **Risk (premium/dialog regression):** the premium explainer dialog and pricing must keep working; mitigate with existing premium tests plus a new legality-before-dialog test.
- **Risk (tutorial gating):** retaining selection after an illegal attempt must not bypass tutorial gating; keep the existing tutorial checks in the pre-flight checks.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "fix everywhere" can expand; constrain to action-consuming move paths and record any unrelated findings as separate linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the producer's seed context specified the desired behaviour ("test legality before any actions are taken; play illegal feedback; let the player choose another move"), the reproduction ("not enough coins to place a business on the street"), and the priority (`critical`). Scope ambiguity ("it might happen elsewhere too") was resolved by repo inspection: the apply-upgrade-from-hand path shares the same defect class. All assumptions are recorded above.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUQZH6Z50035KVU** – Deployment documentation (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU19SF007791K** – Avoid duplicate Main Street card SVG regeneration on game start (open)
- **MS-0MURC68DH0066UPK** – Text the dialog for selling/closing a business (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actionsremaining, actually (+314 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: 0mt24x0sx007rlhn, acceptance, action, actions, actually (+268 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac3, acceptance, action, actually, add (+215 more)

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player in competitive (human vs AI) mode, I want the score target reduced by 50% for each AI opponent, so that a competitive game against more AIs remains winnable in a comparable run length.

## Context

- The score target is `config.winThreshold` (single shared value): Easy 10000, Medium 12000, Hard 15000 (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`).
- The competitive first-to-threshold win check compares every player's per-owner score against that shared value (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`).
- The value is surfaced in the HUD (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`), help content (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`), and used by AI look-ahead (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`).

## Producer decisions (confirmed)

- **Formula:** multiplicative — `effectiveWinThreshold = baseWinThreshold × 0.5 ^ N`, where `N` = number of AI opponents (e.g. 1 AI = 50%, 2 = 25%, 3 = 12.5%).
- **Scope:** the reduced value is **shared** — it is the target for all players in the competitive game (human and AI alike).
- **Endless mode:** applies to the **standard** win condition only (not an endless-mode continuation change).

## Scope

- **In:** derive the effective competitive win threshold from the seat configuration; use it consistently for the win check, AI look-ahead, and all player-facing score-target displays; tests.
- **Out:** changing single-player thresholds; changing the challenge/bankruptcy/reputation end conditions; rebalancing the base difficulty presets.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a competitive game with `N` AI opponents, the effective win threshold used by the first-to-threshold win check equals `baseWinThreshold × 0.5^N`. *Metric: unit test over N = 1, 2, 3 asserting the value passed to the end-condition check and the winner declaration.*
2. The reduced threshold is shared by every player in that game (the same value governs the human and all AI seats). *Metric: integration test where the human and an AI each reach the effective threshold.*
3. Single-player is unchanged: the base `winThreshold` still applies. *Metric: existing single-player tests pass; explicit assertion of the unmodified value.*
4. All player-facing target displays (HUD score line, help text, any scoreboard) show the effective competitive threshold, not the base value. *Metric: rendering/unit tests assert the displayed target.*
5. AI look-ahead uses the effective threshold. *Metric: test asserting the AI horizon/distance computation uses the reduced value.*
6. A competitive game with `N` AI opponents resolves as a win when the first player reaches the effective threshold. *Metric: full-game integration test per N = 1..3.*
7. Save/load round-trips the effective threshold so a resumed competitive game keeps the reduced target. *Metric: serialise/deserialise test.*

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — derive/persist the effective competitive threshold at state creation.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — competitive end-condition check.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI look-ahead horizon.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — player-facing target display.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + integration coverage.

## Dependencies and notes

- Discovered-from `MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP` (Playable AI competitive mode).
- Related balance item: `MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV` (Confirm win thresholds / run length as the difficulty lever).
- Reuse the existing seat-configuration model rather than duplicating opponent-count logic.

## Command Layer: Atomic Action Consumption on Failure (AC2)

**Goal:** Make action consumption atomic in the command layer so failed commands never lose an action.

**Problem:** snapshotAction.do() in MainStreetCommands.ts calls consumeAction(state) before the actual operation. If the operation throws after consuming, the snapshot was captured but the command is never pushed to the undo stack (UndoRedoManager.execute only pushes after do() succeeds). The action is lost.

**Fix:** Wrap the do() body in a try/catch — if an error is thrown, restore the pre-snapshot action budget (actionsRemaining, bankedActions) before re-throwing. This gives any caller (UI handlers, engine, etc.) the same restore-on-failure semantics as the engine's executeAction path.

**Key file:** src/MainStreetCommands.ts — snapshotAction() function

## Acceptance Criteria

- snapshotAction.do() catches any throw from doFn and restores actionsRemaining and bankedActions to their pre-snapshot values before re-throwing.
- Executing playBusinessFromHandCommand and playUpgradeFromHandCommand with insufficient coins via UndoRedoManager throws and leaves actionsRemaining, bankedActions, resourceBank.coins and hand contents unchanged.
- On successful execution the action is consumed exactly once (no double-decrement) and undo restores it exactly.
- No behaviour change for non-action or already-safe commands (refreshMarket, sellBusiness, discardFromHand, resolveEventChoice, etc.).
- Extended tests in tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts cover the command-layer restore-on-throw path and pass.
data.title: Command Layer: Atomic Action Consumption on Failure

## Upgrade Path: Affordability Pre-Check Before Animation (AC2)

**Goal:** Applying an upgrade from hand with insufficient coins (or an otherwise illegal target) must leave the action budget, coins, hand, target business and pending selection unchanged, and show illegal feedback WITHOUT starting the transfer animation.

**Problem:** applyHandUpgradeToSlot in src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts checks target eligibility (via isEligibleUpgradeTarget) but NOT affordability. It clears pendingHandIndex, sets uiPhase = 'animating', and starts animateTransferFromMarket before the command runs. The command layer then throws during playUpgradeFromHand with 'Not enough coins...'.

**Fix:**
1. Add a non-mutating affordability + target-eligibility predicate (e.g. canPlayUpgradeFromHand) in src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts mirroring playUpgradeFromHand's checks (target validity, effectiveUpgradeCost after per-business discount) without mutating.
2. In applyHandUpgradeToSlot, run the predicate BEFORE clearing pendingHandIndex / changing uiPhase / starting animation. On failure: playIllegalFeedback, set instruction text, keep the selection and uiPhase, refresh, and return.

**Key files:** src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts, src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts, src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts.

**Dependencies:** Blocked by MS-0MUUYAZPN0064AW5 (command-layer atomicity) as a belt-and-suspenders restore guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A non-mutating predicate (canPlayUpgradeFromHand or equivalent) returns illegal when coins < effective upgrade cost or the target is ineligible, without mutating any state.
- applyHandUpgradeToSlot with insufficient coins performs no transfer animation, leaves actionsRemaining, bankedActions, resourceBank.coins, hand, target business and pendingHandIndex/uiPhase unchanged, and plays playIllegalFeedback with a clear instruction message.
- applyHandUpgradeToSlot with an ineligible target likewise mutates nothing and retains the selection.
- A legal upgrade still animates and applies exactly as before (no regression to the apply-upgrade flow).
- No path leaves uiPhase === 'animating' after a failed upgrade attempt.

The command layer's restore-on-throw behaviour is covered by extending the existing action-restore suite.

# Cross-owner business actions: seats can sell/close/upgrade businesses they do not own

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, the human seat can open the Manage-Card
dialog on an AI-owned street slot and **sell** or **close** that opponent's
business; the same ownership gap lets the human **upgrade** an opponent's
business. Each seat must only be able to mutate street slots it owns, in both
directions (human→AI and, defensively, AI→human).

## Users

- **Human player (competitive mode)** — expects opponent businesses to be
  untouchable; the current behaviour lets them destroy an opponent's engine and
  (for a sell) even credits the acting seat's wallet.
- **AI opponents** — must be prevented from mutating the human's businesses;
  today they emit no sell/close actions, but no guard exists to stop a future
  AI upgrade/sell/close path from doing so.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want to be unable to sell or close a business I
  do not own, so that opponents' engines are protected and the game is fair.
- As a competitive player, I want clear feedback when I click a slot I do not
  own, so that I understand why the action is unavailable.
- As a game designer, I want ownership enforced in one legality layer, so that
  UI, AI, and headless paths cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive mode, `canSellBusiness`/`sellBusiness` reject a slot whose
   owner (`getSlotOwnerId`) is not the acting seat (`state.activePlayerId`),
   returning a `LegalityResult` with a clear reason; the action mutates no
   state. Single-player (no `ownerTaggedGrid`) behaviour is unchanged.
2. In competitive mode, `canCloseBusiness`/`closeBusiness` reject a slot whose
   owner is not the acting seat with the same guarantees; a rejected close
   consumes no action.
3. In competitive mode, upgrade actions (`canPurchaseUpgrade`,
   `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, and their execution paths) reject targeting an
   opponent-owned business; eligible-target search does not select an
   opponent-owned slot as the default target.
4. Clicking a non-owned occupied slot in the scene blocks the Manage-Card
   dialog and shows illegal-move feedback with an ownership-specific message
   (e.g. "That business belongs to AI 1."); no dialog is opened and no Sell /
   Close / upgrade command runs.
5. Any coins from a permitted sell are credited to the owning seat's wallet
   (not an unrelated seat), and a permitted close leaves the slot immediately
   placeable by its owner; both behaviours are covered by tests.
6. Tests cover: human cannot sell/close/upgrade an AI-owned business; a seat
   can sell/close its **own** business (positive case); single-player
   sell/close/upgrade is unaffected; and the legality helpers return the
   expected reasons.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Enforce at the legality/command layer** (operator decision Q3 = A), not the
  scene layer alone, so UI, AI and headless paths share one source of truth.
- **Preserve single-player behaviour**: single-player states have no
  `ownerTaggedGrid`; the gate must be a no-op there.
- **Reuse existing ownership primitives**: `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`), `ownerTaggedGrid`, `activePlayerId`.
- **No new scoring/economy rules**: this is an access-control fix, not a
  balance change.
- **Headless/Monte-Carlo determinism** must not change for existing seeds where
  neither seat acted cross-owner (the AI emits no such actions today).
- Do not weaken the existing phase, sold-slot, action-budget, or placement-mode
  gates already in `canSellBusiness`/`canCloseBusiness`.

## Existing state

- `canSellBusiness`, `sellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `closeBusiness`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`) contain **no ownership check**.
- `sellBusiness` credits `state.resourceBank.coins` directly, with no per-owner
  routing.
- `onSellCard` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts`) opens the
  Manage-Card dialog for any occupied, non-sold slot in `market` phase.
- `showSellConfirmation` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`) wires Sell
  and Close buttons that execute with no ownership check.
- `canPurchaseUpgrade` / `canPlayUpgradeFromHand` / `purchaseUpgrade`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) have no ownership check;
  `findTargetBusinessSlot` may resolve to an opponent-owned business.
- Ownership is modelled: `getSlotOwnerId`, `tagSlotOwnerIfCompetitive`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`), `ownerTaggedGrid`, `activePlayerId`,
  and `PlayerRecord.controller` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- The AI action enumerator (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
  `enumerateLegalActions`) emits no sell/close actions today; competitive
  income/costs are already routed per owner via `getSlotOwnerId`.

## Desired change

- Add an ownership guard to the sell/close legality and execution functions:
  when `ownerTaggedGrid` is present, require
  `getSlotOwnerId(state, slotIndex) === (state.activePlayerId ?? 0)`; otherwise
  reject with a descriptive reason. Single-player remains a no-op.
- Apply the same guard to upgrade targeting (`canPurchaseUpgrade`,
  `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, and execution), and ensure default target selection
  never picks an opponent-owned slot.
- Gate the scene path (`onSellCard`) and/or the overlay so a non-owned slot
  cannot open the Manage-Card dialog; show the ownership-specific illegal-move
  message instead.
- Ensure a permitted sell credits the owning seat's wallet (the acting seat is
  the owner once the guard is in place — verify no separate routing is needed).
- Add focused unit tests plus a browser/scene-level test for the blocked dialog.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — add ownership gate to `canSellBusiness`,
  `sellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `closeBusiness`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — add ownership gate to
  `canPurchaseUpgrade`, `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, `purchaseUpgrade`; fix
  `findTargetBusinessSlot` default selection.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reuse `getSlotOwnerId`; may add a small
  `canActOnOwner`/`isSlotOwnedByActiveSeat` helper.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the same guard to the legacy
  `sellFromTableau` / `canSellFromTableau` path if still reachable.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` — block `onSellCard` for
  non-owned slots with ownership feedback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — defensive guard in the Sell/Close
  handlers (and hide/disable when non-owned).
- `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` — extend with ownership cases.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-*.test.ts` — add cross-owner sell/close/upgrade
  cases (a new `competitive-ownership-actions.test.ts` is likely cleanest).
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — blocked-dialog case.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — Reject illegal moves before animation and
  action-point deduction (completed; the established pattern for validating a
  move before any state mutation/animation — reuse it for the ownership gate).
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the
  shared street (epic, establishes `ownerTaggedGrid`).
- `MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP` — Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI).
- `MS-0MT5X3N79002S038` — Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware,
  staff-free scoring for shared-street play (ownership-aware AI logic).
- `MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY` — Competitive state model: per-player resources,
  owner-tagged street.
- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident
  resolution (precedent for per-owner routing).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** applying the gate too broadly breaks single-player or legacy saves
  (no `ownerTaggedGrid`). Mitigation: gate strictly on `ownerTaggedGrid`
  presence; add single-player regression tests.
- **Risk:** the AI's default upgrade target (`findTargetBusinessSlot`) changes
  behaviour for competitive games, altering headless Monte-Carlo outcomes.
  Mitigation: scope the fix to exclude opponent-owned slots and add determinism
  regression coverage.
- **Risk:** double-counting the sell refund (shared wallet vs `PlayerRecord`).
  Mitigation: assert the acting/owning seat's wallet in tests.
- **Assumption:** the acting seat is `state.activePlayerId`; for the human seat
  this is `0` during the human's MarketPhase (confirmed in
  `MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive`).
- **Assumption:** the legacy `sellFromTableau` path is still routed somewhere
  in headless flows; verify reachability and gate it if so.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any additional cross-owner action discovered (e.g.
  staff assignment, event targeting) is recorded as a linked work item, not
  absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When playing an AI game it is possible to close/sell the AIs businesses
  — is the report about the AI closing/selling, or the player closing/selling
  the AI's?" — Answer (operator): "It is not about the AI closing/selling
  their business (that is allowed); it is about the player closing/selling the
  AI's businesses (and maybe the AI closing/selling the player's businesses)."
  Source: interactive reply. Research: `canSellBusiness`/`canCloseBusiness` in
  `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` have no ownership check; `onSellCard` opens the
  dialog for any occupied slot; AI `enumerateLegalActions` emits no sell/close.
- Q: "Scope of the ownership gate?" — Answer (operator): **B** — all
  cross-owner street actions: sell, close, and upgrading an opponent-owned
  business. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "UX when the human clicks a slot they don't own?" — Answer (operator):
  **A** — block the Manage-Card dialog with illegal-move feedback and an
  ownership-specific message. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where is the gate enforced?" — Answer (operator): **A** —
  legality/command layer (`canSellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `sellBusiness`,
  `closeBusiness`, plus upgrade legality) so UI, AI and headless paths are
  covered; route refunds to the slot owner's wallet. Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Prevent players from selling, closing, or upgrading businesses they do not own
