# Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) mode the shared closing (Income → Incident → EndCheck) is presented as a single condensed, text-only summary. The full end-of-turn income choreography that single-player players see — base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD coin collection, with per-card coin grids and sound — never runs for the AI seats (nor for the human seat). Much of the end-of-turn phase is therefore lost in an AI game.

## Users

- **Competitive mode players** (especially the human seat) who want to see the outcome of each player's day — what each seat earned and what effects fired — with the same visual feedback as single-player, rather than an unexplained jump to the next day.
- **Maintainers** who want a single end-of-turn presentation path so the single-player and competitive flows cannot drift.

Example user stories:
- "As a competitive player, after I end my day I want to watch each player's income collection in turn, so I understand how the shared day changed every seat's economy."
- "As a competitive player on a slow machine, I want the AI closing to be short and skippable, so playing against AI does not take many minutes per day."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1: Per-seat full closing presentation (phase-major)** — After the shared competitive closing resolves, the presentation runs the full phased income choreography (`animateIncomePhases`: base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD collection) once as a single **phase-major** sweep over all non-eliminated seats, in seat order: each phase plays for the human seat, then AI 1, then AI 2, before the next phase begins, using each seat's own income/effects. The human seat is included; eliminated seats are skipped. (Amended 2026-10-12 per producer audit 2026-10-08: previously seat-major, one full choreography per seat.)
- **AC2: Authoritative per-seat data** — The competitive closing surfaces the per-owner income (`applyCompetitiveIncome` → `OwnerIncomeResult[]`, which already carries a full `IncomeResult.phaseBreakdown`) instead of discarding it, and every presented per-seat value equals the delta actually applied to that `PlayerRecord` (asserted by test).
- **AC3: Per-seat income feedback text** — The closing summary reports each seat's income (e.g. `Player 2: +7 coins`), not the shared host total, which can differ from any player's actual income.
- **AC4: Shared engine semantics unchanged** — Presentation-only change: the closing order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), the single shared incident per day, and seeded-replay determinism are unchanged.
- **AC5: Single presentation primitive** — Single-player and competitive closings are driven by one shared presentation path; `finishTurnPresentation` and `presentCompetitiveClosing` no longer duplicate the income/incident/end-of-turn/advance logic. Single-player behaviour is behaviourally unchanged (existing turn-flow tests pass without modification). This absorbs **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ**.
- **AC6: Bounded and non-blocking** — Full animations run in normal play; reduced motion, replay and headless contexts fall back to per-seat text and always advance the day; the presentation **waits** for the phase-major choreography to finish collecting before the day advances (never leaves it running in the background while the next turn starts), bounded by a global fast-forward cap so a large roster cannot stall the game (honours MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD AC4).
- **AC7: Tests** — New/updated automated tests cover: per-seat animation sequencing (one full choreography per non-eliminated seat, in order), authoritative per-seat values (presented == applied deltas), bounded/headless fallback (day always advances; text-only when animations are disabled), and single-player unchanged.
- **AC8: Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC9: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** (producer decision Q2-A): no change to the engine closing order or the shared-incident contract; income/incident still resolve once per shared day.
- **Bounded** (producer decision Q3-A): the closing must never block the day start indefinitely; reduced motion / replay / headless degrade to text.
- **Determinism**: the presentation must not consume RNG or mutate state (beyond reusing the existing deferred-delta window where applicable), so seeded replay stays reproducible.
- **Single-player parity**: single-player end-of-turn presentation and its deferred-mutation flow (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) must not regress.
- Phaser-free helpers where possible, so the node integration tests can exercise the flow (`MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive` is already Phaser-free).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
  - `endCompetitiveTurnDay` → `driveAiSeatsUntilClosing` → `runCompetitiveClosing` → `presentCompetitiveClosing` → `startTurnPhase`.
  - `presentCompetitiveClosing` shows `Resolving end-of-turn effects...`, a one-line `competitiveClosingSummary` built from the **shared** `result.income.total` and the incident name, then `End of turn complete.` after a ~900 ms hold. It deliberately does **not** run `animateIncomePhases` (test `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` asserts `incomeCalls` is empty).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` calls `applyCompetitiveIncome(state)` and **discards** the returned `OwnerIncomeResult[]`; `TurnResult.income` carries only the shared `applyIncome` result. `applyCompetitiveIncome` already builds a per-owner `IncomeResult` with a full `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — single-player `endTurn` delegates to `processEndOfTurn` (with `deferResourceApplication`) then `animateIncomePhases`, then `finishTurnPresentation`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomePhases(animator, phaseData, options)` runs the phased choreography from `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]` (indexed against the shared street grid) and applies `options.pendingDeltas` exactly once at collection completion; `incomeCollectionActive` gates the HUD delta pop.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — the competitive HUD binds each row to that seat's `state.players` coins/reputation/score (so a per-seat collection can land on the right row).
- `MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD` delivered the condensed text-only competitive closing; `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (open) proposed per-seat income surfacing + presentation dedup and is folded into this item.

## Desired change

After the shared competitive closing resolves, present the results **per seat, in turn**, with full animations:

1. Surface per-owner income/effects from the closing (`OwnerIncomeResult[]`, or an equivalent per-seat breakdown on `TurnResult`) so the presentation has authoritative data.
2. For each non-eliminated seat in seat order, run the full `animateIncomePhases` choreography using that seat's `phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown`, applying that seat's deltas at the appropriate time (reusing the existing deferred-delta window so the HUD updates when the coins land).
3. Show the resolved incident reveal once (unchanged shared semantics) and a per-seat income summary.
4. Extract one shared presentation primitive used by both single-player (`finishTurnPresentation`) and competitive (`presentCompetitiveClosing`); the competitive path iterates seats while single-player presents its single seat — no duplicated logic.
5. Keep it bounded/non-blocking: reduced motion / replay / headless skip animation and show per-seat text; a global fast-forward bound (e.g. per-seat gap reduction or a total-time cap) ensures the day always advances.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — `presentCompetitiveClosing` becomes per-seat; extract a shared primitive; update `competitiveClosingSummary` to per-seat output.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `finishTurnPresentation` consumes the shared primitive (single-seat).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — surface `OwnerIncomeResult[]` from `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (currently discarded); thread it through `TurnResult`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — reuse `animateIncomePhases`; confirm per-seat phase data + per-seat delta application (may need a per-seat `pendingDeltas`/HUD target hook).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `TurnResult` may gain an optional per-seat income field (backwards-compatible; absent for single-player).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — HUD target binding if collection must credit a specific seat row.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` — update/extend (current test asserts the choreography is **not** run; that assertion inverts).
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-*` — reference for per-seat sequencing assertions; `tests/main-street/competitive-income-events.test.ts` for authoritative per-owner income.

## Related work

- **Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)** — this item.
- **Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ)** — **superseded/absorbed** by this item (producer decision Q1-A); closed as superseded.
- **End Turn Phase is missing in AI game (MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD)** — delivered the condensed text-only competitive closing this item replaces with full per-seat animations.
- **Competitive turn orchestration in the scene (MS-0MUTU8IYV0086PF6)** and **Playable AI competitive mode (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP)** — the competitive turn flow this sits on.
- **Coin and Reputation should count up/down (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8)** — open; related HUD-counting polish for end-of-turn reconciliation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — total duration**: full per-seat choreography is ~11 s each; with N seats this could make AI days very long. Mitigation: the bounded requirement (AC6) plus a global fast-forward bound; consider shortening per-seat gaps.
- **Risk — HUD targeting**: the competitive HUD binds per-seat rows; the collection currently assumes the single shared `resourceBank` projection. Mitigation: add a per-seat HUD target to the collection, or animate against the shared HUD only when a single row is present.
- **Risk — deferred-delta window**: competitive closing currently applies deltas before presentation, unlike the single-player deferred path. Mitigation: reuse or extend the existing deferred-delta mechanism so the per-seat values land when each seat's coins collect.
- **Risk — test inversion**: `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` explicitly asserts the full choreography is *not* run; that contract is intentionally inverted here.
- **Assumption**: the presentation is a replay over already-resolved state (per-owner income from `applyCompetitiveIncome`) — no engine-phase change.
- **Assumption**: a per-seat income breakdown is preferable to the shared host total (producer decisions Q1-A/Q2-A).
- **Scope-creep risk**: restyling the HUD, changing the incident system, or adding a player-facing speed toggle are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (relationship to MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ)** — "How should this relate to the per-seat income feedback / presentation-refactor item?" — **Answer (producer): A. Merge/supersede** — this item absorbs the per-seat income feedback AC; MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ is folded in (and closed as superseded). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (engine semantics vs presentation)** — "Should the end-of-turn phase actually run per player in the engine, or should the engine keep the shared closing and only the presentation run per seat?" — **Answer (producer): A. Presentation-only** — keep the shared closing resolved once (shared/street incident semantics, determinism unchanged); replay each seat's economy sequentially with full animations. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (duration / boundedness)** — "Full choreography per seat could take ~11 s each; how should duration be handled?" — **Answer (producer): A. Full choreography per seat, bounded** — full animation normally, global fast-forward bound, and text-only fallback for reduced motion / replay / headless. Source: interactive reply.
- **Research context** (pre-question, recorded for traceability): competitive closing is text-only and discards `applyCompetitiveIncome`'s per-owner results (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`); single-player runs `animateIncomePhases` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`); the competitive HUD binds per-seat rows (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts`).
- **Q4 (plan approval)** — "Do you approve the proposed 6-phase, 10-item feature decomposition (test-first), or would you like to edit/split/merge items?" — **Answer (producer): approve as proposed ("LGTM")** — no changes requested. Final: approved. Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8** – Bank your spare action is a dead end in the tutorial (open)
- **MS-0MURQY8VU002XIQK** – Integration, AI compatibility, and legacy equivalence tests (completed)
- **MS-0MUWE6OER004GNV1** – Full-suite verification and regression (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: animations, effects, end, full, game, lost, perform, phase, player, run, should, turn
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: animations, effects, end, full, game, lost, perform, phase, player, run, should, turn
- `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — matched: animations, effects, end, full, game, much, perform, phase, player, run, should

## Plan — feature decomposition (plan_complete)

Phases are vertical slices; test items precede their implementation items.

### Phase 1 — Surface per-owner closing income
- **Test per-owner closing income data (MS-0MUYFX3YA006JXO2)** — pin the authoritative `OwnerIncomeResult[]` contract (test-first).
- **Surface per-owner closing income in TurnResult (MS-0MUYFX56M006RVIZ)** — depends on the test.

### Phase 2 — Shared presentation primitive
- **Test shared closing presentation primitive (MS-0MUYFX6ER000BLP3)** — depends on Phase 1.
- **Extract shared closing presentation primitive (MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R)** — depends on the test; absorbs `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ`.

### Phase 3 — Per-seat animated closing
- **Test per-seat closing animation sequencing (MS-0MUYFX8V3005VEOG)** — depends on Phase 1 + Phase 2.
- **Per-seat animated competitive closing (MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0)** — depends on the test.

### Phase 4 — Bounded fallback
- **Test bounded fallback closing (MS-0MUYFXBC4003073C)** — depends on Phase 3.
- **Bounded per-seat closing with fallback (MS-0MUYFXCJ5008K6MY)** — depends on the test.

### Phase 5 — Integration & regression
- **Integration and regression: per-seat closing (MS-0MUYFXDNZ002BPEA)** — depends on Phases 2–4; full suite must be green.

### Phase 6 — Documentation

Between phases: review and update the next items' descriptions before starting them.

## Plan: changelog
- 2026-10-07 — plan skill: decomposed into 10 children (4 test tasks, 4 features, 1 integration/regression task, 1 docs task) across 6 phases; 11 test-first dependency edges wired; AC coverage review 100% (9/9 parent ACs); parent AC list normalised to AC-labelled bullets for machine-checkable coverage.

# Intake Brief — Card-level unit and browser integration test framework with CSV result reporting

**Headline:** Build an automated per-card verification mechanism that exercises all 174 Main Street cards through real play states (unit integration) and the real Phaser scene (browser integration), asserting expected discounts/buffs/effects and recording pass/fail plus failure notes back into `src/card-data.csv`.

## Problem statement

Card behaviour — especially staff discounts (`purchaseCostDiscount`, `upgradeCostDiscount`, `refreshCostDiscount`), action/peek/hand-slot staff abilities, and event/business/upgrade effects — can silently diverge from what `card-data.csv` declares. There is no systematic proof that each card, when bought and/or played on a particular board, produces the expected change in game state. Manual spot-checks and balance tooling do not catch regressions in individual cards.

## Users

- **Game designer / producer** — needs confidence that a CSV edit reaches the engine and the UI correctly.
- **Developer** — needs a fast, deterministic regression guard that pinpoints the failing card and the reason.
- **QA** — needs a per-card pass/fail record for release sign-off.

Example user stories:
- As a designer, when I change a staff card's `purchaseCostDiscount`, I want a test that proves the discounted cost is charged end to end.
- As a developer, when I add a new card to `card-data.csv`, I want to add one test definition and have it discovered, executed, and reported automatically.
- As QA, when a card fails, I want a machine-readable note of the observed vs expected game state in the CSV.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

1. A card test framework parses `src/card-data.csv` and discovers all 174 cards (31 business, 8 community-space, 39 upgrade, 25 staff, 71 event); a card with no registered definition is reported as a failure, never silently skipped.
2. A **unit integration** suite (Node/Vitest) tests every card against real play states and turn progressions: controlled state via `setupMainStreetGame`, card acquired/played through real engine APIs, turns advanced, resulting state asserted.
3. A **browser integration** suite (Vitest/Playwright, headless Chromium) tests every card through the real `MainStreetScene`, asserting player-facing UI/state (HUD, activity log, market/hand, applied discount values).
4. Staff cards (the discount/buff-bearing family) receive up to **3 combination tests** each, covering discount stacking, per-business vs street-wide scoping, and synergy/upgrade interaction.
5. Results are written back into `src/card-data.csv` as four new columns — `unitTestStatus`, `unitTestFailReason`, `browserTestStatus`, `browserTestFailReason` — preserving all existing columns and row order; pass rows have an empty reason, fail rows carry a concise note.
6. Meta-tests prove each framework actually fails on a missing definition and on a deliberately wrong expectation (guards against a green-but-useless suite).
7. The browser suite is wired into the project's test profiles so it runs in the standard dev/smoke workflow.
8. The framework is extensible: adding a new card requires only a test definition, not framework changes.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/main-street`.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unit tests are **integration tests**: real play states and turn progressions, not isolated pure-function calls alone.
- Deterministic: seeded `setupMainStreetGame`.
- The CSV is also consumed by `@balance-cards` (parser/`CSV_COLUMNS`/checksum) and the card-art pipeline — appended columns must not break existing tests (`tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts`, `csv-checksum.test.ts`, `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts`).
- The main-street root `vite.config.ts` currently defines only a `unit` project; browser execution needs a browser vitest project (Playwright + `@vitest/browser` are already devDependencies).
- Browser tests are context/GPU sensitive; run serially (`fileParallelism: false`).
- Do not modify `.pi/`, skill, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv`: 174 cards, 46 columns; single source of truth.
- Engine APIs available: `setupMainStreetGame`, `executeWeekStart`, `executeAction`, `purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness`, `hireStaffCard`, `purchaseUpgrade`, `buyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `purchaseEvent`, `playBusinessFromHand`, `playUpgradeFromHand`, `playEventFromHand`, `endTurnHeadless`, `computePurchaseCostDiscount`, `computeUpgradeCostDiscount`, `refreshMarketCost`.
- Existing controlled-state test patterns: `tests/main-street/WeekGatedMarket.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts`.
- Existing browser boot pattern: `tests/e2e/main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts`.
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` covers the balance tool, not live card behaviour.

## Desired change

Introduce a Main Street card verification framework under `tests/main-street/cards/` (shared registry + result writer + per-family definitions + combination definitions) with two sibling test suites — unit integration (Node) and browser integration (Playwright) — that write per-card results back into `src/card-data.csv`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestRegistry.ts` — parse CSV, discover cards, register/resolve per-card definitions
- `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestResultWriter.ts` — append `unitTest*` / `browserTest*` columns safely
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/{business,community-space,upgrade,staff,event,combinations}.ts` — per-card definitions
- `tests/main-street/cards/helpers/stateBuilders.ts` — shared controlled-state builders
- `tests/main-street/cards/unit/CardIntegration.test.ts`, `CardCombinations.test.ts`, `CardTestFramework.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/cards/browser/CardIntegration.browser.test.ts`, `CardCombinations.browser.test.ts`, `sceneHarness.ts`
- `vite.config.ts` — add a `browser` project (Playwright, Chromium)
- `src/card-data.csv` — four appended result columns
- `docs/main-street/` — document the framework and how to add a card test

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (discount implementation under test)
- **MS-0MUOSUN3O003MA1B** — Add comprehensive tests for Investor staff abilities (per-card test precedent)
- **MS-0MULW540X009EP9A** — CSV schema: add `upgradeCostDiscount` column to CsvRow and card-data.csv (CSV schema precedent)
- **MS-0MUMP92O9002772U** — Storyline behaviour regression harness (behaviour-harness precedent)
- **MS-0MUQUBITP000UUX6** — Net payback metric and contract test (contract-test precedent)
- **MS-0MTINKHUT009KHK5** — Market Card Cheat browser smoke test (browser boot pattern)
- Docs: `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** all 174 cards are individually reachable through engine APIs in a controllable state; some duration/choice events may need multi-turn drivage or scripted choices.
- **Assumption:** the scene exposes seams (or tolerates injected state) to build arbitrary boards without long scripted play.
- **Risk — CSV churn / race:** two runners writing the same CSV can clash and create noisy diffs. Mitigation: idempotent writer that only rewrites changed rows, or a merge writer; run writers sequentially.
- **Risk — slow/flaky browser suite:** 174 scene tests are heavy. Mitigation: minimal per-card scenarios, serial execution, warmed-up scene where safe, and keeping the suite in the dev profile rather than the fast unit profile.
- **Risk — false confidence:** a suite that passes without asserting. Mitigation: AC6 meta-tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Monte-Carlo balance tuning and visual snapshot testing are out of scope — capture as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Should tests validate at the unit level, the browser level, or both?** — Answer (producer): "both, create two separate work items one for unit and one for browser. Note the unit tests must test against real play states and turn progressions — these are integration tests." Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Should the design be a parameterised test framework (one test definition per card) rather than 174 hand-written tests?** — Answer (producer): "Yes". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Should tests cover individual card effects only, or also combinations?** — Answer (producer): "Individual plus up to 3 combinations for validation". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Should every event card be tested, or only non-trivial events?** — Answer (producer): "Every card". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Where should results be reported?** — Answer (producer): "Results should be written into a new column in the CSV showing pass/fail and in the event of a fail a note on the problem." Follow-up answer: "Add columns". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Is a multi-turn integration pattern (setup → buy/play → advance turns → assert) acceptable?** — Answer (producer): "yes". Source: interactive reply.
- **Research:** the CSV is consumed by `@balance-cards` (`CSV_COLUMNS`, parser, checksum) and the card-art generator, so appended columns must stay backward compatible; the main-street root `vite.config.ts` has only a `unit` project today, so the browser child must add a browser project (Playwright, Chromium, already a devDependency). Evidence: `src/card-data.csv`, `core/src/balance-cards/csv.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts`.

# Unit integration card test framework + full card coverage

Parent: MS-0MUXW90YE009L4DQ — Card-level unit and browser integration test framework.

## Problem statement

Every one of the 174 Main Street cards (31 business, 8 community-space, 39 upgrade, 25 staff, 71 event) must be verified to behave as its card text declares — particularly the staff discount/buff fields (`purchaseCostDiscount`, `upgradeCostDiscount`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `handSlotsAdded`, `taxAuditRate`) and the event/business/reputation effects. Today there is no per-card verification mechanism; coverage is ad-hoc and discount effects can silently diverge from the CSV.

## Users

- **Game designer / producer**: wants confidence that a card-data.csv edit reaches the engine correctly.
- **Developer**: wants a fast, deterministic regression guard that pinpoints which card broke.

Example user stories:
- As a designer, when I change a staff card's `purchaseCostDiscount`, I want a test that proves the discounted cost is charged end to end.
- As a developer, when I add a new card to card-data.csv, I want to add one test definition and have it automatically picked up, run, and reported.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A card test framework exists that parses `src/card-data.csv`, discovers all 174 cards, and runs a registered test definition for each; a card without a definition is reported as a failure (not silently skipped).
2. Each card has at least one unit integration test that: (a) builds a controlled state via `setupMainStreetGame`, (b) acquires/plays the card through real engine APIs, and (c) advances real turn progressions and asserts on the resulting game state (coins, reputation, income, hand size, slots, active effects).
3. Staff cards have up to 3 combination tests each, covering at least: discount stacking (multiple staff), synergy/upgrade interaction, and per-business vs street-wide discount scoping.
4. A result writer records `unitTestStatus` (pass/fail) and `unitTestFailReason` (failure note; empty on pass) per card back into `src/card-data.csv`, preserving all existing columns and row order.
5. Framework is extensible: adding a new card requires only a new/varied test definition, not framework changes.
6. A meta-test proves the framework itself fails when a card has no definition or when a definition's expectation is deliberately wrong (guards against a green-but-useless suite).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/main-street`.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must use real play states and turn progressions (integration), not isolated pure-function calls only.
- Node/Vitest environment (project `unit`; `npm test`).
- Must be deterministic (seeded `setupMainStreetGame`).
- The CSV is also consumed by `@balance-cards` and the card-art pipeline — column append must not break the existing parser/checksum tests.
- Do not modify `.pi/`, skill, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` (174 cards, 46 columns) is the single source of truth for card data.
- Engine APIs: `setupMainStreetGame`, `executeWeekStart`, `executeAction`, `purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness`, `hireStaffCard`, `purchaseUpgrade`, `buyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `purchaseEvent`, `playBusinessFromHand`, `playUpgradeFromHand`, `playEventFromHand`, `endTurnHeadless`, `computePurchaseCostDiscount`, `computeUpgradeCostDiscount`, `refreshMarketCost`.
- Existing test patterns in `tests/main-street/` (e.g. `WeekGatedMarket.test.ts`, `action-banking.test.ts`) show the controlled-state + engine-call + assert pattern.
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` covers the balance tool, not live card behaviour.

## Desired change

Introduce `tests/main-street/cards/` containing the registry, test definitions per family, the combination definitions, the unit integration suites, and the CSV result writer. Wire into the `unit` vitest project.

## Key files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestRegistry.ts` — parse CSV, register/resolve per-card definitions
- `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestResultWriter.ts` — append `unitTestStatus` / `unitTestFailReason` columns
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/{business,community-space,upgrade,staff,event,combinations}.ts` — per-card definitions
- `tests/main-street/cards/unit/CardIntegration.test.ts` — parameterised runner
- `tests/main-street/cards/unit/CardCombinations.test.ts` — combination runner
- `tests/main-street/cards/unit/CardTestFramework.test.ts` — meta-tests
- `tests/main-street/cards/helpers/stateBuilders.ts` — shared controlled-state builders

## Related work

- MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects
- MS-0MUOSUN3O003MA1B — Add comprehensive tests for Investor staff abilities
- MS-0MULW540X009EP9A — CSV schema: add `upgradeCostDiscount` column
- MS-0MUMP92O9002772U — Storyline behaviour regression harness (pattern precedent)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: all 174 cards are individually reachable through engine APIs in a controllable state; some event/duration cards may require waiting several turns.
- Risk: writing test results into the source CSV on every run creates churn; mitigate by writing only when status changes or by gating behind a flag/env var.
- Risk: a green suite that tests nothing; mitigated by AC6 meta-tests.
- Scope-creep risk: extending coverage to balance/Monte-Carlo tuning is out of scope — record as linked work items.

# Browser integration card test framework + full card coverage (Vitest/Playwright)

Parent: MS-0MUXW90YE009L4DQ — Card-level unit and browser integration test framework.

## Problem statement

The unit integration suite proves card effects at the engine/state level, but it does not prove the player-facing path: real Phaser scene interaction, HUD updates, activity-log entries, affordability gates, animations, and the discount values actually shown/charged when a card is bought, played, or upgraded in the running game. This child delivers the browser-level counterpart, one browser test per card, with results reported back into `src/card-data.csv`.

## Users

- **Game designer**: wants proof that a card behaves correctly in the actual game, not just in an engine harness.
- **QA / producer**: wants a per-card pass/fail record that reflects the shipped UI path.

Example user stories:
- As a designer, I want to see the discounted cost in the market UI when a discount staff member is employed.
- As QA, when a card fails, I want a note of the observed vs expected game state.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A browser-capable vitest project runs card tests in headless Chromium using the real `MainStreetScene` (same boot harness as `tests/e2e/main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts`).
2. Each of the 174 cards has at least one browser test that sets up the board, buys/plays the card through the real scene interaction path, and asserts the resulting UI/state (HUD coins/reputation, activity log, market/hand contents, discount values applied).
3. Staff cards have up to 3 combination browser tests each (discount stacking shown in UI, per-business vs street-wide scoping, upgrade interaction).
4. A result writer records `browserTestStatus` (pass/fail) and `browserTestFailReason` (failure note; empty on pass) per card back into `src/card-data.csv`, without clobbering the unit columns written by the sibling child.
5. The browser card suite is added to the project's test profiles so it runs in the standard dev/smoke workflow.
6. A meta-test proves the browser framework fails when a card has no definition or a deliberately wrong expectation.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/main-street`.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Depends on the shared registry/result-writer contract from the unit child (blocked-by MS-0MUXWGT7G009THBO).
- The main-street repo's root `vite.config.ts` currently defines only a `unit` project; a browser project (Playwright, headless Chromium, `@vitest/browser`) must be added or the suite must run through the core/launcher browser config. Playwright and `@vitest/browser` are already devDependencies.
- Browser tests are slower and GPU/context-sensitive; seed deterministically and run serially (`fileParallelism: false`).
- Do not modify `.pi/`, skill, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- Browser test boot pattern exists in `tests/e2e/main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts`.
- Root `vite.config.ts` has only the `unit` project; core `vite.config.ts` defines browser/smoke/dev projects but is not the main-street root config.
- `npm test` runs only `--project unit`; browser tests are not currently run by the main-street repo CI (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs `npm test`).

## Desired change

Add `tests/main-street/cards/browser/` with scene-driven card suites plus a browser vitest project configuration, share the registry and definitions from the unit child, and write `browserTestStatus` / `browserTestFailReason` back to the CSV.

## Key files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/cards/browser/CardIntegration.browser.test.ts` — parameterised scene tests
- `tests/main-street/cards/browser/CardCombinations.browser.test.ts` — combination scene tests
- `tests/main-street/cards/browser/sceneHarness.ts` — boot/teardown + UI assertion helpers
- `vite.config.ts` — add a `browser` project (Playwright, Chromium)
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — run the browser card suite (optional, if CI time permits)
- shared `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestRegistry.ts` and `CardTestResultWriter.ts` (from the sibling child)

## Related work

- MS-0MUXWGT7G009THBO — sibling unit framework (blocked-by)
- MS-0MTINKHUT009KHK5 — Market Card Cheat browser smoke test (boot pattern precedent)
- MS-0MUMP92O9002772U — Storyline behaviour regression harness (harness precedent)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the real scene exposes enough programmatic seams (or accepts injected state) to set up arbitrary boards without long scripted play.
- Risk: 174 browser tests could be slow and flaky; mitigate with per-card minimal scenarios, serial execution, and a shared warmed-up scene where safe.
- Risk: writing to the same CSV from two runners could race; mitigate by a lock/merge writer or by running the two writers sequentially.
- Scope-creep risk: visual/animation snapshot testing is a separate concern — record as a linked work item if desired.

# Intake Brief — Coin and Reputation should count up/down (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8)

## Problem statement

During the end-of-turn reconciliation, coins and reputation fly from the business cards to the HUD totals line. The HUD totals currently stay frozen at the pre-animation value for the whole choreography (the deferred window, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) and then **jump** to the new value the moment the animations complete. The player therefore never sees the totals building as the coins/reputation arrive. This item makes the HUD totals animate in step with the reconciliation: they count **up** while receiving coins/reputation and **down** when losing, with the counting happening as the coin/pip flights play.

## Users

- **Main Street player (single-player)** — sees their coins and reputation totals climb/fall in step with the coin and pip flights arriving at the HUD at the end of the turn, making the reconciliation legible and satisfying.
- **Game designer** — gets a glanceable read of the end-of-turn income/expense reconciling against the HUD.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the counting to be display-only and deterministic: it must not alter any state, economy, or deferred-mutation invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Counts during the reconciliation.** While the end-of-turn deferred window is active (`incomeCollectionActive`), the HUD "Coins:" total is animated: it steps up as coin flights land at the HUD (the grid-to-HUD collection and any gain flights to the HUD counter), and reaches the post-reconciliation value **exactly** when the last such flight lands. The "Reputation:" total behaves identically for reputation pips.
- **AC2 — Symmetric count-down.** When the end-of-turn reconciliation reflects a loss (coins and/or reputation decrease, e.g. incident or negative upcoming delta with HUD→card flights), the HUD totals count **down** symmetrically as the flights depart from the HUD, ending exactly at the final value.
- **AC3 — Reduced motion, replay and headless unchanged.** Under reduced motion and in replay/headless modes the totals render the final value directly with no counting animation (the existing deferred-path fallbacks are untouched).
- **AC4 — Display-only; invariants preserved.** The counting never mutates `state`, `previousCoins`/`previousReputation`, the exactly-once deferred-delta application (`endOfTurnDeltasApplied` / `applyPendingDeltasOnce`), or any economy/transitional value. The final `refreshAll()` after the window closes still shows the authoritative post-delta values.
- **AC5 — Tests.** Automated coverage asserts: (a) a mid-flight displayed total is strictly between the pre- and post-reconciliation values, (b) the total equals the final value at the last landing, (c) losses count down, and (d) reduced motion never counts. Existing income-collection, deferred-mutation and phase-sequential tests continue to pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** — the counting lives in the renderer/animator; it must never touch the engine or the transcript.
- **Deferred window intact** (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) — `previousCoins`/`previousReputation` continue to drive the pre-animation display; the new *displayed* values are a separate, render-time quantity layered on top.
- **Reduced motion never counts** (existing convention: immediate single final pop, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q).
- The final displayed value must be **exact** at the last landing — no off-by-one or floating drift; rounding follows the existing integer-economy convention (`Math.round` in `refreshHud`).
- Scope is the end-of-turn reconciliation only (producer decision, see Appendix Q1); market buys, Community Favour and mid-turn deltas are out of scope.

## Existing state

- `refreshHud()` (src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts) computes the deferred window from `incomeCollectionActive`/`incidentRevealActive` and renders `previousCoins`/`previousReputation` while it is active; the value is static throughout the ~11s choreography (`animateIncomePhases`), then the window closes and `finishTurnPresentation`'s `refreshAll()` shows the post-delta values — a single jump.
- `animateHudValueChanges()` suppresses the mid-animation delta pop while `incomeCollectionActive` is true, so the only landing feedback is the final `+total` pop.
- `collectIncomeGrids()` (src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts) flies the per-card coin grids to the HUD sequentially; each icon's `onComplete` decrements a `pending` counter and the last landing calls `finalize()` (applies deferred deltas exactly once via `applyPendingDeltasOnce`, then clears the window).
- Upcoming deltas fly point-to-point to/from the HUD via `flyCoinsToPoint`/`flyRepPips` (gain card→HUD, loss HUD→card); the incident reveal (MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts) similarly flies HUD→card for losses.
- Unit tests exist for income collection and phase choreography (`tests/main-street/income-collection-animator.test.ts`, `income-phase-sequential-animator.test.ts`); browser tests cover the deferred window (`tests/main-street/main-street-animators-deferred.browser.test.ts`).

## Desired change

Introduce a display-only, per-resource *displayed total* (e.g. `displayedCoins` / `displayedReputation` on the scene) that:

1. Is initialised to the pre-animation value (`previousCoins`/`previousReputation`) when the deferred window opens.
2. Is stepped +/− as coin/pip flights **land at** (gain) or **depart from** (loss) the HUD during the reconciliation — grid-to-HUD collection, upcoming card/HUD deltas, and incident HUD→card losses — one step per icon using the icon's coin/pip value, so the running total tracks the animation and lands exactly on the final value at the last arrival.
3. Is what `refreshHud()` renders (rounded, per the integer-economy convention) in place of the static pre-animation value while the deferred window is active; outside the window `refreshHud` falls back to the existing `previousCoins`/state logic untouched.
4. Is reset/cleared after the final `refreshAll()` that closes the turn, so the next turn starts from the authoritative state.

The counting hooks live where flights already complete (the `onComplete` handlers in `collectIncomeGrids`, `flyCoinsToPoint`, `flyRepPips` and the incident-reveal flights) so no new flight choreography is introduced. Unit tests cover the stepping logic with a mocked scene; a browser test samples the HUD text mid-animation to prove the intermediate values.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshHud()`: render the display-only totals during the deferred window (replaces the static `previousCoins`/`previousReputation` readout while counting).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — step `displayedCoins`/`displayedReputation` at flight landings/departures (`collectIncomeGrids`, `flyCoinsToPoint`, `flyRepPips`).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — step the displayed totals for incident-reveal HUD→card loss flights.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — new display-state fields + reset conventions (`createScene`, lifecycle).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — initialise displayed totals at `endTurn()` alongside `previousCoins` capture; ensure the displayed values are cleared after the final refresh.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-animator.test.ts` — unit coverage of the stepping logic.
- `tests/main-street/main-street-animators-deferred.browser.test.ts` — browser coverage of mid-flight intermediate values and exact final landing.

## Related work

- `Visual representation of reputation (MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E)` — completed epic; introduced the reputation HUD counter and on-street population.
- `Reputation phase dissolve-to-coins (MS-0MUYGFWXK003QFYB)` — completed; reworked the reputation income source (coins now fly from pedestrians, not the HUD counter) — the count-up applies to the collection phase that follows.
- `Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)` — completed; per-seat end-of-turn phases.
- CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — "Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle" (deferred window; the display-only count-up is a refinement of, and dependent on, this window).
- CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS — Upcoming coin/reputation delta flights to/from the HUD (source of the gain/loss flight directions used by the counting).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** tempting to animate mid-turn HUD changes (market buys, Community Favour) for consistency — out of scope by producer decision (Q1); record as a future work item, not scope.
- **Risk (animation cost):** counting inside `onComplete` per icon adds negligible cost but must stay robust if a flight is destroyed or skipped; the final value must still resolve via the existing `pending`/`finalize` path.
- **Risk (floating drift):** per-icon increments are fractional; use exact accumulation (e.g. set the displayed total to the slot total when the slot's last icon lands, or accumulate with the same `roundHalf` used by the economy) to guarantee the final exactness in AC1/AC2.
- **Risk (regression):** the deferred window (`previousCoins` semantics, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) and reduced-motion/replay exemptions are heavily covered by existing tests; any change must keep `income-collection-animator`, `income-phase-sequential-animator` and `main-street-animators-deferred` suites green.
- **Assumption:** the count-up applies to the *collection* phase only (as coins/reputation animate from the business card to the HUD at the end of the cycle — Q1); competitive per-seat wallets are unchanged.
- **Assumption:** the displayed number is rounded to whole coins/reputation as today (`Math.round`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of the count-up/down — end-of-turn reconciliation only, or all HUD changes?" — Answer (producer): "As the coins/reputation are animating from the business card to the HUD status line at the end of the cycle" → **end-of-turn reconciliation only** (the collection flights to the HUD). Source: interactive reply (2026-10-14). Research: `refreshHud` deferred window renders only during `incomeCollectionActive`/`incidentRevealActive`; mid-turn changes are out of scope. Related: CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q.
- Q2: "Per-flight landing step or smooth tween?" — Answer (producer): **A — per-flight landing** (total steps as each coin/pip arrives at the HUD, reaching the final value exactly when the last one lands). Source: interactive reply (2026-10-14). Research: `collectIncomeGrids` per-icon `onComplete` counts down `pending`; the natural hook already exists.
- Q3: "Negative deltas / reduced motion?" — Answer (producer): **A — symmetric count-down; reduced motion jumps straight to the final value**. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-14). Research: existing reduced-motion convention skips flights and keeps the single final pop (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); an instant final render preserves that.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** – Sell 3 businesses challenge (blocked)
- **MS-0MUWE6MSQ006DEZ4** – End-reason & player-state model (completed)
- **MS-0MUZFVLVS007S56L** – Implement ownership-aware placement scoring (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtr72p14000vo6q, ac4, ac5, acceptance, accumulation (+297 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: 0mtv9as15004ac1e, 0mua1uh3a008m4bs, 0muxaqqon006xa6i, 0muygfwxk003qfyb, 11s (+258 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: 0mtr72p14000vo6q, acceptance, active, add, adds (+237 more)

# Executive should grant an action point and a single hand slot

The Executive staff card (`staff-executive`) should be repurposed from a pure hand-capacity card into an action-economy card: while employed it grants **+1 action per week** and **+1 hand slot**. This extends the `actionsPerTurn` staff mechanic (introduced by MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0) to the tier-10 Executive and reduces its `handSlotsAdded` from `4` to `1`.

## Problem statement

The Executive is the tier-10 premium capacity card (`handSlotsAdded: 4`, cost 2000, ongoing 500) with no ability. Players who want a top-tier action-economy staff choice currently have only the tier-12 General Manager, so the Executive is a dead-end on the action-economy build axis. Granting the Executive `actionsPerTurn: 1` — traded against dropping its hand-slot bonus to a single slot — gives it a distinct, legible role.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a tier-10 action-economy staff option before the tier-12 General Manager is affordable.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to hire an Executive that grants +1 action per week and +1 hand slot so that I can take an extra action each week without waiting for the General Manager.

## Acceptance Criteria

CSV column order is unchanged.
- **AC2** — The parsed `StaffCard` template for `staff-executive` exposes `actionsPerTurn === 1` and `handSlotsAdded === 1`, and `executeWeekStart` composes the weekly budget as `1 base + sum(actionsPerTurn) + banked (capped at 2)` with the Executive included, preserving the existing invariants (staff actions consumed first, never banked; bank cap 2).

- **AC6** — Documentation is updated to reflect the change: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ 6.0 action-economy staff list), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (staff table), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (staff catalogue row + rationale), and `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` (staff template table).

# Intake Brief — Remove Storyline text from top left (MS-0MUYAF2AD0066XO9)

## Problem Statement

The HUD renders a transient **"Storyline: …"** continuity-indicator label just
above the top-left of the info strip (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`),
telling the player which storyline is currently in play. The producer wants
this text gone: it clutters the top-left of the screen and adds little value
alongside the Storyline journal and choice-dialog already surfacing storyline
context.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — sees a cleaner HUD top-left; storyline context
  remains available via the choice dialog (storyline name as dialog title) and
  the Storyline journal button/overlay.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — unaffected; the removal touches
  only the HUD label, not storyline content, validation, or state.

### User Stories

- As a player, I no longer see a "Storyline: …" text floating at the top-left
  of the screen, so the HUD reads cleanly.
- As a player, I can still tell which storyline is in play through the existing
  choice dialog and Storyline journal, so no information is lost that matters
  at decision time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No "Storyline: …" HUD label is rendered: `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` no
      longer imports `continuityIndicatorLabel` and no longer creates the
      storyline label text object at the top-left position (above the strip's
      left edge). Verified by inspection and by the browser HUD test suite (if
      one asserts the label) — otherwise by code review of the removed block.
- [ ] The now-unused continuity-indicator code path is removed or left
      deliberately non-rendered: `continuityIndicatorLabel` and
      `getActiveStorylines` (and `ActiveStoryline`) in
      `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` are removed if no other consumer remains
      (current grep: none). The AC3 continuity-indicator tests in
      `tests/main-street/storyline-player-agency.test.ts` are removed/updated
      so `npm test` stays green with **no dead exports** left in
      `MainStreetStorylineUi.ts`. Verified by a grep showing zero remaining
      references and a passing suite.
- [ ] The named-dialog, outcome-feedback, and journal features
      (`choiceDialogTitle`, `choiceDialogSubtitle`, `storyUpdateLine`,
      `buildJournal`, journal overlay) are **unchanged** — only the top-left
      HUD indicator is removed. Verified by the remaining
      `storyline-player-agency.test.ts` (AC1/AC2) and journal tests passing
      unchanged.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the "Continuity indicator" bullet and cycle-continuity note in
      `docs/main-street/storylines.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

  graph/manifest, or state transitions.
- Do not remove the Storyline journal overlay or the journal button — only the
  transient top-left HUD label.
- No new assets, no new styling work.

## Existing State

## Desired Change

# Piggyback on other players' organiser actions

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, when one player organises a town-wide event such as a Local Festival, the benefits are currently routed only to that acting player's own wallet (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects`). There is no way for the other player(s) to participate in, or benefit from, an event that thematically belongs to the whole town. This makes events feel private rather than communal and removes a legible, interesting per-event decision from the non-acting player.

## Users

Primary user: the **human player in competitive mode**, who wants a meaningful reactive decision when the AI organises a town event.

- As the human player, when the AI organises a festival, I want to choose whether to co-fund it so that I can earn the full reward, or simply enjoy the spill-over benefit for free.
- As the human player, I want the trade-off to be explicit (coins and action cost vs. reward share) so the decision is legible.
- Secondary user: the **AI seat**, which needs a deterministic policy for the same decision so headless Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible.

## Proposed mechanic (design summary)

When a player plays a **piggyback-eligible Investment event** (an "organiser" event — e.g. Local Festival, Harvest Festival) during their MarketPhase, every **other active player** receives a 50% share of that event's rewards **automatically**, and is offered the single choice to **join fully**:

| Option | Cost | Reward |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Join fully** | **150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event** (paid from the piggybacker's own coins); **no action point is spent** | **100%** of the event's rewards |
| **Free-ride (automatic default)** | Nothing | **50%** of the event's rewards, granted automatically |

- The free-ride 50% is always applied, so there is **no "decline everything" option** and no prompt to refuse it — the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade 50% → 100%.
- Joining fully does **not** consume an action point; the seed's "take an additional action" means the player participates in the event (an additional participant), not that a budget action is spent.
- Rewards (coin + reputation) are computed on the **piggybacker's own board**, consistent with the existing per-owner event routing (`SpecificSynergy` rewards count the owner's own matching businesses), then scaled to 100% (join fully) or 50% (free-ride).
- The cost baseline is the amount the acting player **actually paid** for the event (after any cost discounts the acting player holds), not necessarily the card's nominal listed cost.
- If the piggybacker cannot afford 150% of that cost, the join-fully option is unavailable and the 50% free-ride applies.
- The acting player's own reward, and the shared market/incident deck, are unaffected by piggyback decisions.
- The mechanic applies **only in competitive mode (N≥2)**; single-player (N=1) has no other players and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.
- [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).
- [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`, and any relevant PRD/scope notes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

- **MS-0MTIIL1ON006H7IL** – Shared-day phase machine: alternating MarketPhases, shared closing phases (completed)
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – When playing with AI player is credit with AI challenges (open)
- **MS-0MUQZH6BU002113D** – GitHub Pages deploy workflow (completed)

- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: 0muvupwhd0032cu4, acting, action, actionbudget, actions (+301 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, acting, action, actions, active (+283 more)

If they choose not to pay then they get only 50% of the rewards.

Live population reconciliation against the HUD reputation value (parent MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The refresh is triggered from the same path that updates the HUD reputation counter (`animateHudValueChanges` / renderer HUD `repX`), via an animator-context accessor.
- Accessibility and non-rendering modes unchanged: Reduced Motion and replay/headless modes skip the change; no gameplay RNG is drawn; the live refresh never mutates game state or the transcript.
