# Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes

## Problem statement

A storyline choice node currently declares exactly **two** labelled outcomes
— "Accept" (yes) and "Reject" (no), each pointing at one successor card
(`hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` in `src/card-data.csv`).
Authors cannot express richer branches, and a chosen outcome always leads to
the same next card. The goal is to let a node present an **arbitrary number
of labelled outcomes**, where each outcome holds a **set of candidate
successor cards** and the actually-visited successor is selected **uniformly
at random** when the player picks that outcome. Producer direction
(2026-10-14, interactive reply): Q1=B (arbitrary labelled player options,
engine picks the successor from an option's candidate set at random);
Q2=A (extend CSV authoring + author CLI + validator + graph/manifest/schema,
**no backward compatibility** required, mermaid documentation must be
re-worked); Q3=A (uniform selection via the seeded `state.rng()`, one draw
per selection at resolution time so replay/Monte-Carlo stay deterministic).

## Users

- **Content/engine authors** — need to declare multi-outcome nodes with
  random branch targets from CSV without programmatic registration.
- **Players** — see an arbitrary labelled option list instead of a forced
  Accept/Reject; repeat plays of the same storyline can take different
  successor paths.
- **Balance team** — benefit from Monte-Carlo determinism being preserved
  (same seed ⇒ same branch), so the existing harness remains comparable.

Example user stories:

- As a content author, I can declare a node with three outcomes
  ("Negotiate", "Walk away", "Escalate"), each listing two possible next
  cards, so a single choice can fan into varied consequences.
- As a player, when I pick an outcome the game resolves to a uniformly
  random one of that outcome's candidate successors, without me choosing the
  next card.
- As a balance engineer, I can re-run a seeded simulation and observe the
  same random branch taken, so storylines remain auditable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Arbitrary labelled outcomes.** A storyline choice node can declare an arbitrary number (≥ 1, including > 2) of labelled options authored via CSV (`src/card-data.csv`), each option carrying its own ordered candidate list of successor card ids (empty list = the chain ends).
- **Uniform random selection.** When an option is chosen, exactly one successor is drawn uniformly at random from that option's candidate set using the seeded `state.rng()` (one draw per selection, at resolution time); replaying with the same seed produces the same successor, and the option list the player sees is unchanged by the draw.
- **Legacy shape removed.** The two-way `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/ `rejectNextCardId` fields and their compiled Accept/Reject semantics are replaced by the arbitrary-outcome model (no backward compatibility kept); the five shipped storylines are migrated, with the timeline of the change documented in the work item.
- **Tooling consistency.** The authoring CLI, static validator (`validate-storylines.ts`), graph/manifest export and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` all model the new option/successor-set shape, rejecting dangling targets, empty option lists and malformed option encodings.
- **Documentation regeneration.** Mermaid graphs, per-storyline documents (`docs/main-street/storylines/*.md`), the storyline reference (`docs/main-street/storylines.md`) and any doc-drift tests/SVG artefacts are regenerated to show the new multi-outcome nodes and pass their drift guards.
- **Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover compilation, resolution (random draw semantics incl. a seeded replay pair), validator and CLI authoring; the storyline regression harness plus the full project test suite pass with the new changes.
- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
## Constraints

- Determinism: successor selection may consume RNG only from the seeded
  `state.rng()` stream, exactly one draw per selection; `pushChainCard`
  stays RNG-free. Any additional draw shifts the stream and must be pinned
  by tests, so cross-build Monte-Carlo comparisons after this change are not
  numerically identical to before (acceptable — see Risks).
- No backward compatibility: legacy fields, compiled Accept/Reject shape and
  `'accept'`/`'reject'` transcript/save tokens may be removed; per producer
  decision (Q5) no old-save handling is implemented — no saves exist in the
  wild — so legacy load paths are dropped cleanly.
- The generalised `StorylineOption` seam (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`)
  remains the single compilation/resolution point; the AI and UI paths flow
  through it unchanged in structure.
- CSV authoring must keep the deterministic, machine-parseable, validator-
  gated style of the existing tooling.

## Existing state

- Choice data lives on `EventCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) and is
  authored in `src/card-data.csv` via `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`
  (Accept/"yes", effect `apply`) and `rejectNextCardId` (Reject/"no",
  effect `skip`); legacy fields compile to a two-option `StorylineOption`
  list in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`.
- A programmatic registry (`registerStorylineOptions`) already supports
  arbitrary labelled options with `condition` / `successorResolver`
  callbacks; content authoring via CSV has never used it.
- Resolution: `resolveIncident` defers the choice into
  `pendingEventChoice`; `resolveEventOption`/`resolveEventChoice` apply the
  effect policy and push the single successor (`pushChainCard`, no RNG).
  `decideEventChoice` picks an option index on the AI path; transcript
  records `'accept'`/`'reject'` tokens (`MainStreetTranscript.ts`); saves
  store the `chosenOption` token (`MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`).
- The shipped graph has five storylines; the manifest, Mermaid flowchart,
  per-storyline SVG docs and the schema are regenerated via
  `npm run storylines:graph…` and covered by drift guards and
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- Extend the CSV data model so a row can author an arbitrary labelled option
  list, each option with an ordered candidate successor set. Suggested
  encoding (decided in planning, kept deterministic; Q4=B): a single
  `options` column of the form `label|cardA,cardB;label2|cardC` (option
  separator `;`, label/successors separator `|`, candidate separator `,`),
  replacing the three legacy columns; `hasChoices` derives from a non-empty
  list; every CSV-authored option carries `effectPolicy: 'apply'` (`skip`
  remains available only via the programmatic registry seam).
- Change the compiled model: `StorylineOption` gains a candidate successor
  list (`successorIds: string[] | null`) in place of the single
  `successorId`; `resolveStorylineOption` draws one uniform candidate via
  `state.rng()` at resolution time, applies the option's `effectPolicy`
  (always `apply` for CSV-authored options per Q4=B), and pushes the drawn
  card. `successorResolver` (if present) keeps precedence
  over the random draw, and `condition` keeps draw-time filtering with the
  frozen snapshot.
- Migrate the five shipped storylines to the new model, update the
  validator, author CLI (`storyline-author.ts`), graph/manifest export,
  JSON schema, transcript/save/undo tokens, AI decision handling and UI
  option presentation as needed, and regenerate all graph/SVG/doc artefacts.
- Record follow-ups (not in scope): weighted outcomes, per-candidate
  conditions, UI redesign of the option dialog. See Related work.

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — replace `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` with the arbitrary `options` column; migrate five storylines.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` choice fields; `StorylineOption.successorId` → candidate successor list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — compilation of CSV options, uniform draw via `state.rng()`, resolution precedence (resolver > random > none).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution path, transcript token, `resolveEventChoice` indexing.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — validate arbitrary option model (labels, successor sets, dangling targets, empty lists).
- `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — author CLI for multi-outcome nodes.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph*.ts` — edges per option → each candidate successor; Mermaid/SVG re-render.
- `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` — node options + edge model.
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — option-label tokens, save/undo.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI option pick over arbitrary lists (static chain eval re-worked).
- `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` — option label presentation.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md`, `docs/main-street/storylines/*.md`, graph artefacts in `docs/main-street/assets/` — regenerate; drift guards.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/storyline-*.test.ts`, `storyline-regression-harness.test.ts`, `storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, `MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts`, `storyline-graph.test.ts`.

## Related work

- MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N (completed) — generalised `StorylineOption` seam & callback escape hatch; foundation for this change.
- MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9 (open, feature) — conditional/cost-gated options; design overlap, different semantics — keep separate, coordinate on the shared option model.
- MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7 (open, task) — Monte-Carlo storyline coverage analytics; benefits from deterministic random branches.
- MS-0MURO2D6F002WM4Y (blocked) — planned validator/schema extension for conditional fields; superseded/re-scoped by this change.
- MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV (completed) — "write storylines" epic; origin of the shipped content being migrated.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does 'an arbitrary number of yes and no outcomes' mean?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-14 interactive reply): **B** — the node presents N labelled player options (arbitrary labels); each option's successor is randomly drawn from its own candidate set. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up: "Change description to match this new direction" — description rewritten accordingly.
- Q2: "Where are the multiple outcomes authored and which surfaces change?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A** — extend CSV authoring + author CLI + validator + graph/manifest/schema; **no need to maintain backward compatibility**; "there will need to be work on the mermaid graphs in documentation". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "How should random selection behave under deterministic replay?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A** — uniform random using seeded `state.rng()`, one draw per selection at resolution time; replay/Monte-Carlo stay deterministic. Source: interactive reply.

## Risks & assumptions

- **RNG stream shift (accepted).** Adding a seeded draw at each resolution changes the shared RNG stream relative to the previous build; seeded replays *within* the new build are deterministic, but Monte-Carlo/balance numbers are not numerically comparable across the change. Mitigation: pin the draw count and stream position in tests; document in the work item.
- **CSV encoding of nested lists is error-prone.** Mitigation: strict validator with actionable errors; keep separators deterministic and documented in the CSV column reference.
- **Old saves (decided Q5).** No backward compatibility is required, and no old-save handling is implemented — there are no saves in the wild; legacy load paths are dropped cleanly (documented in child F3).
- **AI difficulty heuristics.** Hard-difficulty static chain evaluation is built around accept/reject chains and needs re-work for arbitrary options; AI must still resolve headlessly without stalling.
- **Scope creep.** Weighted outcomes, per-candidate conditions, and a redesigned option dialog are explicitly out of scope; record as follow-up work items (see Related work).

### Related work items

- **MS-0MUVBH589001L7NL** – Competitive game ends on AI seat failure — reputation collapse or bankruptcy (eliminate AI instead of ending human game) (completed)
- **MS-0MV1HAUPR004REDJ** – [test-failure] main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts > suite import failure — failing test (completed)

# Ask about the tutorial before the single-player/competitive choice

## Problem statement

At scene boot the blocking "New Game" overlay asks the player to choose
Single-player vs Competitive **before** the tutorial offer is shown. A player
who actually wants the guided tutorial must therefore pick a game mode first,
even though the tutorial can only ever be played single-player — so the mode
choice is either wasted or misleading. The tutorial decision should be asked
first, and choosing the tutorial should commit the player to single-player
without an unnecessary mode choice.

## Users

- **First-time player (tutorial wanters).** "As a first-time player, I want to
  be asked whether I want the tutorial *before* I am asked to pick a mode, so
  that I am not forced to make a mode choice that the tutorial will ignore."
- **First-time player (tutorial decliners).** "As a first-time player who
  skips the tutorial, I want the Single-player/Competitive selector to appear
  immediately so I can start the game I actually want."
- **Returning player.** "As a returning player (tutorial already completed or
  skipped), I want the mode selector to appear straight away, unchanged from
  today."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On boot, when the tutorial offer is eligible, the tutorial offer modal is
   presented **before** the New Game mode selector (Single-player vs
   Competitive); the mode selector is not visible while the tutorial offer is
   waiting.
2. Selecting **Start Tutorial** starts the existing scripted tutorial as a
   single-player game and the New Game mode selector is not shown for that
   boot. (The tutorial is only available in single-player.)
3. Selecting **Skip for now** on the tutorial offer presents the New Game
   mode selector next, and confirming it starts the selected mode exactly as
   today.
4. When the tutorial offer is **not** eligible (completed, already skipped,
   replay mode, or disabled), the New Game mode selector is presented as the
   first boot modal, exactly as today.
5. The deferred week banner still fires **exactly once** and only after the
   player has committed to playing (after mode confirmation, or suppressed
   for the tutorial path as today). It must not fire while any boot modal is
   waiting for a choice.
6. A browser smoke test asserts the modal ordering: tutorial offer visible
   first; after skipping, the mode selector is visible.
7. A unit test asserts the ordering decision in
   `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` (tutorial offer before mode selector,
   and the mode selector is skipped entirely when the tutorial is started).
8. The scene-restart / menu round-trip behaviour is preserved: the boot flow
   is presented once per boot, and re-presented after `scene.restart()` /
   `scene.start()` (regression guard).
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (for example
   the onboarding flow section of `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md`).
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No changes to the tutorial script/steps, tutorial content, or competitive
  gameplay/state semantics.
- Reuse the existing `TutorialOfferModal` and `MainStreetNewGameOverlay`
  components and the existing localisation keys; no new user-facing strings
  are required unless the producer asks for an explicit "tutorial is
  single-player" note (see Assumptions).
- Must not regress the deferred-banner timing guarantees currently pinned by
  `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts`.
- Must not regress the once-per-boot selector guard
  (`newGameSelectionMade` / `resetNewGameSelectionFlag`).

## Existing state

- `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` currently shows
  `newGameOverlay` first and only calls `showTutorialOfferOnly` from the
  overlay's `onConfirm` callback.
- `TutorialOfferModal.onSkip` (wired in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) currently calls
  `s.playDeferredWeekBanner()` directly.
- `TutorialOfferModal.onStartTutorial` already builds a single-player
  tutorial state via `createTutorialScenario()` and starts the tutorial flow.
- `applyNewGameSelection` (in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`) rebuilds state only for
  competitive; single-player keeps the existing state.
- Eligibility is decided by `shouldShowTutorialOffer` in
  `src/TutorialState.ts` (`not_seen` shows; `completed`/`skipped` do not;
  `forceShowOffer` overrides; `replayMode`/`disableTutorial` suppress).
- The current implementation order contradicts the onboarding flow documented
  in `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` §5 (tutorial check before normal
  run), which predates the competitive mode selector.

## Desired change

Reorder the boot flow so the tutorial offer is the **first** blocking modal:

1. If `showIfEligible` returns true → show the tutorial offer modal.
   - **Start Tutorial** → run the existing single-player tutorial; do not show
     the mode selector this boot.
   - **Skip for now** → show the New Game mode selector.
2. If the offer is ineligible → show the New Game mode selector.
3. After the mode selector is confirmed → `applyNewGameSelection` then play
   the deferred week banner (exactly once).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` — reorder
  `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner` / `showTutorialOfferOnly` so the offer
  precedes the selector.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — rewire
  `onStartTutorial` / `onSkip` callbacks to the reordered flow; keep the
  tutorial single-player setup and the deferred-banner hand-off.
- `src/scenes/TutorialOfferModal.ts` — skip callback should no longer assume
  it owns the deferred-banner hand-off (if the reorder moves that
  responsibility).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameOverlay.ts` — only if the once-per-boot guard
  needs adjusting.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-new-game-restart.test.ts` — update ordering
  expectations for the selector guard.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-modal.test.ts` — add ordering/decision
  coverage where testable without Phaser.
- `tests/main-street/week-banner.browser.test.ts` — pin the deferred-banner
  timing under the new order.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-5.md` — update the onboarding flow section
  to state that the tutorial offer precedes the mode selector.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** — Game-mode selector UI (introduced the current
  boot-time selector ordering).
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (parent epic of the
  selector).
- Automated related-work report appended by `/skill:find-related`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — no copy change.** The modal body/buttons keep their current
  localised copy. The "tutorial is single-player" fact is enforced by the flow
  (choosing the tutorial skips the mode selector) rather than stated in the
  UI. If the producer wants the modal copy to say "single-player", that is an
  additive copy/CSV change.
- **Assumption — tutorial start implies single-player.** "Start Tutorial"
  never shows the mode selector, matching the constraint that the tutorial is
  single-player only.
- **Risk — deferred-banner timing.** Moving the skip hand-off must preserve
  "fires exactly once, never while a modal is waiting". Covered by AC5/AC6.
- **Risk — guard interplay.** The `newGameSelectionMade` once-per-boot guard
  must not suppress the selector when the tutorial offer is skipped, and must
  not show the selector after the tutorial is started.
- **Risk — stale browser tests.** `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` are excluded
  from `npm run test` (unit project only), so browser-ordering tests must be
  run explicitly via the browser profile to verify AC6.
- **Scope creep.** Repositioning/replay of the tutorial from Settings and any
  "tutorial is single-player" copy change are out of scope unless requested;
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the New Game mode selector be skipped entirely when the player
  chooses Start Tutorial (i.e. the tutorial always runs single-player)?" —
  Answer (operator, seed instruction): "If the player wants to play the
  tutorial they can only play single player. Ask if they want the tutorial
  before asking if they want to play single or competitive." Source:
  `/intake` seed command.
- Q: "Should the tutorial offer modal copy explicitly state that the tutorial
  is single-player only?" — Answer: OPEN QUESTION (not specified in the seed).
  Assumption recorded: no copy change; enforced by flow. Research: modal copy
  is localised in `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` and covered by
  `tests/main-street/tutorial-i18n.test.ts` / `tutorial-csv.test.ts`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ** – Reroll to cost more (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)
- **MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4** – Turns do not bank when playing against AI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac5, acceptance, actually, add, additive (+229 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, add, already, always (+176 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac6, acceptance, actually, add, additive (+172 more)

# Intake Brief: Residual Expensive-Tier Branching Upgrades Below Pick-Rate Target

**Work item:** MS-0MV035PRV002QDG4 · `task` · `low`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)

## Headline

Two expensive-tier level-0 branching upgrades (`upg-drive-in`, cost 700; `upg-wellness-center`, cost 900) remain at or near 0% M1 pick rate on the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with higher-weighted upgrades. This task raises their draw-weight (or adjusts cost/incomeBonus) to reach ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% or breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.

## Problem statement

The upgrade-deck composition lever (MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W) added `drawWeight` values to the upgrade-deck: the four level-2 capstones and their level-1 prerequisites received weight boosts (2–3× baseline), but the remaining level-0 branching upgrades — `upg-drive-in` (Cinema, cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (Day Spa, cost 900) — were left with no `drawWeight` (baseline = 1). These two cards compete for the single upgrade slot in the market against weighted cards (drawWeight 2–3), so their market appearance rate is too low to achieve meaningful adoption. The previous rebalance (MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M) left them unchanged to avoid over-tuning the market composition.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the expensive-tier branching path (Cinema → Drive-In, Day Spa → Wellness Center) to be a viable investment option alongside the IMAX/Resort-Spa standard path and the multiplex/luxury-retreat capstone chain.
- **Producer / designer** — wants a balanced economy where all upgrade paths are reachable, with measurable Monte Carlo evidence.
- **Developer** — wants card-data-only changes (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight); no engine modifications.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline captured.** Before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance` prefix, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 pick rate for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. **Target met.** A card-data-only change (cost/incomeBonus/drawWeight) lifts both `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center` to ≥5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`) below 5% M1 and without breaking the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ladder.
3. **Tests pass.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
4. **Fallback escalated (conditional).** If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable by card-data-only tuning without regressing the capstones or the difficulty ladder, the shortfall is documented on this work item with before/after evidence and a follow-up work item is created to escalate (per the Constraints section).

## Constraints

- **Card data only** — no engine-rule changes. Modify `cost`, `incomeBonus`, and/or `drawWeight` in `src/card-data.csv` (or equivalent template).
- If the ≥5% M1 target is unreachable without regressing capstones or breaking the difficulty ladder, document the shortfall and escalate separately.

## Existing state

- **CSV values (current):**
  | Card | Cost | incomeBonus | drawWeight | requiredLevel | targetBusiness |
  |------|------|-------------|------------|---------------|----------------|
  | upg-drive-in | 700 | 200 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Cinema |
  | upg-wellness-center | 900 | 250 | (unset = 1) | 0 | Day Spa |
  | upg-imax | 700 | 300 | 2 | 0 | Cinema |
  | upg-resort-spa | 900 | 350 | 2 | 0 | Day Spa |
  | upg-grand-bakehouse | 900 | 350 | 3 | 1 | Bakery |
  | upg-restaurant | 1400 | 550 | 3 | 1 | Diner |
  | upg-multiplex | 1400 | 700 | 3 | 1 | Cinema |
  | upg-luxury-retreat | 1400 | 700 | 3 | 1 | Day Spa |

- `drawWeight` is read from CSV column 54 (`MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`) into `UpgradeCard` templates (`MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`), and applied to upgrade refill selection in `MainStreetStateSetup.ts` (`upgradeDrawWeight()` / `pickWeightedUpgradeIndex()`). `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` holds no draw-weight logic.
- The `drawWeight` mechanism (verified in source, MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W): absent → weight 1 and **never** eligibility-boosted; a declared weight is the base, **plus `UPGRADE_ELIGIBLE_DRAW_BONUS` (30)** at refill time when the card's `targetBusiness` is on the street at exactly `requiredLevel` and not yet maxed. Selection is one `rng()` cumulative-weight pick over the shuffled deck (`-1` → legacy `pop()` fallback). So declaring a weight on these two level-0 cards (Cinema / Day Spa target, `requiredLevel` 0) makes them surface aggressively as soon as their target business exists — expect the tuning knob to be coarser than the raw weight number suggests, and consider a weight of 1 (declared) if the +30 bonus alone suffices.
- **Related completed work:**
  - MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (task, high)
  - MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W — Upgrade-deck composition lever: raise level-2 capstone reachability (feature, high)
  - MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 — Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption (feature, high)

## Key Files (validated 2026-10-21)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Modify `drawWeight` column (54) for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`; optionally adjust `cost`/`incomeBonus`. Current values: drive-in cost 700 / incomeBonus 200 / drawWeight empty; wellness-center cost 900 / incomeBonus 250 / drawWeight empty.

## Goal
As a Main Street player, I want installed entitled packs' cards dealt into my game and restored on load, so new content is persistent and save-compatible.

Cross-repo child of Tableau-Card-Engine CG-0MUZIS410002Z8EH (epic CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB, DLC support for card packs). The core contract/loader/merge landed in the engine (F1-F7); this item is the Main Street consumer.

- A missing or disabled pack degrades gracefully: warn, continue with base content, and refuse only when a live card instance requires a missing template.

## Minimal Implementation

# Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import

**Headline:** Ship a real, production residential-themed card pack (~10 balanced
cards with bespoke art) for Main Street, gated behind the launcher's unified
content-unlock store, with a scoped simulated-purchase flow that proves the
end-to-end pack **unlock → import** path.

## Problem statement

The card-pack DLC channel (merge, persistence and in-game listing) has shipped,
but there is no real Main Street pack exercising the **unlock → import** path
end-to-end, and no pack gated by the launcher's unified content-unlock store.
Without committed pack content plus a simulated purchase, the DLC feature cannot
be demonstrated or regression-tested beyond in-memory stubs.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — unlocks the residential pack and sees its new cards
  dealt into play.
  - *As a player, I want to buy/unlock a residential card pack and have its
    cards appear in my pool, so new content extends the game.*
  - *As a player, I want a locked pack to stay out of play until I own it, so
    gated content is respected.*
- **Developer / QA** — uses the simulated purchase to verify the whole channel.
  - *As a QA engineer, I want to simulate a pack purchase without a real
    storefront, so I can test lock → unlock → enable → deal → save/load.*
- **Producer** — demonstrates the DLC channel with real, shippable content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A production pack source tree exists under a new top-level `packs/` directory
   (`manifest.json` + `main-street/main-street-residential-pack/` CSV fragment +
   art), reuses Main Street's `card-data.csv` header **exactly**, has unique card
   ids, and builds cleanly with the core card-pack builder into an installable
   `<contentDir>/packs/` root.
2. The pack adds roughly ten new **residential-themed** cards spanning the
   families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space); each row follows
   the existing tier/cost/effect conventions and the set passes the
   balance/catalogue checks.
3. Every new card has bespoke project-generated art in `src/sprites/` and
   resolves to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) art through the regenerated
   `card-art-map.json`.
4. The pack is gated on the unified content-unlock store: while locked its cards
   stay out of play; a scoped simulated purchase (no collateral unlock, state
   persists across restarts) makes it show as unlocked in the Card Packs
   listing, enable-able, merged into the pool, and its cards deal in play.
5. Saves that record the active residential pack restore the same pool on load,
   and a missing/disabled pack degrades gracefully (warn, base content).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Test Plan

- **Unit / content** — pack manifest + CSV validity (exact base header, unique
  ids, family coverage), and balance/catalogue checks over the new rows.
- **Unit / pipeline** — pack gate resolves the pack as locked with no unlock and
  as entitled once a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock
  exists; `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merges the residential rows and the pool
  applies; save/load round-trips the active pack + merged checksum; missing-pack
  degradation.
- **Unit / unlock scope** — the simulated purchase unlocks only the residential
  pack and does **not** unlock the configured itch.io golf reward.
- **Browser / UI** — the Card Packs listing shows the pack locked, the simulated
  purchase flips it to unlocked, and it can then be enabled.
- **Art** — the runtime resolver and the static SVG generator agree that each
  new card resolves to dedicated art (mirrors the existing art-agreement test).

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo surface.** The Main Street pack gate can consume the unified
  store through the existing `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam
  (Main Street side), but the *write* path (a reward rule/verifier simulating the
  purchase) lives in the core launcher. Any core change must be committed to the
  `./core` submodule and the submodule bumped in the same work-item, as previous
  cross-repo items did.
- **Global attestation side effect.** `contentUnlocks.refresh({ attested: true })`
  self-attests *every* configured rule, which would also unlock the itch.io golf
  reward. The simulated purchase must scope verification to the residential pack
  (a `(platform, action)`-keyed verifier or equivalent rule-scoped mechanism).
- **Pack merge rules.** The fragment must reuse the base header exactly;
  duplicate ids or a mismatched header reject the pack whole (core contract).
- **Art.** Art must be project-generated, deterministic/reproducible, and
  licence-clean (CC0 / in-house), matching the existing 1024×1024 source-sprite
  pipeline.
- **Additive only.** No changes to base card data or balance; the pack is purely
  additive.
- **Push policy.** Commit/push to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Existing state

- Card-pack channel complete and shipped: `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
  (merge/persistence, one entry point), `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536`; listing UI/boot
  wiring, `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H`; e2e pipeline test, `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6`; docs
  cross-reference, `MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG`.
- Core pack contract/loader/merge/entitlement and the reference pack live under
  `core/`: `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts`,
  `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` (with a `resolveEntitlement` seam),
  `core/electron/card-pack-entitlements.ts` (Steam-DLC shaped) and
  `core/tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/` (3-card
  `main-street-foundations`).
- Unified content-unlock store shipped in core: `core/electron/action-rewards.ts`
  (+ `FileContentUnlockStore`), `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts`,
  `core/electron/action-rewards.json`, renderer read client
  `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`, and the pure gate
  `core/src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts`.
- The card-pack gate does **not** currently consult `contentUnlocks`; the loader
  resolves entitlement through the Steam-DLC-shaped `cardPackClient`
  (`entitlement.steamAppId` / the DLC catalog placeholder
  `main-street-founders-pack → app 480`).
- Card art is a generated build artefact:
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` builds `src/card-art-map.json`
  from `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` + `src/card-data.csv`.
- `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs` (core `build:card-pack` npm script) turns a
  pack source tree into an installable `<contentDir>/packs/` root.

## Desired change

1. **Pack content** — author a new production pack source tree under `packs/`:
   `packs/manifest.json` declaring `main-street-residential-pack`
   (`gameId: main-street`, version, `coreEngineVersion`, `cards`, `assets`);
   `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` with ~10
   residential-theme cards in the base schema; and
   `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/*.png` pack art. Add a
   Main Street npm script wrapper for the core builder so the build is
   reproducible, and install under `<contentDir>/packs/`.
2. **Art** — generate bespoke 1024×1024 source sprites for the new cards into
   `src/sprites/`, regenerate `src/card-art-map.json`, and (if needed) extend the
   art generator so pack cards are mapped/covered.
3. **Unlock gate** — compose Main Street's pack entitlement resolution so a
   `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` content-unlock (via
   `contentUnlockClientFromWindow`) entitles the pack in addition to the existing
   Steam-DLC status.
4. **Simulated purchase** — add a scoped simulated-purchase reward rule/verifier
   in the core launcher targeting that DLC id, and a dev/QA affordance (for
   example a control in the Card Packs listing) that performs the purchase and
   refreshes the pack pool.
5. **Tests + docs** — cover content validity, the unlock/import pipeline and the
   listing behaviour (per Test Plan); update `README.md`, `src/README.md`,
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and add a pack `README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packs/manifest.json` — New pack catalogue entry for `main-street-residential-pack`.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` — New ~10-card residential fragment.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` — New pack art assets.
- `packs/README.md` — New: authoring/installing the production pack.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — Compose content-unlock entitlement into the loader seam.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Simulated-purchase affordance in the Card Packs panel.
- `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` — New bespoke source sprites (one per new card).
- `src/card-art-map.json` — Regenerated art map covering the new cards.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Extend to include pack card art.
- `package.json` — Add a `build:card-pack` wrapper invoking the core builder.
- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` — Add the scoped residential-pack purchase rule.
- `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts` — (If required) a `(platform, action)`-scoped simulated-purchase verifier.
- `tests/main-street/` — Pack content, unlock/import and listing tests.
- `README.md`, `src/README.md`, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Docs updates.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — art-generator gap.** There is no committed generator for the source
  `*_1024_x_1024.png` sprites; producing ten bespoke sprites reproducibly may
  need a new deterministic generator script. *Mitigation:* author a small
  generator (SVG→PNG via the existing `sharp` dependency) and commit it.
- **Risk — cross-repo change.** The unlock write-path config/verifier is in the
  core launcher; this requires a core commit + submodule bump. *Mitigation:* keep
  the core change minimal and config/verifier-scoped; record both commits.
- **Risk — global attestation.** `refresh({attested:true})` unlocks every rule.
  *Mitigation:* scope the verifier to `(platform, action)` so only the purchase
  rule verifies.
- **Risk — balance.** Monte Carlo / guardrail checks can be slow or flaky.
  *Mitigation:* size the set with the balance tool and catalogue checks; run the
  guardrails once at the end.
- **Risk — packaging.** The new `packs/` tree must reach the built artefact /
  content directory. *Mitigation:* document and wire the install step; verify
  with the e2e pipeline test.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Storyline/tier integration, extra cards or a full
  storefront purchase are out of scope. *Mitigation:* record them as linked
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Assumption — identifiers.** Pack id / DLC id / `dlcId` =
  `main-street-residential-pack`; `gameId` = `main-street`.
- **Assumption — card count.** "~10" cards; 8–12 acceptable if required for
  balance and family coverage.
- **Assumption — simulated payment.** A dev/QA-only simulated purchase, not a
  real storefront transaction.
- **Assumption — art licence.** All generated art is project-owned (CC0),
  matching the existing sprite provenance.

## Related work

- `Main Street pack merge & persistence` — `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536` (done): the
  single merge entry point and save/load persistence this pack flows through.
- `Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring` — `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H` (done):
  the Card Packs listing and boot discovery the unlock affordance extends.
- `End-to-end card-pack pipeline integration test` — `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6`
  (done): the loader → merge → save/load test the pack can be added to.
- `Documentation: Main Street card packs (DLC) cross-reference` —
  `MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG` (done): docs this item updates.
- Core DLC epic `CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB` and the unified content-unlock feature
  `CG-0MUZF156A007OUIT` (referenced via the `./core` submodule).

### Related work (automated report)

Generated by `/skill:find-related` (keywords: dlc, pack, unlock, cards,
residential, create, mechanism, test, …).

**Related work items**
- **MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H** – Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring (completed)
- **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7** – Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name (open) — *low relevance (keyword noise)*
- **MS-0MUYGX03R008FZR2** – Update documentation and code comments for new cost values (completed) — *low relevance (keyword noise)*

**Repository file matches**
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Card Packs contract/builder/entitlement reference.
- `core/docs/the-build/engine-capabilities-audit.md`
- `core/AGENTS.md`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which is the target pack artefact and where should its content live —
  (A) a new `main-street-residential-pack` under the reference fixture, (B)
  reuse `main-street-founders-pack`/app 480, or (C) production content under a
  new top-level `packs/` directory?" — Answer (rgardler): **C — production
  content under a new top-level `packs/` directory**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "How should the simulated payment work — (A) a dev-only Unlock/Buy
  affordance in the Card Packs listing granting the entitlement, (B) an
  npm/CLI grant script, (C) reuse the existing `contentUnlocks` mechanism, or
  (D) an in-game economy purchase?" — Answer (rgardler): **C — reuse the
  existing contentUnlocks mechanism**. Research: the pack gate
  (`core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts`) resolves entitlement through the Steam-DLC
  shaped `cardPackClient` and does **not** consult `contentUnlocks`; the
  renderer exposes only `isUnlocked`/`getUnlocks`/`refresh` (no direct write),
  so the purchase must be a configured reward rule driven through
  `contentUnlocks.refresh`. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- Q: "What is the card-set scope — (A) functional cards with placeholder art,
  or (B) a balance-tuned set plus bespoke generated art?" — Answer (rgardler):A
  **B — balance-tuned set, bespoke generated art, ~10 cards (can be more or
  less as necessary for balance)**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q (round 2): "Describe the differences/pros/cons of the content-unlock (C)
  vs the dev-entitlement (A) purchase simulation." — Answer (rgardler): **chose
  C**. Source: interactive reply.

## Out of scope

- Real storefront/Steam purchase wiring.
- Storyline, tier/meta-progression or challenge integration for the new cards.
- Rebalancing the base card pool.
- Additional packs beyond the residential set.


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-09** — `plan` session (`herdr-1791563523-3083199-21181`) decomposed this item into **10 children** (3 verification, 6 implementation/docs, 1 release verification). Pre-check decision `plan` (effort Medium, risk High); approval gate **not** required (only Extra-Large effort **and** High/Severe risk pause for producer approval). Verification children were **created first** (test-first creation order) with dependency edges pointing verification → implementation so each suite runs green once its code lands. AC-coverage review recommendation: `proceed` (all seven parent ACs are covered by at least one child; see the mapping below).

### Children

| # | ID | Type | Title | Depends on |
|---|----|------|-------|------------|
| 1 | MS-0MV16VX310089U2L | task | Verification: residential pack content & builder contract | F4 |
| 2 | MS-0MV16VXDZ007NBK8 | task | Verification: residential pack art coverage | F5 |
| 3 | MS-0MV16VXPV002JVX5 | task | Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline | F4, F6, F7, F8 |
| 4 | MS-0MV16VY0U0024E4T | feature | Production residential pack content & builder wrapper | — |
| 5 | MS-0MV16VYC20078A36 | feature | Bespoke residential pack art & generator coverage | F4 |
| 6 | MS-0MV16VYN3006SWM4 | feature | Content-unlock pack entitlement gate | — |
| 7 | MS-0MV16VYYB000TI7H | feature | Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher | — |
| 8 | MS-0MV16VZ9R008XTF5 | feature | Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance | F6, F7 |
| 9 | MS-0MV16VZLH007N4PC | docs | Documentation updates for the residential pack | F4–F8 |
| 10 | MS-0MV16VZWP001OUNR | task | Full-suite verification & release readiness | T1–T3, D9 |

### Parent AC → child coverage

- **AC1** (pack source tree, exact header, unique ids, builder) → F4 + T1.
- **AC2** (~10 residential cards across families, balance/catalogue) → F4 + T1.
- **AC3** (bespoke art in `src/sprites/`, dedicated non-`Fallback` map) → F5 + T2.
- **AC4** (gated on the unified content-unlock store; scoped simulated purchase; listing; deal in play) → F6, F7, F8 + T3.
- **AC5** (save/load restores the pack; missing/disabled degrades) → F6 + T3.
- **AC6** (all related documentation) → D9.
- **AC7** (full suite passes) → T10.

### Phasing

Implemented as independently verifiable slices: content/build → art → gate → scoped purchase → listing → docs → full-suite verification. Each slice carries its own automated coverage; the three `Verification:` children are the dedicated acceptance suites for content/builder, art coverage, and the unlock/purchase/save-load pipeline. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it with anything learned (the plan is intentionally a living artefact until each child is implemented).


### Appendix revision (plan session)

No new clarifying questions were asked: the intake Appendix above already resolves the pack-location question (C — production content under a new top-level `packs/`), the simulated-payment question (C — reuse the existing `contentUnlocks` mechanism) and the card-set-scope question (B — balance-tuned set, bespoke generated art, ~10 cards). The plan therefore re-uses those answers and records the following documented assumptions and design decisions rather than re-asking:

- **Gating declaration.** The residential pack is gated on the launcher's unified content-unlock store. The read side composes a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock at the `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam *in addition to* the existing Steam-DLC status. Which packs are content-unlock gated is a data-driven declaration (proposed: an additive entitlement marker surfaced on `CardPackStatusRef`, parsed by the core manifest/loader). A simpler equivalent that preserves the same behaviour is acceptable — the implementer records the final shape in the work item.
- **Scoped purchase.** The write path adds an additive rule-scope filter and an explicit simulated-purchase signal to `ActionRewardService.refresh` (and the `contentUnlocks:refresh` IPC/preload/renderer-client chain) plus a `SimulatedPurchase` verifier. This is the "equivalent rule-scoped mechanism" that prevents `refresh({ attested: true })` from collateral-unlocking anything, and prevents the scoped purchase from unlocking the `itchio-follow` golf reward.
- **Art.** Card-face art lives at `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` and is covered by the regenerated `src/card-art-map.json`; a new deterministic generator is required because no committed source-sprite generator exists. Pack `assets/` are separate pack art files.
- **Identifiers (from intake).** pack id / DLC id = `main-street-residential-pack`; `gameId` = `main-street`; unlock target key = `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack`; proposed dev/QA trigger `(platform: dev, action: simulate-purchase)` and rule id `main-street-residential-pack-purchase`.
- **Test-first ordering.** Verification children are created before implementation children; dependency edges point verification → implementation so each verification suite runs green once the code lands (the TDD red→green cycle executes inside the implementation child).
- **No invented requirements.** Storyline/tier integration, a real storefront purchase and extra packs remain out of scope per the parent's "Out of scope" section.

# Move community space tutorial explanation to the right spot

## Headline

Move the tutorial step "Costs and Reputation" (T13) so it sits immediately before "Move the Library to hand" (T18), where the Library is actually visible in the market row, and strengthen its text to explain why reputation matters (a higher reputation brings more customers and grows income).

## Problem statement

The tutorial step `T13` ("Costs and Reputation", `tutorial.T13.body`) explains that some cards build reputation instead of earning coins, referencing the Library (`cs-library`). It currently sits between `T12` (move the Bookshop to hand) and `T14` (end turn) — several steps before `T18` where the Library is introduced. At that position `ensureTutorialMarketForUpcomingSteps()` never forces the Library into the visible market row (the scan breaks at the next `end-turn`, `T14`), so the step highlights a development row that does not contain the card it is talking about. The explanation belongs right before "Move the Library to hand", both so the referenced card is visible and so the concept lands when it is first used.

## Users

New players following the built-in onboarding tutorial.

- As a new player, I want the "builds reputation" explanation to appear at the moment I see the Library in the market, so the text refers to something I can actually see.
- As a new player, I want to understand why reputation matters, so I feel the Library is worth building even though it does not earn coins.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In `UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS`, the `Costs and Reputation` entry (step id `T13`, unchanged i18n keys `tutorial.T13.*`) is repositioned to sit **immediately before** `T18` with no `end-turn` step between them; the step order reads `… T12, T14, T15, T16, T17, T13, T18, …`. All order-asserting tests and docs are updated accordingly.
2. The strengthened `tutorial.T13.body` explains that the referenced card builds reputation rather than earning coins **and** that a higher reputation brings more customers and grows income (mechanics: reputation scales coin income up to the 1.5× cap — `reputationCoinMultiplier`, CG-0MTINZ5GG007BH44). The resolved body is ≤3 sentences and uses only the `{cardName}` placeholder (no hardcoded card names/costs).
3. With the repositioned step, the Library (`cs-library`) is guaranteed present in the visible market row while `T13` is the active step — covered by a regression test asserting `ensureTutorialMarketForUpcomingSteps()` shows the Library when the current step is `T13`.
4. The full 25-step tutorial still completes sequentially (unit: `tutorial-flow.test.ts` sequential-completion and step-index assertions) and the browser/e2e suite (`main-street-tutorial-e2e-part{4,5,6}.browser.test.ts`, `TutorialOverlayHighlights`, `TutorialOverlayManager`) passes with the new order.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes: `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` (step-flow table, prose, and any budget-table ordering notes) plus affected code comments in `src/TutorialFlow.ts` and `src/TutorialScenario.ts`, the README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep step id `T13` and i18n keys `tutorial.T13.title` / `tutorial.T13.body` (Q1=a). No renumbering of steps.
- `T13` must sit directly adjacent to `T18` — no end-turn between them — or the Library-visibility guarantee breaks again (Q2=a).

## Existing state

- `src/TutorialFlow.ts` — `UNIFIED_TUTORIAL_STEPS` entry index 12 is `T13` (confirm gate, `developmentRow` highlight, `referencedCardId: 'cs-library'`), between `T12` and `T14`.

- Update every order-asserting unit, browser and e2e test, and the tutorial documentation to match.

## Key Files

- `src/TutorialFlow.ts` — reposition `T13` entry before `T18`; refresh order comments; update doc comment (step-order descriptions, gate distribution still holds).
- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` — strengthened `tutorial.T13.body` (and title if needed).

- `tests/main-street/tutorial-flow.test.ts` — order assertion (line 26), sequential-completion assertion (line 146), and step-index counts used to reach `T13`/`T18` (lines 194–204).
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-flow-integration.test.ts` — step-count assertion expecting `T13` (line 76).
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-scenario.test.ts` / `scenario-validation.test.ts` — add/extend the regression assertion that `cs-library` is in the market while `T13` is current.

# Intake Brief: ship — `run-release.js --help` runs post-release steps against a stale tag

## Goal (user story)

As a release operator, when I pass an unsupported flag (e.g. `--help`) to the
ship release wrapper, I want the wrapper to **fail fast with usage** and make
**no** git, worklog, notification, or close-side-effects, so that a mistaken or
exploratory invocation can never close release-ready work items without a real
`dev` → `main` merge.

## Problem statement

`node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --help` did not print wrapper
help. Instead it ran the entire post-release tail of the wrapper:

- it forwarded `--help` to the canonical merge script
  (`scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`), which printed its own usage and
  exited `0` **without merging**;
- Step 8 then read the *latest existing* tag via
  `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (returning the already-shipped `v0.1.18`);
- `verifyReleaseMerge('0.1.18')` **passed** because that tag already exists on
  `origin/main` and is an ancestor of it;
- the wrapper therefore sent a Discord release notification and ran
  `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease('0.1.18')`.

Observed on 2026-10-09 (project `tce-main-street`, dev 72 commits ahead of
main, no merge performed): **98 work items were spuriously closed** (152 close
comments — 150 `Closed with reason: Shipped in v0.1.18` plus 2 cascade
comments). The worklog was subsequently restored to its exact pre-incident
state (0 item-state diffs, 0 extra/missing comments) from the full worklog
snapshot `588ff39` + delta `e7357f3`.

## Root causes

1. `releaseScriptForwardArgs()` strips only documented wrapper-only flags
   (`--skip-checks`, `--refresh-audits`, `--skip-audit-remediation`) and
   forwards everything else — including `--help`/`-h`/unknown flags — to the
   merge script.
2. A merge-script exit `0` is treated as a successful release regardless of
   whether a new tag/merge was produced.
3. Merge verification keys off `git describe` (the newest *reachable* tag),
   which can be an old, already-released tag, so it does not prove *this* run
   produced a release.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `run-release.js --help` and `run-release.js -h` print wrapper usage and exit
   without invoking any gate, merge script, `wl`, git-mutation, Discord
   notification, or close command.
2. An unrecognised flag causes a non-zero exit with usage text; unknown flags
   are never silently forwarded to the merge script.
3. Post-release steps (Discord notification, `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`) run
   only when the released version tag was **newly created by this run** (did
   not exist before the run) and its commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`.
4. Regression test: with `--help` and with a bogus flag, asserts zero side
   effects (no `wl close`, no `sendReleaseNotification`, no merge subprocess).
5. A merge-script invocation that exits `0` without producing a new tag is
   detected and does not run post-release steps.

## Evidence

- Incident window comments: 2026-10-09T07:36:05–07:36:10Z, author `worklog`
  (`Closed with reason: Shipped in v0.1.18`) and author `ship` (cascade).
- Pre-incident snapshot ref: `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`
  full `588ff39` + delta `e7357f3` (2026-10-09T07:34Z).
- `origin/main` stayed at `eebde87`; no `release/*` branch or new tag created.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken merge verification; the fix must be strictly more
  conservative.
- Preserve the existing documented flag set and behaviour for the normal
  no-arg release path.
data.title: ship: run-release.js --help runs post-release steps and closes items against a stale tag

# GitHub Pages Deploy Fails — Playwright Browsers Missing in CI

## Problem

The `Deploy to GitHub Pages` workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) failed at the `npm test` step. `storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` uses Playwright's `chromium.launch()` but the CI runner did not have the Playwright Chromium binary installed.

**Symptom:** Live GitHub Pages site was not updated to v0.1.19.

## Root Cause

- `storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` is in the `unit` vitest project (not `browser`).
- It imports `renderMermaidBatch`, which calls `chromium.launch()` — the Playwright Chromium binary is required.
- `deploy.yml` did not run `npx playwright install chromium` before `npm test`.
- The Pages workflow triggers only on push to `main`, so the ship skill's PR status-check lookup found nothing.

## Fix

Added an `Install Playwright browsers` step (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) between `npm ci` and `npm test` in `deploy.yml`, plus a config-contract regression test.

## Evidence

- CI run: 37913849651 — Test step failed with `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist`
- 5283/5284 tests passed; only this one test was affected.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The GitHub Pages deploy workflow installs Playwright Chromium before the test gate, so `storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` can launch Chromium in CI.
2. A regression test in `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` pins the Playwright install step, the `chromium` target, and its ordering before the `Test` step (fails without the fix).
3. The full unit suite (`npm test`) passes in the worktree.
data.title: GitHub Pages deploy fails — Playwright browsers missing in CI

# Turn log no longer displays

**Regression:** the in-game **Activity Log** panel ("turn log") no longer displays its
entries.

## Problem statement

Players can no longer see the Activity Log panel content, so they lose the running
record of each turn's income, incidents and actions. This is a regression on `dev`
(v0.1.19) and is filed as `critical`.

## Users

- **Main Street players (single-player)** — need the per-turn record to understand
  what happened each turn.
- **Tutorial players** — rely on the log feedback while learning the loop.
- **Competitive players** — need the per-seat action transcript.

Example user stories:

- As a single-player, I want the Activity Log to show each turn's entries as they
  happen, so that I can follow the state of the game.
- As a tutorial player, I want the log to remain visible while the tutorial runs, so
  that I can connect tutorial actions to their outcomes.
- As a competitive player, I want the log to show both seats' actions, so that I can
  follow an AI-vs-AI or mixed match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Activity Log panel renders its entries when the scene loads and updates after each turn completes, in **single-player, tutorial and competitive** modes.
- A new automated test reproduces the blank-log failure on the pre-fix revision and passes after the fix (browser test preferred; supplement with unit coverage where the timing contract is involved). The introducing commit is identified (e.g. via `git bisect` or commit-diff inspection) and the fix restores the pre-regression behaviour without changing documented log content or order.
- The two currently-failing tests in `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` (deferral window) pass; their assertion helper must read Phaser `Text.text` correctly (it currently reads `c.text?.text`, which is always `undefined`).
- The deferred-rendering contract is preserved: entries accumulated during end-of-turn closing still appear **after** the upcoming/phase UI, never before it (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2).
- Log scrolling/auto-scroll behaviour is unchanged (auto-scroll to newest, no yank when the player has scrolled up).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (unit plus the browser project, run explicitly).

## Constraints

- Must not break the deferred log-render ordering contract (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2).
- Keep positioning SLL-driven (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`); no hard-coded
  pixel coordinates.
- The Phaser/browser context is shared and sensitive: browser tests run serially.
- CI (`npm test`) runs **only** the `unit` Vitest project; `*.browser.test.ts` files
  are excluded. Any browser-level regression coverage must be run explicitly via
  `npx vitest run --project browser` and should be noted as such.

## Existing state

- The Activity Log panel is created once in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (title text `Activity Log`).
- Content is rendered by `refreshLog` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, which
  is called from `refreshAll`.
- Deferred rendering is gated by `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, set/cleared in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`
  (`finishTurnPresentation` / `finalizeTurn` → `flushDeferredLog`).
- Log panel state is reset on scene restart in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`.
- On `dev` HEAD (`b3a9941`):
  - `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` (42 tests) and
    `tests/main-street/activity-log-deferred-rendering.test.ts` (6 tests) **pass**.
  - `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts`
    → **2 failed | 15 passed** (re-confirmed by the intake session). The failing cases
    are the deferral-window tests ("suppresses new entry rendering while
    `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete` is set" and "keeps accumulated entries in order
    when rendered after the deferral window"); the failures are caused by the
    assertion helper reading `c.text?.text` (always `undefined` for a Phaser `Text`,
    whose rendered string is the `.text` property itself), which means this browser
    coverage never actually verified the rendered text.
  - Note: `npm test` runs only the `unit` project, so these browser failures do not
    appear in the default suite.

## Desired change

Restore the Activity Log display and make the regression detectable:

1. Identify and fix the root cause of the blank/missing log (prime suspects: the
   deferred-rendering gate never being lifted on some path, or a recent boot/turn-flow
   change on `dev`).
2. Correct the deferral-window browser test helper so it reads the rendered text
   correctly, and add explicit coverage that the log is non-empty on scene load and
   after a turn in each mode.
3. Keep deferral ordering and scroll behaviour intact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshLog` deferral gate, entry rendering
  and scroll bounds; likely fix site.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — sets/clears
  `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`; verify every path flushes.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — log state fields (`logPrevEntryCount`,
  `logAutoScroll`, `logScrollOffset`, …) and `refreshLog` wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Activity Log panel creation.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — log state reset on restart.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` — fix helper; add
  blank-log regression test.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-deferred-rendering.test.ts` — deferral timing
  coverage (unit).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed by producer):** "turn log" means the in-game Activity Log
  panel — the only in-game log that lists per-turn entries. The panel and its title
  bar are visible, but the content area is empty and never fills.
- **Risk:** the symptom may only reproduce in the packaged Electron build or a
  specific mode; confirm repro before assuming the fix site.
- **Risk:** fixing the stale browser assertions may reveal the deferral gate really is
  left set on a path not covered by the unit suite.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a log UI redesign is out of scope; record extra ideas as
  linked work items.
- **Risk:** CI does not run browser tests, so a browser-only regression can recur;
  note explicit browser-run expectation in the fix.

## Related work

### Directly related (context / possible cause)

- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** – Activity Log should not show log line until the results
  have been shown in the UI (completed). Introduced the `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`
  gate and the deferral-window browser tests.
- **MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P** – fire banking hint during the tutorial (gate flip + dead-end
  fix) (most recent functional commit on `dev`; touched the turn flow).
- **MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H** – Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring (changed renderer
  and boot).
- **MS-0MV031AYI007UZ7X** – boot/New Game selector ordering
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`).
- **MS-0MV0319OC002H15F** – Reorder tutorial-offer boot flow.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04** – Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (open)
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed)
- **MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2** – Pedestrians seek the nearest occupied cell (including mid-turn fills) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actually, add (+248 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actually, add (+211 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: action, actions, activity, actually, add (+173 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which surface is "the turn log"? Options: (A) whole panel missing; (B)
  panel/title show but content empty/never updates; (C) turn-specific rows
  missing; (D) other.
  — Answer (operator): **B** — the panel and title show, but the content area is
  empty and never updates. Source: interactive reply (intake session
  `herdr-1791559913-2763730-24821`).
- Q: Where and in which mode is it broken? Options: (A) single-player only; (B)
  competitive only; (C) all modes; (D) not sure.
  — Answer (operator): **C** — all modes. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: What is the visible trigger and when did it last work? Options: (A) broken
  from the first turn / on a fresh game; (B) stops after the first End Turn; (C)
  only after loading a save; (D) only under tutorial / reduced-motion; (E) not
  sure.
  — Answer (operator): **A** — broken from the very first turn / on a fresh
  game; described as a "very recent break". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Does the blank log reproduce in the automated suite? — Research (intake
  session, `dev` HEAD `b3a9941`): `npm test` (unit project) **passes**; the
  explicit browser run
  `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts`
  → **2 failed | 15 passed**, but both failures stem from the stale assertion
  helper (`c.text?.text`), so the suite neither proves nor disproves the
  producer-reported blank log. Source: local run; see "Existing state".

> **Prior-session note:** an earlier intake run (`herdr-1791560667-2819121-4932`)
> drafted this brief but left the three questions above as OPEN QUESTIONs and set
> `needsProducerReview=true`. The producer has now answered them; this appendix
> supersedes those OPEN QUESTIONs.

### Plan session (herdr-1791566842-3344279-31129)

- Q: Are new clarifying questions needed to decompose this work item?
  — Answer (plan, agent): **No.** The intake Appendix answers (surface = panel/
  title visible with empty content; scope = all modes; trigger = broken from the
  first turn on a fresh game) already scope the plan, so no new producer questions
  were raised. Source: intake Appendix above; agent reasoning.
- Q: Is a producer plan-approval gate required?
  — Answer (plan, agent): **No.** The effort/risk pre-check returned
  `decision: "plan"` (effort Small, risk High) and the approval gate returned
  `request_approval: false` — approval is only requested for Extra Large effort
  **and** High/Severe risk. Source: `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` and
  `plan-approval-gate`.
- Q: Why is the regression test created before the fix?
  — Answer (plan, agent): the AC requires an automated test that reproduces the
  blank-log failure on the pre-fix revision and the introducing commit to be
  identified; the fix depends on that diagnosis. Source: parent AC2/AC3.

> **Plan-session decision (formatting):** the parent Acceptance Criteria list was
> reformatted from a numbered multi-line list to single-line markdown bullets so
> the shared AC-coverage and audit tooling (which parses `- ` bullets) can verify
> coverage. Wording and intent are unchanged.
>
> **Known gap (OPEN QUESTION for the implementing agent):** an automated browser
> repro of the producer-reported blank log has not yet been demonstrated — the
> browser harness logs `Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method
> is not supported in WebGL`, and the existing browser log test passes. The
> test-first child work item must pin the introducing commit before the fix
> child is started. Directed to: the implementing agent; why it matters: the
> fix must target the true root cause, not the stale assertion helper alone.

# Verification: residential pack content & builder contract

**Summary:** Author the automated verification that the production residential pack source tree, its CSV fragment and the builder output satisfy the pack contract and the balance/catalogue checks.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read the real authored pack tree (`packs/manifest.json`, `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv`) — not fixtures.
- Drive the real core builder (`core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs`) and the real merge seam (`mergeCardPackCsv`).

# Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

- Cover both unit (Node/Vitest) and browser (Chromium) layers; browser files run under the `browser` Vitest project.

- A unit suite materialises the production pack into a temp `<contentDir>/packs/` and asserts the gate is **locked** when no `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock exists, and that the pack's card ids are absent from the merged pool and live templates.

# Content-unlock pack entitlement gate

**Summary:** Compose Main Street's pack entitlement resolution so a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock in the launcher's unified content-unlock store entitles the pack **in addition to** the existing Steam-DLC status, while an unowned pack stays locked and out of play.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read side only: compose the content-unlock client into the `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam used by `loadMainStreetCardPacks`.
- Do not change the core loader's default behaviour or other games' entitlement.
- Reuse the core `content-unlock-client` (`contentUnlockClientFromWindow`) and, where useful, the pure `DlcGate`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `loadMainStreetCardPacks` composes an entitlement resolver that reports a pack **unlocked** when a `dlc:<gameId>:<packId>` content unlock exists, in addition to the existing Steam-DLC status.
- With no content unlock the residential pack resolves **locked** with an actionable reason and its rows stay out of the merged pool; with the unlock it resolves **unlocked** and its rows merge.
- Only packs declared as content-unlock gated are affected; entitlement for every other pack and game is unchanged.
- The composition is total (never throws): a missing, throwing or malformed content-unlock bridge degrades to the Steam status / base content.
- The gating declaration is data-driven (a pack/manifest or game-config declaration), not a hard-coded pack title in logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add an optional `contentUnlocks` client (defaulting to `contentUnlockClientFromWindow()`) and a composed `resolveEntitlement` in `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` (or a new focused `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` module).
- Determine which pack ids are content-unlock gated from an explicit declaration (proposed: an additive `entitlement` marker surfaced on `CardPackStatusRef`; record the final shape as an assumption if it differs).
- Extend `tests/main-street/MainStreetCardPacks.test.ts` seam coverage in the pipeline verification child.

# Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher

**Summary:** Add a config-driven, rule-scoped simulated purchase to the core launcher's unified content-unlock mechanism so a dev/QA affordance can unlock the residential pack's DLC target without collateral-unlocking other rewards (notably the itch.io golf reward).

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Write path (main process + renderer read client) in the `./core` submodule; commit there and bump the submodule pointer in this work item.
- Keep the change additive and config-driven (no hard-coded game/DLC names in logic).
- Must not weaken the existing `steam-follow` self-attest path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` gains a config rule whose target is `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack`, triggered by a dev/QA `(platform, action)` pair resolved to a simulated-purchase verifier.
- `ActionRewardService.refresh` accepts an additive rule-scope filter and an explicit simulated-purchase signal, forwarded to `ActionVerificationRequest`; a scoped refresh evaluates only the named rule(s) and never self-attests unrelated rules.
- A `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier` (or equivalent) verifies **only** when a simulated purchase is explicitly requested, so a global `refresh({ attested: true })` cannot unlock the residential pack.
- The `contentUnlocks:refresh` IPC handler and preload bridge carry the scoped request, and the renderer `ContentUnlockClient` exposes a typed `refresh` call (the existing `isUnlocked`/`getUnlocks` API is unchanged).
- Tests prove a scoped residential purchase unlocks the residential DLC and does **not** unlock the configured `itchio-follow` golf reward, and that global attestation does not unlock the residential pack.
- The core change is committed to `./core` and the submodule bumped in the same work item; both commit hashes are recorded.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `ActionRewardRefreshOptions` (`ruleIds?`, `simulatePurchase?`) and `ActionVerificationRequest` (`simulatePurchase?`) in `core/electron/action-rewards.ts` / `action-verifiers.ts`.
- Add `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier` (id `simulated-purchase`) and register it in `initContentUnlocks` (`core/electron/main.ts`) with the config's verifier mapping.
- Normalise `ruleIds`/`simulatePurchase` in `core/electron/action-rewards-ipc.ts`; pass through `core/electron/preload.cjs`; add `refresh()` to `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`.
- Add the rule + `verifiers.actions` entry to `core/electron/action-rewards.json` (validated against `core/electron/bonus-catalog.json`, where `main-street` is already registered).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` — New residential-pack purchase rule + verifier mapping.
- `core/electron/action-rewards.ts` — Rule-scope filter + simulated-purchase signal.
- `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts` — `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier`.
- `core/electron/action-rewards-ipc.ts`, `core/electron/preload.cjs` — Scoped refresh transport.
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts` — Typed `refresh`.
- `core/electron/main.ts` — Register the verifier.
- `core/tests/electron/**` — New/extended unit coverage.

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline**.
- Blocks **Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance** (the affordance calls the scoped purchase).

## Deliverables

- Committed core change + submodule bump, with scoping proven by tests.

# Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance

**Summary:** Add a dev/QA affordance in the in-game Card Packs panel that performs the scoped simulated purchase for the residential pack, refreshes the pack pool, and lets the player enable the newly unlocked pack.

# Add Activity Log regression test and pin introducing commit

**Test-first tracer bullet** for the Activity Log regression
(MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6).

## Problem statement

The browser assertion helper in
`tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` reads
`c.text?.text`, but a Phaser `Text` game object stores its rendered string in
`.text` directly, so the expression is always `undefined`. The two
deferral-window tests therefore never actually verified the rendered text.
We need a browser test that genuinely reproduces the blank Activity Log and
fails on the pre-fix revision, plus the introducing commit identified so the
fix targets the true root cause.

## Acceptance Criteria
