# Intake Brief — `unit-cli` project is silently skipped by `npm test`

## Problem statement

`npm test` (the retry runner invoking `vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli`)
regularly executes only the `unit` project: none of the five serialized CLI files in
`CLI_TEST_FILES` are collected, no `|unit-cli|` lines are reported, and the run is still
green. The Playwright-driven `storyline-graph-svg` render/doc-drift guard and the four
storyline/harness CLI suites therefore run in some full-suite runs and not in others, so a
green gate does not mean everything ran.

## Users

- **Implementer / agent** running the changed-scope or full-suite gate before committing —
  needs "green" to mean "every non-browser test file ran".
- **Reviewer / auditor** reading a cached gate result (`.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt`) —
  needs the run's coverage to be reproducible for a given commit.
- **Release engineer** promoting `dev` → `main` — needs the gate evidence to be trustworthy.

### User stories

- As an implementer, when the gate reports green I want evidence that every configured
  project contributed its files, so a CLI-test regression cannot slip through unnoticed.
- As an auditor, I want a green cached run to be reproducible — the same commit must not
  sometimes exercise 375 files and sometimes 380.

## Evidence (verified during intake, 2026-10-23)

- `HEAD` = `582ab9e5` holds **380** non-browser `*.test.ts` files; `CLI_TEST_FILES` in
  `vite.config.ts` holds **5**.
- The most recent cached full run (`5cb02674`, 2026-10-23 11:09Z, exit 0) reports
  `Test Files 375 passed (375)` and contains **zero** occurrences of any of the five CLI
  file names — exactly the 5 CLI files are missing and `unit-cli` contributed nothing.
  Same shape in `6edb5947` (371), `6773e550` (370), `abb42afc` (365), `091fb66e` (373).
- **Arg forwarding is not the cause.** The runner's own diagnostic in a skipping run reads
  `[vitest-runner] attempts=2 status=0 outcome=accepted-transient args="--project unit --project unit-cli"`;
  both retry attempts skipped the project identically, so it is not a transient-teardown
  artefact and not a lost flag.
- **Not a persistent config regression.** The identical main checkout ran `unit-cli`
  successfully at 2026-10-22 16:49Z (`7b5c9894`, five `|unit-cli|` lines) between two runs
  that did not (21:10Z `6edb5947`, 21:53Z `6773e550`). Every run reports
  `RUN v3.2.7 /home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`.
- **Block structure suggests state, not source:** every run up to 2026-10-18 01:21Z shows
  `|unit-cli|`; runs from 2026-10-19 21:21Z on mostly do not — yet no commit touched
  `vite.config.ts` or `package.json` between `a2a25864` (2026-10-18 01:17Z) and
  `866294b5` (2026-10-20 01:02Z).
- The existing guard `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` asserts the
  **declared** config shape (project names, `include`/`exclude`, serialization flags) but
  not the **run-time project selection**, which is precisely why it stays green while the
  project is skipped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Root cause identified and fixed at the cause — the work item records which hypothesis
   (H1 zero-file collection, H2 project filtered out, H3 stale environment state, or another)
   was confirmed, with the evidence that confirmed it; if the cause proves to be a Vitest
   defect, it is documented in the item as an upstream issue rather than papered over.
2. `npm test` deterministically executes all five `CLI_TEST_FILES` in a **single** Vitest
   invocation (both `--project` flags retained — no additional invocation stage): proof is a
   full-suite run containing `|unit-cli|` lines for every one of them (or an equivalent
   machine-checkable record, e.g. JSON-reporter entries with `projectName: unit-cli`), and the
   item records the measured before/after suite duration showing no meaningful increase.
3. A run in which a configured project contributes **zero** test files fails loudly instead
   of reporting green, naming the empty project and its expected files.
4. A regression test pins the run-time selection for the `npm test` argument set: `unit` and
   `unit-cli` are both resolved, every non-browser `tests/**/*.test.ts` file is claimed by
   exactly one project, and the five CLI files are claimed only by `unit-cli` (fast static
   check that runs in the `unit` project).
5. `docs/dev/testing.md` documents the deterministic invocation, the zero-file guard and the
   intermittent-skip symptom, including what a green full-suite run must contain.
6. Full project test suite passes with the changes (`/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- **Fix the quirk, do not route around it** (producer decision, 2026-10-23): keep the single
  `vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli` invocation and repair the project-selection
  behaviour at its cause. Adding a second invocation stage is acceptable only if the root
  cause proves unfixable — and the resulting wall-clock cost must then be measured and
  reported back to the producer.
- **Preserve MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG isolation.** The five CLI files must not return to the
  parallel `unit` pool; they flake under file-level parallelism (spurious
  `expected 1 to be +0`).
- **Repository boundary.** `core/` is the engine submodule: `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`
  and `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` belong to the engine repo. Prefer a fix that
  lives in this repo (`package.json` script, `vite.config.ts`, a local wrapper, tests).
  If an engine-side change proves necessary, **raise it as a separate item in
  `../ContextHub`** (producer instruction, 2026-10-23) rather than bundling it here; an
  engine change also needs its own `engine:sync`/pin discipline. Note for the implementer:
  `./core` resolves to `../Tableau-Card-Engine`, while `../ContextHub` is the Worklog (`wl`)
  tooling repo — confirm the target repository at that point if the distinction matters.
- **`vite.config.ts` is auto-generated** from `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, and that
  template does **not** carry `CLI_TEST_FILES`/`unit-cli`. Keep local edits surgical and
  documented so a future re-scaffold does not silently drop them (precedent:
  MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY applied a surgical sync for the same reason).
- Keep `vitest-run-with-retry.ts` semantics intact: retry-once on transient contention
  signatures, never retry a hang, never mask a genuine failure.
- Do not weaken the masking guard in order to make the gate green.

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `test` and `test:unit` both run
  `tsx core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --timeout-ms 720000 --project unit --project unit-cli`.
- `vite.config.ts` declares three projects: `unit` (parallel, `maxWorkers: 4`,
  `exclude: ['tests/**/*.browser.test.ts', ...CLI_TEST_FILES]`), `unit-cli`
  (`include: CLI_TEST_FILES`, `fileParallelism: false`,
  `sequence: { concurrent: false, groupOrder: 1 }`, 180 s timeout) and `browser`.
- Vitest 3.2.7. In this version a project is dropped silently in exactly two places: it
  throws `VitestFilteredOutProjectError` when no potential project name matches the
  `--project` filter, and it is kept but contributes no specs when its `include` matches
  nothing — neither produces a failure on its own.
- Two guards exist: `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` (config shape)
  and `tests/main-street/testing-docs-projects.test.ts` (docs/config drift).

## Desired change

**Route (producer decision, 2026-10-23): diagnose and fix the quirk itself.** Keep the single
`vitest run --project unit --project unit-cli` invocation; do not add a second invocation
stage unless the root cause proves unfixable, and if it does, measure and report the added
wall-clock cost.

Diagnose, in this order (cheapest discriminating evidence first):

- **H1 — zero-file collection.** The `unit-cli` project initialises but its `include` matches
  nothing (root / `include` resolution inside an `extends: true` project), and Vitest reports
  green for a project that contributed no files.
- **H2 — project filtered out.** `VitestFilteredOutProjectError` drops the project because
  the effective `--project` name filter does not match the declared name
  (`matchesProjectFilter` consults `config.project || cliOptions.project`).
- **H3 — stale environment state.** A cached Vite/Vitest config or dependency artefact (or
  `core` submodule state, which several tests mutate via `engine:sync`) makes project
  resolution vary between runs of the same commit.

First diagnostic step (agent-initiated runs must go through `/skill:test`): capture one
full-suite run with `--reporter=json` and diff the project names present against the three
projects declared in `vite.config.ts`; `vitest list --project unit --project unit-cli` from a
clean `node_modules/.vite` state is the follow-up probe. Record which of H1–H3 the evidence
supports in the work item before changing code.

Then fix at the cause. Candidate remedies, to be chosen by the evidence:

- explicit `root` on the `unit-cli` project (removes dependence on inherited root
  resolution), or a project definition that does not rely on `extends: true` inheriting the
  root `test` block;
- an unambiguous project-name filter (e.g. non-overlapping names, or a documented
  `--project` form) if the filter matching is the culprit;
- clearing/defeating the stale cache path if H3 is confirmed (and documenting the cache
  invalidation requirement in `docs/dev/testing.md`).

Regardless of the remedy, land AC3 (loud zero-file failure) and AC4 (run-time selection +
full file-coverage guard) so a future silent skip fails the gate instead of passing it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — `test` / `test:unit` scripts; possibly split into per-project invocations
- `vite.config.ts` — `CLI_TEST_FILES` and the `unit` / `unit-cli` project definitions
- `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` — extend the contract with
  run-time selection and full file-coverage assertions
- `tests/tooling/` (new file, optional) — zero-file / coverage guard if not folded into the
  existing contract test
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — deterministic invocation, guard, and symptom documentation
- `scripts/` (only if a guard needs orchestration outside the Vitest suite)
- `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`, `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — engine
  repo; read-only here — any change is raised as a separate item in `../ContextHub`
  (producer instruction, 2026-10-23)

## Verification commands

```bash
# full suite (always via the test skill; never ad-hoc)
/skill:test

# change-scope run of only the CLI project (agent-initiated runs go through /skill:test)
npx vitest run --project unit-cli          # all five CLI files must be listed

# proof that a cached full run covered the CLI project
grep -c '|unit-cli|' .worklog/cache/<hash>/stdout.txt   # must be >= 5

# arithmetic check: non-browser test files vs reported file count
find tests -name '*.test.ts' | grep -v browser | wc -l

# wall-clock before/after: compare the `Duration` line of the cached full-suite runs
grep -h '^ *Duration' .worklog/cache/<before>/stdout.txt .worklog/cache/<after>/stdout.txt
```

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the skip may not reproduce on demand, making "verify with a green run" weak
  evidence. Mitigation: the static coverage guard (AC3) and loud zero-file failure (AC2)
  do not depend on reproducing the quirk.
- **Risk:** two Vitest invocations add one extra collect/setup phase (~15–20 s) to a
  ~180–190 s suite. Accepted.
- **Risk:** the chosen route (fix the quirk) gives no structural guarantee, so the guard
  tests (AC3/AC4) are the real safety net; they must land even if the quirk is fixed.
- **Risk:** scope creep into diagnosing an upstream Vitest bug. Record any upstream defect
  as a separate item (`../ContextHub` per producer instruction) rather than expanding this fix.
- **Risk:** the fix silently increases suite wall-clock. Measure the full-suite duration
  before and after and record both in the item; report any increase to the producer.
- **Risk:** a re-scaffold of `vite.config.ts` drops the local `unit-cli` project. Mitigation:
  keep the documented surgical-sync note; the contract test fails loudly if it happens.
- **Assumption:** "green" means every non-browser test file ran; the 375-vs-380 arithmetic
  in the cached runs is accepted as proof of the skip.
- **Assumption:** the retry runner forwards `--project` flags correctly — verified from its
  own `[vitest-runner] ... args=` diagnostic.
- **Assumption:** the five `CLI_TEST_FILES` are the correct set (pinned by the existing
  contract test); this item does not re-scope which files are contention-prone.

---

**Headline:** `npm test` intermittently runs only the `unit` project, silently skipping the
serialized `unit-cli` project (five CLI files, including the Playwright storyline-graph SVG
guard) while still reporting green; the fix must make full-suite coverage deterministic and
make an empty configured project fail loudly.

## Related work

- **MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG** — *[test-failure] Main Street vite-node CLI tests flake under vitest file-level parallelism* (completed): created the `unit-cli` project and `CLI_TEST_FILES`. This item is the follow-up defect: the isolation project is sometimes not executed at all.
- **MS-0MVJPV0BV000LSLW** — *[test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test* (completed): moved `card-diagrams.test.ts` into the serialized project and extended the isolation contract test; its session is where the silent skip was first observed.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** — *Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs* (completed): documents that the scaffold template lacks this repo's local `unit-cli`/`CLI_TEST_FILES` additions, as a surgical integration step.
- **MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6** — phaser/tone dedupe (completed): a sibling cause of whole-suite collection failures; relevant because a collection error can mask project-selection behaviour.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` (project table, `unit-cli` serialization rationale), `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/testing-docs-projects.test.ts`, `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (retry/masking guard), `core/docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` (engine-side suite review guidance).

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG** – [test-failure] Main Street vite-node CLI tests flake under vitest file-level parallelism (completed)
- **MS-0MVFQ5ODR001R7U2** – [test-failure] tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts > AC1 — Deterministic head-to-head execution > should run ≥200 seeds in the batch harness — failing test (completed)
- **MS-0MV16VZWP001OUNR** – Full-suite verification & release readiness (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ac4, acceptable, acceptance, accepted, add (+449 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, accepted, add, added, adding (+326 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac2, ac3, ac4, accepted, add (+288 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Should the fix diagnose the multi-`--project` selection quirk itself, or stop relying
  on it (one Vitest invocation per project)?**
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-23, interactive reply): "fix the quirk."** The single
  `--project unit --project unit-cli` invocation stays; the cause is repaired. Source:
  producer reply to the intake report. Superseded answer: the agent's recommendation was to
  stop relying on multi-project selection; the producer's answer takes precedence.
- **Q: If the root cause turns out to be inside `core/` (engine submodule), should that change
  be bundled here or raised as a separate item?**
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-23, interactive reply): "raise issue in `../ContextHub`."**
  Recorded as: engine-side/framework-side work is raised as a separate item in
  `../ContextHub`, not bundled in this repo. Note for the implementer: `./core` resolves to
  `../Tableau-Card-Engine` while `../ContextHub` is the Worklog tooling repo — confirm the
  target repository if the distinction matters. Source: producer reply.
- **Q: Is an extra ~15–20 s of collect/setup time in the full suite acceptable in exchange
  for determinism?**
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-23, interactive reply): "try not to increase time, but if you
  have to OK - be sure to tell me the results."** Recorded as a constraint: keep the
  single-invocation path; if any wall-clock increase proves unavoidable, measure it (cached
  `Duration` lines before/after) and report the numbers back to the producer. Source:
  producer reply.
- **Q: Which files are the correct `CLI_TEST_FILES` set?** — Answered during intake from the
  repo: the five files pinned by `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` and
  `vite.config.ts`. Evidence: `vite.config.ts` `CLI_TEST_FILES`; MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG.
- **Q: Is the retry runner dropping the `--project` flags?** — Answered during intake from the
  repo/cache: no. The runner's own diagnostic in a skipping run prints
  `args="--project unit --project unit-cli"`. Evidence: `.worklog/cache/5cb02674*/stderr.txt`.
- **Q: Is this a persistent regression from a config edit?** — Answered during intake from the
  repo/cache: no. The same checkout ran `unit-cli` at 2026-10-22 16:49Z between two runs that
  did not, and no relevant commit landed between 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-20. Evidence:
  `.worklog/cache/{7b5c9894,6edb5947,6773e550}`, `git log`.

# Reproduce hand-drag failure and capture evidence

**Parent:** MS-0MVJN9UDS005312W — *Allow drag and drop from the hand* (bug).
Covers parent **AC1** (reproduction captured on `dev`) and **AC2** (root cause
identified with evidence). Investigation-first: no fix lands until this item
names the failing code path.

## Goal

Turn the producer's symptom — "businesses, and possibly other cards, cannot be
dragged and dropped from the hand to the play area", seen on a **local dev
server**, tutorial off, actions remaining, in **Edge** — into an evidenced root
cause, so the fix and its regression test target the real path.

## Why this is separate from the fix

The existing hand-drag tests (`tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-drag-drop.browser.test.ts`,
`tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hand-drag-drop.test.ts`)
drag shortly after boot and pass, so the defect lives in a path they do not
cover. The prime suspect is the refresh cycle: `refreshMarket()` calls
`renderer.unregisterDragDraggables()`, which unregisters **every** tracked
draggable (market *and* hand) and clears `renderer.dragDropRegistered`; only the
later `refreshPlayerHand()` re-registers hand cards, so the invariant depends on
render ordering. Confirm or refute that, with evidence, before coding a fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Served checkout recorded.** A comment records
   `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` + `git rev-parse --short HEAD` of the
   checkout under test, plus the browser used, the tutorial state (skipped/off)
   and the actions remaining at the time of the drag attempt.
2. **Drag attempts recorded per family.** A comment records the result of a
   hand→street drag for a **business**, a **community-space** and an
   **upgrade** card, each attempted (a) immediately at turn start and (b) after
   an action that triggers a scene refresh (buy from market, sell, place, end
   turn) — naming which action was used for (b).
3. **Registration evidence captured at the failed drag.** For a failing drag,
   the comment records the observable drag state *at that moment*:
   membership of the hand card container in `renderer.dragDropRegistered`, the
   container's `input` presence and `input.draggable` flag, and the number of
   drop zones registered by the drag manager. Evidence comes from a dev-console
   probe or an equivalent scene-level probe, never from a source grep.
4. **Root cause attributed.** The failure is attributed to one specific path —
   drag registration, refresh ordering, pointer hit-test, or browser input —
   with the evidence from AC3 (or equivalent) supporting the attribution, and
   the attribution names the concrete file/function responsible.
5. **Contingency recorded.** If the served checkout predates `a447c0b7` (the
   hand-drag commit), the commit hashes proving that are recorded instead, and
   this item closes as a verification close-out; the parent is then re-scoped
   to a publish/ship action rather than a fix.
6. **No repository churn.** Repro diagnostics are console snippets, a throwaway
   script outside the repo, or a `docs/dev`-free comment — no production code
   changes and no test changes land in this item (they belong to the regression
   tests item).
7. **Findings handed forward.** A final comment states, in one or two
   sentences, the invariant that the fix must hold (e.g. "hand draggables must
   be registered after every refresh path") so the test and fix items can start
   without re-investigating.

## Method (suggested)

1. Boot the dev server from the current `dev` tree and reproduce with the
   tutorial skipped.
2. Probe before and after a refresh-triggering action:
   `msRenderer.dragDropRegistered`, the hand card container's
   `input.draggable`, and the manager's drop-zone count.
3. Compare the drag at turn start (expected: works) with the drag after the
   action (suspected: registration lost).
4. If headless Chromium cannot reproduce, record that explicitly and escalate
   to the producer for the Edge capture — do not guess (parent risk R5).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — `unregisterDragDraggables` scope (registry: market-only vs all)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — the `unregisterDragDraggables()` call at the top of `refreshMarket`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshAll` / `refreshAllExceptStreet` ordering
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — `refreshPlayerHand` (the re-registration point)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — partial `refreshPlayerHand()` call site
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — per-family `registerDraggable` calls and click-vs-drag handling

## Out of scope

- Applying a fix (the fix item follows this one).
- Adding regression tests (the regression-tests item follows this one).
- Any change to the core `@ui/dragDrop` manager — if the evidence proves the
  manager at fault, record it and raise a separate item (parent risk R3).

# Add regression tests for post-refresh hand drags

**Parent:** MS-0MVJN9UDS005312W — *Allow drag and drop from the hand* (bug).
Covers parent **AC5** (event cards stay click-only, pinned), **AC6**
(regression tests) and the test-first half of **AC8** (the new tests fail
against the unfixed code).

## Goal

Pin the hand-drag behaviour with tests that fail on today's `dev` and pass once
the fix lands. Test-first: these tests are written and shown red **before** the
fix item (MS-0MVK4E5M00021XEY) starts, so the defect cannot silently return.

**Findings from the repro item (MS-0MVK4E4KU002KU23) — AC scope updated
2026-10-23:** the refresh-cycle itself is **refuted** as the defect. On served
`dev` (`582ab9e5`) hand cards stay registered and drag successfully after every
refresh path (buy-from-market, Research-the-market, `refreshAll`). The real
defect is the **click-select then drag** path: clicking a hand card sets
`uiPhase='placing-from-hand'` (`MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:944/788`),
and `canPickUpHandCard` (`MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts:242`) vetoes any
pickup while `uiPhase !== 'market'`; the drag manager then silently discards the
drop. So the regression centrepiece is the **post-click-select drag** (drag a
hand card after click-selecting it — business, community-space and upgrade),
plus the post-refresh drags, plus the registration-invariant unit test (which
also catches the debug cheat-overlay `refreshMarket()`-only path that would
clear hand registrations).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Browser test: business card after click-select.** A browser test boots the
   scene with the tutorial skipped, performs an action that triggers a refresh
   cycle (buy from market, sell, place, or end turn — or the equivalent direct
   refresh path), then **click-selects** a business/community-space card in the
   hand and drags it onto a legal empty street slot, asserting the placement
   resolves through the existing undoable command with the expected action and
   coin spend. The click-select-then-drag sequence is the path that reproduces
   the defect (centre of AC8).
2. **Browser test: upgrade card after click-select.** The same post-refresh
   click-select-then-drag is covered for a hand-held **upgrade** onto an
   eligible street business, asserting the upgrade is applied through the
   existing undoable from-hand command.
3. **Refresh paths covered.** The tests exercise a full refresh (`refreshAll`)
   and the partial refresh paths named by the findings item, and at minimum
   assert that hand cards remain draggable after `refreshMarket()` +
   `refreshPlayerHand()` have run in sequence; the debug `refreshMarket()`-only
   partial path is asserted by the registration-invariant test (AC6) — it must
   not leave hand cards unregistered.
4. **Click-vs-drag coexistence pinned.** A pure click (below the drag
   threshold) on a hand business and on a hand upgrade still reaches
   `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick` after a refresh, so the
   fix cannot trade drag for click.
5. **Event cards stay click-only.** A test asserts hand-held event cards are
   **not** registered as draggables (no drag starts on a drag gesture) and keep
   the select-then-act `[Play]` / `[Discard]` flow.
6. **Unit-level registration invariant.** A unit test (not a browser boot)
   asserts the invariant directly: after each refresh path, every hand card
   container in the hand is registered with the drag-drop manager, and the
   registry holds no stale/destroyed containers.
7. **Tests genuinely reproduce the defect (AC8).** The evidence that the new
   tests fail against the unfixed code is recorded on this item — the failing
   assertion output, captured via the test skill before the fix lands — and
   then they pass after the fix. In the committed tree the red-phase cases are
   authored `it.fails` (per the repo's test-first tracer-bullet convention) and
   flipped to plain `it` by the fix item (MS-0MVK4E5M00021XEY) once the pickup
   gate accepts the click-selected drag.
8. **Public-surface assertions only.** All assertions go through the scene's
   public interaction surface and the resulting state (`state.hand`,
   `state.streetGrid`, action/coin budget, `renderer.dragDropRegistered`) —
   never source greps.
9. **Load-sensitivity respected.** Reuse the existing boot helper
   (`@core-tests/helpers/waitForScene`, `dismissBootModals`, the Phaser canvas
   pool) and keep added scene boots to the minimum (parent risk R4,
   MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ).
10. **Changed-scope test gate passes.** All agent-initiated test runs go
    through the test skill.

## Suggested shape

- `tests/main-street/hand-drag-post-refresh.browser.test.ts` — one boot per
  scenario: click-select-then-drag for business / community-space / upgrade
  (AC1, AC2, AC7, AC8), the refresh-path green cases (AC3), the click-vs-drag
  coexistence after refresh (AC4), and the event-card click-only case (AC5).
- `tests/main-street/hand-drag-drop.test.ts` — extend with the pickup-gate
  red-phase cases (a click-selected card must be draggable — AC1/AC2/AC7/AC8),
  the registration-invariant cases (AC6) and the event click-only wiring case
  (AC5), reusing the existing Phaser mock.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/main-street/hand-drag-post-refresh.browser.test.ts` — new post-refresh drag cases
- `tests/main-street/hand-drag-drop.test.ts` — pickup-gate + registration invariant + event click-only cases
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-hand-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` — existing boot/probe patterns to reuse
- `tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts` — existing market-drag patterns to reuse
- `tests/main-street/helpers/bootModals.ts` — shared boot helper
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — registry under test
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — hand `registerDraggable` call sites
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts` — `canPickUpHandCard` pickup gate under test

## Out of scope

- The production fix itself (the fix item MS-0MVK4E5M00021XEY follows this one).
- Rewriting the existing hand-drag tests; extend rather than replace where the
  existing coverage still holds.

# Fix hand-drag registration invariant and update docs

**Parent:** MS-0MVJN9UDS005312W — *Allow drag and drop from the hand* (bug).
Covers parent **AC3** (hand drag works for business, community-space and
upgrade cards, drag-vs-click coexistence preserved), **AC4** (registration
survives every refresh path by construction), **AC7** (docs) and **AC9**
(all related documentation updated).

## Goal

Make the hand-drag registration invariant hold **by construction** — hand cards
are draggable after every refresh path — rather than by the current render
ordering (`refreshMarket` unregisters everything; only the later
`refreshPlayerHand` re-registers hand cards). The fix must be minimal and stay
in the game layer: reuse the existing `@ui/dragDrop` manager, street drop
zones, `dragHighlightRects` pool, `canPickUpHandCard` / `canDropHandCard` and
the undoable from-hand commands. No new engine state or action types.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Hand drag works after every refresh path.** With the tutorial off and at
   least one action remaining, a business, a community-space and an upgrade
   card each drag from the hand to a legal street target and resolve through
   the existing undoable commands (`playBusinessFromHandCommand` /
   `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`) with no action or coins spent on an illegal
   drop.
2. **Invariant by construction, not ordering.** Drag registration survives
   `refreshAll`, `refreshAllExceptStreet` and the mid-turn partial refresh
   paths; a guard (or an explicit re-registration step) makes the invariant
   hold regardless of which sequence of refresh functions is called, and does
   not rely on a single call order.
3. **Market-row drag unchanged.** Market-origin drag behaviour is unchanged,
   including the +50 % buy-and-play premium, which does not apply to
   hand-origin drags.
4. **Click-vs-drag coexistence preserved.** Pure clicks still reach
   `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`; hand-held event cards
   remain unregistered as draggables and keep the select-then-act
   `[Play]` / `[Discard]` flow.
5. **No stale registrations.** The drag registry holds no destroyed/stale
   container references after any refresh path (this is where unregistering in
   `refreshMarket` currently clears hand-origin registrations).
6. **Docs updated (AC7).** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` states the supported
   hand-drag families (business, community-space, upgrade), that event cards
   are click-only, and the refresh/registration invariant is documented in the
   code comment where it is enforced (AC9 also: any affected code comments,
   README entries or wiki/site references updated).
7. **Scope discipline and browser matrix.** No changes to the core
   `@ui/dragDrop` manager unless the reproduction evidence names it as the
   fault (then a separate item is raised); no unrelated refactors; UK
   English in code and comments. Any Edge-only behaviour difference from the
   headless Chromium proxy is called out explicitly in the completion
   comment (parent constraint: browser matrix).
8. **Testing/validation.** The changed-scope test gate passes, including the
   new regression tests (they were red before this fix, green after); the full
   suite is enforced at the dev-push gate.

## Suggested approach

The findings item (repro + evidence) names the exact broken invariant. Likely
shapes, in order of preference: (a) make `unregisterDragDraggables` scoped or
guard hand re-registration inside `refreshMarket`/`refreshAll` itself; (b) an
explicit re-registration step for hand cards at the end of every refresh
sequence; (c) if the partial `refreshPlayerHand()` path (e.g.
`MainStreetInputManager.ts`) rebuilds the hand without unregistering first, fix
that specific path. Whichever shape is chosen must be pinned by the
registration-invariant unit test and the post-refresh browser drag test.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — `unregisterDragDraggables` registry scope
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — the unregister call at the top of `refreshMarket`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshAll` / `refreshAllExceptStreet` sequences
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — `refreshPlayerHand` re-registration point
- `src/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — partial hand refresh call site
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — per-family `registerDraggable` calls
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — supported families + click-only events + invariant note

## Out of scope

- Shipping the fix to `main` (a producer-authorised ship-skill action).
- Making event cards draggable (producer decision: they stay click-only).
- Fixing any core `@ui/dragDrop` defect (own item, if evidence points there).

# Intake brief: Scaffold template must emit `resolve.dedupe` in the generated game-repo `vite.config.ts`

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** medium · **Cross-repo:** yes (`Tableau-Card-Engine` core + this repo) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6

## Problem statement

`./vite.config.ts` in this repo is AUTO-GENERATED by the core scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, whose banner tells maintainers to edit the template rather than the generated file. MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6 fixed a 17-file collection failure by adding `resolve.dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` to the *generated* file, but the template still emits only `alias: resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot)` (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, `renderViteConfig`). The next `npm run scaffold` therefore silently drops the guard and reintroduces the duplicate-Phaser module-identity split, which only the regression test `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` would catch — after the fact.

## Users

- **Maintainers/agents who re-scaffold a game repo** — must be able to run `npm run scaffold` without destroying a hand-applied local fix.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold` to regenerate a `vite.config.ts` that already carries the single-copy guard, so a routine re-scaffold cannot regress the suite."
- **Core template owners** (Tableau-Card-Engine) — must have the guard expressed once, in the template, so every scaffolded game repo starts protected.
  - *User story:* "As a core maintainer, I want `renderViteConfig` to emit the dedupe, so new game repos never hit the 17-file `window is not defined` collection failure."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in game repos must not fail on a fresh scaffold (audit F3 / pre-push gate).

## Existing state

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderViteConfig(game, coreRel)` emits `resolve: { alias: resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot) }` with no `dedupe`.
- `./vite.config.ts` (this repo, generated) carries `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` plus a long explanatory comment (lines ~160–171), added by MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6.
- `core/vite.config.ts` carries the same `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` (core-side rationale: `GAMES_CONFIG=full` distribution builds failed to resolve `phaser` from sibling `src/`, F7 CG-0MUJ168XG006DOGK).
- `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` guards the **checked-in** config and proves the dedupe is load-bearing; it does not guard the template.
- `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts:100` asserts the core repo's own config dedupes `phaser`/`tone`; `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` has `describe('renderViteConfig')` (line 352) and `describe('scaffoldGameRepo')` (line 474, real write into a `mkdtemp` fixture).
- This repo's `scaffold` script runs the template **from the `./core` submodule**: `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core` — so the fix reaches this repo only via the submodule pointer.

## Desired change

`renderViteConfig` emits the dedupe immediately after the alias line, with a concise rationale comment (the generated config keeps only a short form of the long local comment, since a re-scaffold rewrites the whole file). The change is authored in the Tableau-Card-Engine repository under its own `CG-…` work item, tested there, committed there, and the `core` submodule pointer here is then bumped to that commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Template emits the guard.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderViteConfig` emits `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` immediately after the `alias: resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot)` entry inside the generated `resolve` block, with a short comment stating that shared runtime deps must resolve to exactly one copy (`phaser`, `tone`) and that this mirrors `core/vite.config.ts`.
2. **Template-level test (core).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` → `describe('renderViteConfig')` asserts the emitted source contains the dedupe, and asserts the *placement* contract: the dedupe appears inside the same `resolve: { … }` block, after `resolveCoreAliases(coreRoot)` (a guard that survives reformatting rather than a bare `toContain` on the file text).
3. **On-disk scaffold test (core).** A real `scaffoldGameRepo` run over the temp fixture writes a `vite.config.ts` that contains `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` (assert the written file, not only the rendered string).
4. **Cross-repo provenance.** The change is committed in `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` under a `CG-…` work item, with that repository's build and test gates passing; the `CG-…` id and commit hash are recorded as a comment on this item, and the `core` submodule pointer here is bumped to that commit.
5. **End-to-end proof after the bump.** Scaffolding into a scratch fixture using the bumped submodule template produces a `vite.config.ts` containing the dedupe, and this repo's `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` still passes unchanged.
6. **Docs.** `docs/dev/testing.md` §"One Phaser copy: `resolve.dedupe` and the `./core` submodule" states that the guard lives in the scaffold template (so a re-scaffold no longer drops it) and names the core-side test that guards the template.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — in the core repository (where the code change lands) and in this repo after the submodule bump.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Two repositories, two worklogs, two gates.** The edit lands in the `Tableau-Card-Engine` repo (own worklog, own build → test → commit order, own worktree). Do not edit files inside `./core` from this repo's session — only bump the pointer here.
- Only the template + core-side tests + docs change; no behaviour change to this repo's `vite.config.ts` (it already carries the dedupe).
- Do not touch `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or agent-infrastructure directories.
- Keep the dedupe list exactly `['phaser', 'tone']` — no speculative additions (e.g. adding more shared deps is separate scope).
- No CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (process):** the cross-repo pattern approved in MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV (core work item → core commit → submodule bump here) still applies. Evidence: same template function, same two-repo composition, and this repo's `scaffold` script runs `./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`.
- **Assumption (content):** after a re-scaffold the generated `vite.config.ts` replaces the long local rationale comment with the template's shorter one. Behaviour is identical; the long-form explanation in `docs/dev/testing.md` remains the canonical narrative.
- **Risk — silent drift both ways:** the checked-in config and the template can diverge again. Mitigation: the two regression guards (game-repo `phaser-single-copy` test for the config, core scaffold test for the template) plus the docs statement.
- **Risk — submodule bump noise:** bumping `core` may pull in unrelated core commits already on `dev`. Mitigation: bump to the specific commit that carries the template fix and note in the commit message/comment which pointer is landed; if `dev` has moved, land the pointer bump as its own commit.
- **Risk — scope creep:** once the template is open for editing, adjacent "also emit X into the generated config" ideas appear. Record those as separate work items (see `discovered-from` note below), not in this change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (Tableau-Card-Engine repo) — `renderViteConfig` (~line 314–412): add `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']` after the alias line plus rationale comment.
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (Tableau-Card-Engine repo) — `describe('renderViteConfig')` (line 352) and `describe('scaffoldGameRepo')` (line 474): placement + on-disk assertions.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — §"One Phaser copy": note the template now carries the guard and the core test that protects it.
- `vite.config.ts` (this repo) — unchanged; reference for the emitted comment text and the dedupe list.
- `core` submodule pointer (`git add core`) — bumped after the core commit.

## Out of scope / discovered

- This repo's `package.json` carries `scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` scripts pointing at a non-existent `./scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (the file lives only in core). Pre-existing, unrelated to this fix, non-blocking — recorded as a separate low-priority chore with `discovered-from:MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL`.
- Porting the dedupe into the 8 sibling game repos' *checked-in* configs is the sibling concern tracked by MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0 (different repo set, different fix surface).

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6** (completed, bug) — the 17-file `ReferenceError: window is not defined` collection failure; added the dedupe to this repo's generated config and the `phaser-single-copy` regression test. This item closes the re-scaffold path that would undo it.
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** (completed, task) — precedent: Core scaffold template Pages base — same cross-repo process (CG item in core → core commit → submodule bump), and the same `renderViteConfig` function.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** (open, intake_complete) — sibling concern: port the Vite watcher-ignore into sibling game repos' *generated* configs; overlapping family, non-overlapping ACs.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** (completed, bug) — ENOSPC watcher-exhaustion family (surfaced by the automated related-work report; background only).
- **CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA** (core, completed) — the closest core-side precedent: `renderViteConfig` omitted `server.watch.ignored`, fixed in the template with a core-side test.
- **CG-0MURAK8MX009WWUC** (core, completed) — Scaffold template: derive game-repo Pages base path.
- **CG-0MUJ168XG006DOGK** (core, completed) — F7 "Verify the merged-core architecture end to end", cited in `core/vite.config.ts` as the origin of the core-side `dedupe: ['phaser', 'tone']`.
- `tests/tooling/phaser-single-copy.test.ts` — guards the checked-in config and proves the dedupe is load-bearing (anti-vacuity control).
- `core/tests/vite-config.test.ts:100` — core-side dedupe assertion ("vite config dedupes shared runtime deps for sibling games").
- `docs/dev/testing.md` §"One Phaser copy: `resolve.dedupe` and the `./core` submodule" — canonical narrative for the failure mode.
- `core/docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — where the scaffold workflow is documented for game authors.
- Automated related-work report (`find-related`): MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0, MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY; its three repository file matches (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`) are keyword noise and add no signal here.

**Deliverables:** the `CG-…` work item in the core worklog, the template edit plus its scaffold tests committed there, the `docs/dev/testing.md` update, the `core` submodule pointer bump here, and the recorded core commit hash as a comment on this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Does this change need the same cross-repo process as MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV (separate `CG-…` item in the core worklog + `core` submodule pointer bump), or can the template be edited in-place from this repo?
  **A** (self-resolved from repository evidence — no producer question needed): same process. Evidence: `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` is a tracked file of the Tableau-Card-Engine repository (`core` is a git submodule per `.gitmodules`), and this repo's `scaffold` script invokes `./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, so the bump is what makes the fix effective here. Source: `.gitmodules`, `package.json` scripts, `wl show MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV`.
- **Q:** Does the generated config need to reproduce the long local rationale comment (lines ~160–171 of this repo's `vite.config.ts`)?
  **A** (self-resolved from repository evidence): a short form only. Evidence: `scaffoldGameRepo` rewrites `vite.config.ts` wholesale, so a 12-line local comment is not preservable; the long narrative already lives in `docs/dev/testing.md`. Source: `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (`scaffoldGameRepo` writes root configs) and the generated-file banner.
- **Q:** Is there an existing completed item covering this (duplicate check)?
  **A** (self-resolved): no. Searches in both worklogs (`scaffold`, `dedupe`, `game-repo-scaffold`, `vite config`, `watcher ignore`) return only the locally-scoped MS-0MVK3SF54006Y6A6, the sibling-config MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0, and unrelated core items; the template still emits only `alias`. Source: `wl search` on both stores, 2026-10-25.
- **Open questions:** none.

# Bump core submodule for the Gym storyline demo unit test

**Headline:** Bump the `core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` to core `50b545e1`, which extracts the Gym storyline demo's pure logic into the Phaser-free `GymStorylineDemo` module and covers it with `tests/gym/GymStorylineDemo.test.ts`.

## Why

The epic audit (MS-0MVCRQ475009CDZI) marked parent AC *"Gym demo scene … pure logic is exercised by a unit test"* **partial**: the demo's fixture (`DEMO_CARDS`), engine adapter and RNG were module-private to the scene, so only a boot smoke test touched them. Core item **CG-0MVKNC9MY006ULES** (commit `50b545e1`) extracts them into an exported Phaser-free module and adds a unit test that drives the branching fixture through the public `@story-line` API.

That work is in the core repo; Main Street only sees it once the submodule pointer moves.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `configs/engine-pin.json` and the `core` gitlink both point at core `50b545e1`.
- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` passes (pin equals the staged gitlink).
- `npm test` in Main Street stays green.

## Constraints

- Pointer-only change: no Main Street source edits in this item.
- Stage the `core` gitlink **before** running the test gate so the pin/pointer consistency assertion holds.

data.description:
# Unable to drag and drop upgrade

Dragging an upgrade from the Development (market) row straight onto its matching
business is rejected as an illegal move whenever the player's coin balance
covers the **listed** price but not the **+50% premium** — even on a two-action
day, where the documented composite-parity rule prices the same move at the
listed cost. Reported case: Bookshop on the board, a 300-cost Bookshop upgrade
in the market, 348 coins and 2 actions (1 banked) — the drop is refused although
the move is legal under the parity rule.

## Problem statement

The market→business upgrade drag hard-codes the premium price and premium action
accounting, ignoring the composite-parity rule that business drags already
implement (2+ actions → listed cost + 2 actions; ≤ 1 action → premium + 1
action). A player with a banked action therefore cannot buy-and-apply an upgrade
they can clearly afford, and the refusal carries no reason — the drag just
shakes and plays the illegal-move sound, so the player cannot tell whether the
target, the coins or the actions are at fault.

## Users

- **The player (human seat), single-player and the human seat in competitive
  play.** The reported case comes from normal play with a banked action.

User stories:

- *As a player with 2 actions and 348 coins, I want to drag a 300-cost upgrade
  from the market onto my matching business so the upgrade is applied at the
  listed price, consuming both actions.*
- *As a player whose drag really is illegal, I want to be told why (need N
  coins at premium / no valid business / no actions) so I can plan around it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Composite-parity pricing for the upgrade drag.** With **2 or more** actions
   remaining, dragging a market upgrade onto an eligible business charges the
   **discounted listed** cost (per-business upgrade discount applied first, no
   premium), consumes **both** actions (the drag's action plus the placement
   action) and fires **no** premium dialog; the confirmation text must not claim
   a premium.
2. **Premium path preserved at ≤ 1 action.** With **1** action remaining the drag
   charges `Math.ceil(discountedListed × 1.5 × 2) / 2` and consumes **1** action;
   the premium explainer dialog fires **before** the purchase (Proceed commits,
   Cancel leaves the card in the market row with no coins and no actions spent,
   honouring the persisted "Don't show this again" preference). Text/confirmation
   states the premium.
3. **Pickup gate and drop gate agree.** One shared price helper is the single
   source of truth for the pickup veto, the drop-zone acceptance (`canAccept` /
   green-red highlights) and the executed command. The pickup gate must reason
   about the **same** price the execution charges (today it uses the raw
   undiscounted `card.cost` premium, so a discounted target can be vetoed at
   pickup yet be legal at drop), and it must not veto a pickup that any eligible
   target could legally accept.
4. **Illegal drags state a reason.** A vetoed pickup or a rejected drop surfaces
   the underlying legality reason (e.g. "Need 450 at premium, have 348", "No
   valid business to upgrade", "No actions remaining") in the instruction text
   alongside the existing illegal-move SFX/shake, reusing the `LegalityResult`
   reason rather than a generic message. Reduced-motion and mute settings are
   respected.
5. **Reported scenario works.** Regression test mirroring the report: Bookshop
   on the board, 300-cost Bookshop upgrade in the market, 348 coins, 2 actions
   (one of them banked) → the drag is accepted, the upgrade is applied, 300 coins
   are deducted (48 remain), both actions are consumed, and banked-action
   accounting follows the documented rule (banked spent per action; a premium
   placement does not consume the bank).
6. **Undo/redo and action accounting.** The composite drag stays a single
   undoable step: undo restores the market card, the business level, the coins
   **and** both actions consumed (including the banked decrement); redo
   re-applies it.
7. **Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the parity price and action split
   (≥ 2 actions listed + 2 actions; 1 action premium + 1 action), gate/execution
   agreement with a per-business upgrade discount, and the reason strings;
   browser test covers the reported 2-action drag end-to-end plus the
   premium-dialog path at 1 action. All agent-initiated test runs go through the
   test skill.
8. **Docs + suite.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (action-economy
   "Direct buy-and-place" row and the same-week composite note) and
   `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (Buy Upgrade rows) state the upgrade drag's
   2-action/listed-cost parity and the premium dialog; the "drag is never
   cheaper than click" principle is shown to hold for upgrades. All related
   documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
   README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. The full project test
   suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Reuse the existing parity plumbing.** `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade(state, cardId,
  targetSlot, priceOverride)` and `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand(state, cardId,
  targetSlot, priceOverride?, extraActions?)` already accept the GM-parity
  price override and extra action; the controller simply never passes them for
  upgrades (the business path does). Prefer extending/using a shared helper over
  new engines or commands.
- **Engine state model unchanged** — no new action types or state fields; the
  drag remains a UI gesture resolving to the existing undoable command.
- **Click-path economy unchanged**: market click → hand (1 action) then
  same-week free / held 1 action apply stays exactly as documented; the hand
  drag (MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0) is out of scope except for keeping pricing
  consistent.
- **Event and staff cards untouched** (click-only / separate paths).
- **No change to AI / Monte Carlo / headless `buy-upgrade` semantics** unless a
  test proves they share the divergent helper.
- Implementation in the implement skill's worktree; all agent-initiated test
  runs via the test skill.

## Existing state

- **Market upgrade drag gate** — `canPickUpUpgradeCard` and `canDropUpgradeCard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts`). Pickup requires
  `uiPhase === 'market'`, `actionsRemaining > 0`, an upgrade card, at least one
  eligible target, tutorial gating, and `coins >= Math.ceil(card.cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`
  — computed from the **undiscounted** cost and applied **unconditionally**, so
  2-action days still demand the premium (the reported 348 vs 450 veto). Drop
  delegates to `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade` **without** a price override, so it
  computes the discounted premium — the two gates can disagree.
- **Execution** — `onDragDropUpgrade` executes
  `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand(s.state, cardId, slotIndex)` with no
  `priceOverride`/`extraActions`; its instruction text always appends
  "(50% premium)", and it never fires
  `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (unlike the business drag).
- **Business parity precedent** — `canPickUpBusinessCard`, `canDropBusinessCard`
  and `onDragDropBusiness` implement the composite rule:
  `price = actionsRemaining >= 2 ? effectiveListed : premium`,
  `extraActions = premiumApplies ? 0 : 1`, premium dialog when
  `actionsRemaining <= 1`, matching confirmation text
  (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN).
- **Engine/price helpers** — `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade` / `buyAndPlaceUpgrade`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) apply the per-business upgrade discount
  first (`computeUpgradeCostDiscount`) then the premium, and honour
  `priceOverride` (listed-cost parity); `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand`
  (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`) accepts `priceOverride` and `extraActions`
  (added with CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT but never wired for drags).
- **Feedback** — `initDragDrop` installs no `onIllegal` handler, so a vetoed
  pickup only shakes and plays ILLEGAL_MOVE (the click paths, by contrast, set
  `instructionText` to the legality reason). Market cards dim only when
  `consumesAction && noActions`, so an unaffordable-at-premium upgrade is neither
  dimmed nor explained.
- **Documentation** — the action-economy table already says the direct
  buy-and-place placement price depends on whether an action remains after the
  move, and that "Upgrade cards use the same gesture", but the GDD Buy Upgrade
  rows still describe the upgrade drag as unconditional premium (1 action).

## Desired change

- Resolve one price/action pair for the upgrade drag from the current
  `actionsRemaining` (discount-first listed cost at ≥ 2 actions, discount-first
  premium + dialog at ≤ 1 action) through a single shared helper used by the
  pickup gate, the drop gate and `onDragDropUpgrade`.
- Pass `priceOverride` and `extraActions` into `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade` /
  `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand` on the listed-cost path so the executed price and
  action spend match the gate.
- Fire the existing premium explainer dialog on the ≤ 1-action path and adjust
  the confirmation text to state premium-or-listed accurately.
- Surface the veto/refusal reason in the instruction text (via the drag-drop
  `onIllegal` hook and the drop handler's failure path), reusing legality
  reasons.
- Align the docs (core rules + GDD) with the parity rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.ts` — rewrite
  `canPickUpUpgradeCard` / `canDropUpgradeCard` / `onDragDropUpgrade` for
  parity, premium dialog, `priceOverride` + `extraActions`, reason feedback.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — export/reuse one discount-first pricing
  helper for the premium and listed-cost variants (shared by gate + execution).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — upgrade drag registration
  (`canPickUp`), dimming and hover-reason for an unaffordable-at-premium card.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts` — drop-zone `canAccept` and
  highlight resolution follow the shared price (no behaviour change expected
  beyond the corrected gate).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` (or the controller init) — install an
  `onIllegal` handler on the drag manager that writes the reason to
  `instructionText`.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` — reported-scenario
  drag, premium-dialog path, reason feedback.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-action-economy.test.ts` (+ a focused unit test such
  as `tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-pricing.test.ts`) — price/action parity and
  gate/execution agreement incl. the discount case.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — parity
  wording for upgrades.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Rule ambiguity (open question, see Appendix Q1).** The GDD currently states
  the upgrade drag is always premium + 1 action, while the core-rules table and
  the "drag is never cheaper than click" principle imply the same parity as
  business cards. The ACs above assume parity. If the producer confirms
  premium-only intent, ACs 1, 5 and 6 shrink to "explain the premium refusal"
  and the item drops to a feedback-only fix. *Mitigation:* recorded as a
  producer question; no implementation starts until it is answered.
- **Second, independent defect (assumption):** the pickup gate's undiscounted
  premium check diverges from the executed price whenever a per-business upgrade
  discount (e.g. Financial Advisor) applies — the same scenario can be vetoed at
  pickup yet legal at drop. Covered by AC3; if the producer prefers a narrower
  fix, this stays as a separate item.
- **Undo across two actions (risk):** the business path already consumes an
  extra action inside the snapshot; the upgrade path must be verified to restore
  both actions and the banked decrement. *Mitigation:* AC6 test.
- **Banked-action interaction (risk):** with 2 actions (1 banked) the parity drag
  spends the banked action; the documented rule says banked actions are spent
  per action but not by premium placements. *Mitigation:* AC5 asserts the
  post-drag budget and bank count.
- **Tutorial gating (assumption):** tutorial days are 1-action, so the parity
  path is unreachable there; `apply-upgrade` gating and the T-series flows must
  remain green.
- **Scope creep (risk):** hand-drag pricing, event-card drags, staff hire, AI
  heuristics and the sell/close economy are out of scope; new ideas found while
  implementing become separate work items.

## Related work

- `MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0` — *Allow drag and drop of upgrades from hand to card*
  (completed): mirrored market drags for the hand origin; the hand→street drag
  pricing model this item must stay consistent with.
- `MS-0MUUYGUVB009QOP6` — *Drag-Drop Handlers: Pre-Drop Legality Audit*
  (completed): the `canAccept` pre-drop gating pattern.
- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — *Reject illegal moves before animation and
  action-point deduction* (completed): legality-before-animation and
  "instruction-text reason" contract AC4 restores.
- `MS-0MUUYD15V003SP0Z` — *Upgrade Path: Affordability Pre-Check Before
  Animation* (completed): the affordability pre-gate the pickup veto mirrors.
- Code-request precedents (not work items): CG-0MT3IYSRL001VVUP (upgrade
drag buy-and-play premium), CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN (same-turn composite parity,
commit `722b30df`), CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (action cost + unused
`priceOverride`/`extraActions` wiring, commit `ad4bfb47`), CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC
(discount-first-then-premium ordering).
- Closed `test-failure` items for `upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts`
  (`MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL`, `MS-0MV1HABBG003CKXE`): the browser file this change
  extends.
- Docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Action economy — Direct
  buy-and-place, same-week composite pricing, banked actions),
  `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (§ Buy Upgrade), `core/AGENTS.md` §10b.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which pricing rule should the market→business **upgrade** drag follow when 2 or more actions remain?" Options: **(A)** business parity — charge the discounted **listed** cost and consume **2 actions** (no premium dialog); **(B)** premium always — charge the +50% premium and consume 1 action; **(C)** parity only on Golden Mile 2-action *weeks*, premium on banked-only second actions. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer answer pending). **Recommended:** **(A) parity** — the core-rules table already says the direct buy-and-place placement price depends on whether an action remains after the move and that "Upgrade cards use the same gesture"; the documented principle is "drag is never cheaper than click", the business path implements exactly this split, and the reported case (348 coins / 300-cost upgrade / 2 actions) becomes legal. Source: work-item report + code reading (no interactive reply yet).
- Q2: "Should a vetoed or rejected upgrade drag explain the reason in the instruction text (coins needed at premium / no valid business / no actions)?" Options: **(A)** yes, state the reason; **(B)** keep the current silent shake + illegal SFX. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer answer pending). **Recommended:** **(A)** — MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W establishes the instruction-text reason as the contract for illegal moves, and the report's complaint ("flagged as an illegal move" with no explanation) is partly a feedback gap. Source: code reading (`initDragDrop` installs no `onIllegal`; click paths do set the reason).
- Q3: "Should the pickup gate's undiscounted-premium check (which can veto a pickup that a discounted target would legally accept) be fixed in this item or filed separately?" Options: **(A)** fix here as part of the shared price helper; **(B)** file a separate bug. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer answer pending). **Recommended:** **(A)** — the same helper rewrites both gates, so fixing it here avoids shipping a known gate/execution divergence; the extra cost is one unit test. Source: code reading (`canPickUpUpgradeCard` uses `card.cost`; `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade` uses the discounted base).

### Research summary

- Reproduction traced in code: `canPickUpUpgradeCard` demands
  `ceil(300 × 1.5 × 2)/2 = 450` coins regardless of remaining actions, so with
  348 coins the pickup is vetoed → illegal feedback, no drag, no reason.
- The business drag (`canPickUpBusinessCard` / `onDragDropBusiness`) already
  implements the composite split (≥ 2 actions → listed cost + 2 actions;
  ≤ 1 action → premium + 1 action + explainer dialog) introduced by
  CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN (commit `722b30df`).
- `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `buyAndPlaceUpgrade` and `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand`
  already support the listed-cost override and extra-action accounting
  (commit `ad4bfb47`); only the controller wiring is missing.
- No existing test exercises the upgrade drag with 2 actions remaining; tests
  cover 0 and 1 action only, so the divergence is untested.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W** – Reject illegal moves before animation and action-point deduction (completed)
- **MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0** – Allow drag and drop of upgrades from hand to card (completed)
- **MS-0MUUYGUVB009QOP6** – Drag-Drop Handlers: Pre-Drop Legality Audit (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: actions, banked, board, coins, costs, drag, drop, flagged, illegal, market, move, one, take, upgrade
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — matched: actions, banked, board, bookshop, coins, costs, drag, drop, market, move, one, take, upgrade, want
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: actions, bookshop, coins, costs, drag, drop, illegal, market, move, upgrade
