data.description:
## Problem statement

When the street map is visible (roads, road markings, ambient pedestrians and the
city-block grid behind the play area) the translucent market box, the unbounded
player hand row and the semi-transparent HUD strip let that background show
through, so the play surfaces no longer read as distinct sections and the UI is
visually confusing. The bottom band also carries a persistent instruction/hint
line that clutters the hand area, while the "Hint" button surfaces a hint
subsystem that is no longer wanted on the play surface.

## Users

Primary user: the player of Main Street (single-player and human-vs-AI
competitive), playing on the 1280×720 (or expanded) viewport.

Secondary: designers/QA reading the screen at a glance to verify layout, and
developers maintaining the layout contract (SLL zones + tutorial highlight
alignment).

Example user stories:

- As a player, I want the market, player hand and HUD strip to be opaque panels
  like the Activity Log, so that roads and the map grid never bleed through the
  surfaces I am reading and clicking.
- As a player, I want the bottom of the screen to be free of persistent
  instruction text, so that the hand is the lowest, clearest thing on screen.
- As a player, I want my hand cards sitting at the bottom of the screen, so the
  play band feels anchored and I do not have to look above a text line to find
  my cards.
- As a player, when an action is refused (no coins, no hand slot, illegal
  target), I still want the reason shown briefly, so failures never feel silent.
- As a designer, I want the Hint feature gone from the game surface, so the
  play area only offers the controls that are part of the current design.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Market section is opaque.** The market box uses the Activity Log panel
   treatment — fill `0x1a1408` at alpha **0.85** with a 1 px `0x665544` border
   and radius `BOX_RADIUS` — replacing the current `BOX_FILL` alpha 0.3 / stroke
   0.4. Verified by a unit/browser assertion on the market panel graphics style
   (no roads/grid visible through the panel).
2. **Player hand is an opaque panel.** The hand renders on an opaque panel with
   the same Activity Log treatment (fill `0x1a1408` @ 0.85, 1 px `0x665544`
   border, radius), drawn **behind** the hand cards and ghost capacity outlines
   (and above the street/roads layer). The panel covers the full capacity row
   (`maxSlots × (handCardW + 8)`), so it grows/shrinks when `maxHandSize` changes
   (staff hire/lay-off) without clipping cards or ghosts. It is **non-interactive**
   so hand-card clicks, hand→street drag and market→hand drop paths behave exactly
   as before, it survives `refreshPlayerHand`'s `removeAll(true)` rebuild, and it is
   torn down/cleared correctly on scene restart.
3. **HUD strip opacity raised.** The HUD strip fill moves from `0x1a1408` alpha
   0.6 to **0.85** (same stroke token), so the strip matches the other panels.
4. **Persistent instruction/hint line removed.** No `HintBar`/instruction text is
   created, positioned, or updated: `createInstructions` no longer instantiates a
   `HintBar`, `instructionText`/`instructionY` (and every `setText` call site)
   are removed, and no persistent text renders in the bottom band at any phase
   (market, placing-from-hand, event selected, applicant, competitive AI turn).
5. **Hint feature removed end-to-end.** The Hint button is no longer rendered, and
   the hint subsystem is deleted: `src/MainStreetHint.ts`, `onHintClick`,
   `hintUsedThisTurn`, `hintedCardId`/`hintedSlotIndex` (including their per-turn
   resets and market/street hint highlighting), the `'hint'` transcript event
   type, and `hintButtonW` layout plumbing. Hint-specific tests
   (`tests/main-street/hint.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hint-bar-placement.browser.test.ts`)
   are removed/replaced; the tutorial "banking hint" system is **not** affected
   and its tests keep passing.
6. **Transient feedback preserved.** Messages that previously used the hint line
   (refusals, errors, confirmations such as "Not enough coins…", "Cannot hire…",
   "stays in hand — placement cancelled", "Applied … to slot N") are surfaced as
   short-lived pop text (reusing `@ui` `popTextOrIcon`, reduced-motion aware) and
   remain recorded where they already were in the Activity Log. A representative
   failure path is covered by a test proving the player still gets a visible
   message after the hint line is removed.
7. **Hand anchored at the bottom.** The hand card row's bottom edge sits
   **8–12 px above the viewport bottom** at the 1280×720 base viewport
   (`handY ≈ 628–632`, up from 620), keeping the existing horizontal anchoring
   (left-anchored capacity row centred on the street column,
   `handCenterX = 467`). The hand panel and the ghost outlines move with it, and
   the margin holds on resize/expanded viewports because the position comes from
   the normalised SLL `hand` zone.
8. **Layout contract stays consistent.** `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`
   `hand` zone and `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json` `hand` zone stay
   in sync (tutorial highlight rect must equal the rendered hand rect), the
   documented rects in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` and the layout tests
   (`layout-adapter.test.ts`, `tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`,
   `TutorialOverlayHighlights.browser.test.ts`) are updated, and the action row
   (End Turn / Peek) keeps its current position — `actionY` must no longer be
   derived from the hand zone — so tutorial highlights and button hit areas do not
   drift.
9. **Regression coverage.** New/updated tests assert: market/hand/HUD panel
   opacity, absence of the Hint button and hint line, hand bottom-margin position,
   hand panel resizing with capacity, and the pop-text feedback replacing the
   instruction line. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
   including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
   (`docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md`,
   `docs/dev/ai-strategy.md`, `src/README.md`, `src/scenes/README.md`).
10. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Positioning comes from the SLL layout authority (`src/layouts/*.json` via
  `computeMainStreetLayoutWithSll()`); no new hard-coded pixel positions.
- Panel styling must reuse existing tokens (`BOX_STROKE`, `BOX_RADIUS`) and the
  Activity Log fill/alpha so the three panels cannot drift.
- `core/` is a submodule (repository boundary): `createMainStreetHintButton` in
  `core/src/ui/Renderer/adapters/MainStreetAdapter.ts` becomes unused after this
  change — file a follow-up core work item rather than editing the submodule here.
- Tutorial hint/banking-hint systems are out of scope and must keep working.
- Do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or other agent infrastructure.
- CHANGELOG.md is managed by the release pipeline and is excluded.

## Existing state

- **Activity Log** (reference style): `0x1a1408` @ 0.85 fill, 1 px `0x665544`
  border, `LOG_TITLE_H` title bar — `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:286-317`.
  Challenge tracker and Upcoming queue share the same treatment.
- **Market box**: `BOX_FILL` (`0x2a1f14`) @ 0.3, stroke 0.4 —
  `MainStreetRendererMarket.ts:52-60`.
- **HUD strip**: `0x1a1408` @ 0.6 rectangle — `MainStreetRendererHud.ts:239-245`.
- **Player hand**: no background panel at all; `HandView` draws cards + ghost
  capacity outlines directly over the scene at `handY = 0.861111 × 720 = 620`
  (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:78-120`, `MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`).
- **Instruction line**: shared `HintBar` created in `createInstructions`
  (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts:78-88`), repositioned to
  `(logX/2, handY − 20)` = `(480, 600)` on resize/refresh
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts:719-721`); 137 references across 11
  source files push phase instructions, errors and confirmations through it.
- **Hint feature**: `src/MainStreetHint.ts` (`generateHint` → Greedy AI move +
  rationale), invoked from `onHintClick` (`MainStreetInputManager.ts:229-269`),
  which sets `hintUsedThisTurn` and `hintedCardId`/`hintedSlotIndex`; the button
  is rendered by `createMainStreetHintButton` (`MainStreetRendererHud.ts:529-542`)
  using `layout.hintButtonW`; the action is also recorded as a `'hint'`
  transcript event and an Activity Log line.
- Road/map rendering (`drawStreetRoads`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:417+`) is
  confined to the masked street viewport, but translucent panels elsewhere still
  let the map backdrop read through when the camera is zoomed/panned.

## Desired change

Three bottom/top play surfaces read as solid, self-contained sections in the
Activity Log style; the bottom band carries no persistent instruction text; the
player hand sits at the very bottom of the screen on its own opaque panel; the
Hint button and hint subsystem are gone; and refusals/confirmations still reach
the player as brief pop text plus Activity Log entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — Market box fill alpha 0.3 → 0.85
  (Activity Log treatment).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — HUD strip alpha 0.6 → 0.85; remove
  `createInstructions`/`HintBar` wiring, Hint button creation and phase-specific
  `hintBar.setText(...)` blocks; compute the action row's leftmost x without
  `hintButtonW`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — add the persistent opaque hand panel
  behind the hand cards (sized from the capacity row), keep ghost outlines on top;
  drop `hintedSlotIndex` highlights.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererLayout.ts` — `refreshPlayerHand` keeps the panel in
  sync with `maxHandSize`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — delete `onHintClick`; pop-text feedback
  for hint-line messages.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController*.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — remove `instructionText`/`hintBar`/
  hint-state call sites and resets; route feedback to pop text + log.
- `src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`, `src/layouts/main-street-tutorial.layout.json`
  — `hand` zone y moved to the bottom margin (628/720 ≈ 0.872222), kept in sync.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` —
  remove `instructionY`/`hintButtonW`; decouple `actionY` from the hand zone.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` — update the documented hand rect.
- `src/MainStreetHint.ts` — **delete** (hint subsystem).
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — remove the `'hint'` event variant.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — comment clean-up where hints are described as a
  consumer of the Greedy strategy.
- `tests/main-street/hint.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hint-bar-placement.browser.test.ts`
  — delete/replace with tests asserting the hint line/button are gone.
- `tests/main-street/layout-adapter.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/TutorialOverlayHighlights.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/TutorialOverlayManager.browser.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/hud-strip-layout.browser.test.ts`,
  plus the ~46 `instructionText` assertions across
  `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` — update to the new layout/feedback contract.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md`,
  `docs/dev/ai-strategy.md`, `src/README.md`, `src/scenes/README.md` — document
  opaque panels, bottom-anchored hand, removed hint system, and the new feedback
  channel.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** (completed) — named storylines / outcome feedback &
  continuity indicator: established the current bottom-band HUD feedback patterns.
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** (completed) — competitive state model: per-player
  resources, owner-tagged street (hand/HUD panels must stay legible in competitive
  mode).
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** (completed) — competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD
  (same HUD strip that gains the 0.85 opacity).
- Automated relation report (find-related skill) for this item records the
  repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (hand/HUD panel semantics),
  `core/CHANGELOG.md`, and `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` (HUD/opaque
  panel guidance) — all read-only references for this change.
- Related docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (§ Player hand layout, undo/redo
  pop "above the hint bar"), `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (§ AI Strategy and Hint
  System), `docs/dev/ai-strategy.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (worktree
  rules).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Input-interception risk.** A full-width background rectangle behind the hand
  would sit over the bottom band; if made interactive it silently swallows hand
  clicks and drag targets. It must be non-interactive (`setInteractive` never
  called) and rendered below the cards, verified by the existing hand click/drag
  browser tests.
- **Legacy transcript tolerance.** Removing the `'hint'` transcript variant only
  affects the TypeScript union; saved transcripts containing historical hint
  events are read tolerantly (replay adapters accept unknown event shapes), so no
  data migration is needed — the assumption is recorded, not silently made.

- **Removing the hint system removes a player-assist feature.** Producer explicitly
  chose full removal (Q5 = C); the GDD § *AI Strategy and Hint System* becomes
  design intent only and must say the feature is not currently surfaced.
- **Silent-failure risk.** ~46 tests and many code paths use the removed text as
  the only failure message; the pop-text channel must keep every refusal visible
  (AC6), otherwise illegal moves read as unresponsive.
- **Layout drift risk.** The tutorial highlight contract pins the hand rect; moving
  the hand without updating `main-street-tutorial.layout.json` breaks highlight
  alignment. `actionY` is currently derived from `handY`, so decoupling it is
  required to keep End Turn/Peek hit areas and highlights stable.
- **Capacity growth risk.** Staff can raise `maxHandSize` beyond 3; a fixed-width
  hand panel would clip cards or ghost outlines. The panel must size from the
  capacity row and update on hire/lay-off.
- **Scope creep.** While touching panels, resist restyling the street slots,
  challenge tracker or Upcoming queue (already 0.85) — record any further visual
  opportunities as separate work items.
- **Assumption.** "Opaque like the Activity Log" means the Activity Log's existing
  0.85 alpha + border + radius (not alpha 1.0), so all panels share one token set.
- **Assumption.** Hand horizontal anchoring is unchanged (left-anchored capacity
  row centred on the street column); only the vertical position changes.
- **Assumption.** `createMainStreetHintButton` lives in the `core` submodule and is
  left in place (unused) with a follow-up core work item, per repository
  boundaries.

## Open Questions

None — all five interview questions were answered by the producer.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1. Scope of the opaque treatment — which surfaces?**
  - Options: (a) market + hand only; (b) market + hand + HUD strip; (c) every
    translucent surface.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — matches the seed wording, minimal change.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(b)** — market panel, player hand
    panel *and* HUD strip at 0.85.
- **Q2. "Remove the hint text" — what exactly?**
  - Options: (a) remove the bottom-centre instruction line, keep the Hint button;
    (b) remove the instruction line *and* the Hint button; (c) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — the line is the clutter; the button is functional.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(b)** — remove the instruction
    line and the Hint button.
- **Q3. Hand destination.**
  - Options: (a) straight down to an 8–12 px bottom margin keeping current
    horizontal anchoring; (b) also re-centre horizontally; (c) other margin.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — simple and preserves street alignment.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(a)** — card bottoms 8–12 px from
    the viewport bottom, horizontal anchoring unchanged.
- **Q4. The removed hint line is also the error/feedback channel — what replaces
  it?**
  - Options: (a) transient pop/toast (`popTextOrIcon`) + keep Activity Log entries;
    (b) a one-line message area that only renders while a message is live;
    (c) drop text feedback entirely (shake + SFX only).
  - **Recommended:** (a) — keeps failures visible without reintroducing clutter.
  - **Research:** transient messaging already exists via `@ui` `popTextOrIcon`
    ("Undid: …" rides above the bottom band, `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md:1015`);
    Activity Log already records outcomes.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(a)**.
- **Q5. What happens to the hint *system* once the "Hint" button goes?**
  - Options: (a) remove the button only, keep `generateHint` + tests; (b) rebind to
    a keyboard shortcut; (c) remove the hint system code and tests entirely.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — surgical, per "mention dead code, don't delete it".
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(c)** — remove the hint subsystem
    and its tests as part of this item.
  - **Research:** hint code is self-contained — `src/MainStreetHint.ts`
    (`generateHint`, `buildRationale`), `onHintClick` in `MainStreetInputManager`,
    `hintedCardId`/`hintedSlotIndex` highlighting in the market and street
    renderers, the `'hint'` transcript variant, and
    `tests/main-street/hint.test.ts`; the tutorial banking-hint system is
    unrelated and stays.

data.description:
# Bank Loans

A player (human or AI) who cannot pay their end-of-turn costs can take a bank loan
instead of going bankrupt: a fixed principal is credited immediately and repaid as a
fixed per-turn amount (principal + 10% total interest) until the term expires. Loans
cost no action point and there is at most one active loan per player.

## Problem statement

Bankruptcy is currently a terminal state (`checkImmediateLoss` fires at `coins < 0`,
`resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` eliminates an AI seat), so a single bad week ends a
run with no recovery path. Players also have no way to convert future income into
present cash, which narrows strategic options in the mid-game. Bank Loans add a
credit mechanic that lets a player buy their way past a cash crunch at the cost of a
fixed debt burden.

## Users

- **Human player (single- and competitive mode)** — "When my end-of-turn costs leave
  me at negative coins, I want to be offered a loan so I can keep playing instead of
  losing the run."
- **Human player, mid-game** — "When I am short of the cash for a strong move at the
  end of a turn, I want to borrow a fixed amount with a repayment schedule I can see,
  so I can judge whether the debt is worth it."
- **AI opponent (competitive mode)** — "When I go bankrupt I should be given the same
  bailout a human gets, so an unlucky week does not knock me out of the game."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Loan offer & taking a loan.** A seat with no active loan can take a loan by
   choosing one option from the configured loan menu (default: 300 coins / 3 turns,
   600 / 6, 1000 / 10). Taking a loan credits the principal to that seat's wallet
   immediately, records the active loan, and **costs no action point**
   (`actionsRemaining` unchanged).
2. **One active loan per player.** A seat that already has an active loan cannot take
   or accept another one; the attempt is rejected with a clear, user-facing reason and
   no resource change.
3. **Fixed per-turn repayment.** At the end of every turn in which a seat holds an
   active loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins are deducted from that seat's wallet
   (`totalRepayment = round(principal × 1.10)`, `perTurnRepayment =
   round(totalRepayment / termTurns)`; e.g. 600 / 6 → 110 per turn, 660 total). The
   deduction is recorded in the turn's net summary as a one-off expense; the loan is
   retired after `termTurns` payments and no further deductions occur.
4. **Bankruptcy bailout.** When a seat would fail on `coins < 0` (single-player loss,
   or competitive seat failure) **and holds no active loan**, the game does not end
   (and the seat is not eliminated): a loan offer is presented instead. Accepting
   credits the principal and play continues; declining, or already holding an active
   loan, preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour. At most one bailout offer is made per
   seat per turn (no offer loop).
5. **AI bailout policy.** An AI seat that hits `coins < 0` with no active loan
   auto-accepts the **largest** loan option and is not eliminated; an AI seat that
   already holds an active loan is eliminated exactly as today. AI seats take no
   proactive (non-bailout) loans.
6. **Visible obligation.** While a loan is active the player can see what they owe:
   the activity log records the loan (amount, per-turn repayment, term) and the
   remaining obligation (turns left + per-turn amount) is surfaced in the HUD, so the
   debt burden is never hidden.
7. **Repayment shortfall.** Repayment is deducted unconditionally, so a payment that
   exceeds the seat's balance leaves `coins < 0` and triggers the normal bankruptcy
   path — which offers a bailout only if the seat has no active loan (per AC4), i.e. a
   seat already repaying a loan simply goes bankrupt.
8. **Headless determinism.** Headless turn execution (`endTurnHeadless`, Monte Carlo,
   balance runs) never stalls on a pending loan offer: it resolves deterministically
   using the AC5 AI policy, and simulations without loans enabled are byte-identical
   to today's results.
9. **Persistence and back-compatibility.** Active loans and a pending offer survive a
   save/load round-trip; pre-loan saves (schema v2) load with no loans and unchanged
   behaviour. Save schema version is bumped with a migration.
10. **Testing/validation.** New unit tests cover the loan maths (option table,
    `perTurnRepayment`, retirement after `termTurns`), single-loan enforcement, bailout
    offer/accept/decline, shortfall → bankruptcy, AI largest-option policy, headless
    resolution and save/load round-trip; the competitive-seat path is covered by an
    integration test.
11. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
    including code comments, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, and the
    in-game help content where it lists end-of-turn economy rules.
12. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No action point cost** — taking a loan must not decrement `actionsRemaining`
  (seed requirement).
- **Fixed menu, no negotiation** — the loan menu is configuration data
  (`config.loanOptions`), identical for every seat in a run; no per-seat or
  per-difficulty negotiation UI. Re-balancing is a config edit only.
- **Interest model** — flat 10% of principal over the whole term, spread evenly
  (`600 / 6 → 110/week`, per the seed's worked example). No compounding, no
  per-turn-on-outstanding-balance interest.
- **One active loan per player** (producer decision Q1 = A) — no debt stacking.
- **Bailout-only AI** (Q3 = A) — AI strategy changes are limited to auto-accepting a
  bailout offer; no new AI heuristics otherwise.
- **Economy realism** — repayment moves through the existing `EconomyLedger` /
  `resourceBank` sync path; no direct wallet mutation.
- **Config defaults** — `loansEnabled: true` in the `Easy`/`Medium`/`Hard` presets
  (the mechanic is live in the game), and `false` for headless/simulation configs so
  existing Monte Carlo and balance baselines stay unchanged until a simulation opts in.
- **No turn-summary dependency** — the Turn Summary dialog
  (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) does not exist yet; this item must not block on it.

## Existing state

- Bankruptcy is terminal and evaluated in two places:
  `checkImmediateLoss` (single-player, `coins < 0` → `endReason 'bankruptcy'`) and
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` (competitor seats; human → loss, AI →
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`), both in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`.
  An opening-day grace already exists (`applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`,
  MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41), which bailout evaluation must respect.
- Pending-decision pausing is an established pattern: `state.pendingEventChoice` and
  `state.pendingPiggyback` both defer the closing tail and are resolved by the UI
  before the closing re-runs — a pending loan offer should follow the same shape.
- Turn economy closes in `processEndOfTurn` (income, ongoing costs, incident) and
  summarises into the activity log via `appendTurnNetRow`; a repayment expense belongs
  in that same sequence so the net row reflects it.
- Per-seat wallets live in `state.players[].coins` (competitive) while
  `state.resourceBank` is the working mirror bound by `bindCompetitiveSeat` /
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`; `state.players` is `undefined` in single-player.
- `GameConfig` (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) is a numeric-parameter bag derived from
  difficulty presets, consumed by the engine — the natural home for loan config.
- No loan code exists anywhere in the repo (`grep -ri loan src core tests docs` is
  empty) — this is net-new capability.
- Save/load uses `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState` with a
  strict schema-version check (`MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`) and a migration
  hook, so a version bump plus defaults is the established path for new fields.

## Desired change

1. **Loan model** — new `LoanOption` / `ActiveLoan` types and `MainStreetLoans.ts`
   holding the option table, offer computation, and pure apply/resolve helpers.
   State gains `loans: ActiveLoan[]` (invariant: at most one entry per `ownerId`) and
   `pendingLoanOffer?: { ownerId, reason, options }`.
2. **Config** — `loansEnabled`, `loanInterestRate` (0.10) and `loanOptions` added to
   `GameConfig` and all difficulty presets (`loansEnabled: true`); headless/simulation
   configs default it to `false` so existing balance baselines are unchanged.
3. **Taking a loan** — a `takeLoan` command (no AP cost) validated against the
   one-active-loan rule, crediting principal via the ledger and logging the decision.
4. **Repayment** — `applyLoanRepayments(state)` invoked in the closing sequence ahead
   of the end-condition checks, decrementing `turnsRemaining` and logging the expense
   into the turn net row.
5. **Bailout offer** — `maybeOfferBailout(state)` evaluated *before* the bankruptcy /
   seat-failure declarations: when a seat with no active loan is at `coins < 0`, set
   `pendingLoanOffer` (reason `bankruptcy`) and pause the closing instead of ending the
   game; `acceptLoanOffer` / `declineLoanOffer` resume it. Declining, a second offer in
   the same turn, or an already-active loan preserves current behaviour.
6. **Visible obligation** — log the loan at acceptance and surface
   "Loan: X coins/turn, N turns left" in the HUD beside the coin/reputation readouts.
7. **UI** — a bailout overlay (option list with per-turn and total repayment shown,
   plus Decline) rendered when a pending offer exists, wiring the deferred-closing
   resume path in `MainStreetTurnController`. The mid-game entry point on the Turn
   Summary dialog is **out of scope** here (see Non-goals).
8. **AI** — bailout auto-accept of the largest option in the AI/headless path.
9. **Persistence** — serialise `loans` and `pendingLoanOffer`; bump the save schema to
   v3 with a migration defaulting legacy saves to an empty loan list.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Wiring the "Bank Loan" button into the Turn Summary dialog
  (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) — a thin follow-up once that dialog lands. Per producer
  decision Q4, **if the dialog is not completed in time, raise a separate follow-up
  work item** for the wiring rather than expanding this item.
- Multiple concurrent/stacked loans, variable or negotiated interest, per-seat credit
  limits.
- Deducting outstanding principal from the score, or any loan effect on reputation.
- Proactive (non-bailout) AI loan strategy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — **new**. Option table (`DEFAULT_LOAN_OPTIONS`), repayment
  maths, `takeLoan`, `applyLoanRepayments`, `maybeOfferBailout`,
  `acceptLoanOffer` / `declineLoanOffer`, active-loan lookup per owner.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LoanOption`, `ActiveLoan`, `PendingLoanOffer`
  types; `loans` and `pendingLoanOffer` fields on `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `loansEnabled`, `loanInterestRate`, `loanOptions` on
  `GameConfig` plus all presets (`Easy`/`Medium`/`Hard`).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — call `applyLoanRepayments` and
  `maybeOfferBailout` ahead of `checkImmediateLoss` / `checkEndConditions` /
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`; defer the closing tail while an offer is pending.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — active-loan readout (turns left,
  per-turn repayment) beside the coin/reputation HUD.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — end-of-turn economy help text: loan menu and
  bailout rule.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `pendingLoanOffer` on `TurnResult` (mirroring
  `choicePending` / `piggybackPending`) and a `TakeLoanAction` in `PlayerAction`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` handler
  and command dispatch; assert no AP consumption.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — bailout auto-accept (largest option) for AI seats.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — **new**. Bailout dialog: option rows with
  per-turn/total repayment, Accept and Decline.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — show the overlay instead of the game-over
  summary while a bailout offer is open; resume the deferred closing on resolution.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — serialise/restore
  loans and the pending offer; bump `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3 with a
  migration.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — headless deterministic resolution of a pending offer.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoans.test.ts` — **new**. Maths, one-loan rule, config.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — **new**. Bailout offer/accept/
  decline, shortfall, AI policy, headless.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanSaveLoad.test.ts` — **new**. Round-trip + v2
  migration.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — economy section: loan menu, repayment
  schedule, bailout rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — interest arithmetic.** The seed's worked example (600 over 6 turns at
  110/turn = 660 total) is read as "10% of principal over the whole term, spread
  evenly", not "10% per turn on the outstanding balance" (which would be ~137/turn).
  Low risk: the example is unambiguous arithmetic; a config-driven `loanInterestRate`
  makes the alternative a one-line change.
- **Assumption — default option menu.** Three options (300/3, 600/6, 1000/10) all
  yielding 110/turn are proposed so the producer's choice (Q2 = B, "a choice among
  options") has a concrete, balanced default. Pure config data; re-balancing needs no
  code change.
- **Assumption — loans do not affect scoring.** Debt only drains coins; outstanding
  principal is not deducted from `finalScore`. Recorded as a possible follow-up rather
  than scope.
- **Risk — end-condition ordering.** The bailout intercept must run *before*
  `checkImmediateLoss` / `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, and must respect the
  existing first-turn solvency grace, or the game will end before the offer is shown.
  Mitigation: explicit ordering tests plus a per-turn "already offered" guard.
- **Risk — deferred closing loops.** Reusing the `pendingLoanOffer` pause means the
  closing can be re-entered; an unresolvable offer (decline with no other option) must
  converge to game over in one pass. Mitigation: idempotency tests and the per-turn
  offer guard.
- **Risk — headless/Monte Carlo regressions.** A pending offer that blocks headless
  closing would hang balance runs. Mitigation: AC7 determinism tests plus
  `loansEnabled: false` default for simulation configs, with before/after result
  comparison.
- **Risk — save schema.** Bumping the shared save schema risks older-campaign
  compatibility. Mitigation: v2 migration test that loads a pre-loan save unchanged.
- **Risk — scope creep.** The Turn Summary dialog entry point, proactive AI lending and
  score effects are natural "while we're here" additions; each is recorded as a
  non-goal/follow-up rather than absorbed into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 — End of Turn summary** (stage `idea`). Defines the
  turn-summary dialog with a "Bank Loan" button that is explicitly waiting on this
  feature. **Related, not blocking**: this item ships the engine, bailout flow and
  `takeLoan` command without it; the dialog wiring is a follow-up (see Non-goals).
- **MS-0MUWE6MSQ006DEZ4 — End-reason & player-state model** (completed). Introduced the
  `EndReason` union (`bankruptcy`, `reputation_collapse`, …) and the per-seat failure
  badges that the bailout path intercepts.
- **MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2 — AI seat elimination / last standing** (completed via
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`, `checkLastStanding`). The bailout must run before
  elimination so an AI survives, which in turn delays last-standing wins.
- **MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41 — Play Again does not reset the AI** (completed). Also
  introduced the opening-day solvency grace (`applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`) that
  bailout evaluation must respect.
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM — Provide reason for game ending** (completed). Game-over
  copy/end-reason surfacing that the "declined bailout" path must still produce.
- **MS-0MUYC47EL005Z69H / CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128 — pending-decision pausing**
  (`pendingEventChoice`, `pendingPiggyback`). The `pendingLoanOffer` pause should
  follow this established deferred-closing pattern.
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item covers bank loans; the only overlap is
  the turn-summary dialog item above (partial relationship, not a duplicate).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Round 1

- **Q1: Can a player hold more than one loan at once?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — one active loan per player; further
  offers deferred until it is repaid.** Source: interactive reply, session
  `herdr-1792944777-2932233-30937`.
- **Q2: What shape is the loan offer?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B — a choice among options (e.g. 300/3,
  600/6), pick one.** Source: interactive reply, same session. Consequence: the brief
  defines a config-driven option menu rather than a single fixed offer.
- **Q3: How do AI opponents use loans?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — bankruptcy bailout only; auto-accept
  when an AI seat hits `coins < 0`.** Source: interactive reply, same session.
  Consequence: no proactive AI lending in this item.

Round 2

- **Q4: Entry point while the Turn Summary dialog does not exist yet?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — build the loan engine + `takeLoan`
  command + bankruptcy-bailout UI now; wire the Turn-summary "Bank Loan" button when
  that dialog lands, and create a follow-up item if the dialog has not been completed
  in time.** Source: interactive reply, same session.
- **Q5: Which option does an AI auto-accept on bailout?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — the largest available option.** Source:
  interactive reply, same session.
- **Q6: Repayment shortfall behaviour?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — deduct anyway; negative coins trigger
  the existing bankruptcy flow, and a seat that already holds a loan gets no new
  offer.** Source: interactive reply, same session.

Research notes: repo searched for existing loan code (`grep -ri loan src core tests
docs` — no matches) and for the bankruptcy hooks (`checkImmediateLoss`,
`resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`). Related
work items found via `wl search "loan"` / `wl search "bankrupt"`; the turn-summary
dependency item (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) was read in full and is at stage `idea`.
## Related work (automated report)

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41)

## Problem statement

After the End of Turn phase animations finish, the player currently gets only a
one-line instruction text (`Income: +N coins | Incident: <name>`, via
`closingSummary`) and the next day starts automatically. There is no moment to
understand what happened that turn — how much income came in and from where,
what was spent (ongoing costs), one-off events, and each player's standing.
This item adds a **Turn Summary dialog** that appears once all End of Turn
animations have completed, showing the current state of the game (businesses
owned per player, this turn's income and expenses, one-off income/expenses from
events, and other useful state), with a **[ Next Turn ]** button to continue
and a **[ Bank Loan ]** button (disabled until MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands).

## Users

- **Main Street single-player player** — after each turn's closing
  animations, wants a readable summary of what just happened and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action instead of an auto-advance.
- **Main Street competitive player** — unchanged for now (see Constraints:
  competitive is deliberately out of scope in this item).

**User stories:**

- As a player, when my turn's income/incident animations finish, I see a dialog
  summarising the turn (income by phase, expenses by category, one-off event
  deltas, net change, businesses owned) so I can learn from each turn.
- As a player, I can click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next week — the day
  does not advance until I do.
- As a player, I see a **[ Bank Loan ]** affordance that is visibly
  unavailable until the loans feature exists, so I know the option is planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In normal single-player play (deferred/closing path), after all End of Turn
   animations (phased income show + incident reveal) complete, a Turn Summary
   dialog appears and the next day does **not** start until the player clicks
   **[ Next Turn ]**. Reduced-motion, tutorial and replay modes skip the
   dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog reports, for the turn just closed: businesses owned, income
   subtotals per phase (base / synergy / reputation / events), ongoing expenses
   per category (staff / community / business), incident and one-off event
   deltas, net coin / reputation / score change, and closing coin /
   reputation / score values. The underlying ledger is **owner-keyed** (ready
   for per-player rows), but the panel renders the single (human) seat because
   the competitive dialog is deferred (see Constraint: competitive out of
   scope).
3. The dialog's **[ Bank Loan ]** button is always rendered **disabled** with
   an explanatory hint, behind a single wiring seam that
   MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans) will replace. It is never shown enabled by
   this item.
4. The dialog is NOT presented in competitive mode (operator decision) —
   existing per-seat closing text (`perSeatClosingSummary`) is unchanged.
5. A Phaser-free model (`MainStreetTurnSummary`, mirroring
   `MainStreetGameOverSummary`) renders the dialog content from committed
   engine data; the engine's `TurnResult` is extended with an end-of-turn
   ledger (expense subtotals, per-phase income subtotals, one-off deltas, net
   change) so every value shown is testable without a browser.
6. At least one automated test per surfaced value (model tests, engine ledger
   tests, and a dialog overlay test); **all related documentation is updated**
   (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md end-of-turn section, plus any references in
   README/dev docs); **the full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground`
  + `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`; all elements parented into
  `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201; everything pushed into
  `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance (reduced-motion safe);
  button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- The dialog is presentation-only: it reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In the deferred path the turn's
  deltas land exactly once (idempotent `endOfTurnDeltasApplied` guard) before
  the panel renders, so the panel shows post-turn state; the checkpoint save
  stays in `finalizeTurn` (existing ordering — no mid-animation saves).
- Tutorial pacing and the one-shot banking-hint presentation must not regress.
  Assumption: when a banking hint is pending on the gated turn, the hint is
  presented after the dialog dismisses (dialog → Next Turn → hint → day start)
  so it is not occluded; the exactly-once flag behaviour is preserved.
  (Flagged in Risks for implementer verification.)
- Undo stack clearing, log-render deferral (`flushDeferredLog`) and the
  incident reveal hold ordering are unchanged.
- Competitive closes are untouched (operator decision Q2 = B): no dialog, and
  `perSeatClosingSummary` text stays as-is. `TurnResult` ledger fields must
  not break competitive callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`,
  `presentCompetitiveClosing`) — keep additions optional/backwards-compatible.
- **Fidelity note (producer intent vs Q2):** the seed asked for "# of
  businesses owned by *each* player". With the competitive dialog deferred,
  this item satisfies that for the human seat only; the owner-keyed ledger and
  the model's row shape keep the multi-seat panel a small follow-up rather than
  a rewrite.

## Existing state

- `finishTurnPresentation` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`)
  drives the closing: `presentTurnClosing` (shared primitive in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`) writes the one-line
  `closingSummary`, runs the incident reveal, then calls `advanceTurn` →
  `finalizeTurn` → `startTurnPhase`. The new gate slots at the top of
  `advanceTurn` in the deferred (`deferred === true`) path only.
- Expenses are applied in `processEndOfTurn`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`): `applyStaffOngoingCosts` /
  `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` / `applyBusinessOngoingCosts`, folded into
  `pendingCoinDelta`. **They are not currently reported on `TurnResult`** — the
  ledger extension is required to show them.
- Overlay precedent: `showEventChoiceDialog` / `showPiggybackDialog` /
  `showGameOverOverlay` in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, delegated
  via `MainStreetScene.ts`; pure model precedent:
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.

## Desired change

1. Engine: extend `TurnResult` (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`) with an
   end-of-turn ledger — e.g. `turnLedger?: { incomeByPhase, ongoingCosts:
   { staff, community, business }, incidentCoinChange, incidentRepChange,
   oneOffDeltas, netCoinChange, netRepChange, netScoreChange, businessesOwned
   }` — populated in `processEndOfTurn` for both the deferred and legacy
   paths; competitive may populate per-seat data but the dialog does not
   consume it yet.
2. Model: new Phaser-free `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` building the
   panel rows (per-player businesses, income phases, expense categories,
   one-off/incident lines, net change, closing totals) from the ledger +
   `state`.
3. UI: `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` in `MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
   following the event-choice-dialog overlay pattern; **[ Next Turn ]** button
   (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (disabled, hint text) with a single seam
   (`onBankLoanAction?: () => void` style hook) for MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG.
4. Gating: in `finishTurnPresentation`, wrap `advanceTurn` so the deferred
   path shows the dialog (deltas applied idempotently first) and only runs the
   remaining flow (`advanceTurn` body incl. banking hint, income-wait,
   `finalizeTurn`) after **[ Next Turn ]** is clicked.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — NEW Phaser-free summary model (per-player businesses, income/expense rows, net change, closing totals)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — gate the deferred path's `advanceTurn` on the dialog
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showTurnSummaryDialog` overlay (Next Turn + disabled Bank Loan)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — delegation method for the dialog (pattern: `showEventChoiceDialog`)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` with the turn ledger
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — populate the ledger in `processEndOfTurn` (deferred + legacy)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — `closingSummary` retained for reduced-motion/non-deferred paths
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-model.test.ts` (pure), `tests/main-street/end-of-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- **MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD** – End Turn Phase is missing in AI game (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP** – Export end-of-turn income-collection cap constant
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`,
  `docs/dev/prd-milestone-3.md`, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
  (keyword overlap: end-of-turn, bank, businesses, button)

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item.
- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — this item (end of turn dialog).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on the Game Over overlay; consumes the same per-turn data
  this item's ledger introduces (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's one-line `closingSummary` and the shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` (completed) — competitive per-seat income
  choreography: the reason competitive cadence is deliberately excluded here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (banking hint ordering):** the one-shot banking hint, when
  pending on the gated turn, presents after the dialog dismisses; exactly-once
  persistence behaviour is preserved. Implementer must verify the tutorial
  banking-hint step still passes (risk: minor regression if ordering changes).
- **Assumption (delta window):** deltas land before the panel renders so
  "closing coins/reputation/score" are post-turn values; finalizeTurn's
  idempotent guard keeps the existing save-point semantics.
- **Risk (competitive type churn):** extending `TurnResult` touches shared
  types used by competitive closings — keep ledger fields optional so
  `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn` / `presentCompetitiveClosing` are
  unaffected; guard with tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** competitive-mode dialog, post-game per-turn graphs
  (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), and live loans (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) are outside this
  item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the summary dialog block the automatic next-week advance?"
  — Answer (operator): "A — Yes, blocks the advance in normal play (dialog
  with Next Turn button); reduced-motion, tutorial and replay modes keep
  auto-advancing." Source: interactive reply 2026-10-25.
- Q2: "Competitive cadence — once per round, once per seat, or skip?"
  — Answer (operator): "B — Skip the dialog in competitive for now."
  Source: interactive reply 2026-10-25. (Recorded as related-work opportunity
  for a future item.)
- Q3: "Bank Loan button while loans don't exist?"
  — Answer (operator): "A — Render it present-but-disabled with an explanatory
  hint, plus a single wiring seam for the loans item." Source: interactive
  reply 2026-10-25.
- Q4: "Expense data sourcing — engine ledger or presentation-only?"
  — Answer (operator): "A — Extend TurnResult with an end-of-turn ledger
  (income-phase subtotals, ongoing costs per category, incident/one-off
  deltas, net change, businesses owned) consumed by a new Phaser-free model."
  Source: interactive reply 2026-10-25.

# Add shared load-tolerant `waitForCondition` helper to `core/tests/helpers/`

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Give every game repo one shared browser-test poll helper whose timeout budget is
derived from the **production cap it races** rather than guessed, so a
CPU-starved host cannot make a green scene look like a red test.

## Scope (in)

1. New `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` (sibling to `waitForScene.ts`),
   carrying the existing 49 per-file copies' behaviour **plus** a documented
   budget model:

   ```ts
   resolveWaitBudget({ capMs, starvationFactor = 1.5, floorMs = 5_000 })
     // budget = max(round(capMs * starvationFactor), capMs + floorMs)
     // throws when the result is not strictly greater than capMs
   waitForCondition(predicate, { capMs, starvationFactor?, floorMs?, intervalMs?, label? })
   ```

   - `capMs` is the **nominal** production cap (e.g. the 16 000 ms income-collection
     deferral, or `DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS`).
   - `starvationFactor` widens the nominal cap for rAF starvation (default 1.5).
   - `floorMs` guarantees a fixed scheduling margin even for tiny caps (default 5 000).
   - The invariant `budget > capMs` is enforced in code, so a caller can never
     configure a poll shorter than the cap it documents as racing.
   - Timeout message keeps the existing shape
     (`Timed out waiting for <label> after <budget>ms (cap <capMs>ms)`) so
     existing triage signatures stay greppable.
   - Raw `timeoutMs` remains accepted for callers that do not race a production
     cap (backwards-compatible with the copied implementations).

2. New `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.test.ts` — **written first (TDD)**:
   derivation for nominal/starvationFactor/floor, invariant throw, budget strictly
   greater than cap, predicate polling, timeout error content, `intervalMs`
   honouring.

## Scope (out)

- Migrating the 49 existing `waitForCondition` copies (explicit non-goal of the
  parent item; record as a discovered `discovered-from` item if a follow-up is
  desired).
- Any production pacing change.

## Key Files

- `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` (new)
- `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.test.ts` (new)
- `configs/engine-pin.json` (pin bump)
- submodule pointer `core`

## Cross-repo workflow (core is a submodule — precedent MS-0MVKNRV6T0019KHJ)

`./core` is the `Tableau-Card-Engine` submodule, currently detached at the pinned
SHA in `configs/engine-pin.json`. Deliver this child as:

1. Implement + test in the game worktree's `core/` checkout (it is a real git
   repo there: `.git` is a gitdir file under `.git/worktrees/<wt>/modules/core`).
   If `core/` is empty in the worktree: `git submodule update --init core`.
2. In `core/`: check out `dev` (never `main`), run the affected unit suite via
   `/skill:test` in the core checkout, `npm run build` (tsc + vite) — build before
   test-commit order applies there too.
3. Commit on `dev` with the parent id, push `dev`, record the core commit hash in
   a comment on this child.
4. In the game repo: update the submodule pointer and bump `configs/engine-pin.json`
   to the new core SHA; run `npm run engine:verify`; commit the pointer + pin.
5. Record the cross-repo change on this child (core repo has no Worklog store).

**Fallback gate:** if the core push or pin bump is impossible in-session
(offline remote, core gate failure), STOP and raise an OPEN QUESTION to the
producer rather than silently relocating the helper into the game repo. If the
producer authorises relocation, the helper goes to `tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts`
in the game repo, this child is rescoped, and the parent AC wording is amended.

## Constraints

- No Phaser import; the helper must run in both the browser project and the
  node `unit` project (it is pure `Date.now()` + `setTimeout` polling).
- Pending 60 s browser `testTimeout` headroom: default derivation must keep a
  single wait well inside 60 s (16 000 → 24 000, 1 500 → 7 500).
- Core writes follow the engine-sync workflow (`npm run engine:sync` /
  `engine:verify`); never `npm install` inside `./core` (root dependencies serve
  the engine — see `docs/dev/testing.md`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts` exists, exports
      `resolveWaitBudget` and `waitForCondition`, and documents the
      `nominal cap + starvation margin` model in its module docblock.
- [ ] `resolveWaitBudget` returns `max(round(capMs * starvationFactor), capMs + floorMs)`
      for the default and custom factors/floors, and throws when the derived
      budget is not strictly greater than `capMs`.
- [ ] `waitForCondition` polls at `intervalMs`, resolves on the first truthy
      predicate, and rejects with a message containing the label and the derived
      budget.
- [ ] `core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.test.ts` covers derivation,
      the invariant throw, successful polling, and timeout (unit project, cheap).
- [ ] The affected core unit suite passes via `/skill:test` and the core build
      passes; core `dev` branch is pushed and the hash recorded on this child.
- [ ] The game repo's submodule pointer and `configs/engine-pin.json` are bumped
      to the new core SHA in the same delivery, and `npm run engine:verify` passes.
- [ ] No production pacing constant is changed.
- [ ] A shared, load-tolerant `waitForCondition` helper is added under
      `core/tests/helpers/` (sibling to `waitForScene.ts`) — the module
      docblock documents the `nominal cap + starvation margin` model.
- [ ] At least one unit test covers the new helper's budget derivation
      (`capMs` nominal, `starvationFactor`, `floorMs`), so the guard test
      above is part of the suite.

# Export the end-of-turn income-collection cap as a named constant

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Give the test suite one importable source of truth for the 16 000 ms safety cap
that the Enter-to-end-turn wait races, so the wait can be *derived* instead of
guessed — and so the 15 000 ms-vs-16 000 ms mismatch becomes structurally
impossible.

## Scope

1. Add `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS = 16_000` to `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`
   (the existing single source of truth for income choreography timing, already
   exported to tests), with a docblock stating it is the bounded safety cap that
   forces the day start / forced dialog if the income choreography never clears
   `incomeCollectionActive` (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5, AC7).
2. Replace the three inline `s.time.now + 16_000` literals in
   `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (lines ~432, ~616, ~782) with
   the named constant.
3. Default `incomeCollectionCapMs` in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`
   (line ~219, `?? 16_000`) to the named constant; keep the competitive override
   (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) untouched.
4. Unit test (game `unit` project) asserting the four consumers agree with the
   exported constant — e.g. a new exported accessor
   `getDefaultIncomeCollectionCapMs()` in `MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`
   (returns the default) plus a source-constant assertion, and a guard that the
   three turn-flow deferral sites use `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` rather than a
   literal (source scan in `tests/tooling/` or `tests/main-street/`).

## Scope (out)

- Changing the cap value (no production pacing change — parent constraint).
- Touch-tooling refactors of the three duplicated deferral blocks.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`
- `tests/main-street/` or `tests/tooling/` (new unit test)

## Constraints

- Value stays exactly 16 000 ms; behaviour, timings and deferral semantics are
  unchanged (pure constant extraction).
- `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` is a constants-only module ("No runtime logic") —
  keep it logic-free.
- Vitest `unit` project (not browser) for the guard: it must stay cheap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` is exported from
      `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` with a docblock naming the
      deferral it bounds and its feature id.
- [ ] No `16_000` literal remains in the three `startAt = s.time.now + ...`
      deferral sites in `MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, nor in the
      `incomeCollectionCapMs` default in `MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts`.
- [ ] A unit test imports the constant and fails if any consumer's default or
      deferral cap diverges from it (no restated literal in the test).
- [ ] `npm run build` (tsc + vite) and the affected unit suite pass via
      `/skill:test`; production pacing behaviour is unchanged.

# Guard browser-test wait budgets against production caps

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Land the cheap unit guard and the budget-model documentation **before** the waits
are adopted, so the "a wait may never be shorter than the cap it races" invariant
exists in the suite first. This child is the test-first half of the adoption.

## Scope

1. `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` (node `unit` project — cheap, not the
   serial browser project):

   ```ts
   import { resolveWaitBudget } from '@core-tests/helpers/waitForCondition';
   import { INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS } from '../../src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming';
   import { DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS } from '../../src/scenes/MainStreetConstants';
   ```

   Assertions:
   - `resolveWaitBudget({ capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS }) > INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`;
   - `resolveWaitBudget({ capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS }) > DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS`;
   - each derived budget plus the documented boot allowance (the 20 000 ms
     `waitForScene` default) stays within the 60 000 ms browser `testTimeout`,
     so the wait always fails with its own label rather than the hook timeout;
   - the production caps are the values the tests document (16 000 /
     1 500) *only* as an assertion input derived from the imports — never as a
     restated budget literal.
2. Comment block in the guard explaining the model (`nominal cap + starvation
   margin`), why it exists (rAF starvation under host CPU contention; the retry
   runner does not retry `waitForCondition` timeouts — one spike fails the gate),
   and links to the precedent waits (`incident-reveal.browser.test.ts`
   `4_000 + 16_000`, `income-collection.browser.test.ts` `PHASED_SHOW_MS + 16000`).

## Scope (out)

- Editing `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` (the adoption child does that and
  extends this guard with its source scan).
- Deriving every other wait in the browser suite (explicit parent non-goal).
- Introducing a separate budget-constants module: the shared helper's `capMs`
  API **is** the derivation surface, so there is no second list to keep in sync.

## Key Files

- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the shared helper (`core/tests/helpers/waitForCondition.ts`).
- Blocked by the exported `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` constant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` imports both production caps and
      the helper's `resolveWaitBudget`; it restates no budget literal.
- [x] It fails if a derived budget is not strictly greater than its production
      cap (verified by temporarily raising a cap in a scratch run — not committed).
- [x] It asserts the derived budget plus the documented boot allowance stays
      within the 60 000 ms browser `testTimeout`.
- [x] It lives in the node `unit` project (`.test.ts`, not `.browser.test.ts`) and
      runs in well under a second.
- [x] `/skill:test --type unit` (changed scope) passes.
- [x] A regression guard fails the build if any browser-test wait budget is
      smaller than the production cap it is documented as racing — the guard
      imports the cap constants rather than restating literals.

# Adopt derived wait budgets in MainStreetScene browser test

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Remove the two load-sensitive literals from the browser test and consume the
shared, cap-derived helper — so the Enter-to-end-turn and buy-to-hand waits can
never again be shorter than the production caps they race.

## Scope

1. In `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`:

   - import `waitForCondition` from `@core-tests/helpers/waitForCondition`, plus
     `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming`) and
     `DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS` (`src/scenes/MainStreetConstants`);
   - `allows pressing Enter to end the turn when legal`:
     `waitForCondition(() => scene.state.turn > beforeTurn, { capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS, intervalMs: 100, label: 'turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation' })`
     — replaces `{ timeoutMs: 15_000, ... }`;
   - `only materializes purchased cards at destination after transfer animation completes`:
     `{ capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS, label: 'business bought to hand' }`;
   - the sibling `first business bought to hand` wait (same 6 000 ms, same
     transfer cap) uses `capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS` too;
   - the `hand card selected for placement` wait has no production cap to race
     (UI transition) — leave its budget, but keep it out of the guard's scope.
2. The file keeps its local `waitForCondition` for every other wait (explicit
   non-goal: no wholesale migration of the 49 copies). Mark the local copy
   `@deprecated` in a comment pointing at the shared helper.
3. Extend `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` with a source scan of
   `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`: for each documented label, the surrounding
   wait call must pass `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` /
   `capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS` and must not pass a `timeoutMs`
   literal — so `timeoutMs: 15_000` / `timeoutMs: 6000` cannot be reintroduced
   for those waits.
4. Update the in-test comments to explain the derivation (replace "allow the
   engine to process" with the cap + starvation-margin rationale).
5. Verify with `/skill:test` (browser project for the file, unit project for the
   guard). No ad-hoc `npx vitest` runs.

## Scope (out)

- Production code changes (previous child).
- Changing any other test's waits.

## Key Files

- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` (extended)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait passes
      `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` to the shared helper; no `15_000` /
      `timeoutMs` literal remains for it, and its budget is strictly greater than
      the 16 000 ms cap (helper invariant).
- [ ] The `business bought to hand` and `first business bought to hand` waits pass
      `capMs: DRAG_TRANSFER_DURATION_MAX_MS`; no `6000` / `timeoutMs` literal
      remains for them.
- [ ] The guard's source scan fails if either literal (or a mismatched cap
      constant) is reintroduced for the documented labels.
- [ ] `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`
      passes when invoked through `/skill:test` (or the project's soak type), and

- [ ] No other test in the file changes its wait semantics.

- [ ] The `business bought to hand` wait in the same file is derived from the

# Document the load-tolerant browser wait budget model

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Make the new budgeting rule discoverable so future browser tests derive their
waits instead of guessing, and so the next 15 000-vs-16 000 mismatch is caught in
review rather than in a red gate.

## Scope

1. `docs/dev/testing.md` — new subsection under the browser project guidance
   ("Load-tolerant wait budgets"), covering:
   - the problem: browser tests race Phaser `requestAnimationFrame` tweens and
     bounded scene deferrals; under host CPU contention rAF starves and nominal
     durations stretch;
   - the rule: **never hard-code a wait for an animation-gated outcome** — pass
     `capMs` (the production cap) to the shared helper, which derives
     `budget = max(capMs * starvationFactor, capMs + floorMs)`;
   - the invariant: the derived budget is strictly greater than the cap, enforced
     by `resolveWaitBudget` and by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`;
   - the 60 000 ms `testTimeout` headroom rule (budget + boot allowance);
   - why "accept the flake" is not an option here: the retry runner
     (`core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts`) retries only the three transient
     contention signatures, not a `waitForCondition` timeout.
2. Code comments: the helper's module docblock (cross-check it matches the docs),
   `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`'s docblock, and the two adopted waits in
   `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`.
3. `docs/dev/testing.md` soak evidence section: how to run the soak
   (`/skill:test --type soak`, or the script it wraps) and how to read its
   summary, so a future flake has a reproduction path.
4. Check for other documentation that states the old fixed budgets (grep `15_000`,
   `15000`, `6_000`, `waitForCondition`) and update the game-facing pacing notes
   (`docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`) only if they assert test-budget numbers —
   do **not** change production pacing documentation.

## Scope (out)

- README.md edits unless it actually documents test-wait budgets (verify first;
  if it does not, record that finding in the completion comment instead of
  padding the README).
- Wiki/docs-site regeneration beyond the existing docs pipeline (`docs/` is the
  VitePress source; do not edit `docs/.vitepress/dist/`).

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/testing.md`
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (only if it states test budgets)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` (docblock cross-check)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the adoption child (documents the final shape, not the interim one).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/dev/testing.md` documents the `nominal cap + starvation margin`
      model, the `capMs` API, the strict-greater-than invariant, the 60 000 ms
      headroom rule, and why retries are not a substitute.
- [ ] The docs name the guard test and the soak command an implementer should
      run, with the exact commands.
- [ ] A grep for `15_000`/`15000`/`6_000` in `docs/` and `tests/` shows no
      remaining statement of the old budgets for these two waits.
- [ ] README/docs-site statement: either updated, or the "no budget guidance
      there" finding is recorded in the completion comment.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README (or a recorded finding that it documents no test
      budgets), and the `docs/` testing guidance.

# Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run

Parent: MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — make `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` waits load-tolerant.

## Goal

Turn "20 consecutive local runs pass, including at least one under imposed CPU
load" from an anecdote into a repeatable, policy-compliant soak with recorded
evidence — so the parent AC is proven, not assumed.

## Scope

1. `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh` (game repo `scripts/`) — soak harness:
   - loops `--runs N` (default 20) invoking the project's canonical browser
     runner, `npx tsx core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts --project browser
     tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`, so the retry/hang
     semantics match the real gate;
   - `--load` mode: spins up `$(nproc)` CPU burners for the duration of the run,
     records `loadavg` before/during/after, and tears them down on exit (trap);
   - aborts on the first failure (fail-fast, prints the failing run's output);
   - per-run wall time, pass/fail and peak load average in a markdown summary
     written to `results/soak-browser-waits-<timestamp>.md`; exit non-zero if any
     run fails.
2. `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — add a project-local `soak` type
   whose command is `bash scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh --runs 20`, so the soak is
   an agent-initiated run that goes **through the test skill**
   (`/skill:test --type soak`) per the test-execution policy, instead of an ad-hoc
   loop of `npx vitest`. This is the documented extension mechanism
   (`docs/dev/skill-extensions.md`); keep the edit to that single file and record
   it as an intentional, in-scope config addition (do not otherwise touch `.pi/`).
3. Execute the soak: one quiet-host run of 20 consecutive passes, then at least
   one `--load` run. Run it as a background job per the background-job etiquette
   (launch → prepare docs/review → single completion-aware wait via
   `wait_for_job.py`, no fixed `sleep` polling).
4. Comment the evidence on this child and on the parent: run count, load
   averages, per-run durations, summary-file path, and any anomaly.

## Scope (out)

- Improving the retry runner's transient classification (separate concern; record
  as `discovered-from` if the soak reveals a genuine transient signature gap).
- Soaking any other browser file.

## Key Files

- `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh` (new)
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` (new `soak` type)
- `results/soak-browser-waits-*.md` (generated; confirm `results/` is gitignored —
  if it is not, write summaries to an already-ignored path instead)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the adoption child.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `scripts/soak-browser-waits.sh --runs 20` exits 0 after 20 consecutive
      passes of `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`, and exits
      non-zero on the first failing run.
- [x] `--load` mode imposes CPU load (≥ `nproc` burners, load average recorded),
      is cleaned up via `trap`, and at least one full under-load pass is recorded.
- [x] The soak is runnable through `/skill:test --type soak` (project-local test
      type), not by an ad-hoc `npx vitest` loop.
- [x] Evidence comment on this child and on the parent states runs, passes,
      load averages, wall times, and the summary path.
- [x] No flake was accepted: any failing run is triaged before the child closes.
- [x] Reliability proven, not assumed: at least 20 consecutive local runs of
      `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`
      pass (through the project soak type), including at least one run under
      imposed CPU load.
- [x] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes:
      `/skill:test` (`--type full`) is green at the end of the chain and the
      evidence is recorded on the parent.
