# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation
   completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round
   — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned,
   income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category
   (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins /
   reputation / score. The next shared day does **not** start until the player
   clicks **[ Next Turn ]**. Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven
   paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive
   close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on
   `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so
   every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the
   single-player ledger. Additions are optional/backwards-compatible —
   `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the
   headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the
   Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive
   scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours);
   **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an
   explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that
   MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay
   conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in
   `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`,
   `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.
4. Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in
   the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing
   and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the
   engine/headless close path. Checkpoint save ordering
   (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged; the
   dialog adds no save and mutates no state.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value (Phaser-free model tests for
   owner-keyed rows, engine per-seat ledger tests, and a competitive-mode
   browser dialog test); **all related documentation is updated**
   (docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md competitive closing section and the end-of-turn
   summary section, plus any README/dev references); **the full project test
   suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Blocked-by MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (outbound dependency): the parent item is
  still `open` (stage `intake_complete`) — its `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger
  does **not exist in the code yet**. This item builds on and consumes that
  ledger; implementers must land/coordinate with the parent first. Per-seat
  expense capture does not exist anywhere today — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  returns `void` and only logs — so the per-seat ledger extension is real
  engine work on top of the parent's ledger shape (kept optional and
  backwards-compatible throughout).
- Presentation-only contract: the dialog reads committed state / `result` and
  never mutates engine state or consumes RNG. In competitive, deltas are
  already applied to each `PlayerRecord` before the closing is presented, so
  the panel shows post-round values; the checkpoint save stays in
  `presentCompetitiveDayTail` (existing ordering).
- Overlay conventions (AGENTS.md UI best practices) exactly as the parent
  item constrains: `createOverlayBackground` + `createOverlayButton` from
  `@ui`; elements parented into `s.hudContainer`; depths 199 / 200 / 201;
  everything pushed into `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal; instant appearance
  (reduced-motion safe); button SFX via `safePlaySound`.
- Headless determinism and bounded pacing must not regress: Monte-Carlo /
  AI headless days (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`)
  never invoke the scene presentation and must never show/block on the dialog;
  the competitive closing bound (`COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`) stays.
- **Assumption (Q-scope, from repo evidence):** a "round" equals **one
  completed shared day** — all non-eliminated seats finished and the shared
  closing ran. The engine has no separate "round" concept beyond the shared
  day (`round-robin` seat iteration only), so "one panel per completed round"
  = one dialog per shared day.
- **Assumption (blocking safety):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one device
  (no networked multiplayer), so a blocking dialog gated on the single human
  seat cannot stall other humans. Interactive Q1 = A.
- The parent item's banking-hint ordering assumption is single-player-only and
  does not apply to the competitive panel (no banking-hint step exists in the
  competitive closing).
- `TurnResult` / `OwnerIncomeResult` additions must not break competitive
  callers (`MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing`,
  `perSeatClosingSummary`, scoreboard/HUD consumers) — keep ledger fields
  optional/absent-undefined-safe and guard with tests.

## Existing state

- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`):
  ends the human's MarketPhase, drives AI seats to the shared closing, runs
  `runCompetitiveClosing`, then `presentCompetitiveDayTail` →
  station checkpoint save → `presentCompetitiveClosing(closing, () =>
  startTurnPhase())`. The new gate slots at the end of the closing
  presentation, before `startTurnPhase` (presentation path only).
- `TurnResult.playerIncome?: OwnerIncomeResult[]` **already exists**
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`): owner-keyed income, non-eliminated seats,
  in seat order, populated by `applyCompetitiveIncome`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`, through `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`
  in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`). Each entry carries
  `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` (base / synergy / reputation /
  events / upcoming slots per owner).
- Per-seat ongoing costs are computed in `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) — staff salaries per owner, community +
  business running costs per slot owner via `ownerTaggedGrid` — but are
  **not surfaced** on any result (void, log-only). Businesses owned per seat
  are derivable from `ownerTaggedGrid` / `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`).
- Per-seat row conventions exist in `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`): `You` / `AI n` labels,
  `resolveSeatColour` seat colours, coin/rep/score columns — reused by the
  Game Over overlay model `MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`.
- Overlay precedent and single-player dialog model come from
  MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (its `MainStreetTurnSummary` model +
  `showTurnSummaryDialog`); docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md documents the
  competitive closing presentation (section "Competitive phase-major closing
  presentation …"), including the current auto-advance behaviour that this
  item changes.

## Desired change

1. Engine: capture and surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult` —
   per-owner ongoing expenses (staff / community / business), businesses
   owned, net coin change — extending the `OwnerIncomeResult` shape (or the
   parent's owner-keyed ledger) inside `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` /
   `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`; keep everything optional so
   single-player, N=1 and headless calls are untouched.
2. Model: extend the single-player Phaser-free `MainStreetTurnSummary` to
   render **owner-keyed competitive rows** (seat label + colour from the
   competitive scoreboard conventions) for the round just closed.
3. UI: extend the single-player `showTurnSummaryDialog(...)` (or a thin
   competitive sibling sharing the same panel) with **[ Next Turn ]**
   (primary) and a **disabled [ Bank Loan ]** button behind the shared wiring
   seam; gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` so the deferred
   (animations-enabled) path presents the dialog when the closing completes
   and only calls `startTurnPhase` after **[ Next Turn ]** — reduced-motion /
   replay / headless keep today's auto-advance.
4. Tests and docs: Phaser-free model tests, engine per-seat ledger tests, a
   competitive browser dialog test; update docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md
   (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections).

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — gate `presentCompetitiveDayTail` on the dialog (between closing-complete and `startTurnPhase`); presentation path only
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` / `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`: surface the per-seat round ledger on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts`: return/capture the per-owner expense breakdown (staff / community / business)
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — extend `TurnResult` (and/or `OwnerIncomeResult`) with the optional owner-keyed round ledger (expenses, businesses owned, net change)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` / `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — `OwnerIncomeResult` shape extension
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — extend the Phaser-free summary model to render owner-keyed competitive rows (reusing scoreboard label/colour conventions)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` + `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — dialog presentation + delegation (shared with the single-player panel); `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` per overlay conventions
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — reuse `You` / `AI n` labels, `resolveSeatColour` colours for rows
- Docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive closing + end-of-turn summary sections)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` (pure model), `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` (engine), `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` (competitive overlay)

## Related work

### Automated related-work report (`find_related.py`)

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary dialog (single-player seed)
  (open)
- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG** – Bank Loans (open)
- **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ** – Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove
  single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback
  (completed)
- Repository matches: `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `core/AGENTS.md`,
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (keyword overlap: competitive,
  ledger, end-of-turn, dialog, seat, round, businesses).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "turn summary competitive"` returned only the
  parent, the deferred Bank Loans seam and End of game stats — **no
  overlapping completed item**; no duplicate/partial-overlap rewrite needed.

### Hand-curated context

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — **parent / blocked-by**: single-player End of Turn
  summary dialog + `TurnResult` owner-keyed ledger; this item's panel consumes
  that ledger and the parent's overlay/model. Not yet implemented (open,
  intake_complete) — ordering constraint.
- `MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG` — **Bank Loans**: the seam this item's disabled Bank
  Loan button exposes; enablement blocked by that item (shared with
  single-player panel).
- `MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` — **End of game stats** (open, low): turn-by-turn
  history + graphs on Game Over; consumes the same per-turn ledger data
  (synergy, not duplication — distinct screen).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (completed) — end-of-turn presentation refactor:
  source of today's `closingSummary` / shared closing primitive.
- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` + `MS-0MUYFXA36009EMH0` (completed) — competitive
  per-seat income choreography and per-seat animated closing: the cadence this
  panel extends; `TurnResult.playerIncome` originates here.
- `MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM` (completed) — game-over overlay epic: the
  Phaser-free-model + overlay-convention precedent (`MainStreetGameOverSummary`
  reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (round = day):** "one panel per completed round" maps to one
  panel per completed shared day (every seat finished + closing ran); the
  engine has no separate round concept. Recorded from repo evidence; if a
  day-vs-round distinction exists conceptually (e.g. a preset defining round
  length), the panel cadence would need revisiting — flagged for implementer
  verification.
- **Assumption (single human seat):** competitive is human-vs-AI on one
  device, so a blocking dialog on the human's **[ Next Turn ]** cannot stall
  other humans; multifloored safety holds for the current product shape.
  (If networked multiplayer ever lands, blocking semantics need a per-seat
  pause protocol.)
- **Risk (parent not landed):** the owner-keyed ledger this item consumes does
  not exist yet; if the parent lands without the per-seat expense capture
  (today `void`/log-only), this item must extend it — keep additions optional
  and guarded so `presentCompetitiveClosing` and headless/Monte-Carlo flows are
  byte-stable when absent.
- **Risk (blocking regresses headless pacing):** the gate must live in the
  scene presentation tail only (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`), never in engine
  close functions; Monte-Carlo / AI headless days never touch the scene and
  must continue to auto-advance under `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
- **Risk (eliminated seats):** the closing already omits eliminated seats from
  `playerIncome`; the panel must render exactly the seats the closing surfaced
  (no ghost rows for bankrupt/eliminated seats) and say so in its test.
- **Risk (loans are per-owner):** the shared disabled Bank Loan seam is a
  single hook today; when MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG lands, competitive loans are
  likely per-seat — keep the seam shaped so it can become
  `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` without re-plumbing the panel.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-round history across days (post-game stats,
  MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV), networked multiplayer, live loans
  (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) and any round-summary log/graph features are outside
  this item; tracked as linked items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Blocking behaviour — in single-player the dialog blocks the next-day
  advance until [ Next Turn ] is clicked; in competitive the day currently
  auto-advances after the closing presentation. Options: A) Block like
  single-player — next day starts only after [ Next Turn ]. B) Non-blocking —
  panel appears but the day advances behind it / auto-dismisses."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — consistency
  with the single-player dialog; accepted as chosen.)
- Q2: "Per-seat data source — per-seat expenses aren't captured anywhere
  today (TurnResult.playerIncome covers income only). Options: A) Extend the
  engine with an owner-keyed per-seat ledger on TurnResult (per-seat ongoing
  costs, businesses owned, net change — engine-computed, testable headless),
  mirroring the parent's ledger. B) Derive presentation-only at panel time
  from committed state."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — matches the
  parent item's owner-keyed ledger design intent; accepted as chosen.)
- Q3: "Bank Loan button parity — the single-player dialog renders a disabled
  [ Bank Loan ] button with a wiring seam for MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG. Options:
  A) Same disabled Bank Loan button in the competitive panel (parity).
  B) Omit it — strictly the seed's content."
  — Answer (operator): "A". Source: interactive reply, intake session
  MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI, 2026-10-25. (Recommended option was A — one shared
  loans seam avoids divergent affordances; accepted as chosen.)

# Make the composed engine explicit: fail loudly when a worktree's `./core` is stale

**Headline:** Every in-repo test invocation currently composes whatever `./core` happens to be checked out (worktrees keep the gitlink they were created from, silently behind the engine pin), so a green run can hide engine regressions. Add a fast, offline preflight to the test entry path that names the composed engine SHA and fails loudly when `./core` is behind (or diverged from) `configs/engine-pin.json`, then document the composition matrix.

## Problem statement

`npm test`, the changed-scope `npx vitest run <files>` gate and the dev-push browser gate all compose the `./core` submodule exactly as checked out; nothing in the test path verifies *which* engine that is. Worktrees created by `implement.py` only run `git submodule update --init --recursive`, which checks out the gitlink recorded by the commit the worktree was branched from — a commit that silently predates the engine pin. Observed in this repo: `.worklog/worktrees/wl-MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT-*/core` at `e4d0e10b` (`v0.1.21-6`) and `.worklog/worktrees/f7-competitive-before-85d23dbb/core` at `8c602332` (`v0.1.20-39`), both behind the pinned `9ee194e0` and the `1c9900a1` dev tip. Only `npm run build` / `build:electron` (via `engine:sync`) advance a worktree's `core`.

## Users

- **Implement agent — user story:** "As an implement agent working in a fresh worktree, I need my first test run to tell me the engine it composed is stale and how to fix it, instead of returning a green suite that never saw the pinned engine code."
- **Release/producer — user story:** "As a producer reviewing a green suite, I need each run to record the engine SHA it composed, so a green result is evidence about a known engine, not an anonymous one."
- **Maintainer — user story:** "As a maintainer I need the composition matrix (test run vs build vs release verify vs fresh worktree) written down in one place, so 'which engine did this test?' has a single documented answer."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Offline preflight on the test path.** A fast (target < 1 s), network-free preflight runs for every Vitest invocation in this repo — `npm test`, changed-scope `npx vitest run <files>` and `npx vitest run --project browser` — and fails the run loudly, naming the composed SHA, the pin SHA and the remediation, when `./core` is **not** the pin and **not** a descendant of the pin (behind or diverged), when the pin commit is absent from the local `./core` clone, or when `./core` is uninitialised/empty. A dirty `./core` is reported loudly but does not fail (composition is still identifiable). Deliberate bypass is `ENGINE_CHECKOUT_CHECK=warn|off`, logged every time it is used. The wiring is a documented local surgical addition to `vite.config.ts` (that file is auto-generated from the engine-owned `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) and is held in place by a drift-guard test, so a re-scaffold cannot silently drop the gate. Verified by unit tests over temp-git fixtures plus a manual stale-worktree reproduction.
- **AC2 — The composed engine is explicit.** A passing preflight records the composed engine identity (short SHA plus `git describe` tag when available) alongside the pin, so any green suite states which engine it composed — at most one identical line per process, even when several Vitest projects (each `extends: true`) trigger the global setup, and verified by a unit test asserting the rendered line through an injected logger.
- **AC3 — Composition matrix documented.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` gains a composition matrix covering: `npm test` / changed-scope / dev-push browser gate → checkout present, preflight must accept it (pin or descendant); `npm run build` / `build:electron` → dev head after `engine:sync`; `npm run build:release` → detached at the pin after `engine:verify`; a freshly created worktree → whatever gitlink its branch recorded, until `engine:sync` runs. `docs/dev/testing.md` documents the preflight in the `npm test` pipeline, and README/DEPLOYMENT note it where they describe the submodule and the test command. Code comments in the new module state the rules and their rationale.
- **AC4 — Existing engine contract tests stay green.** `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` (dirty guard, pin mismatch, release pin contract) still passes unchanged, and the new preflight tests cover: pin → pass, ahead-of-pin (post-`engine:sync` dev head) → pass, behind pin → fail with remediation, pin commit missing locally → fail, uninitialised `core` → fail, documented bypass env var → warning path.
- **AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** The VitePress site under `docs/` is generated from these Markdown pages, so updating them updates the published site; no separate docs-site entry exists or is required.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **In-repo scope only.** `implement.py` (worktree creation, the framework's `_ensure_submodules`) lives in SorraAgents, and `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` is engine-owned and must never be hand-edited from here. The refresh-at-worktree-creation half of the original AC is therefore out of scope for this repo and is recorded as a follow-up (see Risks); this item delivers the *fails-loudly* half, which is entirely in-repo.
- **Offline by default.** The preflight must not fetch, not contact the remote, and not depend on a cached `origin/dev` ref: worktrees routinely have stale refs and airgapped runs must still gate. Reachability from the pin is therefore decided from the local commit graph (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), not from the branch tip.
- **Fast and fail-fast.** The check must be cheap enough to sit in front of every Vitest run, including the changed-scope gate, which runs per test file group.
- **No CI beyond the npm builds** (MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED) — the test path *is* the gate, so the check must live there, not in a workflow file.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `package.json`: `"test": "tsx scripts/run-tests.ts --timeout-ms 720000 --project unit --project unit-cli"`, `"pretest": "tsx src/scripts/check-playwright-chromium.ts"`, `"build": "npm run engine:sync && tsc --noEmit && vite build"`, `"engine:sync"`/`"engine:verify"` wrap `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`.
- `vite.config.ts` defines three Vitest projects (`unit-cli`, `unit`, `browser`) at the root config; there is **no** `globalSetup` today, so a config-level setup is the one place that covers every invocation, including direct `npx vitest run` calls. It is **auto-generated** by the engine-owned `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, so the accepted pattern for local changes is a documented "LOCAL SURGICAL ADDITION" header comment plus a drift-guard test (existing precedents: `CLI_TEST_FILES` / `unit-cli`, the `sequence.groupOrder` split, `projectCoverageReporter` — guarded by `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts` and `tests/main-street/testing-docs-projects.test.ts`).
- Precedent for the pattern: `src/scripts/check-playwright-chromium.ts` is a sub-second, network-free `pretest` pre-check with injectable dependencies and printed remediation (MS-0MVJPV0BV000LSLW), documented in `docs/dev/testing.md` § "npm test".
- Fixture precedent: `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` builds network-free temp git repos (`makeGame()`: engine repo on `dev` + game repo with a `core` submodule and a pin file) via `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`.
- Current repo state (evidence): pin `9ee194e0`, committed gitlink `9ee194e0`, `origin/dev` cached ref `1c9900a1` (pin is an ancestor, 2 commits behind), six worktree `core` checkouts behind at `09723c4b`/`7e43108c`/`e4d0e10b`/`8c602332`.

## Desired change

1. **New preflight module** (e.g. `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`) exporting a pure `checkEngineCheckout({ repoRoot, env, deps })` that returns `{ ok, composedSha, pinSha, describe, reason, message }`. Rules: pass when `HEAD === pin` or `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pin> <HEAD>`; fail when behind/diverged, when `<pin>` is not present in the local `core` clone, or when `core` has no `HEAD`; warn (not fail) on a dirty `core`. Bypass via `ENGINE_CHECKOUT_CHECK=warn|off` (logged every time it is used).
2. **Wire it once, for every project**: register it as Vitest's `globalSetup` in the root `test` config so `npm test`, the changed-scope gate and browser runs all pass through it, and expose it as `npm run engine:check` for manual/CI use. (Alternative wiring — a second `pretest` command — covers only `npm test`; the config-level setup is preferred because the changed-scope gate invokes Vitest directly.)
3. **Tests** (offline, temp-git fixtures in the style of `engine-submodule-sync.test.ts`): pin pass, ahead-of-pin pass, behind fail, missing-pin-object fail, uninitialised `core` fail, bypass env var behaviour, and the message text carrying both SHAs plus the `npm run engine:sync` remediation.
4. **Docs**: composition matrix in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`; preflight description in `docs/dev/testing.md`; short notes in `README.md` (submodule/checkout section) and `DEPLOYMENT.md` (test/build commands).

**Order of work (test-first):** write the offline fixture tests (item 3) against the agreed contract *first*, then the
preflight module (item 1), then the wiring plus its drift guard (item 2), then the docs (item 4). Keep
`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` green throughout.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts` — New: pure checker plus the Vitest `globalSetup` entry point.
- `tests/main-street/engine-checkout-precheck.test.ts` — New: offline fixture tests for every pass/fail branch (AC1/AC4).
- `tests/main-street/vite-config-engine-check-guard.test.ts` — New: drift guard (precedent `tests/main-street/vitest-cli-project-isolation.test.ts`, `testing-docs-projects.test.ts`) asserting `vite.config.ts` still registers the precheck as root `test.globalSetup` and `package.json` still exposes `engine:check`, so an engine re-scaffold cannot silently drop the gate (AC1).
- `vite.config.ts` — Wire `test.globalSetup` to the precheck so every project and every direct Vitest run is gated.
- `package.json` — Add `engine:check` script (manual invocation, same code path); keep `pretest` unchanged.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — New "Composition matrix" section: which engine each invocation composes and which gate applies.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — Document the preflight in the `npm test` pipeline and the changed-scope caveat.
- `README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — Point at the preflight where the submodule and the test/build commands are described.
- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — Unchanged, but must stay green (regression guard on the pin contract).

**Reuse (do not re-implement):** `readPin` and `submoduleIsDirty` are already exported by the engine-owned
`core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (import via the `@core-scripts/engine-sync.mjs` alias, as
`tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` does). The precheck should consume those rather than re-parse
`configs/engine-pin.json` or re-run `git status`. **Do not edit** `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` or
`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — both are engine-owned (repo boundary rule).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — acceptance window.** "Pin or descendant of the pin" is chosen over "pin only" and over "reachable from `origin/dev`": a descendant contains the pinned engine, so the stale-engine hazard is gone, while an unrefreshed `origin/dev` ref cannot produce a false failure. A pin-only rule would reject the post-`npm run build` checkout that the dev workflow deliberately creates.
- **Assumption — scope of the fix.** The refresh-at-worktree-creation option is out of this repo's boundary (framework + engine-owned scripts); the fails-loudly option satisfies the same AC user-visibly and is fully testable here. Follow-up (not filed by this item): have `implement.py`'s `_ensure_submodules` run `engine:sync` (network-tolerant, best-effort) so worktrees start current.
- **Risk — first-run friction.** Agents in existing stale worktrees will now fail every test run until they run `npm run engine:sync` (needs network). Mitigation: the failure message names the exact remediation, the bypass env var exists for deliberate cases, and the docs matrix explains it. Expect a burst of loud failures in the oldest worktrees.
- **Risk — false failure if the pin is rewritten out of the engine's history** (force-push/rebase upstream). Mitigation: the failure message distinguishes "pin commit not present in this clone" from "behind the pin", and the check never fetches.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Adjacent items (pin lag, spurious gitlink staging in releases, pin/tip policy) are separate work items and are *not* folded in here; they are linked below instead.
- **Assumption — dirty `core` is a warning, not a failure.** Composition remains identifiable; the clobber guard belongs to `engine:sync`/`engine:verify`.
- **Risk — test-path coupling.** A shared `globalSetup` that throws turns every suite red at once if the precheck itself is buggy. Mitigation: pure checker with unit tests over fixtures (no dependency on this repo's live `core` state in the tests), a documented bypass env var, and the manual `npm run engine:check` path for diagnosis.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX** — "Engine pin lags the core dev tip, so engine:verify throws PIN MISMATCH" (`intake_complete`): establishes the *pin tracks the dev tip* policy and the mechanical re-pin. This item consumes that pin but does not change it; if the pin is stale, the preflight still passes for a pin-descendant checkout.
- **MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57** — "Release derived-files step commits a spurious core submodule bump…" (`intake_complete`): the *other* direction of submodule drift (gitlink moved by the build during release). Both items concern "the tree you test/build is not the engine you claim"; keep the fixes disjoint.
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** — the build-scripts-decide-the-engine decision that `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` implement; the composition matrix extends its documentation.
- **MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F** (completed) — the historical dev-HEAD pin/pointer mismatch (`engine-pin.json` vs `core` gitlink); the closest prior instance of "the recorded engine and the composed engine disagree".
- **MS-0MVJPV0BV000LSLW** — precedent for the fast, offline, remediation-printing pre-check pattern (`check-playwright-chromium.ts`).
- **MS-0MVK37SK5009M0NG** (completed) — the project-coverage guard; its H3 hypothesis "stale `core` submodule state" is the same hazard this item makes explicit.
- Docs: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`, `docs/dev/testing.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `README.md`; code: `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts`.

A machine-generated "Related work (automated report)" section is appended to this description by the `find-related` skill (top matches, ranked by keyword overlap); it is regenerated on every run and is not hand-edited.

## Plan review record

Planning was **decomposed-skip** (effort Small / risk Low, per `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed`): the item is one
deliverable and is implemented directly, so no child work items were created. The six automated review stages ran over
the existing content.

| Stage | Checked | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Requirements & AC alignment | Each of AC1–AC6 traced to the Desired change / Users / Constraints sections | AC1 gained the documented bypass env var and the "wiring survives re-scaffold" clause (both were only in Desired change / Risks, so the ACs understated them). AC2 reworded to "at most one identical line per process" because every Vitest project `extends: true` and may each trigger the global setup. |
| 2. Completeness | Required fields, `**Key Files:**` syntax (`validate_key_files_format` → no issues) and accuracy vs the real tree | Added the missing drift-guard test to Key Files; added a **Reuse** note (`readPin` / `submoduleIsDirty` are already exported by `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`); recorded that `vite.config.ts` is auto-generated by the engine-owned scaffold, so the change is a surgical addition + guard, not a template edit. |
| 3. Sequencing & dependencies | Test-before-implementation ordering; dependency edges (none — single leaf item) | Added an explicit test-first **Order of work**; no dependency edges needed. |
| 4. Scope sizing | One deliverable increment? | Yes — Small (~9–13 h), one module + wiring + guard + docs; no child items warranted. |
| 5. Acceptance & testability | Every AC pass/fail and drivable from the test suite | All ACs are now testable: pure checker over temp-git fixtures, injected logger for the identity line, drift guard for wiring. The one non-automated clause ("manual stale-worktree reproduction", AC1) is kept as a manual confirmation step. |
| 6. Polish & handoff | Clarity, formatting, executability | Description restructured only where the review added content; existing sections kept intact. |

**Plan: changelog** — 2026-10-25: six review stages applied (AC1, AC2, Key Files, Existing state, Desired change); no
children created; stage advanced to `plan_complete`. Open question for the producer: none blocking — the follow-up to
refresh `./core` at worktree creation (framework-side `implement.py`) stays out of scope per Constraints.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**No producer interview was required** — the seed context (observed SHAs, failure mode, ACs and documentation targets) was sufficient to draft the brief. The open choices in the seed AC were resolved by repository investigation; each is recorded here for producer review.

- Q: "Refresh each worktree's `core` at creation/entry, or fail loudly when a worktree's `core` is neither the pin nor dev-tip-reachable?" — Answer (agent, from repository investigation): **fail loudly in the test path**. Research: worktree creation is `_ensure_submodules` in `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents, outside this repo's boundary), and `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` is engine-owned ("never edit a game-repo copy by hand" — `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`). Only the in-repo fails-loudly half is implementable here; recorded as a follow-up in Risks. Source: `implement.py:1819-1870`, `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`, repo boundary rule in AGENTS.md.
- Q: "What is an acceptable composed engine — pin only, or pin plus anything reachable from the dev tip?" — Answer (agent): **pin, or any descendant of the pin**; never behind, never diverged. Research: the practical dev flow (`npm run build` → `engine:sync`) leaves `./core` *ahead* of the pin, so a pin-only rule would fail the documented dev workflow; an `origin/dev` reachability rule would false-fail on the stale refs worktrees actually have (cached ref here is `1c9900a1` while `core` checkouts range down to `09723c4b`). Source: `package.json` build scripts, `git -C core` ref survey.
- Q: "How should the preflight behave offline / without a cached dev ref?" — Answer (agent): **never fetch**; decide from the local commit graph, and fail with a distinct message when the pin object is absent from the local `core` clone (remediation: `npm run engine:sync`, needs network). Source: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` offline-fallback note; the observed mix of stale worktree checkouts.
- Q: "Where should the gate live so it covers the gates that actually run?" — Answer (agent): **Vitest root `test.globalSetup`**, plus `npm run engine:check`. Research: `.pi/test-config.json` suiteCommands run `npm --silent test` *and* a direct `npx vitest run --project browser …`; the changed-scope gate also invokes Vitest directly, so a `pretest`-only hook would miss both. # Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.
5. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (changed-scope test gate plus the added regression tests; core-side suite green in the engine repo). The new `tests/tooling/` file is collected by the existing `unit` project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts:222`) — no project-config change needed.

> **Traceability to the original ACs:** brief AC1 ← original AC1; brief AC2 + AC3 ← original AC2 ("resolve which is true first" resolved: the template emits them by inheritance, so a template filter is required); brief AC4 ← original AC3; brief AC5 ← original AC4.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery** — the template fix lives in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo (`core/` submodule); this item cannot satisfy AC2 in-repo. Push policy applies to both repos: `dev` only.
- **No `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout** — re-scaffolding this repo today **drops 10 locally-added scripts** (`docs`, `docs:build`, `docs:preview`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, `validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph:svg`, `docs:diagrams`, `balance:synergy-diversity-report`) because the template does not preserve repo-local extras. AC1 must be done with a hand edit; fixture-based re-scaffold verification lives in tests.
- **No CI beyond npm builds** — the npm build/test scripts are the verification vehicle.
- Implementation follows the mandatory worktree + build→test→commit order of the implement skill; work-item tracking via wl only.

## Existing state

- Issue type stays `chore`: the change removes dead config keys and adjusts the scaffold's config generation; it changes no runtime app behaviour (matches the `discovered-from` item's classification).

- `package.json` (this repo, lines 34–35): `"scaffold:game": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts"`, `"scaffold:games": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root . --repos-dir .."`. Root `scripts/` contains only `run-tests.ts` and `soak-browser-waits.sh` — the target does not exist.
- `package.json` line 50: `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core"` — the working entry point (exists in all sibling repos too).
- `core/package.json` lines 31–32 declare the same two scripts **validly** (core has `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson` (lines ~274–312) inherits all core scripts, then overrides repo entry points; `scaffold:game(s)` pass through unchanged.
- 9 sibling game repos (`../tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-f5-verify`, `tce-fresh-verify`, `tce-repos-f9`) carry the same two broken lines — separate repositories, out of scope for this item's ACs (see Follow-ups).
- Related inherited-scripts bug of the same class: 8 more core-only entries arrive broken in every game repo (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — the last breaks `npm run package`/`package:win|linux|mac`). Excluded from scope (see Follow-ups).

## Desired change

1. Remove `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` from this repo's root `package.json` (hand edit; see Constraints).
2. In `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, filter the core-only keys out of the inherited scripts map — a small explicitly-named drop-list (or drop any inherited script that still references the core-only `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` target) with a comment explaining the Option C no-root-`scripts/` rationale and pointing at the follow-up item for the broader class.
3. Add/extend unit tests on both sides; bump the `./core` submodule pointer to the engine commit carrying the template fix.
4. Update `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (and the one-line core-doc clarification in Tableau-Card-Engine).

## Key Files

- `package.json` — remove the two `scaffold:game(s)` entries (this repo).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson`: drop core-only inherited scripts (template fix, engine repo).
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — extend MANIFEST fixture with `scaffold:game(s)` and assert they are omitted from the rendered `package.json`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` (new) — regression guard: no `scaffold:game(s)` declared; every `scaffold*` script target exists.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo entry point; note `scaffold:game(s)` are core-only.
- `.gitmodules` / `gitlink core` — submodule pointer bump to the engine commit with the template fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Dead-key approach is undocumented assumption.** Assumption (recorded, not operator-confirmed): the fix is the narrow one from the item title — drop only `scaffold:game(s)`; the other 8 broken inherited scripts are a separate discovered follow-up (below). If the operator prefers the general filter (fixes all 10), AC1–AC5 grow; flagged, not blocking.
- **R2 — Submodule bump pulls unrelated engine commits.** The engine `dev` head is ahead of the pinned submodule (pinned `9ee194e0…` vs engine `dev` `1c9900a1…`). Mitigation: keep the bump to a reviewable commit; full suite must stay green (AC5).
- **R3 — Incomplete inheritance semantics.** Filtering only `scaffold:game(s)` is a stop-gap while the general class remains broken; over time more core-only scripts may be added. Mitigation: follow-up item tracks the general fix (`discovered-from` link).
- **R4 — Re-scaffold destructiveness discovered during intake.** If the template's preserve-on-re-scaffold behaviour is later expected to keep repo-local scripts, that is a separate enhancement — out of scope here.
- **Scope-creep guard:** sibling-repo clean-up, the 8-script general fix, and template local-script preservation are all recorded as follow-ups, not folded into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** — "[test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts" (the `discovered-from` parent; same scaffold-template class of bug).
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED ↔ CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — engine-sync wiring precedent: core template change (in engine repo) + game-repo side + re-scaffold; the MS↔CG pairing model this item follows.
- **CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R** — version policy in `renderPackageJson` (the same function being changed).
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** — sibling-repo port of a core template guard; same cross-repo pattern.
- **CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA** — scaffold vite.config template ownership.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** – [test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)
- **MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O** – Engine dev tip renamed the story-line docs seam section (game doc-drift test pinned old heading) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mvcrgkzy007died, ac4, appear, banner, broken (+68 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: appear, banner, changes, context, core (+54 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, appear (+50 more)
> Assessment: `MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL` and `MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED` are genuinely related (same template/entry-point class). `MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O` matched on keyword noise (story-line docs seam) and is **not** relevant to this item; repo-file matches are incidental IDF matches. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0.md`.

## Follow-ups (recorded; out of scope)

- **Generalise the inherited-scripts filter** to all core-only entries that reference the absent game-repo `scripts/` tree (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — `build:electron-main` breakage disables `npm run package*` in every game repo). `discovered-from: MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`.
- **Re-scaffold sibling game repos** (golf, blackjack, lost-cities, coloretto, feudalism, beleaguered-castle, f5/fresh-verify, repos-f9) or hand-remove the two lines; each is its own repo/worklog item.
- **Template preservation of repo-local scripts** on re-scaffold (R4).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview was required: the seed context and acceptance criteria were sufficiently defined, and repository search resolved the description's open question ("resolve which is true first") directly:

- Q: Does `renderPackageJson` emit the two broken scripts, or were they hand-copied into game repos? — Answer (agent, repo search): It emits them **by inheritance** — `renderPackageJson` copies the core manifest's whole `scripts` map; `core/package.json` lines 31–32 are the source, and the rendered fixture (core test + node simulation) reproduces both keys. Source: `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (lines ~280–285), `core/package.json` (lines 31–32), `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (MANIFEST/inheritance assertions at lines 293–317), sibling repos `../tce-golf` etc. (same two lines at offset 21–22).
- Q: Can AC1 be satisfied by re-scaffolding this repo? — Answer (agent, simulation): No — re-scaffold would drop 10 locally-added scripts (`docs`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, …); AC1 must be a hand edit. Source: node simulation of `renderPackageJson` over the live `core/package.json` vs current root `package.json` (listed in Constraints/Existing state).
- Q: Are the docs that mention `scaffold:game(s)` in game-repo context? — Answer (agent, repo search): No — all three sites (`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md:2075`, `core/docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md:119–123`, `core/docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md:271`) describe core-checkout invocation and stay accurate; they keep the core scripts' validity. This repo's own `docs/` never mentions `scaffold:game(s)`.

`discovered-from` MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX (plan child) — the pin's intent is undocumented and self-contradictory, so a lag is indistinguishable from real drift.

## Goal

Make the engine-pin policy explicit and testable in prose: **the pin tracks the core `dev` tip**; a pin that lags the tip is a genuine failure, and the pin and the `core` gitlink always travel together (one actor, one moment). Document which command/gate composes which engine commit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented intent is explicit and tested: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (plus `README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, and engine `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Engine sync/verify scripts in generated game repos", delivered by `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`) state that the pin tracks the core `dev` tip; the behaviours behind the engine-composition matrix are the ones asserted by the engine-side policy tests. `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` carries that matrix as a table.
- `README.md` and `DEPLOYMENT.md` pin/re-pin statements agree with the policy: no text implying the pin is written *only* by the release process; dev `engine:sync` advances the pin together with the gitlink once the engine fix lands (cross-reference `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`).
- The composition matrix table documents: `npm test` + pre-push/dev-push suite gate compose the checkout present in `./core`; `npm run build` / `build:electron` / `implement.py finish` build step compose the dev head after `engine:sync` (pin follows after the fix); `build:release` / `engine:verify` compose detached at exactly the pinned SHA.
- The documented behaviour is traceable to the asserting tests: `core/tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` (engine-side policy suite) and `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` (local contract) are named as the tests behind each documented behaviour.
- No documentation claims behaviour the current tree does not have: statements about the mechanical pin write are scoped to "after the engine fix (`CG-0MVO268500071BPI`) lands"; the manual release-time edit is recorded as the pre-fix state.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — `docs/dev/build-and-release.md`, `README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md`, the relevant code comments, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries; no stale text claiming the pin is written only by the release process remains.
- No code changes; the item is docs-only and leaves the full suite green.

## Minimal implementation

1. Rewrite the "Release verify" / "Updating the engine / releasing" sections of `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` around the pin-tracks-the-tip policy.
2. Add the engine-composition matrix table in the same file.
3. Align the pin statements in `README.md` (project-layout table + dev-vs-release paragraph) and `DEPLOYMENT.md` (build + release steps).
4. Cross-reference the two asserting test suites by path from the docs.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — policy statement + engine-composition matrix (canonical game-repo doc)
- `README.md` — project-layout pin row and dev-vs-release paragraph
- `DEPLOYMENT.md` — build and release-verify steps
- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — named in docs as the local contract test
- `core/tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` — named in docs as the engine-side policy suite (engine repo, `~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`)

## Dependencies

- None. This is the only unblocked child of `MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX`; it may land while the engine-side fix (`CG-0MVO268500071BPI`) is outstanding.

## Out of scope (delivered elsewhere)

- The engine repo's `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Engine sync/verify scripts in generated game repos", the `engine-sync.d.mts` type comments and the `engine-sync.mjs` code comments are the canonical engine-side documentation of this policy — they are delivered by `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`, not by hand-editing the vendored submodule copy.

## Assumptions

`discovered-from` MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX (plan child) — re-pin `./core` and `configs/engine-pin.json` together to the engine tip that carries the fix, and prove `engine:verify` is green afterwards.

## Goal

Eliminate the observed lag (pin `9ee194e0` vs core `dev` tip `1c9900a1`) by bumping the `core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` in one change to the engine tip that carries the `CG-0MVO268500071BPI` fix, then prove the release-style verify is green on the re-pinned tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run engine:verify` succeeds on a clean dev checkout whose pin equals the committed `core` gitlink which equals the resolved remote engine `dev` target — no `PIN MISMATCH` on a correctly pinned tree; the SHAs are recorded as evidence in a comment on this item.
- The committed `core` gitlink and `configs/engine-pin.json` stay identical after the change and both point at the engine `dev` tip that carries the fix; the release-pin contract test `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` → "release pin contract" remains green.
- The re-pin is mechanical in execution: `engine:sync` advances `./core`, and the pin is written by the fixed script (not hand-edited); the commit records the gitlink + pin together. If the fixed script is not yet available at the chosen tip, the re-pin stops rather than falling back to a hand edit.
- The commit contains no unrelated changes: no docs rewrites, no test additions beyond keeping existing assertions green.
- Full project test suite passes on the re-pinned tree (dev-push gate green).

## Minimal implementation

1. Confirm `CG-0MVO268500071BPI` has landed on the engine `dev` branch and note the tip SHA (must contain the sync-writes-pin behaviour).
2. `npm run engine:sync` (clean `./core`) → advance the submodule and the pin together; verify `git diff` shows exactly `core` (gitlink) + `configs/engine-pin.json`.
3. If the pin was not written by the sync, stop and comment on `CG-0MVO268500071BPI` — do not edit the pin by hand.
4. `npm run engine:verify` (release-style, network) → record SHAs as evidence.
5. Commit gitlink + pin together; run the changed-scope gate.

## Key Files

- `configs/engine-pin.json` — pin advanced to the fix-carrying tip
- `core` gitlink — submodule pointer advanced with the pin
- `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` — the fixed script that writes the pin (engine repo source, re-scaffolded into the submodule)
- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — pin-contract assertions that must stay green
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — the release-verify/re-pin procedure followed here

## Dependencies

- **Blocked-by `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`** (cross-store, engine repo `~/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine`): the mechanical pin write and lag/bad-pin diagnostics must exist at the re-pin target; otherwise AC2/AC3 cannot be met.
- Does **not** depend on the docs child (documentation may land before or after).
- Relation to `MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57` (release derived-files staging bug): distinct scope — that item stops the pipeline staging spurious submodule bumps; this one performs the legitimate coordinated bump. No AC overlap.

## Assumptions

- Re-pin target = engine `dev` tip **at re-pin time**, which carries the fix (Appendix Q5-A), not the literal `1c9900a1`.
- Release-time verify assumes network access (unchanged from today).
- If engine `dev` advances mid-flight, the re-pin follows to the newer tip (policy: lag is a genuine failure).

`discovered-from` MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX (plan child) — the local suite must assert the pin policy and the lag-vs-bad-pin diagnostics so a future lag cannot regress silently.

## Goal

Extend the local game-repo suite with offline assertions that the pin policy holds and that `verifyEngine` diagnoses lag separately from a bad/foreign pin — so the trusted-guard behaviour is regression-tested in this repo as well as engine-side.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` asserts `syncEngine` writes `configs/engine-pin.json` to the new HEAD and stages it with the `core` gitlink when it advances the checkout; a second no-op sync leaves the pin byte-identical.
- The suite asserts offline-fallback sync (remote unreachable, checkout kept) leaves the pin untouched.
- `verifyEngine` diagnostics distinguish **lag** ("pin is an ancestor of the tracked tip by N commits — re-pin: the pin and gitlink travel together") from a **bad/foreign pin** ("pin does not resolve on the tracked branch") — both fail hard (throw `EngineSyncError`), only the diagnosis and next steps differ (asserted by offline fixtures).
- The existing dirty-guard, exact-checkout, single-`sha`-field and pin==gitlink contract assertions remain green and unmodified in intent.
- Testing/validation: engine `core/tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` and main-street `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` cover the new behaviour offline; all fixtures stay network-free (`file://` submodule remotes via `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`) — no `ls-remote` against a real remote. (The one release-style `npm run engine:verify` validation run belongs to the re-pin child.)
- Full project test suite passes with the new assertions.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend the existing `makeGame()` fixture helpers where needed (e.g. an offline/remote-unreachable variant, and an off-branch commit for the bad-pin case).
2. Add sync-writes-pin + no-op-idempotence + offline-fallback cases.
3. Add lag-vs-bad-pin `verifyEngine` diagnosis cases asserting distinct message fragments (not the shared `PIN MISMATCH` string only).

data.comment:
question: The producer's review asks for the banking hint to fire *when the tutorial is active and the player banks their first action point*. I have flipped the gate (shouldTriggerBankingHint now requires tutorialActive) and fixed the dead-end (end-turn step completion is deferred while the hint is pending, then completed/advanced on hint dismiss). However, the scripted tutorial never leaves a spare action: every day contains exactly one action-consuming step and the day starts with exactly 1 action (Easy preset, no staff, no bank), so actionsRemaining is 0 at every one of the seven End Turns (T6, T8, T11, T14, T17, T19, T21). The banking hint therefore cannot fire in the scripted tutorial with the current flow.

This conflicts with the earlier producer-mandated flow fix in this same work item (2026-10-04): 'no day ends without spending its action', enforced by tests/main-street/tutorial-action-economy.test.ts ('every day spends exactly one action'). The only tutorial day that ever banked was the old favour-only day, which that fix removed.

Question for the producer: which should change?
(a) Add a deliberate 'banking day' to the tutorial (a day that ends with an unused action so the hint fires) — this reverses/adjusts the 'every day spends exactly one action' rule and needs a flow + coin-budget decision.
(b) Fire the hint proactively on the first tutorial End Turn even when nothing banks (teaches the concept before it is used) — this relaxes AC1's 'actionsRemaining > 0' condition and the current copy ('Any unused action banks up to 2...').
(c) Keep the hint tutorial-only but accept that it only appears if the player genuinely banks (may not appear in the scripted run).

Work completed so far (local commit d9634a0, not pushed): gate flip + dead-end fix + updated unit tests; tsc clean; 144 targeted tutorial tests green.

## Clarifying Questions

**Q1: Alternating turn structure for shared-street mode.** The description notes this is a design decision to confirm. Which approach do you prefer?

- **Option A — Alternating MarketPhases within a shared day:** Each day has one MarketPhase where players alternate turns (Player A acts, Player B acts, Player A acts, etc.), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck phases resolve once both players have had a chance to act. This creates tight interplay — each player reacts to the other's placements before income/event resolution.
- **Option B — Alternating full days:** Each player gets their own full day/turn cycle (Player A's complete day: Market -> Income -> Incident -> EndCheck, then Player B's complete day). This is simpler to implement and closer to the existing single-player flow.

**Preference?** (Option A / Option B / Other approach)

data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Q2: Child item coverage.** The epic lists 5 ACs. AC1 (state model), AC2 (AI strategy), AC3 (income/events), and AC4 (Monte Carlo) map to existing/sub-plan children. AC5 (game scene) is noted as "may be split into a child at planning." Should we create the AC5 child now (competitive-mode scene with owner-coloured street, turn alternation, SLL layout, audio feedback), or defer to planning?

**Q3: Denial reasoning scope.** The AI-strategy child (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038) explicitly marks opponent-aware *denial* reasoning as out of scope. Confirm: denial (blocking opponent's best slot, buying to deny) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up? Or should we include basic denial as a minimum viable feature?

**Q4: Win condition for competitive mode.** The single-player win condition is a score threshold. In competitive mode, does the game end when:
- Either player reaches the threshold (first to win), or
- A fixed number of shared days elapses (higher score wins), or
- Both reach threshold / both go bankrupt (simultaneous end)?

**Preference?**

data.comment:
## Producer Decisions (intake response)

**Q1: Alternating turn structure — Answer: Option A**
Alternating MarketPhases within a shared day. Each day has one MarketPhase where players alternate turns (Player A acts, Player B acts, etc.), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck phases resolve once both have acted.

**Q2: Child item coverage for AC5 — Answer: Deferred to planning**
AC5 (competitive-mode scene) will be created as a child work item during planning. For now, focus on the engine/state layer (AC1-AC4).

**Q3: Denial reasoning scope — Answer: Deferred**
Opponent-aware denial reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.

**Q4: Win condition — Answer: First to threshold wins, with optional endless mode**
When either player reaches the win threshold, that player wins. The game includes an option to carry on in endless mode where both players continue building beyond the threshold.

**Clarification on "owner-coloured street" (AC5):** This means rendering the shared street grid where each business slot is visually tinted to show which player owns it — e.g., player businesses get a blue tint, AI opponent's businesses get a red tint. This is a visual UI concern for the scene child (deferred to planning).

**Intake (Round 1) — non-interactive dispatch; 3 questions need producer confirmation**

The intake brief was drafted with recommended defaults (documented in the Appendix of the description and used throughout the ACs). The item is flagged for producer review because the following decisions materially shape the implementation. **Recommended defaults are shown in brackets.**

1. **Free re-roll semantics.** The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's "free re-roll" free you from, and how does it interact with the escalating cost item `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`? *[Recommended: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack.]*
2. **Relevance definition & application.** How is "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" defined, and how does the 75% apply? *[Recommended: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback.]*
3. **Movement cost & scope.** Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? *[Recommended: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free.]*

Secondary assumptions (not blocking): generalist Investor, 0 hand slots, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125; dedicated 1024×1024 art or an approved pending-art entry (else blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`); rename coordination with `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1`.

If the defaults are accepted, no further action is needed and the item can proceed to planning/implementation.

data.comment:
Planning Complete — decomposed into 7 children (test-first, dependency-ordered).

## Plan (feature list)

| # | Item | Type | Depends on |
|---|------|------|-----------|
| F1 | Reputation-phase invariant regression tests `MS-0MUYGFVIJ00070MB` | task | — |
| F2 | Pedestrian count pure helper `MS-0MUYGFVVG009KONJ` | task | — |
| F3 | Pedestrian silhouette layer `MS-0MUYGFW7T00579Z1` | feature | F2 |
| F4 | Live population reconciliation `MS-0MUYGFWKG008GUA5` | feature | F3 |
| F5 | Reputation phase dissolve-to-coins `MS-0MUYGFWXK003QFYB` | feature | F3, F1 |
| F6 | Pedestrian layer documentation `MS-0MUYGFXA70009OWV` | docs | F4, F5 |
| F7 | Full-suite and build verification `MS-0MUYGFXMK009L1UU` | task | F1–F5 |

## Acceptance-criteria coverage (parent → child)

- Parent AC1 (population reflects reputation) → F2 (pure helper), F4 (live count).
- Parent AC2 (wander the street, no gameplay RNG) → F3.
- Parent AC3 (live population update) → F4.
- Parent AC4 (income sourced from pedestrians; credited total unchanged) → F5, guarded by F1.
- Parent AC5 (reduced-motion/replay exemptions, non-blocking, no new RNG) → F1, F3, F4, F5.
- Parent AC6 (documentation updated) → F6.
- Parent AC7 (build and full suite green) → F7.

_Note:_ the parent ACs are a numbered list, so the automated coverage helper (`tree_coverage.run_coverage_review`) extracts zero parent ACs and returns `proceed` (100%). The mapping above is the human traceability record. Parent formatting was left unchanged to preserve author intent.

## Automated review stages

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — every parent AC maps to ≥1 child AC (above); no invented requirements; out-of-scope items kept out of the children.
2. **Completeness** — every child has a description, `## Acceptance Criteria`, and `**Key Files:**`; key-file paths validated (each has a `/` and an extension); predicted parent paths corrected to the repo's actual layout (`src/scenes/...`, `src/coin-grid.ts`).
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — test-first: F1 (invariant regression tests) precedes the phase rework (F5); edges F3←F2, F4←F3, F5←F3+F1, F6←F4+F5, F7←F1..F5.
4. **Scope sizing** — 7 deliverable increments; each is a minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs).
5. **Acceptance & testability** — child ACs are pass/fail and testable (unit + browser tests, credited-total assertions, exemption tests).
6. **Polish & handoff** — child titles ≤7 words; descriptions copy-pasteable for `implement`.
7. **AC coverage review** — `recommendation: proceed`.

## Assumptions (documented)

- The layer is parented to the street container so it pans/clips with the street camera view.
- Presentation randomness is a module-local seeded PRNG, never the seeded gameplay RNG.
- Edge case: `repBonus` can be > 0 while zero pedestrians are on screen (repBonus is independent of the current reputation total). `dissolveIntoCoins` falls back to a street-area anchor (road band / street centre) — never the HUD counter. The producer may override this fallback.
- Per-seat competitive populations are out of scope until `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` lands.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No new questions were required in this planning session. The intake Appendix (Q1–Q6) already answers appearance (solid silhouettes, `#88bbff`), wandering (free wander), ratio (1 per 50, uncapped), conversion (figures dissolve into coins; credited total unchanged), live vs end-of-turn (live fade in/out) and density cap (uncapped). No prior answer was changed or superseded.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-07: decomposed into 7 children (F1–F7), wired 11 dependency edges, ran the six review stages and the AC coverage review (`proceed`), refreshed effort/risk (Small / Medium, expected 14.83h, recommended 20.33h).

data.comment:
## Blocked — new AC is ambiguous and conflicts with the open parent item

**Question for the producer. I have not modified any code because the definition gate fails.**

### Context

The producer audit of 2026-09-21 rejected the previous attempt and requested:

> "We need a new AC in which no tutorial step proceeds without using the available action point."

This requirement is **not** in the work item's formal acceptance criteria, and it conflicts with the still-open parent item **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** ("Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking"), whose AC1 requires the banking hint to fire **while the tutorial is active** when the player ends a turn with spare actions.

### Current code state (dev)

The prior one-line fix (commit `8ffdae34`, branch `fix-bank-hint-tutorial`, author Sorra the Orc) is **not merged into `dev`**. On `dev` the original condition is still present at `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts:118`:

```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
```

### Why the requested AC needs clarification

A literal reading — block **End Turn** during the tutorial while `actionsRemaining > 0`, forcing the player to spend the action point first — **deadlocks the 26-step flow**:

- Day 5 is **T15 Community Favour** then **T16 End Turn**.
- T15 is a *free* once-per-turn action and does **not** consume the daily action (`TutorialFlow.ts` and `tests/main-street/tutorial-action-economy.test.ts` both assert this).
- The player therefore reaches T16 with 1 action remaining, and `isTutorialActionAllowed` only permits the current step's required action, so there is no legal way to spend it.

The scripted economy also intentionally leaves a spare action on several later days because of banking (see the "simulated run with banking" test).

### Questions

1. **Which behaviour is intended?**
   - **A. Block End Turn during the tutorial while actions remain** ("use your action point first" feedback). If so, how should Day 5 (T15 free Community Favour) be resolved — make T15 consume the daily action, restructure the T14/T16 day boundaries, or allow an extra spend during an end-turn step?
   - **B. Do not bank spare actions during the tutorial** (forfeit them) so the day budget never drifts, while End Turn stays allowed. Note this conflicts with parent AC1.
   - **C. Keep the one-line hint fix and add an assertion-only AC** that every action-gated step consumes exactly one action point, with no runtime change to End Turn.
   - **D. Other** — please give the exact AC wording and the expected player-visible behaviour.

2. Does parent item **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** still stand with AC1 as written, or should its AC1 be re-scoped/replaced by this item?

3. If the two items genuinely conflict, which item owns the fix?

Answering Q1 (and Q2) is sufficient for me to implement the hint fix plus the new AC with tests and push to `dev`.

### AC status

- AC1 (hint must not fire during tutorial): **unmet on `dev`** — the one-line fix exists only on the unmerged branch.
- AC2–AC5: **not yet verified** on `dev`.

data.comment:
## Intake: context gathered and open questions

### Context (from repo + work-item search)

- This work item is a migrated producer note: "Charity shop, 1.5 income per turn, 0.15 reputation per turn. Costs 3".
- Main Street uses a **×100 integer economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6), so the note converts to: `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`.
- Every business also pays a standard **ongoing cost** of one quarter of its purchase price (`75` for a 300-cost card, CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE), stored in the CSV `ongoingCost` column.
- Card rows live in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` and are the source of truth; `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` documents them. A new business generally also needs a catalog entry, tier registration (automatic via the CSV `tier` column), and tests.
- There is currently **no** charity shop (or equivalent thrift/op-shop) card in the CSV or catalog, so this is a net-new business template.
- Related work items:
  - `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated note; sets the precedent for ×100 values and negative reputation).
  - `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — integer economy (coin/rep ×100).
  - `CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE` — business ongoing cost (1/4 purchase price).
  - `CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I` — Reconcile event card text to integer data; `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` — validate all card text (ongoing text/data consistency).

### Open questions

**Q1 — Are the stated numbers gross or net of the standard ongoing cost?**
Every business pays `ongoingCost = cost / 4` per turn (`75` for a 300-cost card). "1.5 income per turn" is therefore ambiguous.

- **A (Recommended):** 1.5 is **gross `baseIncome`** → `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 75`, net `0.75`/turn. Matches how every other business stat is documented (gross income + separate ongoing cost).
- **B:** 1.5 is **net after ongoing cost** → `baseIncome = 225`, `ongoingCost = 75`.
- **C:** The charity shop is **exempt from ongoing cost** → `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 0`.

**Q2 — Which synergy type should the Charity Shop belong to?**
The CSV requires a `synergyTypes` value (affects adjacency bonuses).

- **A (Recommended):** `Commerce` — a charity shop retails donated second-hand goods (matches Pawn Shop / Boutique).
- **B:** `Service` — treated as a non-profit community service.
- **C:** `Culture` — a community/volunteering asset.
- **D:** No synergy (like Pawn Shop: `synergyCoinBonus = 0`, `synergyRepBonus = 0`).

**Q3 — Which progression tier, and should it have an upgrade path?**

- **A (Recommended):** `tier = 2`, standalone (`upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1`) — matches the other 300-cost, no-upgrade Commerce singles (Pawn Shop, Boutique).
- **B:** `tier = 1`, standalone (matches the 300-cost T1 basics: Bakery, Diner, Bookshop, Hardware Store).
- **C:** `tier = 2` with a single upgrade step (a new upgrade card name would be needed, e.g. "Charity Superstore").

### Non-blocking assumptions (will be used unless corrected)

- `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`.
- Description and `art_notes` generated in the existing house style (e.g. "Sells donated goods. … Provides +0.15 reputation per turn.").
- Tests: CSV/validation plus a unit test asserting the card's cost, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, and ongoing cost.
- Docs: add the card to `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and update deck-size/expansion counts.

Please answer Q1–Q3 (or confirm the recommended options) and I will complete the intake brief.
