data.comment:
## Pre-drop legality audit (AC3)

Every action-consuming UI handler enumerated in the parent AC3 was inspected for the "animate/consume before validate" ordering. Verdicts:

| Handler | Entry point | Pre-mutation legality gate | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| place-business-from-hand | MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.onSlotClick | canPlaceFromHand (incl. premium) | Present (parent AC1) |
| apply-upgrade-from-hand | MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.applyHandUpgradeToSlot | canPlayUpgradeFromHand | Fixed in MS-0MUUYD15V003SP0Z |
| buy-and-place drag (business) | MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.onDragDropBusiness | drop zone canAccept -> canDropBusinessCard | Present; animation starts only via onDrop after canAccept |
| buy-and-place drag (upgrade) | MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop.onDragDropUpgrade | drop zone canAccept -> canDropUpgradeCard | Present; animation starts only via onDrop after canAccept |
| move-to-hand (business) | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onBusinessCardClick | actionsRemaining + canAddToHand | Present |
| move-to-hand (upgrade) | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onUpgradeCardClick | actionsRemaining + canAddToHand | Present |
| move-to-hand (event) | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onEventCardClick | canPurchaseEvent | Present |
| buy event | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onEventCardClick | canPurchaseEvent | Present |
| play held event | MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.onPlayHeldEvent | canPlayEvent | Fixed in this item (was execute-then-catch) |
| hire-staff | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onStaffCardClick | canPurchaseStaff | Present |
| peek | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onPeekClick | actionsRemaining + peekUsedThisTurn + staff + deck guards | Present |
| community-favour | MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.onCommunityFavourClick | tutorial + favourUsedThisTurn + resource >= cost; engine executeAction restores on throw | Present |
| close-business | MainStreetOverlayContent close button | canCloseBusiness | Present |
| end-turn | MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.endTurn | tutorial gate; no action consumed | Present |

### Findings and fix

- onPlayHeldEvent was the only offender: it executed playEventCommand and relied on the catch block. It never animated before mutating and the command layer now restores on throw (MS-0MUUYAZPN0064AW5), so no action was lost, but it lacked the required pre-mutation predicate. Fixed inline: canPlayEvent is now checked before the command, with playIllegalFeedback + instruction text and no mutation. Two regression tests added to tests/main-street/illegal-afford-feedback.test.ts (unaffordable -> no action/undo command; legal -> exactly one action).
- onDragDropBusiness/onDragDropUpgrade: core/ui/dragDrop.ts only invokes onDrop when the registered drop zone's canAccept returns true, so the transfer animation starts strictly after a non-mutating predicate. The drag-drop module-wiring tests in tests/main-street/drag.test.ts already assert the snap-back/no-buy behaviour for rejected drops.
- No handler leaves uiPhase === 'animating' on a failed attempt: the drag/click handlers set uiPhase = 'animating' only after the gate passes, and every afterTransfer path resets uiPhase = 'market' (success or catch).

### Discovered-from items

None — the single offender was fixed inline and is within minimal remediation.

question: **Producer confirmation requested on two non-blocking scope assumptions (intake is otherwise complete and recorded).**

1. **Competitive mirror scope.** Both the single-player heuristic (`scoreAction`) and the competitive mirror (`competitiveFavourScore`) encode the same loose "stalled + buffer" rep→coins rule. Should the fix apply the shared enablement/value helper to **both** (recommended: yes — prevents behavioural divergence), or single-player only (competitive tuning deferred)?
2. **Loss-mode band gate.** Should the PRD loss-mode band (reputation collapse 20–40% of Medium losses) be a **hard gate** for this item? Recommended: **no** — keep this item's primary gate behavioural (rep→coins usage + enablement/value), with the win-rate ladder and committed-baseline tolerances; the band is owned by the pending R2 reputation re-tune (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE), and changing both at once confounds attribution.

Both assumptions are recorded as OPEN QUESTIONs in the intake brief Appendix. Intake stage is `intake_complete`; implementation can proceed on the recommended defaults unless the producer directs otherwise.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Intake root-cause finding (evidence)

The defect is confirmed in the code path:

- `checkImmediateLoss` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:711-731`) reads only the shared `state.resourceBank` (coins/reputation) — there is no per-seat variant.
- `checkCompetitiveEndConditions` (`:773-777`) calls it first and returns on a hit, leaving `competitiveWinnerId = null`.
- `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts:264-267`) and `finishCompetitiveClosingTail` (`:196`) call it **without binding the human seat**.
- `bindCompetitiveSeat`/`restoreCompetitiveSeat` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:2013-2037`) mirror the acting seat into the shared fields; restore writes back but does **not reset** the shared fields, so `resourceBank` persists as the last-acting seat.
- `endCompetitiveTurnDay` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts:353-392`) drives the AI seats last, so at closing `state.resourceBank` = the last **AI** wallet.

Therefore any AI with `reputation <= 0` (turn > 1) or `coins < 0` ends the whole game as a loss (no winner) even when the human is healthy — exactly the operator report. Corroborated by the `competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts:70` seed swap (`ac1-cap-1` → `ac1-cap-3`) recorded in MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN / MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J.

## Open questions for producer (blocking implementation detail)

- **OQ1 (elimination policy):** eliminate the failing AI (skip rotation, close its businesses) and continue, **or** end the game with the surviving seat as winner? *(Recommended: eliminate + continue.)*
- **OQ2 (human collapse):** keep human collapse as an immediate loss (existing semantics)? *(Recommended: yes.)*
- **OQ3 (last standing):** with 1 human + 1 AI, does eliminating the AI make the human win immediately, or continue solo to the score threshold? *(Recommended: immediate win, `competitiveWinnerId = 0`.)*

Effort/risk: Medium, ~25h recommended, risk High (18/25), confidence 74%. Stage set to `intake_complete`; pending producer confirmation of OQ1–OQ3 before plan/implementation.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Operator answers to OQ1–OQ3

- **OQ1 — elimination policy: A.** Eliminate the failing AI seat (remove it from turn rotation, close its businesses) and let the survivors play on; an AI's failure must not end the game.
- **OQ2 — human collapse: yes.** When the human seat itself collapses (reputation <= 0 / coins < 0), the game still ends immediately as a human loss (existing single-player semantics).
- **OQ3 — last standing: win immediately, with an option to continue solo.** When the last AI is eliminated, declare the human the winner (`competitiveWinnerId = 0`) and offer an explicit opt-in to keep playing solo (mirroring endless mode's `score_threshold_continue`).

data.comment:
## Follow-up: does it also end on coin exhaustion?

**Answer:** There is **no** game-over at `coins == 0` ("coin exhaustion") — ongoing costs are clamped at 0 and a player can sit at 0 coins indefinitely (single-player and competitive). The coin loss condition is **bankruptcy: `coins < 0`** (a genuine overdraft), which is reachable per-owner because `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` does `owner.player.coins += coinsGained` with no clamp (`src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts:449-451`).

**Yes, the same defect applies to coins:** `checkImmediateLoss` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts:716-723`) checks `state.resourceBank.coins < 0` **before** the reputation branch, so if the last-acting AI seat's coins go negative at closing, the whole game ends with `endReason = 'bankruptcy'` — even when the human has plenty of coins. The fix is the same per-seat evaluation, and the brief's AC1/AC2 already covered `coins < 0`; the title and problem statement have now been updated to make the reputation/bankruptcy symmetry explicit.

## Clarifying Questions for Producer

1. **Presentation scope**: Should the closing phase feedback show per-player (per-seat) income breakdown, or just the shared total? In competitive mode, each player has their own economy — showing per-player details would be informative but more complex.

## Plan

### Bug Analysis

The root cause is confirmed: bindCompetitiveSeat sets state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget without including the shared state.bankedActions pool. In competitive mode, the shared banked actions are a collective resource that every seat should be able to draw from, but currently only the first seat to bind sees the banked actions (baked into actionBudget at week start). Subsequent seats lose the bank entirely.

### Fix (2 changes)

1. bindCompetitiveSeat (MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:2020):
   OLD: state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget;
   NEW: state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget + state.bankedActions;

2. restoreCompetitiveSeat (MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:2039) — needed to prevent double-counting:
   OLD: player.actionBudget = state.actionsRemaining;
   NEW: player.actionBudget = state.actionsRemaining - (state.bankedActions ?? 0);

Without fix #2, if a seat does not consume banked actions, the next seat would incorrectly receive the banked actions twice (once baked into actionBudget, once added at bind).

Fix #2 also satisfies the constraint that actionBudget remains the player's base budget without banked actions.

### Test
- Add a dedicated banking test to competitive-scene-turn-flow.test.ts:
  - Simulate a competitive day with 2 banked actions at start
  - Human uses 1 action (consuming 1 banked), verify AI gets budget+0 banked
  - Human uses 0 actions, verify AI gets budget+2 banked
  - Verify closing tail banks correctly after both scenarios

### Single-player unchanged
Both functions are no-ops when not in competitive state (early return when getCompetitivePlayer returns null). No single-player impact.

## Implementation notes (session herdr-1791269670-2182822-14900)

### Root cause
In competitive mode the shared banked pool was baked into each seat's `actionBudget` at WeekStart, so `bindCompetitiveSeat` gave every seat the *full day-start* bank. A banked action spent by the human was then handed to the AI again (double-count), and the closing tail banked from the last seat's already-drained counter — the practical 'turns do not bank' symptom.

### Fix (scope)
1. `executeCompetitiveWeekStart`: `p.actionBudget = 1 + staffBonus` (bank-free base) — required by the work-item constraint that `actionBudget` is the daily base budget without banked actions. Without this the bind-side addition would double-count **and** the existing test expected the old (bank-inclusive) value.
2. `bindCompetitiveSeat`: `state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget + state.bankedActions` (AC2).
3. `restoreCompetitiveSeat`: `player.actionBudget = state.actionsRemaining - state.bankedActions` so the base field stays bank-free across bind/restore cycles and the *remaining* shared bank is what the next seat sees.
4. Updated the stale `actionBudget` JSDoc and the competitive-banking note in `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.

### Tests
- Updated `competitive-phase.test.ts` hand-off test to assert the new contract (base-only `actionBudget`; bind adds the shared bank). It previously encoded the buggy bank-inclusive budget.
- Added a `Competitive action banking` block to `competitive-scene-turn-flow.test.ts`: bind grants base+remaining bank (AC2); an idle shared day banks exactly one action then caps at 2 (AC1); a banked action spent by the human is not re-granted to the AI (the regression).
- Single-player: `bindCompetitiveSeat`/`restoreCompetitiveSeat` are no-ops without a roster and `executeCompetitiveWeekStart` only derives per-seat budgets when `players[]` exists, so single-player banking is byte-for-byte unchanged (AC3).

### Assumption
The work item's stated fix named only `bindCompetitiveSeat`, but its own constraint ('`actionBudget` is the daily base budget without banked actions') cannot hold while `executeCompetitiveWeekStart` bakes the bank in; the WeekStart change is the minimal way to make the ACs coherent.

data.comment:
## Re-implementation notes (session herdr-1791271951-2932806-15491)

### Why the prior fix (c2d7d27) did not resolve the manual rejection
The prior fix correctly added the shared bank at `bindCompetitiveSeat`, but the **day-end banking** still read only the shared `state.actionsRemaining`, which each seat's bind **resets** to its own budget. So at the shared closing it reflected only the **last** seat's MarketPhase.

Reproduction (deterministic): human binds with base 1, leaves the action unused and ends; the AI seat then spends its own base action. `state.actionsRemaining` is 0 at closing, so `bankable = min(0,1) = 0` — the human's unused base action was silently discarded. This is exactly "turns do not bank when playing against AI": the human idles, the AI acts, and no bank appears.

### Fix
`finishCompetitiveClosingTail` now banks from the **largest remaining non-eliminated seat budget** (`players[].actionBudget`, which `restoreCompetitiveSeat` keeps bank-free) rather than the last seat's shared counter:
- any seat's unused base action banks, capped at 1/day (cap 2), matching single-player ("one unused base action banks");
- N<=1 keeps the legacy single-counter behaviour;
- eliminated seats are ignored.

No change to `consumeAction`, `actionBudget` semantics, single-player (`processEndOfTurn`), or the HUD (it reads `state.bankedActions`, now correct).

### Tests
Added to `tests/main-street/competitive-scene-turn-flow.test.ts` (Competitive action banking):
- human's unused base action banks even when the AI spends its action (the regression);
- a banked action persists to the next day start and re-banks after the AI draws it down;
- the shared pool banks when the AI idles and the human spends ("regardless of how many seats acted").

### Docs
Updated the competitive banking note in `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` to state that the day's unused action is taken from the largest remaining per-seat budget.

data.comment:
## Follow-up fix (session herdr-1791271951-2932806-15491): bank must clear when the human spends it

### Producer repro
1. End a turn without spending an action -> bank 1.
2. Next turn correctly have 2 APs (base 1 + banked 1).
3. Spend both APs and end the turn.
4. Bank did not clear -> next turn incorrectly had 2 APs (one banked).

### Cause
The previous fix banked from the **largest remaining seat budget**, so an AI seat that idled (or had a spare action) re-banked into the shared pool every day, even when the human had spent their full budget. The bank could never drain.

### Fix
`finishCompetitiveClosingTail` now banks from the **human seat's** unused base action only (`findHumanSeatId` -> `players[human].actionBudget`). An AI seat's unused action no longer tops up the human's bank, so:
- human idles -> bank +1 (day 1 repro);
- human spends both APs -> bank clears to 0 (day 2 repro), even if the AI idles;
- N<=1 / legacy engine path keep the shared-counter fallback.

### Tests
Replaced the incorrect "AI idles banks" assertion with the producer repro in `tests/main-street/competitive-scene-turn-flow.test.ts`: idle day -> bank 1 -> 2 APs -> spend both -> bank 0 -> next day 1 AP.

### Docs
Updated the competitive banking note in `core-rules-and-mechanics.md`: the bank belongs to the human and is topped up from the human seat's own unused base action only.

data.comment:
question: Q1 (overlap) — This item overlaps the deferred/closed owner-coloured rendering item. How should they relate?

`MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` ("Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation, SFX") scoped owner-coloured street rendering but was **deferred on 2026-10-03 and closed `done` without implementation** (implementation aborted; the current street renderer has no owner tinting/border). This item ("Identify different AI players") overlaps its owner-colour AC.

- **A (Recommended):** Treat this item as the focused "seat identity colour" delivery (colour-blind-friendly seat palette + log prefixes + placed-card borders) and reference `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` as **superseded for the owner-colour part**; its phase-alternation/SFX scope stays separate.
- **B:** Create this as a child of a **re-opened** `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` so one item owns all owner-colour rendering.
- **C:** Keep them independent — this item only adds log prefixes + card borders; full street owner colour stays with a re-opened `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K`.

**Recommended:** A — avoids duplicate work while keeping this item focused.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
question: Q2 (palette and assignment) — The description says "assign a random (distinct) colour to each AI player". Which palette and assignment model should be used?

- **A (Recommended):** A fixed **colour-blind-safe palette** (e.g. Okabe–Ito, 8 colours) **shuffled per game** with an injected RNG, and the assignment persisted in competitive state/save so it is stable across reloads and testable. This satisfies "random" while remaining deterministic per seed.
- **B:** Fixed by seat index (AI 1 always colour 1, AI 2 colour 2, …) — simplest and fully deterministic, but not "random".
- **C:** Producer specifies exact hex colours per seat.

**Recommended:** A — meets the "random" wording while remaining deterministic/testable and accessible.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
question: Q3 (card border vs upgrade border) — The description notes the AI-owner border "will likely need to upgrade border to be removed". How should owner colour and upgrade state coexist on a placed card?

The street card currently draws a full-card upgrade border via `applyUpgradeOverlays` (`spec.upgradeBorder` in `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`). The owner-coloured border would occupy the same card frame.

- **A (Recommended):** Owner colour becomes the **outer card border** for placed cards; the upgrade indicator moves to the existing **top-left level badge / a corner accent**, removing the full-card upgrade border so both ownership and upgrade level stay legible.
- **B:** Keep the upgrade border and add the owner colour as a separate **inner/outer ring** (double border).
- **C:** Owner colour only for AI-owned cards; retain the upgrade border for the human's cards.

**Recommended:** A — a single, unambiguous ownership border while preserving upgrade legibility.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
research (Q1): WebGL conversion impact (agent, 2026-10-09).

Stack: Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 (package.json). In Phaser 4 the Canvas renderer is explicitly deprecated and everything new (Filters) is WebGL-only. main.ts pins type: Phaser.CANVAS; createCardGame defaults to Phaser.AUTO, so the switch itself is a one-line config change (Phaser.WEBGL, or AUTO with Canvas fallback).

Benefits of WebGL: unlocks the Phaser 4 Filter system (Mask, Blend, Gradient Map, Threshold, Shine via AddEffectShine, Bloom via AddEffectBloom, custom single-shader filters) plus lighting/self-shadows — the machinery a card shader would use. Filters are also the migration target for the removed Phaser 3 FX/pipelines.

Breaking-change cost (larger than a config flip):
1. GeometryMask is Canvas-only in Phaser 4 (node_modules/phaser/src/display/mask/GeometryMask.js:27: 'GeometryMask is only supported in the Canvas Renderer'). It is used by Main Street (log-content mask and street-map mask in MainStreetRendererStreet.ts; MainStreetScene.logContentMask) and by shared core UI (core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts, Overlay.ts, SettingsPanel.ts) plus gym scenes. All must migrate to the Mask filter / AddMaskShape.
2. WebGL supports only NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN blend modes (of 27 Canvas modes). Main Street uses none of the exotic ones (only the gym spike uses these four), so low impact here.
3. WebGL context loss/restoration is a new failure mode; the game's canvas-based SVG textures (textures.addCanvas in core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts) and generateTexture outputs must survive GPU re-upload.
4. Rendering output is not byte-identical across Canvas/WebGL/GPUs; thumbnail/visual-regression determinism needs re-checking (replay mode already sets preserveDrawingBuffer, a WebGL concept).

CI/test impact (high): createCardGame documents Canvas as ~10x faster than WebGL under SwiftShader in headless CI; TestGamePool forces Phaser.CANVAS and every browser test boots Canvas. Switching production to WebGL while tests stay Canvas means WebGL-only filters are never exercised by the suite; testing the shader needs at least one WebGL browser project (Playwright Chromium + SwiftShader), which is slower and potentially flaky.

WebGPU: No — converting to WebGL does not take us to WebGPU. Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 exposes only AUTO/CANVAS/WEBGL (no WEBGPU constant), and the rendering-concepts doc states the renderer 'uses the original WebGL... It shouldn't be too difficult to extend these principles to WebGL2 and WebGPU.' So WebGL is the necessary intermediate step and Phaser 4's RenderNode + managed-state architecture is designed for a future WebGPU backend, but WebGPU is not available today. Code should use Phaser's filter/shader API (never raw gl), which is the code most likely to survive that future migration.

Recommendation: if a true shader is wanted, treat the renderer migration (GeometryMask->Mask filter across Main Street + core UI, plus a WebGL test project) as a separate prerequisite work item; the card shader then becomes a filter on top. Option A (Canvas-compatible effect via the existing overlay pipeline) remains the low-risk path that delivers the visual distinction now.

Planning Complete — Create a card shader decomposed into 5 vertical slices.

## Plan summary

Approach is fixed by the 2026-10-09 producer decisions (Q1 = A Canvas-compatible shader-style effect; Q2 = upgraded business/community-space cards only; Q3 = do not recreate the removed full-card `upgradeBorder`; Q4 = animated with reduced-motion static fallback; Q5 = no suite regression, animation paused in replay/headless).

Decomposition (vertical slices, each carries its own tests — tests authored first within the slice per TDD):

1. **Pure upgrade shader-effect spec** (`MS-0MV5I4NTU002D3V4`, feature) — extend the pure, Phaser-free `UpgradeOverlaySpec` with a `shaderEffect` spec (colour stops, animation params, static form); `null` for level 0. Unit-tested.
2. **Render the static shader accent** (`MS-0MV5I4O8U001SU5J`, feature, depends on 1) — draw the Canvas-safe static accent in `applyUpgradeOverlays()`, confined to the top-left accent, coexisting with the owner-coloured outer border; browser integration test for presence/absence.
3. **Animate the accent with reduced-motion and replay fallback** (`MS-0MV5I4ONA000Z7NV`, feature, depends on 2) — deterministic tween gated by `!reducedMotion && !replayMode`, static otherwise, tween lifecycle cleanup.
4. **Update upgrade-rendering documentation** (`MS-0MV5I4P3G007EV1Q`, docs, depends on 3) — `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` § "Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline" and `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`; remove stale `upgradeBorder` / `OverlayBorderSpec` references.
5. **Full-suite regression verification** (`MS-0MV5I4PI7004JZ15`, task, depends on 3 and 4) — run the full suite and triage any failures.

Dependency chain: 1 → 2 → 3 → {4, 5}.

## AC coverage mapping

- AC1 (distinctive effect on upgraded cards; base unchanged) → slices 2, 3
- AC2 (pure Phaser-free spec; null for level 0) → slice 1
- AC3 (reduced-motion static; no animation in replay/headless) → slice 3
- AC4 (no full-card border; coexist with owner colour; colour not sole carrier) → slices 2, 3
- AC5 (unit + browser tests) → slices 1, 2, 3
- AC6 (documentation) → slice 4
- AC7 (full suite passes) → slice 5

## Vertical-slice verification

Each implementation slice is end-to-end (pure spec + renderer + tests); slice 1 is the tracer bullet that establishes the spec contract and slice 2 makes it visible, with slice 3 layering motion. No horizontal "all-spec-then-all-render" phasing. Between slices, the next item's description is reviewed and updated by the implement skill.

## Assumptions recorded (design-level; non-blocking)

- **A1 (colour stops):** reuse the existing golden accent palette already used by `levelAccent` (`0xffaa22`) plus a lighter highlight stop (e.g. `0xffe08a`) so the effect reads as an upgrade accent and not a new colour language.
- **A2 (animation):** deterministic shimmer/gradient sweep (fixed from/to values, no RNG) at roughly 1800–2400 ms per cycle, following the `animateLevelUp` deterministic precedent.
- **A3 (reduced-motion static form):** the static form is the mid-gradient fill (no tween), which is also the state used in replay/headless.
- **A4 (sequencing):** the coordination risk with `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` is largely resolved — F4 (`MS-0MV34MIUY009WRME`) has already removed `spec.upgradeBorder` and introduced `levelAccent`; this plan therefore builds on `levelAccent`, not `upgradeBorder`.
- **A5 (no new texture keys):** the effect is drawn with Phaser `Graphics`/rectangles, not baked into SVG textures, so texture-cache keys stay one-per-base-card.

## Appendix: plan addendum (idempotent)

- **Q1–Q5** were answered by the producer on 2026-10-09 and are recorded in the work item description Appendix (see `MS-C0MV1HJLC5002YZ3U`). The plan re-used those answers; no questions were re-asked.
- **Q6 (plan-time, OPEN QUESTION — non-blocking):** "Exact visual parameters (colour stops, shimmer duration, accent geometry)?" No producer answer sought — A1–A3 above are documented agent assumptions that the implement skill applies; the producer can override during review. Directed to the producer only if the rendered result is judged insufficient.

data.comment:
Remediation after manual-review rejection ("I see no difference in the upgraded cards").

**Root cause.** The slice-2/3 shader gradient was drawn over exactly the same 30x16 top-left region as the flat `ms-upgrade-accent` rectangle, using the same gold palette (0xffaa22 / 0xffe08a) at ~full alpha. Gold-on-gold at the same coordinates = no visible change. The child slices' ACs ("confined to the accent region") were technically met but the parent AC1 ("distinctive at a glance") was not.

**Fix (accent-confined, no full-card sheen).** Reworked `applyUpgradeOverlays()` to draw the effect as a translucent **corner shard**: a right triangle filling the card's top-left quadrant, gold -> pale -> warm-white (0xfff4d6) -> gold gradient, with a moving white highlight band. It stays strictly inside the top-left quadrant (enforced by a unit test), so it is never a full-card stroke, coexists with the owner-coloured outer border, and does not mask the 64x64 art zone or the right-hand text column. The `Lvl N` badge is drawn on top. I interpreted AC4's "confined to the upgrade accent" as the top-left quadrant accent (not a full-card sheen) and used the "inner glow" reading explicitly allowed by AC1.

**Measured visibility (new browser pixel test).** Mean top-left-quadrant luminance for the same card texture: base level 0 = 16.63 -> upgraded level 2 = 34.53 (2.1x). The assertion requires > base + 5.

**Spec.** Added pure fields `sheenAlpha`, `highlightColour`, `highlightAlpha`, `highlightBand`; removed the now-unused `animationAmplitude`; added pure helpers `wrapShaderPhase()` and `circularDistance()` for the seamless sweep. Base cards (level 0) still return a null `shaderEffect` and render unchanged.

**Motion.** Unchanged gating: `shouldAnimateShaderEffect({reducedMotion, replayMode})`; reduced-motion and replay/headless draw the static shard and create no tween; the tween is killed on container destroy.

**Tests.** Unit: `upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` (spec shape, phase helpers, base-vs-upgraded, motion predicate), `owner-card-border.test.ts` (quadrant confinement, shard area > 2x the old accent, vivid multi-colour, motion gating). Browser: `upgrade-shader-effect.browser.test.ts` (presence/absence, measured visibility, animated tween, reduced-motion no-tween, replay no-tween). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; 81 related unit tests and 15 related browser tests pass.

**Docs.** `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Card Upgrade Rendering Pipeline) and `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` updated to describe the corner shard, the foil palette and the measured visibility rationale.

**Assumption to confirm at review.** The shard is translucent over the top-left quadrant of the card art; if the producer prefers a subtler or differently-shaped accent, only the geometry/alpha in `applyUpgradeOverlays()` and the palette constants in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` need tuning.

**BLOCKER — producer decision needed: R2 G5 loss-mode band vs. the mandated enablement gate.**

Implementation is complete and builds; 4730/4734 unit tests pass. The single failure is R2's guard added in MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE:

`tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts > greedy Medium loss mode stays inside the PRD §G5 band`
`AssertionError: expected 0.1212... to be greater than or equal to 0.2`.

**Measured on the post-R2 dev base (200 seeds, mc-balance, 60 turns, greedy):**

| Metric (Medium) | R2 base, old heuristic | + this item's gate |
|---|---:|---:|
| rep→coins / run | 4.79 | 1.60–2.31 |
| reputation-collapse share of losses | 0.320 | **0.121** |
| bankruptcy share of losses | 0.680 | ~0.879 |
| win rate | 0.750 | 0.670 |

The drop is caused by the **enablement gate itself** (AC2), not the value threshold: ratios 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 16 all produce Medium rep-collapse 0.121. The item's goal (spend/keep less reputation on favour) inherently removes the reputation bleeding that R2's band relies on, so no value-threshold in the AC2/AC3 family can keep the band satisfied.

**Parent producer decision already on record (2026-10-06, intake Appendix):** *"the loss-mode band remains owned by R2 (MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE) via card-data, and changing both ... conflicts attribution"* — i.e. the band is **not** a hard gate for this item. The parent's own AC5 only requires that the Medium rep-collapse share **does not increase** (it falls) plus the win-rate ladder and committed-baseline tolerances (both hold: ladder 0.735 ≥ 0.670 ≥ 0.385; winRate/coins within ±0.25 / ±30%).

**Question for the producer:** which resolution?
1. **Widen/refresh the R2 G5 band** to the combined design (e.g. reputation collapse 0.05–0.40, bankruptcy 0.60–0.95) — recommended, since the combined state reduces rep-collapse losses (better outcome) and the parent producer already de-scoped the band; or
2. **Keep the R2 band as a hard gate** — then the favour heuristic must be relaxed enough to restore Medium rep-collapse ≥ 0.20, which contradicts the item goal of using Community Favour less.

Implementation (ratio 12) is staged in this item's worktree, awaiting the decision before commit/push.

## Interview round 1 — clarifying questions (intake)

Context gathered: the competitive closing already runs once after every seat has acted (`resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases`: shared `applyIncome` + per-owner `applyCompetitiveIncome` → shared incident → EndCheck) and is presented text-only/short by `presentCompetitiveClosing` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`). Single-player runs the full phased income choreography (`animateIncomePhases`, ~11s) with coin-grid VFX. `applyCompetitiveIncome` already computes an `OwnerIncomeResult` (with `IncomeResult.phaseBreakdown`) per seat, but the closing currently discards it.

The ask ("run the end of turn phase for each player in turn with full animations and effects") materially changes depending on the answers below, so I need producer input before drafting the brief.

**Q1 — Relationship to MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ ("Refactor end-of-turn presentation … per-seat income feedback")**

- **A. Merge/supersede** — this item absorbs the per-seat income feedback AC; MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ is folded in (or narrowed to only the single/competitive dedup refactor).
- **B. Sequence** — MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ lands first (surface authoritative per-seat income + single presentation path); this item depends on it and layers the full per-seat animations.
- **C. Independent** — this item restores full animations only; MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ keeps the per-seat text breakdown + refactor.

**Recommended: A** — full per-seat animations require the authoritative per-seat income data that MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ's ACs ask for, so folding it in avoids two competing per-seat implementations and duplicated tests.

**Q2 — Engine semantics vs presentation**

- **A. Presentation-only** — keep the shared closing resolved once (shared/street incident semantics, determinism unchanged); after it, replay each seat's income/effects sequentially with full animations.
- **B. Per-seat income in the engine** — restructure the closing so Income + ongoing costs run per seat in turn (shared incident still once).
- **C. Full per-seat closing** — run Income → Incident → EndCheck for every seat (multiple incidents per day).

**Recommended: A** — preserves the established shared-street/incident contract and seeded-replay determinism; the reported loss is presentation ("animations"), and the engine already computes per-owner income.

**Q3 — Duration / boundedness**

- **A. Full choreography per seat, bounded** — full animation per seat in normal play, with a global fast-forward bound and text-only fallback for reduced motion / replay / headless.
- **B. Full choreography per seat, uncapped** — N seats × full single-player duration (~11s each).
- **C. Add a "fast AI turns" toggle** — player-selectable full vs condensed AI closing.

**Recommended: A** — honours MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD AC4 (non-blocking, the day always advances) while restoring effects in normal play.

data.comment:
## Audit-gap remediation (producer audit 2026-10-08)

The parent was rejected because the per-seat closing ran **seat-major** and **in the background** (the next day started while the animations were still playing). Implementing the producer's amended requirement:

### What changed
- **Phase-major ordering (AC1 amended):** `presentPerSeatCompetitiveClosing` now concatenates every non-eliminated seat's `income.phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown` in seat order and calls `animateIncomePhases` **once**. `runIncomePhase` walks the combined slot list per phase, so each phase (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → collection) plays for the human seat, then AI 1, then AI 2, before the next phase begins — exactly the ordering requested in the audit.
- **No background execution (AC6):** `presentTurnClosing` gained `waitForIncomeCollection` + `incomeCollectionCapMs`. The competitive path passes `waitForIncomeCollection: true` and caps the wait at `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS` (180 s), so the day waits for the combined choreography to finish collecting before it advances (bounded; can never hang).
- Removed the now-unused `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_SEAT_STAGGER_MS` constant.
- Docs updated: `src/scenes/README.md`, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, `src/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`, and code comments.

### Tests
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` — rewritten per-seat sequencing suite: one combined phase-major call covering all seats in order, eliminated seats skipped, per-seat text, reduced-motion/replay fallback, and a new "day does not advance until collected" test.
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-sequential-animator.test.ts` — added phase-major tests: each phase runs once over a combined roster, and within a phase seat 0's cards animate before seat 1's.
- Full unit suite green (345 files, 5577 passed, 3 skipped).

### Assumptions (documented per AGENTS.md)
- Producer audit 2026-10-08 is the authoritative latest requirement and amends AC1 to phase-major ordering.
- The global cap for the collection wait is `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS` (180 s); a large roster therefore cannot stall the day beyond that bound.
- HUD coin-collection routing is unchanged from the previous implementation (the combined grid-to-HUD collection still lands on the shared coin counter); per-seat HUD row targeting remains the known risk and is out of scope here.

Supersedes the audit rejection.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implemented display-only HUD reconciliation counting (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8).

Design (documented in code + docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md):
- New scene fields displayedCoins/displayedReputation — display-only running totals initialised to the pre-animation values when the deferred window opens (normal, non-reduced-motion, non-replay path only; the reduced-motion/tutorial/replay fallbacks are untouched).
- refreshHud() renders the running totals during the deferred window (falls back to previousCoins/state as before); animateHudValueChanges keeps receiving the pre-deferred values so sound/pop routing is unchanged.
- Steps: collectIncomeGrids counts up per collected grid icon (slot credited amount / icon count); flyCoinsToPoint/flyRepPips step up at a gain landing and down at a loss departure (signed displayDelta param); animateIncidentDeltaBubbles counts once per logical incident delta (capped bubbles share the signed total).
- Exactness: snapDisplayedTotals sets the totals to previous + pendingDelta at the collection finalize and the incident-reveal cleanup, so the final value lands exactly regardless of per-icon rounding or unanimated ongoing costs.
- Double-count guard: the incident delta is flown in the 'upcoming' phase AND re-enacted by the reveal; displayedIncomeCounted is set by the collection finalize so the reveal replay does not move the totals again.
- In-place text sync (syncHudTotals) so the on-screen totals visibly count without a full transient-clearing refresh.

Tests: new tests/main-street/hud-total-counting.test.ts (pure stepping + collection + upcoming flights + incident bubbles + reduced-motion exemption) and browser coverage added to main-street-renderer-deferred.browser.test.ts (mid-flight intermediate, in-place sync, final value, down-count).

data.comment: Fix attempt 2 (producer rejection of 85d23dbb): Live probe reproduced the rejection exactly — the HUD coin total stayed at the pre value for ~90% of the choreography and only counted in the final collection burst (~0.4–0.8s), and the Reputation total never moved in a normal turn (300→300 while state gained +3).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Fix description: The previous build only counted the HUD totals at the final grid->HUD collection burst (the last phase of the choreography), so a typical turn showed a frozen total for ~6s followed by a sub-second count-up — indistinguishable from 'the total appears at the end'. Reputation never counted at all in a normal turn (only the final snap moved it).

Fix:
- Coins now count as they accrue during each phase (base count-out, synergy line landings, reputation/event fly-ins, negative-event fly-outs), so the HUD visibly builds through the whole choreography.
- Reputation now counts in step with the reputation-phase coin flights (income reputation, excluding the incident share flown in the upcoming phase).
- The grid-to-HUD collection is now a pure visual delivery of already-counted coins; the exact post-reconciliation value is still snapped at the last landing (AC5b).
- Live browser regression tests added (tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts) that drive a REAL end turn and sample the HUD mid-choreography — this is exactly the scenario the producer reported as broken.

**F7 competitive balance check — before/after attribution (MS-0MV8BKEGT002T2H2)**

Canonical competitive profile (200 seeds, 40 shared days, competitive-greedy, 2 players) — full evidence in docs/main-street/monte-carlo-piggyback-evidence.md.

| Point | State | Commit | Seat0 win | Seat1 win | Seat0 avg coins | Seat1 avg coins |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | pre-piggyback code | 85d23dbb | 61.5% | 8.5% | 1991 | 1176 |
| B | current dev, flag OFF (control) | 00a30dcf | 58.5% | 8.0% | 1894 | 1117 |
| C | current dev, piggyback ON | 00a30dcf | 59.0% | 8.0% | 1910 | 1095 |

- Piggyback-only delta (B→C, same-commit flag on/off): win-rate +0.5 pp, coins +0.8%/-2.0% — **within Monte Carlo noise** (n=200, 95% band ≈ ±7 pp).
- Adoption: mechanic fires in 33/200 runs (16.5%); 34 decisions, only 1 join-fully (2.9%) — the 150% premium + F4 liquidity/reward-floor policy keeps the 100% tier rare; 6,862 coins / 6,050 rep flowed through the mechanic, net +5,512 coins.
- Economy verdict: coins did NOT inflate (every seat lower after); direction is deflationary, no unmitigated runaway from 100%-reward participation. **Recommended: no balance change.** Do NOT regenerate docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json (single-player guardrail, unaffected — guardrail tests green). Monitor join-fully rate if the AI policy or event costs change.

Frame-cost measurement (high-reputation frame-cost risk, AC3)

Method: pure per-frame model step (`stepPedestrianFigure` position + bob + bounds reflection) over 3,600 frames (60s at 60fps) on the 16-core host, seeded PRNG. Excludes GPU sprite rendering.

| reputation | figures | ms/frame |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 10 | 0.0031 |
| 5,000 | 100 | 0.0067 |
| 50,000 | 1,000 | 0.0129 |
| 500,000 | 10,000 | 0.1337 |

At 10,000 figures the model step is ~0.13 ms/frame, negligible against the 16.6 ms (60fps) budget; at representative reputations (tens of figures) it is immaterial. The measurement covers the per-figure model update, not GPU render cost, so the uncapped population remains an accepted risk rather than a blocker. Recorded in docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md.

data.comment:
## Implementation evidence — MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W (upgrade-deck draw weight)

**Mechanism.** Added an optional `drawWeight` column to `src/card-data.csv` (default `1`), plumbed through `UpgradeCard.drawWeight` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) and the `upgTemplates` mapping (`src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`). At market refill, `refillSingleRowMarket` now performs a weighted upgrade draw (`drawUpgrade` → `pickWeightedUpgradeIndex`) instead of a plain `decks.upgrade.pop()`. The 78-card deck size and the `shuffleArray` Fisher–Yates call count are unchanged, so the RNG stream stays attributable. An undecorated deck keeps the legacy zero-RNG `pop()` path.

**Eligibility bonus (important design note).** A *static* weight alone could not raise capstone M1 (measured: 4/2 through 100/100 all left capstones at 0–3.4%) because the market shows at most one upgrade per turn and each card is drawn at most once before the game ends — a capstone drawn before its parent reaches level 1 is discarded and never seen again. Refill therefore adds `UPGRADE_ELIGIBLE_DRAW_BONUS = 30` to a **declared** card's weight when a business on the street matches its `targetBusiness` at exactly `requiredLevel` (and below `maxLevel`). This keeps an ineligible chain card at its low base weight (so it stays in the deck) and surfaces it once its prerequisite chain is ready. Non-chain upgrades are never boosted (no declared weight). Weights: capstones `3`, level-1 prerequisites `2`. No card stats/costs changed.

**Before/after M1 pick rate** — canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 turns, greedy/Medium). Before at `3056bd9` (dev HEAD), after on this branch:

| Capstone | Before (purch/appear) | Before M1 | After (purch/appear) | After M1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| upg-grand-bakehouse | 0/33 | 0.0% | 5/67 | **7.5%** |
| upg-restaurant | 0/34 | 0.0% | 6/60 | **10.0%** |
| upg-multiplex | 0/37 | 0.0% | 5/63 | **7.9%** |
| upg-luxury-retreat | 1/32 | 3.1% | 5/57 | **8.8%** |

**Level-1 prerequisite M1 (Medium) rose:** bread-factory 6.5%→26.0%, fast-food 3.6%→34.4%, imax 9.1%→32.3%, resort-spa 7.4%→23.3%.

**Ladder preserved:** Easy 79.0%→76.5%, Medium 69.0%→67.5%, Hard 40.5%→42.0% (Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard; Medium −1.5 pp, within ±5 pp).

**US-19 preserved:** no change to `requiredLevel` on any upgrade or to `canPurchaseUpgrade()`.

**Baseline regenerated (producer-approved Q2(a)):** `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` (greedy + banking-greedy) via `npx vite-node src/scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts`; the guardrail test passes against the new snapshot.

**Tests:** new `tests/main-street/upgrade-draw-weight.test.ts` (9 tests: CSV→deck plumbing, cumulative-weight selection, zero-weight exclusion, eligibility bonus, composition invariants, seeded determinism). Quick affected suites green (139 tests); guardrail tests green.

## Intake interview — open questions (round 1)

**Context gathered.** `evt-farm-table` (Farm-to-Table Feature) is a terminal positive Incident in the Restaurant Renaissance chain (`storyline-restaurant`): trigger `evt-popular-menu` (+300 coins, reject → `evt-farm-table`). Current rewards in `src/card-data.csv`: **coinDelta = 600, reputationDelta = 100**, target `All` (flat, once). `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` asserts the rejected escalation is strictly *better* than the trigger (`coinDelta + reputationDelta > 300`), so a straight cut to one third (200 + 33 = 233) would violate that documented invariant.

**Q1 — Retune target?**
- A) Reduce **by** at least 1/3 → 600→400 coins, 100→66 rep (keeps the escalation-better-than-trigger invariant).
- B) Reduce **to** one third → 600→200 coins, 100→33 rep (largest cut; requires updating/removing the chain-content invariant test, or also lowering Popular Menu Item).
- C) Other exact values.

**Recommended: A** — satisfies “at least 1/3”, keeps the documented chain invariant and the suite green without weakening a design rule.

**Q2 — Scale reputation too?**
- A) Yes — scale both coin and reputation by the same factor.
- B) Coins only (keep reputation at 100).
- C) Reputation only.

**Recommended: A** — preserves the card's coin:rep character.

**Q3 — Validation scope (balance change)?**
- A) Include the canonical 200-seed greedy Monte Carlo guardrail run + short evidence note (matches MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5).
- B) Data + unit/doc updates only (smaller/faster).

**Recommended: A** — repo convention for balance retunes.

## Intake clarifying questions

Context: "phases" could mean the **engine** closing sequence
(`InvestmentResolution -> IncomePhase -> IncidentPhase -> EndCheck`) or the
**presentation** phased income show
(`base -> synergy -> reputation -> events -> upcoming -> collect`,
`animateIncomePhases`). The example "events" is a literal key in the
presentation `phaseMeta` loop, and the phrase "iterate over all phases"
matches that `forEach` — so I lean presentation, but the engine also has an
event-related phase (`InvestmentResolution`).

**Recommended:** A — the presentation phased income show; a phase is empty
when no producing slot contributes to it.

1. **Which sequence should skip empty phases?**
   - A) The presentation phased income show (`animateIncomePhases`: base,
     synergy, reputation, events, upcoming, collect). *(Recommended — matches
     "iterate over all phases" and the "events" example.)*
   - B) Also the engine closing phases
     (`InvestmentResolution/Income/Incident/EndCheck`).
   - C) Also the competitive per-seat closing (same `animateIncomePhases` path).

2. **Skip semantics.** When a phase has nothing to do, should the show:
   - A) Fully skip it — no phase label and no inter-phase gap consumed, so the
     whole show compacts and its total duration shortens accordingly.
     *(Recommended — matches "skip it".)*
   - B) Keep the total show duration fixed and only suppress the empty VFX,
     redistributing the saved time.

3. **Pacing invariant.** `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` currently states
   the phase pace (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, ~11s total) "MUST NOT be shortened".
   If we skip empty phases the show inevitably shortens. Confirm that skipping
   empty phases **supersedes** that note for those phases (the note stays true
   for non-empty phases).
   - A) Yes — skipping shortens the show; update the doc note accordingly.
     *(Recommended.)*
   - B) No — the total must stay ~11s regardless; find another way.

**Empty-phase definition (assumed, correct if wrong):** base = no slot with
`baseIncome > 0`; synergy = no `synergyPhaseFlights`; reputation = no slot with
`repBonus > 0`; events = no `eventDeltaEffects`; upcoming = no slot with a
non-zero `upcomingDeltas` entry. Reduced-motion/replay/headless behaviour is
unchanged.

Implementation approach (MS-0MUYT57J80021CWW):

- **Published anchors.** `refreshHud()` now computes and publishes `scene.hudCoinAnchor` / `scene.hudRepAnchor` — the centre of the numeric portion of each HUD label (label origin + prefix width + number-width/2), measured from the label's own Phaser canvas context via new `hudNumberAnchor`/`measureTextWidth` helpers in `MainStreetRendererHud.ts`. `null` until the first render.
- **Single consumer helper.** New `hudFlightTarget(host, kind, layout)` in `MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` resolves the destination from the published anchor, falling back to the legacy approximate coordinate only when no anchor exists. The legacy coordinates are centralised in `hudCoinFallback`/`hudRepFallback` (`MainStreetConstants.ts`), so no `MainStreetAnimator*` file hard-codes a HUD-flight destination (AC2, enforced by a new source-contract unit test).
- **Wired paths (AC1):** `animateIncomeCollection`, `collectIncomeGrids`, `runIncomePhase` (upcoming `hudCoin`/`hudRep`), `animateSell`, `animateIncidentReveal` → `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`; the HUD delta pop in `animateHudValueChanges` is passed the same anchor `x` from `refreshHud`.
- **Tests:** updated `income-collection-animator`, `upcoming-flow-animation`, `incident-reveal-animator`, `sell-demolition-animator` unit tests to assert destinations equal the published anchors (plus fallback coverage); new `hud-anchor-source-contract.test.ts` structural guard; `hud-strip-layout.browser.test.ts` asserts the published anchor matches the rendered number centre (≤2px, re-render and 7-digit value).

Planning Complete. Decomposed the competitive effective-win-threshold change into four test-first vertical slices and resolved both intake open questions with the producer.

## Resolved producer decisions

- **Q1 = (a)** — adopt `base winThreshold / playerCount` (total seats, human + AI) and supersede the producer-confirmed `base × 0.5^N` formula on **MS-0MUUE0FVZ001VE2D**. That item is now **closed as superseded** (no implementation work).
- **Q2 = nearest 50** — the quotient rounds to the nearest 50 (`Math.round(base / P / 50) * 50`, ties up), so Easy 10000 ÷ 3 → **3350** rather than 3333.

## Plan decomposition (test-first vertical slices)

- **MS-0MUZK64F8000XYO0** — Effective threshold helper and competitive win check *(high; prerequisite for the rest)*. AC1, AC3, AC5.
- **MS-0MUZK64R5008Z8MA** — AI look-ahead uses the effective win threshold *(depends on the above)*. AC4.
- **MS-0MUZK652V001L71C** — Player-facing win target consistency HUD tooltip help *(depends on the first)*. AC2.
- **MS-0MUZK65EI004X4UB** — Document the competitive target rule and validate the suite *(depends on the first)*. AC7.

Every slice opens with failing tests, ends with a green `npm test`, and carries the parent AC text it covers as traceable acceptance criteria.

## Automated review stages

- **Finished Requirements & AC alignment review:** all seven parent ACs map to at least one child slice AC (AC1→slice 1, AC2→slice 3, AC3→slices 1/3, AC4→slice 2, AC5→slice 1, AC6→every slice, AC7→slice 4); no invented or contradictory ACs; removed the stale `tests/main-street/` directory-only Key Files entry and replaced it with concrete test files.
- **Finished Completeness review:** every slice has a goal, `## Acceptance Criteria`, minimal implementation, Key Files, dependencies and deliverables. `validate_key_files_format` returns no issues for the parent and all four children.
- **Finished Sequencing & dependencies review:** slice 1 has no prerequisites; slices 2–4 each carry an inbound edge from slice 1. Test-first is enforced inside each vertical slice (the first AC of each slice requires the tests to be written red before implementation) rather than as a separate test-only item — a standalone all-tests-first item could never satisfy the project rule that every work item ends with a green suite. Recorded as an intentional resolution of that tension.
- **Finished Scope sizing review:** four slices of roughly 1–4 h each, consistent with the Small parent estimate; no slice is a horizontal layer.
- **Finished Acceptance & testability review:** each slice AC names a concrete pass/fail check (unit or rendering test, source grep, or `npm test`); the persistence assertions in slice 1 are explicitly labelled regression guards because they are green once the helper lands.
- **Finished Polish & handoff review:** descriptions use UK English, carry the worked threshold table (Easy 10000 → 5000/3350/2500), the exact helper formula and concrete file/test paths; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit is required.

## AC coverage review

`run_coverage_review(MS-0MUZH6V7C0091SGE)` → `recommendation: proceed`, parent ACs extracted 7/7, coverage 100 %, uncovered `[]`, unresolvable conflicts `[]`.

data.comment:
## Intake research & clarifying questions (round 1)

**Context.** Choice cards are authored in `src/card-data.csv` with `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId` (yes/Accept), `rejectNextCardId` (no/Reject) — exactly one successor per branch. A generalised `StorylineOption` model (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) plus a programmatic registry (`registerStorylineOptions`) already supports arbitrary option lists, but content authoring via CSV still keeps to the two-way Accept/Reject shape. Randomness in the engine is seeded (`state.rng()`) and replay/Monte-Carlo deterministic; `pushChainCard` deliberately consumes no RNG.

### Q1 — Core semantics
What does "an arbitrary number of yes and no outcomes" mean?
- **A)** The player still makes a binary Accept/Reject (yes/no) decision; after the choice, the engine **randomly picks one successor** from a set of candidate yes-outcomes or no-outcomes.
- **B)** The node presents N player options (arbitrary labels), and each option's successor is randomly drawn from its own candidate set.
- **C)** The node presents no player choice; the engine randomly picks one successor from many.

**Recommended:** A — matches "single yes and a single no outcome node" and preserves today's Accept/Reject decision.

### Q2 — Authoring surface / data model
Where do the multiple outcomes get authored, and which surfaces must change?
- **A)** Extend the CSV: new list columns (e.g. `acceptNextCardIds` / `rejectNextCardIds`, delimiter TBD) with legacy single-ID fallback; update author CLI, validator, graph/manifest/schema accordingly.
- **B)** Author only in the generalised JSON/pack model (not CSV), leaving CSV as-is.
- **C)** Implement only as a programmatic seam (registry) with no content-authoring change.

**Recommended:** A — content is CSV-authored and the graph/validator/author tooling all key off CSV.

### Q3 — Randomness & weighting
How should selection behave under deterministic replay?
- **A)** Uniform random using seeded `state.rng()`, one draw per selection at resolution time; replay/Monte-Carlo stay deterministic.
- **B)** Weighted per outcome (default uniform).
- **C)** No engine randomness — content supplies a `successorResolver` callback that performs the selection.

**Recommended:** A for v1 — simplest replay-safe behaviour that matches the request; weighting is a follow-up.

**Status:** awaiting producer answers before the brief is drafted (stage not advanced).

- **Date:** 2026-10-15
- **Before:** seven choice rows authored via legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` (two-way Accept/Reject; Reject skipped the event effect).

data.comment:
## RNG-stream shift (F9 AC)

Monte-Carlo/balance numbers from the pre-change build are **not** numerically comparable: the migrated model consumes exactly one seeded `state.rng()` draw per option selection at resolution time (F3 AC2), shifting the shared stream relative to the old build. Replays *within* this build are deterministic (seeded replay pairs in the harness pin player and AI paths). The Monte-Carlo baseline was regenerated (`generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts`) as part of F6 because the content semantics changed (reject-applies) and the AI decision rule changed (F7); the guardrail tolerances (±0.25 winRate, ±30% coins) hold against the new baseline.

## Follow-ups (recorded, not implemented)
- Weighted outcomes
- Per-candidate conditions
- Option dialog redesign
- UI/i18n copy refinement for the generalised clarity labels (F7 note)

data.comment:
## Test-first tracer bullet complete — findings

### Assertion-helper fix (AC1)
The browser assertion helper read `c.text?.text`, which is always `undefined` for a Phaser `Text` (the rendered string is `.text` itself). Added a `renderedLogTexts()` helper that filters to `Text` objects and reads `.text`, and used it in the two deferral-window tests. Both now pass.

### Introducing commit (AC2)
**`7441311` — MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2 "Defer activity log rendering until after upcoming/phase UI" (2026-10-03).**

Identified by commit-diff inspection: `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete` appears in the source diff for that commit only, and the `create()` lifecycle log-state reset (which does clear `logScrollOffset`, `logMaxScroll`, `logTotalContentH`, `logAutoScroll`, `logPrevEntryCount`) never clears it.

### Root cause
`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete` is a scene-instance field. It is set during the end-of-turn closing presentation and cleared on flush, but is **not reset on scene creation**. Phaser reuses the scene instance across `scene.restart()` / `scene.start()` and state replacements, so a flag left set keeps `refreshLog` early-returning and the Activity Log stays blank for the rest of the session. The fix (child MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9) is to reset the flag in `create()`.

### New browser coverage
- Non-empty log content on load **and** after a completed turn in **single-player**, **tutorial** and **competitive** modes.
- Red-phase repro: flag left set, `scene.restart()`, then assert the flag resets and the log renders "Turn 1". Authored as `it.fails` (project red-phase convention) so the suite stays green until the fix lands; the fix child flips it to a plain `it`.
- Verified: with the one-line reset applied temporarily, the red-phase repro unexpectedly passes (confirming it will pass after the fix), then reverted.

### Browser run (pre-fix revision)
`npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` → **21 passed (21)**. The red-phase repro fails as expected (captured by `it.fails`).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Root cause

The drag gesture never engaged because the boot flow was showing the blocking **New Game mode selector** (MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1) on top of the scene. The suite seeds the tutorial state as `skipped`, so the tutorial offer is answered and the boot flow proceeds to the New Game selector, whose full-screen backdrop is `setInteractive()`. Every synthetic `mousedown`/`mousemove` dispatched at the market row was hit-tested to that backdrop instead of the upgrade card, so Phaser's drag state never left `0` and `beginDrag` exhausted its 30 s deadline:

```
Timed out waiting for the drag to engage after 30000ms (container.x=328, container.y=136)
```

Diagnosed by logging the Phaser input state after `mousedown`: `_temp` (hit-test result) contained a single unnamed `Rectangle` at depth 200, 1280x720 instead of the container at `_list[47]`. Hiding the selector made `_dragState` go `2 -> 4` and the container follow the pointer.

## Secondary issue: the resume overlay / wedged boot flow

The suite originally only cleared `localStorage`, so a run checkpoint saved by an earlier test in the same file (IndexedDB is origin-scoped and shared) was offered to the next boot as the blocking resume overlay. An earlier attempt to fix that by deleting the `save-load-store` IndexedDB database directly wedged the store's open connection: `_campaignLoadPromise` never resolved, so the boot flow never reached its modal decision (and the `New Game` selector never appeared).

## Fix (test-only)

1. New shared helper `tests/main-street/helpers/bootModals.ts` — `dismissBootModals(scene)` polls for the New Game selector, marks `newGameSelectionMade = true` and hides it. Returns without dismissing when no modal is due (replay/resume boot).
2. `upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` — call `dismissBootModals` in `bootGame`; clear the run checkpoint through the live store (`scene.saveStore.clear()`) in `afterEach` instead of deleting the IndexedDB database.
3. `drag.browser.test.ts` — same fix; this also clears MS-0MV1HAOC8006SCON (its failing test `drag onto an empty slot buys and places in one undoable step` had the identical root cause and now passes).

## Verification

`npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts tests/main-street/drag.browser.test.ts` — **11 passed (11)**. Repeated runs are green. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. No production code changed.

## Plan review: root-cause diagnosis (plan session herdr-1791614407-2525662-18202)

The failure is **reproducible in isolation** and is **not** a Phaser-input flake:

```
npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/expanded-viewport.browser.test.ts
→ 1 failed | 1 passed
→ Error: Timed out waiting for card placed on the shared corner
   (slot clicks: [13], uiPhase: market)
```

**Root cause:** `canPlaceFromHand()` in `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` validates the
slot index against the legacy 1×1 grid size with a hard-coded bound:

```ts
if (slotIndex < 0 || slotIndex >= 10) {
  return { legal: false, reason: `Invalid slot index: ${slotIndex}. Must be 0-9.` };
}
```

The test grows the playable lattice to 2×2 (`setStreetPlayableLattice(2, 2)`), where
`worldSlotCount(2, 2) === 40` world slots, and clicks slot **13** — a valid, empty plot.
`onSlotClick` reaches this pre-flight check, which rejects slot 13 as out of range, sets
`s.uiPhase = 'market'` (exactly the observed `uiPhase: market`) and returns before the
card is placed. The `slot clicks: [13]` instrumentation proves the click itself landed;
the test's last-resort fallback also calls `onSlotClick(13)` directly, so Phaser's hit
test is not implicated.

**Supporting evidence:** the execution path `playBusinessFromHand()` in
`src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` already validates against `state.streetGrid.length`, so the
pre-flight check is the only blocker.

**Same defect in three sibling functions** (same file, same hard-coded `10`):

- `placeFromHand` (throws) — line ~56
- `sellFromTableau` (throws) — line ~148
- `canSellFromTableau` (returns illegal) — line ~293

**Related documentation to update:** the `Must be 0-9` error messages; and the
`streetSlotToWorldIndex` docstring in `src/MainStreetAdjacencyGeometry.ts`, which still
describes the removed seam-sharing model ("Shared nodes map to a single index: … the
four-way intersection is one card slot") and is contradicted by
`tests/main-street/expanded-grid-contract.test.ts`.

**Relationship to the other browser-suite failures:** independent. The sibling
`test-failure` items (click-place, composite-click, upgrade-drag-drop, drag visuals) use
the default 1×1 lattice or fail in the drag/pointer pipeline, not this bound check.

Auto-plan completed with review (effort/risk below threshold: **Extra Small** / **Low** → no decomposition needed).

**Review stages**
- Requirements & AC alignment: ACs trace to the reported failure; no invented/contradictory ACs. No change needed.
- Completeness: description covered failure signature/evidence/impact/ACs. Fixed the stale reproduction command (project uses vitest, not pytest) and added a **Key Files** section. No children exist.
- Sequencing & dependencies: N/A (no children). Test work is already the deliverable.
- Scope sizing: N/A (no children); single-test-failure bug, XS.
- Acceptance & testability: ACs are pass/fail and testable by running the suite; AC2 ("related documentation updated") is generic but harmless.
- Polish & handoff: description now copy-pasteable; reproduction command corrected.

**Investigation findings (planning, no code changed)**

Root cause of the named failure: the browser test boots the game but never dismisses the blocking pre-game **New Game mode selector** (`MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1`). That overlay adds a full-screen interactive backdrop at depth 200 which is the top-most hit object under `topOnly`, so the synthetic `mousedown`/`mouseup` dispatched at the empty-slot coordinates is absorbed by the backdrop and `onSlotClick` is never called (confirmed via a temporary diagnostic: `hitTestPointer` returns `Rectangle@200 (1280×720)` above `ms-empty-slot-0`).

Fix direction (for implement): call the existing shared helper `dismissBootModals(scene)` from `tests/main-street/helpers/bootModals.ts` in `bootGame()` after `waitForScene`, as `upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts` and `drag.browser.test.ts` already do.

Adjacent defect exposed by the same file: the second case (`rejecting an unaffordable placement…`, MS-0MUUYI950004TG7F) currently passes only because the click was absorbed by the same backdrop. Once the modal is dismissed the click reaches `onSlotClick`, whose pre-flight legality path intentionally resets `uiPhase` to `'market'` while retaining `pendingHandIndex` (see `MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` and commit `28bb656`). The case asserts `uiPhase === 'placing-from-hand'`, which contradicts the documented code intent and `MS-0MUUYI950004TG7F`'s own AC ("never sticks in `animating`", "keeps the card selected"). data.comment: Design note (browser distribution direction). Q: does Option B (build-time virtual pack registry) support remotely hosted bundles? A: NOT on its own — Option B inlines packs at build time, so it cannot host packs remotely. BUT remote hosting is a *runtime* pack source that already exists in the loader (`contentDir` accepts an `https://` URL and the `fetchManifest`/`fetchCsv` transports fetch over the network). Adopt a **pack-source registry** so the bundled registry is one source among several: (1) bundled/build-time (Option B/C), (2) same-origin static `<base>/packs/` (Option A), (3) remote URL (future, additive). This is a superset of A+B and makes remote bundles a future source rather than a rewrite. Remote hosting adds a trust/supply-chain surface (a remote pack injects card rows); the merge contract rejects bad headers/duplicate ids but not malicious content, so future remote work needs signing/hashing + the content-unlock gate. Decision: build the source-registry abstraction now, implement the bundled source in this item, leave remote as a linked follow-up. Pending producer confirmation of the source-registry refinement.

Tableau-Card-Engine worklog, `dev`). F2 tracks it and bumps the `core` submodule
pointer. Cross-store dependency edges are not supported by `wl`, so the

(F1–F2) → Phase 2 resolution seam (F3) → Phase 3 boot wiring + real assets
(F4–F5) → Phase 4 base-map decoupling (F6) → Phase 5 verification + docs

children; F7 is the acceptance-verification child. Every child keeps the suite
green (tests are added with the behaviour they exercise, never committed red).

**Out of scope (recorded, not expanded here):** remote pack hosting
(`MS-0MV26X8T200852AC`), the browser bundle/discovery mechanism
(`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`), audio/non-art pack assets, and base art-pipeline
changes for base cards.

  F1–F8 and wired 11 dependency edges (test-first order); created cross-repo TCE
  item `CG-0MV590RLL0026M7G`; ran the six automated review stages and the
  AC-coverage review; effort/risk refined to Medium/Medium.

### Appendix: plan-round clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the pack-asset byte transport seam live?** Options:
  (a) Main Street-only injectable `fetchAssetBytes`; (b) add `fetchAsset` /
  inlined `data:` URIs to the core `CardPackLoader`. **Recommended: (a)** —

  dependency is tracked by `CG-0MV590RLL0026M7G` in the Tableau-Card-Engine
  worklog.

  Options: (a) new `src/MainStreetCardPackArt.ts` module; (b) extend

  2026-10-12): **A.** Final: **(a)** — a new module with module-level registry
  state, populated during bootstrap before texture generation.

  extension; the registry inlines a `data:image/png;base64,…` URI. Recorded as
  an assumption; trivially changeable to WebP if the asset extension changes.

data.comment:
Producer review required — clarifying questions for remote pack source:

**Q1 — Configuration mechanism.** How should remote source URLs be declared?
  A. Build-time config constant (requires rebuild to change URL) — simplest, matches existing bundled source pattern.
  B. Launcher-provided setting at runtime (e.g. window.tce.remotePackUrl) — no rebuild needed.
  C. A well-known manifest URL derived from the game version — automatic discovery.
  D. Freeform — describe your preference.

  **Recommended: A** for the initial implementation (simplest, consistent with bundled source). B/C can be added as follow-ups.

**Q2 — Pack-integrity model.** Remote packs inject card rows — what trust mechanism applies?
  A. Host allow-list only (known URLs are trusted; malformed manifests rejected). Lowest friction, minimal change.
  B. Host allow-list + SHA-256 checksum pin on the manifest file. Detects tampering without crypto deps.
  C. Signed manifests (e.g. Ed25519). Strongest trust but requires crypto library and key management.
  D. Freeform — describe your preference.

  **Recommended: A** for initial implementation (host allow-list), with B as a natural follow-up.

**Q3 — Timeout and degradation behaviour.** What is the remote fetch timeout and how is degradation communicated?
  A. Hard timeout (e.g. 3 seconds); remote failures logged as warnings to console; no UI change (bundled packs shown).
  B. Same as A, plus a brief in-game toast/notification when remote packs fail to load.
  C. Same as A, plus the Card Packs panel shows a visible remote packs unavailable indicator.

  **Recommended: A** for initial implementation (conservative, matches existing degradation patterns).

**Q4 — Merge precedence when the same pack id exists in multiple sources.**
  A. Bundled always wins (remote cannot override bundled content). Safest, simplest.
  B. Last-registered wins (remote can override bundled if registered after). More flexible.
  C. First-registered wins (current registry default).
  D. Freeform — describe your preference.

  **Recommended: A** (bundled always wins) to prevent accidental override of core game content by a remote source.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Implementation (pack-source registry + bundled source)

**Design decision (recorded per the item):** the bundled source uses **Option C** — a game-side `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` with Vite `import.meta.glob` (`?raw` for `packs/manifest.json` and `**/cards.csv`, `?url` for pack assets). No `virtual:card-pack-registry` plugin was added; the registry abstraction admits a same-origin or remote source additively without a plugin or core change.

**What landed**
- `PackSource` (total text reader + optional asset-URL resolver) and an ordered, additive, idempotent-by-id `PackSourceRegistry` (first non-null source wins; rejects/nulls degrade to base content).
- `createBundledPackSource()` (the compiled-in production pack) and `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry()`.
- `createPackSourceTransports(registry = bundled)` adapts the registry to the core loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` seams; `packPathFromManifestUrl` / `packPathFromPackUrl` / `resolvePackAssetUrl` are the pure URL→packs-path helpers.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` gains a `packSources` option on load/bootstrap; registry transports are the default for `fetchManifest`/`fetchCsv` while explicit transports (Electron content-dir path) still win. Core loader `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` is unchanged.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts` — 18 tests covering ordering, additive registration, unknown path / empty registry / rejecting source degradation, real-glob resolution of the committed production pack, URL mapping, and end-to-end loader wiring with **no `fetch` / `tce-packs://` request** (spy asserted).

**Build-artefact evidence (manual):** `npm run build` succeeds; the emitted `dist/` embeds `packs/manifest.json` (chunk `manifest-*.js`), the residential `cards.csv` (chunk `cards-*.js`) and all ten pack assets (per-asset `?url` chunks; the committed placeholder PNGs are 1×1 and Vite inlines them as data URIs). No `<contentDir>/packs/` copy step is involved. The automated build-artefact assertion (`BundledPackBuildArtefact.test.ts`) is owned by the verification child MS-0MV53CEUR0097K0H per the parent plan.

**Assumptions:** placeholder pack PNGs are tiny, so Vite inlines them; the verification assertion should scan the emitted bundle text rather than expect standalone `.png` files. Boot-time fallback to the bundled registry (absent `window.tce.contentDir`) is the dependent child MS-0MV53CG6L001A56B, not this item.

data.comment:
Fix pushed to dev (commit 4b91f475).

Root cause: the banking hint's one-shot flag (bankingHintShownAt) lives in per-browser localStorage and no game path EVER cleared it — clearBankingHint/clearTutorialState had zero callers in src/, and updateTutorialStatus explicitly preserves the field. Once the hint fired in a browser (including during earlier playthroughs of this feature), every later new game was permanently muted — matching the operator repro (new game -> play tutorial -> first bank -> no hint).

Fix: re-arm the flag at every new-playthrough boundary:
- applyNewGameSelection (all modes, incl. the single-player early-return path) clears bankingHintShownAt before starting;
- onStartTutorial clears it when the tutorial is (re)started.
The hint stays one-shot within a run (markBankingHintShown unchanged; persistence across restarts of the same save preserved).

Tests:
- unit: rearmBankingHintForNewGame clears flag / preserves state / no-op when never shown; one-shot helpers (tutorial-state.test.ts).
- browser: tutorial-banking-hint-rearm.browser.test.ts — fresh profile fires, stale-flag+new game fires after re-arm, stale-flag+Start Tutorial clears.
- Full suite green at the pushed commit (npm --silent test, scope=full, returncode 0).

data.comment:
Triage: NOT a code regression — environmental ENOSPC (inotify file-watcher exhaustion).

Evidence:
1. Commit 02714453 (the failing commit cited) passed the full suite TWICE via independent gates: the implement finish gate (~22:31, 526s green run) and the pre-push hook (~23:39, push succeeded only because the pre-push full --scope full gate passed). Both preceded the 00:14 start of an orphaned sibling browser vitest.
2. All 9 'failing' tests pass in isolation: tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts (40/40) and harness-cli.test.ts passed together (43/43); a 2-file isolated run was green while the concurrent 4-file run failed.
3. Measured host inotify watches peak at ~62,005/65,536 during my isolated 4-file run; ambient alone is ~28k (orphaned browser vitest 11,001 + tce vite dev server 10,980 + AI_Hell vite 5,905).
4. The errors are 'ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached' from vite-node CLI subprocesses (spawned by the CLI tests) registering recursive watchers on the project root, which now contains 18 sibling worktrees.

Root cause: an ORPHANED process (pid 3027431, ppid=1, parent session dead, hung ~4h, no output for 2h+, holding ~11k inotify watches: 'npx vitest run --project browser') + two long-running vite dev servers. Together they consume the host watch budget; any full-suite run now trips ENOSPC in the CLI-spawn tests.

Recommended fix (operator): kill the orphaned browser vitest (pid 3027431 and its chrome children) and/or raise fs.inotify.max_user_watches (currently 65536). Then re-run the suite — it will be green (file: conflicts are environmental, unrelated to test code).

data.author: rgardler
data.comment:
Resolved: environmental ENOSPC (inotify file-watcher exhaustion), not a code defect.

Root cause: an orphaned `npx vitest run --project browser` process (pid 3027431, ppid=1, hung ~9.7h since 00:14, holding ~13k inotify watches) plus two long-lived `vite --host` dev servers consumed most of fs.inotify.max_user_watches (65536). Full-suite runs then tripped ENOSPC in vite-node CLI subprocesses (unit-cli tests spawing recursive watchers on the project root with 18 sibling worktrees).

Remediation: killed the orphaned process tree; watch usage dropped from ~31k to ~19k.

Verification: full suite green (362 files, 5865 passed, 3 skipped) via the test skill; implement finish gate (full scope x2) green; build (tsc + vite) green.

Docs: added an ENOSPC troubleshooting section to docs/dev/testing.md (MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C).

Commit da4b7936 pushed to dev.

- **Docs drift found.** `docs/game/storylines.md` §4 states the AI picks "the option whose worst-case candidate severity is lowest" with no cost/effect terms, and §2 claims "the AI path needs no changes" — both need updating (child 4).

- **MS-0MVNU5M7Z0095CEM** — *Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect* (bug, P2). `mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` has no `applyResourceDelta`, so a presented cost option is never charged and `extraEffect` never applies (core appends a warning line). The AI projection contract still holds, but end-to-end payment needs this. Same item notes the secondary authoring gap: CSV `options` encoding and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json#/definitions/option` cannot express `cost`/`extraEffect`.

1. Reputation is weighted at `REPUTATION_SEVERITY_SCALE` (100) in the cost/extra-effect projection, matching `eventSeverity`'s existing scale — documented as a re-tunable constant.
2. `decideEventChoice` keeps a backwards-compatible signature: the pending choice becomes an optional extra argument; existing 3-argument callers keep compiling.
3. Cost-bearing options are exercised through the existing `registerStorylineOptions` seam (CSV authoring is a separate item), so no schema change is required here.
4. `conditionalSuccessors` projection is **out of scope** — the parent ACs name `cost`/`extraEffect` only, and conditional successors would add a second resolution-order contract.
5. Resource *enforcement* is out of scope (see MS-0MVNU5M7Z0095CEM).

Directed to whoever runs the balance pass after MS-0MVNU5M7Z0095CEM lands, because the projection cannot be validated end-to-end until costs are actually charged.

AC2 requires evidence of the failed drag's registration state; AC4 requires an explicit guard (not a reordered call); AC6 requires the new test to fail against the unfixed code.
